G737.full: Adverb from a derivative of G142 (compare G740) through the idea of suspension; just now: - this day (hour), hence [-forth], here [-after], hither [-to], (even) now, (this) present.

G738.full: From G737 and G1084; just born, that is, (figuratively) a young convert: - new born.

G739.full: From G737; fresh, that is, (by implication) complete: - perfect.

G740.full: From G142; bread (as raised) or a loaf: - (shew-) bread, loaf.

G741.full: From a presumed derivative of G142; to prepare, that is, spice (with stimulating condiments): - season.

G742.full: Of Hebrew origin [H775]; Arphaxad, a post diluvian patriarch: - Arphaxad.

G743.full: From G757 and G32; a chief angel: - archangel.

G744.full: From G746; original or primeval: - (them of) old (time).

G745.full: From G757 and G2994; people ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish king: - Archelaus.

G746.firstSense: beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, princ…
G746.full: From G756; (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concrete) chief (in various applications of order, time, place or rank): - beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule.

G747.full: From G746 and G71; a chief leader: - author, captain, prince.

G748.full: From G746 and a derivative of G2413; high priestly: - of the high-priest.

G749.firstSense: chief (high) priest, chief of the priests
G749.full: From G746 and G2409; the high priest (literally of the Jews, typically Christ); by extension a chief priest: - chief (high) priest, chief of the priests.

G750.full: From G746 and G4166; a head shepherd: - chief shepherd.

G751.full: From G746 and G2462; horse ruler; Archippus, a Christian: - Archippus.

G752.full: From G746 and G4864; director of the synagogue services: - (chief) ruler of the synagogue.

G753.full: From G746 and G5045; a chief constructor, that is, "architect": - masterbuilder.

G754.full: From G746 and G5057; a principal tax gatherer: - chief among the publicans.

G755.full: From G746 and a compound of G5140 and G2827 (a dinner bed, because composed of three couches); director of the entertainment: - governor (ruler) of the feast.

G756.full: Middle voice of G757 (through the implication of precedence); to commence (in order of time): - rehearse from the) begin (-ning).

G757.full: A primary verb; to be first (in political rank or power): - reign (rule) over.

G758.full: Present participle of G757; a first (in rank or power): - chief (ruler), magistrate, prince, ruler.

G759.full: From G142 (in the sense of sending off scent); an aromatic: - (sweet) spice.

G760.full: Of Hebrew origin [H609]; Asa, an Israelite: - Asa.

G761.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4531; unshaken, that is, (by implication) immovable (figuratively): - which cannot be moved, ummovable.

G762.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4570; not extinguished, that is, (by implication) perpetual: - not to be quenched, unquenchable.

G763.full: From G765; impiety, that is, (by implication) wickedness: - ungodly (-liness).

G764.firstSense: commit (live, that after should live) ungodly
G764.full: From G765; to be (by implication act) impious or wicked: - commit (live, that after should live) ungodly.

G765.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4576; irreverent, that is, (by extension) impious or wicked: - ungodly (man).

G766.full: From a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed óåëãḉò selgēs (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent); licentiousness (sometimes including other vices): - filthy, lasciviousness, wantonness.

G767.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G4591; unmarked, that is, (figuratively) ignoble: - mean.

G768.full: Of Hebrew origin [H836]; Aser (that is, Asher), an Israelite tribe: - Aser.

G769.full: From G772; feebleness (of body or mind); by implication malady; moral frailty: - disease, infirmity, sickness, weakness.

G770.firstSense: be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak
G770.full: From G772; to be feeble (in any sense): - be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak.

G771.full: From G770; a scruple of conscience: - infirmity.

G772.firstSense: more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak (-er, -ness, thing)
G772.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G4599; strengthless (in various applications, literally, or figuratively and morally): - more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak (-er, -ness, thing).

G773.full: Of uncertain derivation; Asia, that is, Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore: - Asia.

G774.full: From G773; an Asian (that is, Asiatic) or inhabitant of Asia: - of Asia.

G775.full: From G773 and G746; an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor: - chief of Asia.

G777.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G4621; without (taking) food: - fasting.

G778.full: Probably from the same as G4632; to elaborate, that is, (figuratively) train (by implication strive): - exercise.

G779.full: From the same as G778; a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle: - bottle.

G780.full: Adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237; with pleasure: - gladly.

G781.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G4680; unwise: - fool.

G782.full: From G1 (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of G4685; to enfold in the arms, that is, (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome: - embrace, greet, salute, take leave.

G783.full: From G782; a greeting (in person or by letter): - greeting, salutation.

G784.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G4695; unblemished (physically or morally): - without spot, unspotted.

G785.full: Of uncertain derivation; a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp": - asp.

G786.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4689; literally without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), that is, (by implication) truceless: - implacable, truce-breaker.

G787.full: Of Latin origin; an assarius or as, a Roman coin: - farthing.

G788.full: Neuter comparative of the base of G1451; more nearly, that is, very near: - close.

G789.full: Probably of foreign origin; Assus, a city of Asia Minor: - Assos.

G790.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2476; to be non stationary, that is, (figuratively) homeless: - have no certain dwelling-place.

G791.full: Fromá̓́óôõ astu (a city); urbane, that is, (by implication) handsome: - fair.

G792.full: Probably from the base of G4766; a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively: - star.

G793.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivation of G4741; unfixed, that is, (figuratively) vacillating: - unstable.

G794.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of óôǻñãù stergō (to cherish affectionately); hard hearted towards kindred: - without natural affection.

G795.full: From a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and óôḯé÷ïò stoichos (an aim); to miss the mark, that is, (figuratively) deviate from truth: - err, swerve.

G796.full: From G797; lightning; by analogy glare: - lightning, bright shining.

G797.full: Probably from G792; to flash as lightning: - lighten, shine.

G798.full: Neuter from G792; properly a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial): - star.

G799.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4793; incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian: - Asyncritus.

G800.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G4859; inharmonious (figuratively): - agree not.

G801.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G4908; unintelligent; by implication wicked: - foolish, without understanding.

G802.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4934; properly not agreed, that is, treacherous to compacts: - covenant-breaker

G803.full: From G804; security (literally or figuratively): - certainty, safety.

G804.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and óöá́ëëù sphallō (to "fail"); secure (literally or figuratively): - certain (-ty), safe, sure.

G805.full: From G804; to render secure: - make fast (sure).

G806.full: Adverb from G804; securely (literally or figuratively): - assuredly, safely.

G807.full: From G809; to be (that is, act) unbecoming: - behave self uncomely (unseemly).

G808.full: From G809; an indecency; by implication the pudenda: - shame, that which is unseemly.

G809.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2192 (in the sense of its congener G4976); properly shapeless, that is, (figuratively) inelegant: - uncomely.

G810.full: From a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4982; properly unsavedness, that is, (by implication) profligacy: - excess, riot.

G811.full: Adverb from the same as G810; dissolutely: - riotous.

G812.full: From G813; to be (that is, act) irregular: - behave self disorderly.

G813.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5021; unarranged, that is, (by implication) insubordinate (religiously): - unruly.

G815.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5043; childless: - childless, without children.

G816.firstSense: behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastl…
G816.full: From a compound of G1 (as a particle of union) and ôåé́íù teinō (to stretch); to gaze intently: - behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes.

G817.full: A particle probably akin to G427; aloof, that is, apart from (literally or figuratively): - in the absence of, without.

G818.firstSense: despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully
G818.full: From G820; to render infamous, that is, (by implication) contemn or maltreat: - despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully.

G819.full: From G820; infamy, that is, (subjectively) comparative indignity, (objectively) disgrace: - dishonour, reproach, shame, vile.

G820.firstSense: despised, without honour, less honourable [comparative degree]
G820.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5092; (negatively) unhonoured or (positively) dishonoured. May show a comparative degree such as less honourable: - despised, without honour, less honourable [comparative degree].

G821.full: From G820; used like G818, to maltreat: - handle shamefully.

G822.full: From the same as G109; mist: - vapour.

G823.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G5114; uncut, that is, (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time): - moment.

G824.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5117; out of place, that is, (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked: - amiss, harm, unreasonable.

G825.full: From Á̓́ôôáëïò Attalos (a king of Pergamus); Attaleia, a place in Pamphylia: - Attalia.

G826.full: From G827; to beam forth (figuratively): - shine.

G827.full: Of uncertain derivation; a ray of light, that is, (by implication) radiance, dawn: - break of day.

G828.full: From Latin ("august"); Augustus, a title of the Roman emperor: - Augustus.

G829.full: From G846 and the base of G2237; self pleasing, that is, arrogant: - self-willed.

G830.firstSense: of own accord, willing of self
G830.full: From G846 and the same as G140; self chosen, that is, (by implication) voluntary: - of own accord, willing of self.

G831.full: From a compound of G846 and å̔́íôçò hentēs (obsolete; a worker); to act of oneself, that is, (figuratively) dominate: - usurp authority over.

G832.full: From G836; to play the flute: - pipe.

G833.full: From the same as G109; a yard (as open to the wind); by implication a mansion: - court, ([sheep-]) fold, hall, palace.

G834.full: From G832; a flute player: - minstrel, piper.

G835.full: Middle voice from G833; to pass the night (properly in the open air): - abide, lodge.

G836.full: From the same as G109, a flute (as blown): - pipe.

G837.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to grow ("wax"), that is, enlarge (literally or figuratively, actively or passively): - grow (up), (give the) increase.

G839.full: From a derivative of the same as G109 (meaning a breeze, that is, the morning air); properly fresh, that is, (adverbially with ellipsis of G2250) tomorrow: - (to-) morrow, next day.

G840.full: From a (presumed) derivative of the same as G109 (meaning blown); rough (properly as a gale), that is, (figuratively) severe: - austere.

G841.full: From G842; self satisfaction, that is, (abstractly) contentedness, or (concretely) a competence: - contentment, sufficiency.

G842.full: From G846 and G714; self complacent, that is, contented: - content.

G843.full: From G846 and a derivative of G2632; self condemned: - condemned of self.

G844.full: From G846 and the same as G3155; self moved ("automatic"), that is, spontaneous: - of own accord, of self.

G845.full: From G846 and G3700; self seeing, that is, an eye witness: - eye-witness.

G846.firstSense: her, it (-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, ([self-], the) same, ([him-, my-, th…
G846.full: From the particle áõ̓͂ au (perhaps akin to the base of G109 through the idea of a baffling wind; backward); the reflexive pronoun self, used (alone or in the compound of G1438) of the third person, and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons: - her, it (-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, ([self-], the) same, ([him-, my-, thy-]) self, [your-] selves, she, that, their (-s), them ([-selves]), there [-at, -by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with], they, (these) things, this (man), those, together, very, which. Compare G848.

G847.full: Genitive (that is, possessive) of G846, used as an adverb of location; properly belonging to the same spot, that is, in this (or that) place: - (t-) here.

G848.firstSense: her (own), (of) him (-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them (-selves), they
G848.full: Contraction for G1438; self (in some oblique case or reflexive relation): - her (own), (of) him (-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them (-selves), they.

G849.full: From G846 and G5495; self handed, that is, doing personally: - with . . . own hands.

G850.full: From áõ̓÷ìḯò auchmos (probably from a base akin to that of G109; dust, as dried by wind); properly dirty, that is, (by implication) obscure: - dark.

G851.full: From G575 and G138; to remove (literally or figuratively): - cut (smite) off, take away.

G852.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5316; non apparent: - that is not manifest.

G853.full: From G852; to render unapparent, that is, (actively) consume (becloud), or (passively) disappear (be destroyed): - corrupt, disfigure, perish, vanish away.

G854.full: From G853; disappearance, that is, (figuratively) abrogation: - vanish away.

G855.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5316; non manifested, that is, invisible: - vanished out of sight.

G856.full: From a compound of G575 and the base of G1476; a place of sitting apart, that is, a privy: - draught.

G857.full: From a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and G5339; unsparingness, that is, austerity (ascetism): - neglecting.

G858.full: From a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and öǻëëïò phellos (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); smoothness, that is, (figuratively) simplicity: - singleness.

G859.full: From G863; freedom; (figuratively) pardon: - deliverance, forgiveness, liberty, remission.

G860.full: From G680; probably a ligament (as fastening): - joint.

G861.full: From G862; incorruptibility; generally unending existence; (figuratively) genuineness: - immortality, incorruption, sincerity.

G862.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5351; undecaying (in essence or continuance): - not (in-, un-) corruptible, immortal.

G863.firstSense: cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) aw…
G863.full: From G575 and é̔́çìé hiēmi (to send; an intensive form of åé̓͂ìé eimi (to go)); to send forth, in various applications: - cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up.

G864.full: From G575 and the base of G2425; to go (that is, spread) forth (by rumor): - come abroad.

G865.firstSense: depiser of those that are good
G865.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5358; hostile to virtue: - depiser of those that are good.

G866.firstSense: without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre
G866.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5366; unavaricious: - without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre.

G867.full: From G864; properly arrival, that is, (by implication) departure: - departing.

G868.firstSense: depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self
G868.full: From G575 and G2476; to remove, that is, (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc.: - depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self.

G869.full: Adverb from G852 (contracted); unawares, that is, unexpectedly: - suddenly.

G870.full: Adveb from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and G5401; fearlessly: - without fear.

G871.full: From G575 and G3666; to assimilate closely: - make like.

G872.full: From G575 and G3708; to consider attentively: - look.

G873.full: From G575 and G3724; to set off by boundary, that is, (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc.: - divide, separate, sever.

G874.full: From a compound of G575 and G3729; a starting point, that is, (figuratively) an opportunity: - occasion.

G875.full: From G876; to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy): - foam.

G876.full: Apparently a primary word; froth, that is, slaver: - foaming.

G877.full: From G878; senselessness, that is, (euphemistically) egotism; (morally) recklessness: - folly, foolishly (-ness).

G878.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5424; properly mindless, that is, stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specifically) egotistic, (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving: - fool (-ish), unwise.

G879.full: From a compound of G575 and G5258; properly to become awake, that is, (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber: - fall asleep.

G880.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5456; voiceless, that is, mute (by nature or choice); figuratively unmeaning: - dumb, without signification.

G881.full: Of Hebrew origin [H271]; Achaz, an Israelite: - Achaz.

G882.full: Of uncertain derivation; Achaia (that is, Greece), a country of Europe: - Achaia.

G883.full: From G882; an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian: - Achaicus.

G884.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5483; thankless, that is, ungrateful: - unthankful.

G885.full: Probably of Hebrew origin (compare [H3137]); Achim, an Israelite: - Achim.

G886.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5499; unmanufactured, that is, inartificial: - made without (not made with) hands.

G887.full: Of uncertain derivation; dimness of sight, that is, (probably) a cataract: - mist.

G888.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5534 (compare G5532); useless, that is, (euphemistically) unmeritorious: - unprofitable.

G889.full: From G888; to render useless, that is, spoil: - become unprofitable.

G890.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5543; inefficient, that is, (by implication) detrimental: - unprofitable.

G891.firstSense: as far as, for, in (-to), till, (even, un-) to, until, while
G891.full: Akin to G206 (through the idea of a terminus); (of time) until or (of place) up to: - as far as, for, in (-to), till, (even, un-) to, until, while. Compare G3360.

G892.full: Perhaps remotely from ÷ǻù cheō (to shed forth); chaff (as diffusive): - chaff.

G893.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5579; veracious: - that cannot lie.

G894.full: Of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, that is, [figuratively] calamity): - wormwood.

G895.full: From G1 (as a negative particle) and G5590; lifeless, that is, inanimate (mechanical): - without life.

G896.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1168]; Baal, a Phaenician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry): - Baal.

G897.full: Of Hebrew origin [H894]; Babylon, the capital of Chaldaea (literally or figuratively as a type of tyranny): - Babylon.

G898.full: From the same as G899; a step, that is, (figuratively) grade (of dignity): - degree.

G899.full: From the same as G901; profundity, that is, (by implication) extent; (figuratively) mystery: - deep (-ness, things), depth.

G901.full: From the base of G939; profound (as going down), literally or figuratively: - deep, very early.

G902.full: A diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of G939; a palm twig (as going out far): - branch.

G903.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1109]; Balaam, a mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher): - Balaam.

G904.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1111]; Balak, a Moabite: - Balac.

G905.full: Probably remotely from G906 (as a depository); a pouch (for money): - bag, purse.

G906.firstSense: arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust
G906.full: A primary verb; to throw (in various applications, more or less violent or intense): - arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust. Compare G4496.

G907.full: From a derivative of G911; to make whelmed (that is, fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism: - baptist, baptize, wash.

G908.full: From G907; baptism (technically or figuratively): - baptism.

G909.full: From G907; ablution (ceremonially or Christian): - baptism, washing.

G910.full: From G907; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner: - Baptist.

G911.full: A primary verb; to whelm, that is, cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or specific sense, that is, (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye): - dip.

G912.full: Of Chaldee origin ([H1347] and G5 (Greek)); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite: - Barabbas.

G913.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1301]; Barak, an Israelite: - Barak.

G914.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1296]; Barachias (that is, Berechijah), an Israelite: - Barachias.

G915.full: Of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (that is, non Greek): - barbarian (-rous).

G916.full: From G926; to weigh down (figuratively): - burden, charge, heavy, press.

G918.full: Of Chaldee origin [H1247] and [H8526]; son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomaeus, a Christian apostle: - Bartholomeus.

G919.full: Of Chaldee origin [H1247] and [H3091]; son of Jesus (or Joshua); Barjesus, an Israelite: - Barjesus.

G920.full: Of Chaldee origin [H1247] and [H3124]; son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite: - Bar-jona.

G921.full: Of Chaldee origin [H1247] and [H5029]; son of Nabas (that is, prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite: - Barnabas.

G922.full: Probably from the same as G939 (through the notion of going down; compare G899); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively a load, abundance, authority: - burden (-some), weight.

G923.full: Of Chaldee origin [H1247] and probably [H6634]; son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Barsabas, the name of two Israelites: - Barsabas.

G924.full: Of Chaldee origin [H1247] and [H2931]; son of Timaeus (or the unclean); Bartimaeus, an Israelite: - Bartimus.

G926.full: From the same as G922; weighty, that is, (figuratively) burdensome, grave: - grievous, heavy, weightier.

G927.full: From G926 and G5092; highly valuable: - very precious.

G928.full: From G931; to torture: - pain, toil, torment, toss, vex.

G931.full: Perhaps remotely from the same as G939 (through the notion of going to the bottom); a touch stone, that is, (by analogy) torture: - torment.

G932.full: From G935; properly royalty, that is, (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively): - kingdom, + reign.

G933.full: Neuter of G934; a palace: - king's court.

G935.full: Probably from G939 (through the notion of a foundation of power); a sovereign (abstractly, relatively or figuratively): - king.

G936.full: From G935; to rule (literally or figuratively): - king, reign.

G937.full: From G935; regal (in relation), that is, (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent: - king's, nobleman, royal.

G938.full: Feminine from G936; a queen: - queen.

G939.full: From âáé́íù bainō (to walk); a pace ("base"), that is, (by implication) the foot: - foot.

G940.full: Akin to G5335; to malign, that is, (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations): - bewitch.

G941.full: Perhaps remotely derived from the base of G939 (through the idea of removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.): - bear, carry, take up.

G942.full: Of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub: - bramble, bush.

G943.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1324]; a bath, or measure for liquids: - measure.

G944.full: Of uncertain derivation; a frog: - frog.

G945.full: From Âá́ôôïò Battos (a proverbial stammerer) and G3056; to stutter, that is, (by implication) to prate tediously: - use vain repetitions.

G946.full: From G948; a detestation, that is, (specifically) idolatry: - abomination.

G947.full: From G948; detestable, that is, (specifically) idolatrous: - abominable.

G948.full: From a (presumed) derivative ofâäǻù bdeō (to stink); to be disgusted, that is, (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry): - abhor, abominable.

G949.full: From the base of G939 (through the idea of basality); stable (literally or figuratively): - firm, of force, stedfast, sure.

G950.full: From G949; to stabilitate (figuratively): - confirm, (e-) stablish.

G952.full: From the base of G939 and âçëḯò bēlos (a threshold); accessible (as by crossing the door way), that is, (by implication of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked: - profane (person).

G954.full: Of Chaldee origin (by parody upon [H1176]); dung god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan: - Beelzebub.

G955.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1100]; worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan: - Belial.

G956.full: From G906; a missile, that is, spear or arrow: - dart.

G957.full: Neuter of a compound of a derivative of G906 (used for the compound of G18); better: - very well.

G958.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1144]; Benjamin, an Israelite: - Benjamin.

G959.full: From a provincial form of G5342 and G3529; victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family: - Bernice.

G960.full: Perhaps a provincial from a derivative of G4008 (Peraea, that is, the region beyond the coast line); Beraea, a place in Macedonia: - Berea.

G961.full: From G960; a Beraeaean or native of Beraea: - of Berea.

G962.full: Of Hebrew origin ([H1004] and [H5679]); ferry house; Bethabara (that is, Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan: - Bethabara.

G963.full: Of Chaldee origin; date house; Bethany, a place in Palestine: - Bethany.

G964.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H1004] and [H2617]); house of kindness; Bethesda, a pool in Jerusalem: - Bethesda.

G965.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1036]; Bethleem (that is, Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine: - Bethlehem.

G966.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H1004] and [H6719]); fishing house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine: - Bethsaida.

G967.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H1004] and [H6291]); fig house; Bethphage, a place in Palestine: - Bethphage.

G968.full: From the base of G939; a step, that is, foot breath; by implication a rostrum, that is, tribunal: - judgment-seat, set [foot] on, throne.

G970.full: Probably akin to G979 (through the idea of vital activity); force: - violence.

G971.full: From G970; to force, that is, (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized: - press, suffer violence.

G973.full: From G971; a forcer, that is, (figuratively) energetic: - violent.

G974.full: A diminutive of G975; a booklet: - little book.

G975.full: A diminutive of G976; a roll: - bill, book, scroll, writing.

G976.full: Properly the inner bark of the papyrus plant, that is, (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing: - book.

G977.full: A reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of G1006); to eat: - eat.

G978.full: Of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia: - Bithynia.

G979.full: A primary word; life, that is, (literally) the present state of existence; by implication the means of livelihood: - good, life, living.

G980.full: From G979; to spend existence: - live.

G981.full: From G980; living (properly the act, by implication the mode): - manner of life

G982.firstSense: of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life
G982.full: From a derivative of G980; relating to the present existence: - of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life.

G984.full: A primary verb; properly to hinder, that is, (by implication) to injure: - hurt.

G985.full: From âëáóôḯò blastos (a sprout); to germinate; by implication to yield fruit: - bring forth, bud, spring (up).

G986.full: Perhaps the same as the base of G985; Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa: - Blastus.

G987.firstSense: (speak) blaspheme (-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil
G987.full: From G989; to vilify; specifically to speak impiously: - (speak) blaspheme (-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil.

G988.full: From G989; vilification (especially against God): - blasphemy, evil speaking, railing.

G989.full: From a derivative of G984 and G5345; scurrilous, that is, calumnious (against man), or (specifically) impious (against God): - blasphemer (-mous), railing.

G990.full: From G991; vision (properly concrete; by implication abstract): - seeing.

G991.firstSense: behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed
G991.full: A primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively): - behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed. Compare G3700.

G992.full: From G906; fit to be cast (that is, applied): - must be put.

G993.full: Of Chald origin ([H1123] and [H7266]); sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the Apostles: - Boanerges.

G994.full: Apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; to halloo, that is, shout (for help or in a tumultuous way): - cry.

G995.full: From G994; a halloo, that is, call (for aid, etc.): - cry.

G996.full: From G998; aid; specifically a rope or chain for frapping a vessel: - help.

G997.full: From G998; to aid or relieve: - help, succour.

G998.full: From G995 and èǻù theō (to run); a succorer: - helper.

G999.full: Akin to G900; a hole (in the ground); specifically a cistern: - ditch, pit.

G1000.full: From G906; a throw (as a measure of distance): - cast.

G1001.full: From G1002; to heave the lead: - sound.

G1002.full: From G906; a missile, that is, javelin: - dart.

G1003.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1162]; Booz, (that is, Boaz), an Israelite: - Booz.

G1005.full: Of uncertain derivation; the north (properly wind): - north.

G1006.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb (compare G977 and G1016); to pasture; by extension to fodder; reflexively to graze: - feed, keep.

G1007.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1160]; Bosor (that is, Beor), a Moabite: - Bosor.

G1008.full: From G1006; herbage (as if for grazing): - herb.

G1009.full: Of uncertain derivation; a bunch (of grapes): - (vine) cluster (of the vine).

G1010.full: From G1011; an adviser, that is, (specifically) a councillor or member of the Jewish Sanhedrim: - counsellor.

G1011.firstSense: consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose
G1011.full: From G1012; to advise, that is, (reflexively) deliberate, or (by implication) resolve: - consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose.

G1012.full: From G1014; volition, that is, (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose: - + advise, counsel, will.

G1013.full: From G1014; a resolve: - purpose, will.

G1014.firstSense: be disposed, minded, intend, list (be, of own) will (-ing)
G1014.full: Middle voice of a primary verb; to "will", that is, (reflexively) be willing: - be disposed, minded, intend, list (be, of own) will (-ing). Compare G2309.

G1015.full: Probably of foreign origin; a hillock: - hill.

G1016.full: bous booce Probably from the base of G1006; an ox (as grazing), that is, an animal of that species ("beef"): - ox.

G1017.full: From âñáâåṍò brabeus (an umpire; of uncertain derivation); an award (of arbitration), that is, (specifically) a prize in the public games: - prize.

G1018.full: From the same as G1017; to arbitrate, that is, (generally) to govern (figuratively prevail): - rule.

G1019.full: From G1021; to delay: - be slack, tarry.

G1020.full: From G1021 and a prolonged form of G4126; to sail slowly: - sail slowly.

G1021.full: Of uncertain affinity; slow; figuratively dull: - slow.

G1023.full: Properly a compound of G1024, but apparently in the sense of âñá́óóù brassō (to wield); the arm, that is, (figuratively) strength: - arm.

G1024.full: Of uncertain affinity; short (of time, place, quantity, or number): - few words, little (space, while).

G1025.full: Of uncertain affinity; an infant (properly unborn) literally or figuratively: - babe, (young) child, infant.

G1026.full: A primary verb; to moisten (especially by a shower): - (send) rain, wash.

G1027.full: Akin to âñǻìù bremō (to roar); thunder: - thunder (-ing).

G1029.full: Of uncertain derivation; a noose: - snare.

G1030.full: From G1031; a grating (of the teeth): - gnashing.

G1031.full: A primary verb; to grate the teeth (in pain or rage): - gnash.

G1032.full: A primary verb; to swell out, that is, (by implication) to gush: - send forth.

G1033.full: From the base of G977; food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonial) articles allowed or forbiden by the Jewish law: - meat, victuals.

G1035.full: From the base of G977; (abstractly) eating (literally or figuratively); by extension (concretely) food (literally or figuratively): - eating, food, meat.

G1036.full: From G1037; to sink; by implication to drown: - begin to sink, drown.

G1037.full: A variation of G899; depth, that is, (by implication) the sea: - deep.

G1038.full: From âṍñóá bursa (a hide); a tanner: - tanner.

G1039.full: From G1040; made of linen (neuter of linen cloth): - fine linen.

G1040.full: Of Hebrew origin [H948]; white linen: - fine linen.

G1041.full: From the base of G939; properly a stand, that is, (specifically) an altar: - altar.

G1042.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H1355]); the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem: - Gabbatha.

G1043.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1403]; Gabriel, an archangel: - Gabriel.

G1044.full: From ãñáé́íù grainō (to gnaw); an ulcer ("gangrene"): - canker.

G1045.full: Gad gad Of Hebrew origin [H1410]; Gad, a tribe of Israelite: - Gad.

G1046.full: From Ãáäáñá́ Gadara (a town East of the Jordan); a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara: - Gadarene.

G1047.full: Of foreign origin; a treasure: - treasure.

G1048.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5804]; Gazah (that is, Azzah), a place in Palestine: - Gaza.

G1049.full: From G1047 and G5438; a treasure house, that is, a court in the temple for the collection boxes: - treasury.

G1050.full: Of Latin origin; Gaius (that is, Caius), a Christian: - Gaius.

G1052.full: From G1053; a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia: - Galatian.

G1053.full: Of foreign origin; Galatia, a region of Asia: - Galatia.

G1054.full: From G1053; Galatic or relating to Galatia: - of Galatia.

G1056.full: Galilaia gal-il-ah-yah Of hebrew origin [H1551]; Galilaea (that is, the heathen circle), a region of Palestine: - Galilee.

G1057.full: From G1056; Galilaean or belonging to Galilaea: - Galilan, of Galilee.

G1058.full: Of Latin origin; Gallion (that is, Gallio), a Roman officer: - Gallio

G1059.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1583]; Gamaliel (that is, Gamliel), an Israelite: - Gamaliel.

G1060.full: From G1062; to wed (of either sex): - marry (a wife).

G1061.full: From G1062; to espouse (a daughter to a husband): - give in marriage.

G1062.full: Of uncertain affinity; nuptials: - marriage, wedding.

G1063.firstSense: and, as, because (that), but, even, for indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, veri…
G1063.full: gar gar A primary particle; properly assigning a reason (used in argument, explanation or intensification; often with other particles): - and, as, because (that), but, even, for indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, verily, what, why, yet.

G1064.full: Of uncertain derivation; the stomach; by analogy the matrix; figuratively a gourmand: - belly, + with child, womb.

G1065.firstSense: and besides, doubtless, at least, yet
G1065.full: ge gheh A primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other particles prefixed): - and besides, doubtless, at least, yet.

G1066.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1439]; Gedeon (that is, Gideon), an Israelite: - Gedeon.

G1067.full: Of Hebrew origin ([H1516] and [H2011]); valley of (the son of) Hinnom; gehenna (or Ge-Hinnom), a valley of Jerusalem, used (figuratively) as a name for the place (or state) of everlasting punishment: - hell.

G1068.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H1660] and [H8081]); oil press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem: - Gethsemane.

G1069.full: From G1093; a neighbor (as adjoining one's ground); by implication a friend: - neighbour.

G1070.full: Of uncertain affinity; to laugh (as a sign of joy or satisfaction): - laugh.

G1071.full: From G1070; laughter (as a mark of gratification): - laughter.

G1072.full: Transitive from G1073; to fill entirely: - fill (be) full.

G1073.full: A primary verb; to swell out, that is, be full: - be full.

G1074.full: From (a presumed derivative of) G1085; a generation; by implication an age (the period or the persons): - age, generation, nation, time.

G1075.full: From G1074 and G3056; to reckon by generations, that is, trace in genealogy: - count by descent.

G1076.full: From the same as G1075; tracing by generations, that is, "genealogy": - genealogy.

G1077.full: Neuter plural of a derivative of G1078; birthday ceremonies: - birthday.

G1078.full: From the same as G1074; nativity; figuratively nature: - generation, nature (-ral).

G1079.full: Feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G1074; birth: - birth.

G1080.firstSense: bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring
G1080.full: From a variation of G1085; to procreate (properly of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively to regenerate: - bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring.

G1081.full: From G1080; offspring; by analogy produce (literally or figuratively): - fruit, generation.

G1082.full: Of Hebrew origin (compare [H3672]); Gennesaret (that is, Kinnereth), a lake and plain in Palestine: - Gennesaret.

G1084.full: From G1080; born: - they that are born.

G1085.firstSense: born, country (-man), diversity, generation, kind (-red), nation, offspring, stock
G1085.full: From G1096; "kin" (abstractly or concretely, literally or figuratively, individually or collectively): - born, country (-man), diversity, generation, kind (-red), nation, offspring, stock.

G1086.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1622]; a Gergesene (that is, Girgashite) or one of the aborigines of Palestine: - Gergesene.

G1087.full: From G1088; the eldership, that is, (collectively) the Jewish Sanhedrim: - senate.

G1088.full: Of uncertain affinity (compare G1094); aged: - old.

G1089.full: A primary verb; to taste; by implication to eat; figuratively to experience (good or ill): - eat, taste.

G1090.full: From G1092; to till (the soil): - dress.

G1091.full: Neuter of a (presumed) derivative of G1092; cultivable, that is, a farm: - husbandry.

G1092.full: From G1093 and the base of G2041; a land worker, that is, farmer: - husbandman.

G1093.full: Contracted from a primary word; soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application): - country, earth (-ly), ground, land, world.

G1094.full: Akin to G1088; senility: - old age.

G1095.full: From G1094; to be senescent: - be (wax) old.

G1096.firstSense: arise be assembled, be (come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to p…
G1096.full: A prolonged and middle form of a primary verb; to cause to be ("gen" -erate), that is, (reflexively) to become (come into being), used with great latitude (literally, figuratively, intensively, etc.): - arise be assembled, be (come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, be done, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought.

G1097.firstSense: allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) known (-ledge), perceive, be resolved, can speak, be…
G1097.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to "know" (absolutely), in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as shown at left, with others not thus clearly expressed): - allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) known (-ledge), perceive, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand.

G1098.full: Akin to G1099; sweet wine, that is, (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine: - new wine.

G1099.full: Of uncertain affinity; sweet (that is, not bitter nor salt): - sweet, fresh.

G1100.full: Of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication a language (specifically one naturally unacquired): - tongue.

G1101.full: From G1100 and the base of G2889; properly a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind instruments in), that is, (by extension) a casket or (specifically) purse: - bag.

G1102.full: By variation for a derivative from êíá́ðôù knaptō (to tease cloth); a cloth dresser: - fuller.

G1103.full: From the same as G1077; legitimate (of birth), that is, genuine: - own, sincerity, true.

G1104.full: Adverb from G1103; genuinely, that is, really: - naturally.

G1105.full: Akin to G3509; gloom (as of a storm): - blackness.

G1106.firstSense: advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will
G1106.full: From G1097; cognition, that is, (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.): - advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will.

G1107.firstSense: certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot
G1107.full: From a derivative of G1097; to make known; subjectively to know: - certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot.

G1108.full: From G1097; knowing (the act), that is, (by implication) knowledge: - knowledge, science.

G1110.full: From G1097; well known: - acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable.

G1111.full: Of uncertain derivation; to grumble: - murmur.

G1112.full: From G1111; a grumbling: - grudging, murmuring.

G1114.full: From ãïá́ù goaō (to wail); properly a wizard (as muttering spells), that is, (by implication) an impostor: - seducer.

G1115.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H1538]); the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem: - Golgotha.

G1116.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6017]; Gomorrha (that is, Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea: - Gomorrha.

G1117.full: From G1073; a load (as filling), that is, (specifically) a cargo, or (by extension) wares: - burden, merchandise.

G1118.full: From the base of G1096; a parent: - parent.

G1120.full: From a compound of G1119 and the alternate of G4098; to fall on the knee: - bow the knee, kneel down.

G1121.firstSense: bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written
G1121.full: From G1125; a writing, that is, a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning: - bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.

G1122.full: From G1121; a writer, that is, (professionally) scribe or secretary: - scribe, town-clerk.

G1124.full: From G1125; a document, that is, holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it): - scripture.

G1125.full: A primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively to describe: - describe, write (-ing, -ten).

G1126.full: From ãñáõ͂ò graus (an old woman) and G1491; crone like, that is, silly: - old wives'.

G1127.full: From G1453; to keep awake, that is, watch (literally or figuratively): - be vigilant, wake, (be) watch (-ful).

G1128.full: From G1131; to practise naked (in the games), that is, train (figuratively): - exercise.

G1129.full: From G1128; training, that is, (figuratively) asceticism: - exercise.

G1130.full: From a derivative of G1131; to strip, that is, (reflexively) go poorly clad: - be naked.

G1131.full: Of uncertain affinity; nude (absolutely or relatively, literally or figuratively): - naked.

G1132.full: From G1131; nudity (absolutely or comparatively): - nakedness.

G1133.full: A diminutive from G1135; a little (that is, foolish) woman: - silly woman.

G1135.full: Probably from the base of G1096; a woman; specifically a wife: - wife, woman.

G1136.full: Gōg gogue Of Hebrew origin [H1463]; Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist: - Gog.

G1137.full: Probably akin to G1119; an angle: - corner, quarter.

G1138.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1732]; Dabid (that is, David), the Israelite king: - David.

G1139.firstSense: have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil (-s)
G1139.full: Middle voice from G1142; to be exercised by a daemon: - have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil (-s).

G1140.full: Neuter of a derivative of G1142; a daemonic being; by extension a deity: - devil, god.

G1141.full: From G1140 and G1142; daemon like: - devilish.

G1142.full: From äáé́ù daiō (to distribute fortunes); a demon or super natural spirit (of a bad nature): - devil.

G1143.full: A prolonged form of a primary root; to bite, that is, (figuratively) thwart: - bite.

G1144.full: Of uncertain affinity; a tear: - tear.

G1145.full: From G1144; to shed tears: - weep. Compare G2799.

G1146.full: From G1147; a finger ring: - ring.

G1147.full: Probably from G1176; a finger: - finger.

G1148.full: Probably of Chaldee origin; Dalmanutha, a place in Palestine: - Dalmanutha.

G1149.full: Probably of foreign derivation; Dalmatia, a region of Europe: - Dalmatia.

G1150.full: A variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to tame: - tame.

G1151.full: Probably from the base of G1150; a heifer (as tame): - heifer.

G1152.full: Probably from the base of G1150; perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman: - Damaris.

G1153.full: From G1154; a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus: - Damascene.

G1154.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1834]; Damascus, a city of Syria: - Damascus.

G1155.full: From G1156; to loan on interest; reflexively to borrow: - borrow, lend.

G1156.full: From äá́íïò danos (a gift); probably akin to the base of G1325; a loan: - debt.

G1158.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1840]; Daniel, an Israelite: - Daniel.

G1159.full: From G1160; to expend, that is, (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a bad one) to waste: - be at charges, consume, spend.

G1160.full: From äá́ðôù daptō (to devour); expense (as consuming): - cost.

G1161.firstSense: also, and, but, moreover, now [often unexpressed in English]
G1161.full: de deh A primary particle (adversative or continuative); but, and, etc.: - also, and, but, moreover, now [often unexpressed in English].

G1162.full: From G1189; a petition: - prayer, request, supplication.

G1163.firstSense: behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need (-ful), ought, should
G1163.full: Third person singular active present of G1210; also äåḯí deon which is neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was, etc.) necessary (as binding): - behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need (-ful), ought, should.

G1164.full: From the base of G1166; a specimen (as shown): - example.

G1165.full: From G1164; to exhibit: - make a shew.

G1166.full: A prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to show (literally or figuratively): - shew.

G1168.full: From G1167; to be timid: - be afraid.

G1169.full: From äǻïò deos (dread); timid, that is, (by implication) faithless: - fearful.

G1170.full: Probably from the same as G1171 (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, that is, strange); so and so (when the person is not specified): - such a man.

G1171.full: Adverb from a derivative of the same as G1169; terribly, that is, excessively: - grievously, vehemently.

G1172.full: From G1173; to dine, that is, take the principal (or evening) meal: - sup (X -per).

G1173.full: From the same as G1160; dinner, that is, the chief meal (usually in the evening): - feast, supper.

G1174.full: The compound of a derivative of the base of G1169 and G1142; more religious than others: - too superstitious.

G1175.full: From the same as G1174; religion: - superstition.

G1176.full: A primary number; ten: - [eight-] een, ten.

G1177.full: From G1176 and G1417; two and ten, that is, twelve: - twelve.

G1178.full: From G1176 and G4002; ten and five, that is, fifteen: - fifteen.

G1179.full: From G1176 and G4172; the ten city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria: - Decapolis.

G1180.full: From G1176 and G5064; ten and four, that is, fourteen: - fourteen.

G1181.full: Feminine of G1182; a tenth, that is, as a percentage or (technically) tithe: - tenth (part), tithe.

G1183.full: From G1181; to tithe, that is, to give or take a tenth: - pay (receive) tithes.

G1185.full: From the baes of G1388; to entrap, that is, (figuratively) delude: - allure, beguile, entice.

G1186.full: Probably from äñṍò drus (an oak); a tree: - tree.

G1187.full: From G1188 and G2983; a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light armed soldier: - spearman.

G1188.full: From G1209; the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually takes): - right (hand, side).

G1189.full: Middle voice of G1210; to beg (as binding oneself), that is, petition: - beseech, pray (to), make request. Compare G4441.

G1190.full: From G1191; a Derbaean or inhabitant of Derbe: - of Derbe.

G1191.full: Of foreign origin; Derbe, a place in Asia Minor: - Derbe.

G1193.full: From G1192; made of hide: - leathern, of a skin.

G1194.full: A primary verb; properly to flay, that is, (by implication) to scourge, or (by analogy) to thrash: - beat, smite.

G1195.full: From a (presumed) derivative of G1196; to be a binder (captor), that is, to enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load): - bind.

G1196.full: From G1199; to tie, that is, shackle: - bind.

G1198.full: From G1199; a captive (as bound): - in bonds, prisoner.

G1199.full: Neuter and masculine respectively from G1210; a band, that is, ligament (of the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively an impediment or disability: - band, bond, chain, string.

G1200.full: From G1199 and G5441; a jailer (as guarding the prisoners): - jailer, keeper of the prison.

G1201.full: From a derivative of G1199 (equivalent to G1196); a place of bondage, that is, a dungeon: - prison.

G1202.full: From the same as G1201; (passively) a captive: - prisoner.

G1203.full: Perhaps from G1210 and ðḯóéò posis (a husband); an absolute ruler ("despot"): - Lord, master.

G1204.full: Of uncertain affinity; here; used also as an imperative hither!; and of time, hitherto: - come (hither), hither [-to].

G1205.full: From G1204 and an imperative of åé̓͂ìé eimi (to go); come hither!: - come, X follow.

G1206.full: From G1208; secondary, that is, (specifically) on the second day: - next day.

G1207.full: From G1208 and G4413; second first, that is, (specifically) a designation of the Sabbath immediately after the Paschal week (being the second after Passover day, and the first of the seven Sabbaths intervening before Pentecost): - second . . . after the first.

G1208.full: As the compound of G1417; (ordinal) second (in time, place or rank; also adverbially): - afterward, again, second (-arily, time).

G1209.full: Middle voice of a primary verb; to receive (in various applications, literally or figuratively): - accept, receive, take. Compare G2983.

G1210.firstSense: bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind
G1210.full: A primary verb; to bind (in various applications, literally or figuratively): - bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind. See also G1163, G1189.

G1211.full: Probably akin to G1161; a particle of emphasis or explicitness; now, then, etc.: - also, and, doubtless, now, therefore.

G1212.full: Of uncertain derivation; clear: - + bewray, certain, evident, manifest.

G1213.full: From G1212; to make plain (by words): - declare, shew, signify.

G1214.full: Probably for G1216; Demas, a Christian: - Demas.

G1215.full: From a compound of G1218 and G58; to be a people gatherer, that is, to address a public assembly: - make an oration.

G1216.full: From Äçìḉôçñ Dēmētēr (Ceres); Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a Christian: - Demetrius.

G1217.full: From G1218 and G2041; a worker for the people, that is, mechanic (spoken of the Creator): - maker.

G1218.full: From G1210; the public (as bound together socially): - people.

G1219.full: From G1218; public; (feminine singular dative as adverb) in public: - common, openly, publickly.

G1220.full: Of Latin origin; a denarius (or ten asses): - pence, penny [-worth].

G1221.full: From G1211 and G4218; a particle of generalization; indeed, at any time: - (what-) soever.

G1222.full: From G1211 and G4225; a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless: - verily.

G1223.firstSense: after, always, among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause)
G1223.full: A primary preposition denoting the channel of an act; through (in very wide applications, local, causal or occasional). In composition it retains the same general import: - after, always, among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause) . . . fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that, thereby, therefore, X though, through (-out), to, wherefore, with (-in). In composition it retains the same general import.

G1224.full: From G1223 and the base of G939; to cross: - come over, pass (through).

G1225.full: From G1223 and G906; (figuratively) to traduce: - accuse.

G1226.full: Middle voice of a compound of G1223 and G950; to confirm thoroughly (by words), that is, asseverate: - affirm constantly.

G1227.full: From G1223 and G991; to look through, that is, recover full vision: - see clearly.

G1228.full: From G1225; a traducer; specifically Satan (compare [H7854]): - false accuser, devil, slanderer.

G1229.full: From G1223 and the base of G32; to herald thoroughly: - declare, preach, signify.

G1230.firstSense: X after, be past, be spent
G1230.full: From G1223 and G1096; to elapse meanwhile: - X after, be past, be spent.

G1231.full: From G1223 and G1097; to know thoroughly, that is, ascertain exactly: - (would) enquire, know the uttermost.

G1232.full: From G1223 and G1107; to tell abroad: - make known.

G1234.full: From G1223 and G1111; to complain throughout a crowd: - murmur.

G1235.full: From G1223 and G1127; to waken thoroughly: - be awake.

G1236.full: From G1223 and G71; to pass time or life: - lead life, living.

G1237.full: From G1223 and G1209; to receive in turn, that is, (figuratively) succeed to: - come after.

G1238.full: From a compound of G1223 and G1210; a "diadem" (as bound about the head): - crown. Compare G4735.

G1239.full: From G1223 and G1325; to give throughout a crowd, that is, deal out; also to deliver over (as to a successor): - (make) distribute (-ion), divide, give.

G1240.full: From G1237; a successor in office: - room.

G1241.full: From G1223 and G2224; to gird tightly: - gird.

G1242.full: From G1303; properly a disposition, that is, (specifically) a contract (especially a devisory will): - covenant, testament.

G1243.full: From G1244; a distinction or (concretely) variety: - difference, diversity.

G1244.full: From G1223 and G138; to separate, that is, distribute: - divide.

G1245.full: From G1223 and G2511; to cleanse perfectly, that is, (specifically) winnow: - throughly purge.

G1246.full: Middle voice from G1223 and a compound of G2596 and G1651; to prove downright, that is, confute: - convince.

G1247.firstSense: (ad-) minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon
G1247.full: From G1249; to be an attendant, that is, wait upon (menially or as a host, friend or [figuratively] teacher); technically to act as a Christian deacon: - (ad-) minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon.

G1248.full: From G1249; attendance (as a servant, etc.); figuratively (eleemosynary) aid, (official) service (especially of the Christian teacher, or technically of the diaconate): - (ad-) minister (-ing, -tration, -try), office, relief, service (-ing).

G1249.full: Probably from äéá́êù diakō (obsolete, to run on errands; compare G1377); an attendant, that is, (generally) a waiter (at table or in other menial duties); specifically a Christian teacher and pastor (technically a deacon or deaconess): - deacon, minister, servant.

G1250.full: From G1364 and G1540; two hundred: - two hundred.

G1251.full: Middle voice from G1223 and G191; to hear throughout, that is, patiently listen (to a prisoner's plea): - hear.

G1252.firstSense: contend, make (to) differ (-ence), discern, doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver
G1252.full: From G1223 and G2919; to separate thoroughly, that is, (literally and reflexively) to withdraw from, or (by implication) oppose; figuratively to discriminate (by implication decide), or (reflexively) hesitate: - contend, make (to) differ (-ence), discern, doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver.

G1253.full: From G1252; judicial estimation: - discern (-ing), disputation.

G1254.full: From G1223 and G2967; to hinder altogether, that is, utterly prohibit: - forbid.

G1255.full: From G1223 and G2980; to talk throughout a company, that is, converse or (generally) publish: - commune, noise abroad.

G1256.full: Middle voice from G1223 and G3004; to say thoroughly, that is, discuss (in argument or exhortation): - dispute, preach (unto), reason (with), speak.

G1257.full: From G1223 and G3007; to leave off in the middle, that is, intermit: - cease.

G1258.full: From G1256; a (mode of) discourse, that is, "dialect": - language, tongue.

G1259.full: From G1223 and G236; to change thoroughly, that is, (mentally) to conciliate: - reconcile.

G1260.firstSense: cast in mind, consider, dispute, muse, reason, think
G1260.full: From G1223 and G3049; to reckon thoroughly, that is, (generally) to deliberate (by reflection or discussion): - cast in mind, consider, dispute, muse, reason, think.

G1261.full: From G1260; discussion, that is, (internal) consideration (by implication purpose), or (external) debate: - dispute, doubtful (-ing), imagination, reasoning, thought.

G1262.full: From G1223 and G3089; to dissolve utterly: - scatter.

G1263.full: From G1223 and G3140; to attest or protest earnestly, or (by implication) hortatively: - charge, testify (unto), witness.

G1264.full: From G1223 and G3164; to fight fiercely (in altercation): - strive.

G1265.full: From G1223 and G3306; to stay constantly (in being or relation): - continue, remain.

G1266.full: From G1223 and G3307; to partition thoroughly (literally in distribution, figuratively in dissension): - cloven, divide, part.

G1267.full: From G1266; disunion (of opinion and conduct): - division.

G1268.full: From G1223 and the base of G3551; to distribute, that is, (of information) to disseminate: - spread.

G1269.full: From G1223 and G3506; to nod (or express by signs) across an intervening space: - beckon.

G1270.full: From a compound of G1223 and G3539; something thought through, that is, a sentiment: - thought.

G1271.full: From G1223 and G3563; deep thought, properly the faculty (mind or its disposition), by implication its exercise: - imagination, mind, understanding.

G1272.full: From G1223 and G455; to open thoroughly, literally (as a first born) or figuratively (to expound): - open.

G1273.full: From G1223 and a derivative of G3571; to sit up the whole night: - continue all night.

G1274.full: From G1223 and á̓íṍù anuō (to effect); to accomplish thoroughly: - finish.

G1275.full: From G1223 and the genitive of G3956; through all time, that is, (adverbially) constantly: - alway (-s), continually.

G1276.full: From G1223 and a derivative of the base of G4008; to cross entirely: - go over, pass (over), sail over.

G1277.full: From G1223 and G4126; to sail through: - sail over.

G1278.full: From G1223 and a derivative of G4192; to toil through, that is, (passively) be worried: - be grieved.

G1279.firstSense: go through, journey in, pass by
G1279.full: From G1223 and G4198; to travel through: - go through, journey in, pass by.

G1280.full: From G1223 and G639; to be thoroughly nonplussed: - (be in) doubt, be (much) perplexed.

G1281.full: From G1223 and G4231; to thoroughly occupy oneself, that is, (transitively and by implication) to earn in business: - gain by trading.

G1282.full: From G1223 and the base of G4249; to saw asunder, that is, (figuratively) to exasperate: - cut (to the heart).

G1283.full: From G1223 and G726; to seize asunder, that is, plunder: - spoil.

G1284.full: From G1223 and G4486; to tear asunder: - break, rend.

G1285.full: From G1223 andóáöḉò saphēs (clear); to clear thoroughly, that is, (figuratively) declare: - tell unto.

G1286.full: From G1223 and G4579; to shake thoroughly, that is, (figuratively) to intimidate: - do violence to.

G1287.full: From G1223 and G4650; to dissipate, that is, (generally) to rout or separate; specifically to winnow; figuratively to squander: - disperse, scatter (abroad), strew, waste.

G1288.full: From G1223 and G4685; to draw apart, that is, sever or dismember: - pluck asunder, pull in pieces.

G1289.full: From G1223 and G4687; to sow throughout, that is, (figuratively) distribute in foreign lands: - scatter abroad.

G1290.full: From G1289; dispersion, that is, (specifically and concretely) the (converted) Israelites resident in Gentile countries: - (which are) scattered (abroad).

G1291.full: Middle voice from G1223 and G4724; to set (oneself) apart (figuratively distinguish), that is, (by implication) to enjoin: - charge, that which was (give) commanded (-ment).

G1293.full: From G1291; a variation: - difference, distinction.

G1294.full: From G1223 and G4762; to distort, that is, (figuratively) misinterpret, or (morally) corrupt: - perverse (-rt), turn away.

G1295.firstSense: bring safe, escape (safe), heal, make perfectly whole, save
G1295.full: From G1223 and G4982; to save thoroughly, that is, (by implication or analogy) to cure, preserve, rescue, etc.: - bring safe, escape (safe), heal, make perfectly whole, save.

G1296.full: From G1299; arrangement, that is, institution: - instrumentality.

G1297.full: From G1299; an arrangement, that is, (authoritative) edict: - commandment.

G1298.full: From G1223 and G5015; to disturb wholly, that is, agitate (with alarm): - trouble.

G1299.firstSense: appoint, command, give, (set in) order, ordain
G1299.full: From G1223 and G5021; to arrange thoroughly, that is, (specifically) institute, prescribe, etc.: - appoint, command, give, (set in) order, ordain.

G1300.full: From G1223 and G5055; to accomplish thoroughly, that is, (subjectively) to persist: - continue.

G1301.full: From G1223 and G5083; to watch thoroughly, that is, (positively and transitively) to observe strictly, or (negatively and reflexively) to avoid wholly: - keep.

G1302.full: From G1223 and G5101; through what cause?, that is, why?: - wherefore, why.

G1303.full: Middle voice from G1223 and G5087; to put apart, that is, (figuratively) dispose (by assignment, compact or bequest): - appoint, make, testator.

G1304.full: From G1223 and the base of G5147; to wear through (time), that is, remain: - abide, be, continue, tarry.

G1305.full: From a compound of G1223 and G5142; nourishment: - food.

G1306.full: From G1223 and G826; to glimmer through, that is, break (as day): - dawn.

G1307.full: From G1223 and G5316; appearing through, that is, "diaphanous": - transparent.

G1308.firstSense: be better, carry, differ from, drive up and down, be (more) excellent, make matter, pub…
G1308.full: From G1223 and G5342; to bear through, that is, (literally) transport; usually to bear apart, that is, (objectively) to toss about (figuratively report); subjectively to "differ", or (by implication) surpass: - be better, carry, differ from, drive up and down, be (more) excellent, make matter, publish, be of more value.

G1309.full: From G1223 and G5343; to flee through, that is, escape: - escape.

G1310.firstSense: blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame
G1310.full: From G1223 and a derivative of G5345; to report thoroughly, that is, divulgate: - blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame.

G1311.full: From G1223 and G5351; to rot thoroughly, that is, (by implication) to ruin (passively decay utterly, figuratively pervert): - corrupt, destroy, perish.

G1313.full: From G1308; varying; also surpassing: - differing, divers, more excellent.

G1314.full: From G1223 and G5442; to guard thoroughly, that is, protect: - keep.

G1315.full: From G1223 and a derivative of G5495; to handle thoroughly, that is, lay violent hands upon: - kill, slay.

G1316.full: From G1223 and the middle voice of G5563; to remove (oneself) wholly, that is, retire: - depart.

G1317.full: From G1318; instructive ("didactic"): - apt to teach.

G1318.full: From G1321; (subjectively) instructed or (objectively) communicated by teaching: - taught, which . . . teacheth.

G1319.full: From G1320; instruction (the function or the information): - doctrine, learning, teaching.

G1320.full: From G1321; an instructor (generally or specifically): - doctor, master, teacher.

G1321.full: A prolonged (causative) form of a primary verb äá́ù daō (to learn); to teach (in the same broad application): - teach.

G1322.full: From G1321; instruction (the act or the matter): - doctrine, hath been taught.

G1323.full: From G1364 and G1406; a double drachma (didrachm): - tribute.

G1324.full: Prolonged from G1364; double, that is, twin; Didymus, a Christian: - Didymus.

G1325.firstSense: adventure, bestow, bring forth, commit, deliver (up), give, grant, hinder, make, minist…
G1325.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which is used as an alternate in most of the tenses); to give (used in a very wide application, properly or by implication, literally or figuratively; greatly modified by the connection): - adventure, bestow, bring forth, commit, deliver (up), give, grant, hinder, make, minister, number, offer, have power, put, receive, set, shew, smite (+ with the hand), strike (+ with the palm of the hand), suffer, take, utter, yield.

G1326.full: From G1223 and G1453; to wake fully, that is, arouse (literally or figuratively): - arise, awake, raise, stir up.

G1327.full: From G1223 and G1841; an outlet through, that is, probably an open square (from which roads diverge): - highway.

G1329.full: From G1223 and G2059; to explain thoroughly; by implication to translate: - expound, interpret (-ation).

G1330.firstSense: come, depart, go (about, abroad, every where, over, through, throughout), pass (by, ove…
G1330.full: From G1223 and G2064; to traverse (literally): - come, depart, go (about, abroad, every where, over, through, throughout), pass (by, over, through, throughout), pierce through, travel, walk through.

G1331.full: From G1223 and G2065; to question throughout, that is, ascertain by interrogation: - make enquiry for.

G1332.full: From G1364 and G2094; of two years (in age): - two years old.

G1333.full: From G1332; a space of two years (biennium): - two years.

G1334.full: From G1223 and G2233; to relate fully: - declare, shew, tell.

G1336.full: Neuter of a compound of G1223 and a derivative of an alternate of G5342; carried through, that is, (adverb with G1519 and G3588 prefixed) perpetually: - +continually, for ever.

G1337.full: From G1364 and G2281; having two seas, that is, a sound with a double outlet: - where two seas met.

G1338.full: From G1223 and the base of G2425; to reach through, that is, penetrate: - pierce.

G1339.firstSense: go further, be parted, after the space of
G1339.full: From G1223 and G2476; to stand apart, that is, (reflexively) to remove, intervene: - go further, be parted, after the space of.

G1340.full: From G1223 and a derivative of G2478; to stout it through, that is, asseverate: - confidently (constantly) affirm.

G1341.full: From G1342 and G2920; a just sentence: - righteous judgment.

G1342.full: From G1349; equitable (in character or act); by implication innocent, holy (absolutely or relatively): - just, meet, right (-eous).

G1343.full: From G1342; equity (of character or act); specifically (Christian) justification: - righteousness.

G1344.full: From G1342; to render (that is, show or regard as) just or innocent: - free, justify (-ier), be righteous.

G1345.full: From G1344; an equitable deed; by implication a statute or decision: - judgment, justification, ordinance, righteousness.

G1346.full: Adverb from G1342; equitably: - justify, (to) righteously (-ness).

G1347.full: From G1344; acquittal (for Christ's sake): - justification.

G1348.full: From a derivative of G1349; a judger: - judge.

G1349.full: Probably from G1166; right (as self evident), that is, justice (the principle, a decision, or its execution): - judgment, punish, vengeance.

G1350.full: Probably from a primary verb äé́êù dikō (to cast); a seine (for fishing): - net.

G1351.full: From G1364 and G3056; equivocal, that is, telling a different story: - double-tongued.

G1352.full: From G1223 and G3739; through which thing, that is, consequently: - for which cause, therefore, wherefore.

G1353.full: From G1223 and G3593; to travel through: - go throughout, pass through.

G1354.full: From Äéḯíõóïò Dionusos (Bacchus); reveller; Dionysius, an Athenian: - Dionysius.

G1355.full: From G1352 and G4007; on which very account: - wherefore.

G1356.full: From the alternate of G2203 and the alternate of G4098; sky fallen (that is, an aerolite): - which fell down from Jupiter.

G1357.full: From a compound of G1223 and a derivative of G3717, meaning to straighten thoroughly; rectification, that is, (specifically) the Messianic restoration: - reformation.

G1358.full: From G1223 and G3736; to penetrate burglariously: - break through (up).

G1359.full: From the alternate of G2203 and a form of the base of G2877; sons of Jupiter, that is, the twins Dioscuri: - Castor and Pollux.

G1360.full: From G1223 and G3754; on the very account that, or inasmuch as: - because (that), for, therefore.

G1361.full: From the alternate of G2203 and G5142; Jove nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity: - Diotrephes.

G1362.full: From G1364 and (probably) the base of G4119; two fold: - double, two-fold more.

G1363.full: From G1362; to render two fold: - double.

G1364.full: dis dece Adverb from G1417; twice: - again, twice.

G1365.full: From G1364 properly to duplicate, that is, (mentally) to waver (in opinion): - doubt.

G1366.full: From G1364 and G4750; double edged: - with two edges, two-edged.

G1367.full: From G1364 and G5507; two thousand: - two thousand.

G1368.full: From G1223 and õ̔ëé́æù hulizō (to filter); to strain out. ("strain at" is probably by misprint.): - strain at [prob. by misprint].

G1369.full: From a derivative of G1364; to make apart, that is, sunder (figuratively alienate): - set at variance.

G1370.full: From a derivative of G1364 and G4714; disunion, that is, (figuratively) dissension: - division, sedition.

G1371.full: From a compound of a derivative of G1364 and a derivative of ôǻìíù temnō (to cut); to bisect, that is, (by extension) to flog severely: - cut asunder (in sunder).

G1372.full: From a variation of G1373; to thirst for (literally or figuratively): - (be, be a-) thirst (-y).

G1374.full: From G1364 and G5590; two spirited, that is, vacillating (in opinion or purpose): - double minded.

G1377.firstSense: ensue, follow (after), given to, (suffer) persecute (-ion), press toward
G1377.full: A prolonged (and causative) form of a primary verb äé́ù diō (to flee; compare the base of G1169 and G1249); to pursue (literally or figuratively); by implication to persecute: - ensue, follow (after), given to, (suffer) persecute (-ion), press toward.

G1378.full: From the base of G1380; a law (civil, ceremonial or ecclesiastical): - decree, ordinance.

G1379.full: From G1378; to prescribe by statute, that is, (reflexively) to submit to ceremonial rule: - be subject to ordinances.

G1380.firstSense: be accounted, (of own) please (-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow
G1380.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb äḯêù dokō (used only as an alternate in certain tenses; compare the base of G1166); of the same meaning; to think; by implication to seem (truthfully or uncertainly): - be accounted, (of own) please (-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow.

G1381.firstSense: allow, discern, examine, X like, (ap-) prove, try
G1381.full: From G1384; to test (literally or figuratively); by implication to approve: - allow, discern, examine, X like, (ap-) prove, try.

G1382.full: From the same as G1384; test (abstractly or concretely); by implication trustiness: - experience (-riment), proof, trial.

G1383.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G1382; a testing; by implication trustworthiness: - trial, trying.

G1384.full: From G1380; properly acceptable (current after assayal), that is, approved: - approved, tried.

G1385.full: From G1209 (through the idea of holding up); a stick of timber: - beam.

G1387.full: From G1386; to be guileful: - use deceit.

G1388.full: From äǻëëù dellō (an obsolete primary probably meaning to decoy; compare G1185); a trick (bait), that is, (figuratively) wile: - craft, deceit, guile, subtilty.

G1389.full: From G1388; to ensnare, that is, (figuratively) adulterate: - handle deceitfully.

G1390.full: From the base of G1325; a present: - gift.

G1391.full: From the base of G1380; glory (as very apparent), in a wide application (literally or figuratively, objectively or subjectively): - dignity, glory (-ious), honour, praise, worship.

G1392.firstSense: (make) glorify (-ious), full of (have) glory, honour, magnify
G1392.full: From G1391; to render (or esteem) glorious (in a wide application): - (make) glorify (-ious), full of (have) glory, honour, magnify.

G1393.full: gazelle; Dorcas, a Christian woman: - Dorcas.

G1394.full: From the base of G1325; a giving; by implication (concretely) a gift: - gift, giving.

G1395.full: From the base of G1325; a giver: - giver.

G1396.full: From a presumed compound of G1401 and G71; to be a slave driver, that is, to enslave (figuratively subdue): - bring into subjection.

G1397.full: From G1398; slavery (ceremonially or figuratively): - bondage.

G1398.full: From G1401; to be a slave to (literally or figuratively, involuntarily or voluntarily): - be in bondage, (do) serve (-ice).

G1399.full: Feminine of G1401; a female slave (involuntarily or voluntarily): - handmaid (-en).

G1401.full: From G1210; a slave (literally or figuratively, involuntarily or voluntarily; frequently therefore in a qualified sense of subjection or subserviency): - bond (-man), servant.

G1402.firstSense: bring into (be under) bondage, X given, become (make) servant
G1402.full: From G1401; to enslave (literally or figuratively): - bring into (be under) bondage, X given, become (make) servant.

G1403.full: From G1209; a reception, that is, convivial entertainment: - feast.

G1404.full: Probably from an alternate form of äǻñêïìáé derkomai (to look); a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate): - dragon.

G1405.full: Perhaps akin to the base of G1404 (through the idea of capturing); to grasp, that is, (figuratively) entrap: - take.

G1406.full: From G1405; a drachma or (silver) coin (as handled): - piece (of silver).

G1407.full: From äñǻðù drepō (to pluck); a gathering hook (especially for harvesting): - sickle.

G1408.full: From the alternate of G5143; a race, that is, (figuratively) career: - course.

G1409.full: A feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name); Drusilla, a member of the Herodian family: - Drusilla.

G1410.firstSense: be able, can (do, + -not), could, may, might, be possible, be of power
G1410.full: Of uncertain affinity; to be able or possible: - be able, can (do, + -not), could, may, might, be possible, be of power.

G1411.firstSense: ability, abundance, meaning, might (-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle (-s), power…
G1411.full: From G1410; force (literally or figuratively); specifically miraculous power (usually by implication a miracle itself): - ability, abundance, meaning, might (-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle (-s), power, strength, violence, mighty (wonderful) work.

G1413.full: From G1410; a ruler or officer: - of great authority, mighty, potentate.

G1414.full: From G1415; to be efficient (figuratively): - be mighty.

G1415.firstSense: able, could, (that is) mighty (man), possible, power, strong
G1415.full: From G1410; powerful or capable (literally or figuratively); neuter possible: - able, could, (that is) mighty (man), possible, power, strong.

G1416.full: Prolonged forms of an obsolete primary word äṍù duō (to sink); to go "down": - set.

G1417.full: A primary numeral; "two": - both, twain, two.

G1418.full: dus doos A primary inseparable particle of uncertain derivation; used only in composition as a prefix; hard, that is, with difficulty: - + hard, + grievous, etc.

G1419.full: From G1418 and a derivative of G941; oppressive: - grievous to be borne.

G1420.full: From G1418 and a compound of G1787 (meaning a bowel); a "dysentery": - bloody flux.

G1421.full: From G1418 and a presumed derivative of G2059; difficult of explanation: - hard to be uttered.

G1422.full: From G1418 and êḯëïí kolon (food); properly fastidious about eating (peevish), that is, (generally) impracticable: - hard.

G1424.full: From G1416; the sun set, that is, (by implication) the western region: - west.

G1425.full: From G1418 and a derivation of G3539; difficult of perception: - hard to be understood.

G1426.full: From a compound of G1418 and G5345; defamation: - evil report.

G1427.full: From G1417 and G1176; two and ten, that is, a dozen: - twelve.

G1429.full: From G1427 and G5443; the commonwealth of Israel: - twelve tribes.

G1430.full: From äǻìï demō (to build); properly an edifice, that is, (specifically) a roof: - housetop.

G1432.firstSense: without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain
G1432.full: Accusative case of G1431 as adverb; gratuitously (literally or figuratively): - without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain.

G1433.full: Middle voice from G1435; to bestow gratuitously: - give.

G1435.full: A present; specifically a sacrifice: - gift, offering.

G1436.full: Apparent imperative of G1439; properly let it be, that is, (as interjection) aha !: - let alone.

G1437.firstSense: before, but, except, (and) if, (if) so, (what-, whither-) soever, though, when (-soever…
G1437.full: From G1487 and G302; a conditional particle; in case that, provided, etc.; often used in connection with other particles to denote indefiniteness or uncertainty: - before, but, except, (and) if, (if) so, (what-, whither-) soever, though, when (-soever), whether (or), to whom, [who-] so (-ever). See G3361.

G1438.firstSense: alone, her (own, -self), (he) himself, his (own), itself, one (to) another, our (thine)…
