G2728.full: From G2596 and a derivative of G2447; to rust down, that is, corrode: - canker.

G2729.full: From G2596 and G2480; to overpower: - prevail (against).

G2730.full: From G2596 and G3611; to house permanently, that is, reside (literally or figuratively): - dwell (-er), inhabitant (-ter).

G2731.full: From G2730; residence (properly the act; but by implication concretely the mansion): - dwelling.

G2732.full: From a derivative of G2730; a dwelling place: - habitation.

G2733.full: residence (properly the condition; but by implication the abode itself): - habitation.

G2734.full: Middle voice from a compound of G2596 and a derivative of G3700 (compare G2072); to mirror oneself, that is, to see reflected (figuratively): - behold as in a glass.

G2735.full: From a compound of G2596 and a derivative of G3717 (compare G1357); something made fully upright, that is, (figuratively) rectification (specifically good public administration): - very worthy deed.

G2736.full: [Compare G2737]; adverb from G2596; downwards: - beneath, bottom, down, under.

G2737.full: Compound from G2736; inferior (locally, of Hades): - lower.

G2738.full: From G2545; properly a burn (concretely), but used (abstractly) of a glow: - heat.

G2740.full: From G2545; burning (the act): - be burned.

G2741.full: From G2740; to set on fire: - with fervent heat.

G2743.full: From a derivative of G2545; to brand ("cauterize"), that is, (by implication) to render unsensitive (figuratively): - sear with a hot iron.

G2744.full: From some (obsolete) base akin to that of áõ̓÷ǻù aucheō (to boast) and G2172; to vaunt (in a good or a bad sense): - (make) boast, glory, joy, rejoice.

G2745.full: From G2744; a boast (properly the objective; by implication the act) in a good or bad sense: - boasting, (whereof) to glory (of), glorying, rejoice (-ing).

G2746.firstSense: boasting, whereof I may glory, glorifying, rejoicing
G2746.full: From G2744; boasting (properly the act; by implication the objective), in a good or a bad sense: - boasting, whereof I may glory, glorifying, rejoicing.

G2747.full: Probably from êǻã÷ñïò kegchros (millet); Cenchreae, a port of Corinth: - Cenchrea.

G2748.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6939]; Cedron (that is, Kidron), a brook near Jerusalem: - Cedron.

G2749.firstSense: be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie
G2749.full: Middle voice of a primary verb; to lie outstretched (literally or figuratively): - be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie. Compare G5087.

G2750.full: Of uncertain affinity; a swathe, that is, winding sheet: - graveclothes.

G2751.full: A primary verb; to shear: - shear (-er).

G2752.full: From G2753; a cry of incitement: - shout.

G2753.full: From a primary word êǻëëù kellō (to urge on); "hail"; to incite by word, that is, order: - bid, (at, give) command (-ment).

G2754.full: From G2755; empty glorying, that is, self conceit: - vain-glory.

G2755.full: From G2756 and G1391; vainly glorifying, that is, self conceited: - desirous of vain-glory.

G2756.full: Apparently a primary word; empty (literally or figuratively): - empty, (in) vain.

G2757.full: From a presumed compound of G2756 and G5456; empty sounding, that is, fruitless discussion: - vain.

G2758.firstSense: make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain
G2758.full: From G2756; to make empty, that is, (figuratively) to abase, neutralize, falsify: - make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain.

G2759.full: From êåíôǻù kenteō (to prick); a point ("centre"), that is, a sting (figuratively poison) or goad (figuratively divine impulse): - prick, sting.

G2760.full: Of Latin origin; a centurion, that is, captain of one hundred soldiers: - centurion.

G2761.full: Adverb from G2756; vainly, that is, to no purpose: - in vain.

G2762.full: Feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G2768; something horn like, that is, (specifically) the apex of a Hebrew letter (figuratively the least particle): - tittle.

G2764.full: From G2766; made of clay, that is, earthen: - of a potter.

G2765.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G2766; an earthenware vessel, that is, jar: - pitcher.

G2766.full: Probably from the base of G2767 (through the idea of mixing clay and water); earthenware, that is, a tile (by analogy a thin roof or awning): - tiling.

G2767.full: A prolonged form of a more primary word êåñá́ù keraō (which is used in certain tenses); to mingle, that is, (by implication) to pour out (for drinking): - fill, pour out. Compare G3396.

G2768.full: From a primary word êá́ñ kar (the hair of the head); a horn (literally or figuratively): - horn.

G2769.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G2768; something horned, that is, (specifically) the pod of the carob tree: - husk.

G2770.full: From G2771; to gain (literally or figuratively): - (get) gain, win.

G2771.full: Of uncertain affinity; gain (pecuniary or generally): - gain, lucre.

G2772.full: From G2751; a clipping (bit), that is, (specifically) a coin: - money.

G2773.full: From a derivative of G2772; a handler of coins, that is, money broker: - changer of money.

G2774.full: Neuter of a derivative of G2776; a principal thing, that is, main point; specifically an amount (of money): - sum.

G2775.full: From the same as G2774; (specifically) to strike on the head: - wound in the head.

G2776.full: Probably from the primary wordêá́ðôù kaptō (in the sense of seizing); the head (as the part most readily taken hold of), literally or figuratively: - head.

G2777.full: From G2776; properly a knob, that is, (by implication) a roll (by extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was rolled): - volume.

G2778.full: Of Latin origin; properly an enrolment ("census"), that is, (by implication) a tax: - tribute.

G2779.full: Of uncertain affinity; a garden: - garden.

G2780.full: From G2779 and ïõ̓͂ñïò ouros (a warden); a garden keeper, that is, gardener: - gardener.

G2781.full: Diminutive from êçḯò kēos (wax); a cell for honey, that is, (collectively) the comb: - [honey-] comb.

G2782.full: From G2784; a proclamation (especially of the gospel; by implication the gospel itself): - preaching.

G2783.full: From G2784; a herald, that is, of divine truth (especially of the gospel): - preacher.

G2784.full: Of uncertain affinity; to herald (as a public crier), especially divine truth (the gospel): - preach (-er), proclaim, publish.

G2785.full: Probably from the base of G5490; a huge fish (as gaping for prey): - whale.

G2786.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H3710]); the Rock; Cephas (that is, Kepha), surname of Peter: - Cephas.

G2787.full: Of uncertain derivative; a box, that is, the sacred ark and that of Noah: - ark.

G2788.full: Of uncertain affinity; a lyre: - harp.

G2789.full: From G2788; to play on a lyre: - harp.

G2790.full: From G2788 and a derivative of the same as G5603; a lyre singer (player), that is, harpist: - harper.

G2791.full: Probably of foreign origin; Cilicia, a region of Asia Minor: - Cilicia.

G2793.firstSense: be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy
G2793.full: From G2794; to undergo peril: - be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy.

G2795.full: From êé́ù kiō (poetic for [åé̓͂ìé eimi to go]); to stir (transitively), literally or figuratively: - (re-) move (-r), way.

G2797.full: Kis kis Of Hebrew origin [H7027]); Cis (that is, Kish), an Israelite: - Cis.

G2798.full: From G2806; a twig or bough (as if broken off): - branch.

G2799.full: Of uncertain affinity; to sob, that is, wail aloud (whereas G1145 is rather to cry silently): - bewail. weep.

G2801.full: From G2806; a piece (bit): - broken, fragment.

G2802.full: Of uncertain derivation; Claude, an island near Crete: - Clauda.

G2803.full: Feminine of G2804; Claudia, a Christian woman: - Claudia.

G2804.full: Of Latin origin; Claudius, the name of two Romans: - Claudius.

G2805.full: From G2799; lamentation: - wailing, weeping, X wept.

G2806.full: A primary verb; to break (specifically of bread): - break.

G2807.full: kleis klice From G2808; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively: - key.

G2808.full: A primary verb; to close (literally or figuratively): - shut (up).

G2809.full: From G2813; stealing (properly the thing stolen, but used of the act): - theft.

G2810.full: Probably contracted from Êëåḯðáôñïò Kleopatros (compounded from G2811 and G3962); Cleopas, a Christian: - Cleopas.

G2811.full: From a shorter form of G2564; renown (as if being called): - glory.

G2812.full: From G2813; a stealer (literally or figuratively): - thief. Compare G3027.

G2813.full: A primary verb; to filch: - steal.

G2814.full: From G2806; a limb or shoot (as if broken off): - branch.

G2815.full: Of Latin origin; merciful; Clemes (that is, Clemens), a Christian: - Clement.

G2816.full: From G2818; to be an heir to (literally or figuratively): - be heir, (obtain by) inherit (-ance).

G2817.full: From G2818; heirship, that is, (concretely) a patrimony or (generally) a possession: - inheritance.

G2818.full: From G2819 and the base of G3551 (in its original sense of partitioning, that is, [reflexively] getting by apportionment); a sharer by lot, that is, an inheritor (literally or figuratively); by implication a possessor: - heir.

G2819.full: Probably from G2806 (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for the purpose); a die (for drawing chances); by implication a portion (as if so secured); by extension an acquisition (especially a patrimony, figuratively): - heritage, inheritance, lot, part.

G2820.full: From G2819; to allot, that is, (figuratively) to assign (a privilege): - obtain an inheritance.

G2821.full: From a shorter form of G2564; an invitation (figuratively): - calling.

G2822.full: From the same as G2821; invited, that is, appointed, or (specifically) a saint: - called.

G2823.full: Of uncertain derivation; an earthen pot used for baking in: - oven.

G2824.full: From G2827; a slope, that is, (specifically) a "clime" or tract of country: - part, region.

G2825.full: From G2827; a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating): - bed, table.

G2826.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G2825; a pallet or little couch: - bed.

G2827.firstSense: bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear away
G2827.full: A primary verb; to slant or slope, that is, incline or recline (literally or figuratively): - bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear away.

G2828.full: From a derivative of G2827; properly reclination, that is, (concretely and specifically) a party at a meal: - company.

G2830.full: From êëṍæù kluzō (to billow or dash over); a surge of the sea (literally or figuratively): - raging, wave.

G2831.full: Middle voice from G2830; to surge, that is, (figuratively) to fluctuate: - toss to and fro.

G2832.full: Of Chaldee origin (corresponding to G256); Clopas, an Israelite: - Clopas.

G2833.full: From a primary word êíá́ù knaō (to scrape); to scratch, that is, (by implication) to tickle: - X itching.

G2834.full: Probably of foreign origin; Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor: - Cnidus.

G2835.full: Of Latin origin; a quadrans, that is, fourth part of an as: - farthing.

G2836.full: From êïé͂ëïò koilos ("hollow"); a cavity, that is, (specifically) the abdomen; by implication the matrix; figuratively the heart: - belly, womb.

G2837.firstSense: (be a-, fall a-, fall on) sleep, be dead

G2838.full: From G2837; sleeping, that is, (by implication) repose: - taking of rest.

G2839.full: Probably from G4862; common, that is, (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane: - common, defiled, unclean, unholy.

G2843.full: From G2844; communicative, that is, (pecuniarily) liberal: - willing to communicate.

G2845.full: From G2749; a couch; by extension cohabitation; by implication the male sperm: - bed, chambering, X conceive.

G2846.full: From G2845; a bed room: - + chamberlain.

G2847.full: From G2848 (from the kernel shape of the insect); crimson colored: - scarlet (colour, coloured).

G2850.full: From a derivative of êḯëáî kolax (a fawner); flattery: - X flattering.

G2851.full: From G2849; penal infliction: - punishment, torment.

G2852.full: From a derivative of the base of G2849; to rap with the fist: - buffet.

G2853.full: From êḯëëá kolla ("glue"); to glue, that is, (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively): - cleave, join (self), keep company.

G2855.full: From a presumed derivative of êḯëëõâïò kollubos (a small coin; probably akin to G2854); a coin dealer: - (money-) changer.

G2856.full: From a derivative of the base of G2849; to dock, that is, (figuratively) abridge: - shorten.

G2857.full: Apparently feminine plural of êïëïóóḯò kolossos ("colossal"); Colossae, a place in Asia Minor: - Colosse.

G2858.full: From G2857; a Colossaean, that is, inhabitant of Colossae: - Colossian.

G2859.full: Apparently a primary word; the bosom; by analogy a bay: - bosom, creek.

G2860.full: From êïëõìâïò kolumbos (a diver); to plunge into water: - swim.

G2861.full: From G2860; a diving place, that is, pond for bathing (or swimming): - pool.

G2862.full: Of Latin origin; a Roman "colony" for veterans: - colony.

G2863.full: From G2864; to wear tresses of hair: - have long hair.

G2867.full: Fromêïíé́á konia (dust; by analogy lime); to whitewash: - whiten.

G2868.full: From the base of G2867 and ï̓́ñíõìé ornumi (to "rouse"); pulverulence (as blown about): - dust.

G2869.full: From G2873; to tire, that is, (figuratively) to relax: - cease.

G2870.full: From G2875; mourning (properly by beating the breast): - lamentation.

G2871.full: From G2875; cutting, that is, carnage: - slaughter.

G2872.full: From a derivative of G2873; to feel fatigue; by implication to work hard: - (bestow) labour, toil, be wearied.

G2873.full: From G2875; a cut, that is, (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength), literally or figuratively; by implication pains: - labour, + trouble, weariness.

G2874.full: From êḯðñïò kopros (ordure; perhaps akin to G2875); manure: - dung (-hill).

G2876.full: Perhaps from G2880; a crow (from its voracity): - raven.

G2877.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of êḯñç korē (a maiden); a (little) girl: - damsel, maid.

G2879.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7141]; Core (that is, Korach), an Israelite: - Core.

G2880.full: A primary verb; to cram, that is, glut or sate: - eat enough, full.

G2881.full: From G2882; a Corinthian, that is, inhabitant of Corinth: - Corinthian.

G2882.full: Of uncertain derivation; Corinthus, a city of Greece: - Corinth.

G2883.full: Of Latin original; Cornelius, a Roman: - Cornelius.

G2884.full: Of Hebrew origin [H3734]; a cor, that is, a specific measure: - measure.

G2885.full: From G2889; to put in proper order, that is, decorate (literally or figuratively); specifically to snuff (a wick): - adorn, garnish, trim.

G2886.full: From G2889 (in its secondary sense); terrene ("cosmic"), literally (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt): - worldly.

G2887.full: From G2889 (in its primary sense); orderly, that is, decorous: - of good behaviour, modest.

G2888.full: From G2889 and G2902; a world ruler, an epithet of Satan: - ruler.

G2889.full: Probably from the base of G2865; orderly arrangement, that is, decoration; by implication the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively [morally]): - adorning, world.

G2890.full: Of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian: - Quartus.

G2891.full: Of Chaldee origin [H6966]; cumi (that is, rise!): - cumi.

G2892.full: Of Latin origin; "custody", that is, a Roman sentry: - watch.

G2893.full: From êïõ͂öïò kouphos (light in weight); to unload: - lighten.

G2894.full: Of uncertain derivation; a (small) basket: - basket.

G2895.full: Probably of foreign origin; a mattress: - bed.

G2896.full: A primary verb; properly to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, that is, (generally) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat): - cry (out).

G2897.full: Probably from the same as G726; properly a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, that is, (by implication) a debauch (by analogy a glut): - surfeiting.

G2898.full: Diminutive of a derivative of the base of G2768; a skull ("cranium"): - Calvary, skull.

G2899.full: Of uncertain derivation; a margin, that is, (specifically) a fringe or tassel: - border, hem.

G2901.full: From G2900; to empower, that is, (passively) increase in vigor: - be strenghtened, be (wax) strong.

G2902.firstSense: hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by)
G2902.full: From G2904; to use strength, that is, seize or retain (literally or figuratively): - hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by).

G2903.full: Superlative of a derivative of G2904; strongest, that is, (in dignity) very honorable: - most excellent (noble).

G2904.full: Perhaps a primary word; vigor ["great"], (literally or figuratively): - dominion, might [-ily], power, strength.

G2905.full: From G2906; to clamor: - cry out.

G2906.full: From G2896; an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief): - clamour, cry (-ing).

G2907.full: Perhaps a primary word; (butcher's) meat: - flesh.

G2908.full: Neuter of an alternate form of G2909; (as noun) better, that is, greater advantage: - better.

G2909.full: Comparative of a derivative of G2904; stronger, that is, (figuratively) better, that is, nobler: - best, better.

G2910.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang: - hang.

G2911.full: From G2910; overhanging, that is, a precipice: - steep place.

G2912.full: Krēs krace From G2914; a Cretan, that is, inhabitant of Crete: - Crete, Cretian.

G2913.full: Of Latin origin; growing; Cresces (that is, Crescens), a Christian: - Crescens.

G2914.full: Of uncertain derivation; Crete, an island in the Mediterranean: - Crete.

G2916.full: From G2915; consisting of barley: - barley.

G2917.firstSense: avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment
G2917.full: From G2919; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ["crime"]): - avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment.

G2918.full: Perhaps a primary word; a lily: - lily.

G2919.full: Properly to distinguish, that is, decide (mentally or judicially); by implication to try, condemn, punish: - avenge, conclude, condemn, damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law, ordain, call in question, sentence to, think.

G2920.full: (Subjectively or objectively, for or against); by extension a tribunal; by implication justice (specifically divine law): - accusation, condemnation, damnation, judgment.

G2921.full: Of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian: - Crispus.

G2922.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G2923; a rule of judging ("criterion"), that is, (by implication) a tribunal: - to judge, judgment (seat).

G2923.full: From G2919; a judge (generally or specifically): - judge.

G2924.full: From G2923; decisive ("critical"), that is, discriminative: - discerner.

G2925.full: Apparently a primary verb; to rap: - knock.

G2926.full: Feminine of G2927; a hidden place, that is, cellar ("crypt"): - secret.

G2927.full: From G2928; concealed, that is, private: - hid (-den), inward [-ly], secret.

G2928.full: A primary verb; to conceal (properly by covering): - hide (self), keep secret, secret [-ly].

G2929.full: From G2930; to make (that is, intransitively resemble) ice ("crystallize"): - be clear as crystal.

G2930.full: From a derivative of êñṍïò kruos (frost); ice, that is, (by analogy) rock "crystal": - crystal.

G2931.full: Adverb from G2928; privately: - in secret.

G2932.full: A primary verb; to get, that is, acquire (by any means; own): - obtain, possess, provide, purchase.

G2933.full: From G2932; an acquirement, that is, estate: - possession.

G2934.full: From G2932; property, that is, (specifically) a domestic animal: - beast.

G2936.full: Probably akin to G2932 (through the idea of the proprietorship of the manufacturer); to fabricate, that is, found (form originally): - create, Creator, make.

G2937.full: From G2936; original formation (properly the act; by implication the thing, literally or figuratively): - building, creation, creature, ordinance.

G2938.full: From G2936; an original formation (concretely), that is, product (created thing): - creature.

G2939.full: From G2936; a founder, that is, God (as author of all things): - Creator.

G2940.full: From êṍâïò kubos (a "cube", that is, die for playing); gambling, that is, (figuratively) artifice or fraud: - sleight.

G2941.full: From êõâåñíá́ù kubernaō (of Latin origin, to steer); pilotage, that is, (figuratively) directorship (in the church): - government.

G2942.full: From the same as G2941; helmsman, that is, (by implication) captain: - (ship) master.

G2943.full: Adverb from the same as G2945; from the circle, that is, all around: - (round) about.

G2944.full: From the same as G2945; to encircle, that is, surround: - compass (about), come (stand) round about.

G2945.full: As if dative case of êṍêëïò kuklos (a ring, "cycle"; akin to G2947); that is, in a circle (by implication of G1722), that is, (adverbially) all around: - round about.

G2946.full: From G2947; a wallow (the effect of rolling), that is, filth: - wallowing.

G2947.full: From the base of G2949 (through the idea of circularity; compare G2945 and G1507); to roll about: - wallow.

G2948.full: From the same as G2947; rocking about, that is, crippled (maimed, in feet or hands): - maimed.

G2949.full: From êṍù kuō (to swell [with young], that is, bend, curve); a billow (as bursting or toppling): - wave.

G2950.full: From a derivative of the base of G2949; a "cymbal" (as hollow): - cymbal.

G2951.full: Of foreign origin (compare [H3646]); dill or fennel ("cummin"): - cummin.

G2952.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G2965; a puppy: - dog.

G2953.full: From G2954; a Cyprian (Cypriot), that is, inhabitant of Cyprus: - of Cyprus.

G2954.full: Of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean: - Cyprus.

G2955.full: Probably from the base of G2949; to bend forward: - stoop (down).

G2956.full: From G2957; a Cyrenaean, that is, inhabitant of Cyrene: - of Cyrene, Cyrenian.

G2957.full: Of uncertain derivation; Cyrene, a region of Africa: - Cyrene.

G2958.full: Of Latin origin; Cyrenius (that is, Quirinus), a Roman: - Cyrenius.

G2959.full: Feminine of G2962; Cyria, a Christian woman: - lady.

G2960.full: From G2962; belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus): - Lord's.

G2961.firstSense: have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over
G2961.full: From G2962; to rule: - have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over.

G2962.full: From êõ͂ñïò kuros (supremacy); supreme in authority, that is, (as noun) controller; by implication Mr. (as a respectful title): - God, Lord, master, Sir.

G2963.full: From G2962; mastery, that is, (concretely and collectively) rulers: - dominion, government.

G2964.full: From the same as G2962; to make authoritative, that is, ratify: - confirm.

G2965.full: A primary word; a dog ("hound"), (literally or figuratively): - dog.

G2966.full: From the base of G2849; a limb of the body (as if lopped): - carcase.

G2967.firstSense: forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand
G2967.full: From the base of G2849; to estop, that is, prevent (by word or act): - forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand.

G2968.full: From G2749; a hamlet (as if laid down): - town, village.

G2969.full: From G2968 and G4172; an unwalled city: - town.

G2970.full: From G2749; a carousal (as if a letting loose): - revelling, rioting.

G2971.full: Apparently from a derivative of the base of G2759 and a derivative of G3700; a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis): - gnat.

G2972.full: Kōs koce Of uncertain origin; Cos, an island in the Mediterranean: - Cos.

G2973.full: Of Hebrew origin (compare [H7081]); Cosam (that is, Kosam), an Israelite: - Cosam.

G2974.full: From G2875; blunted, that is, (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb): - deaf, dumb, speechless.

G2975.firstSense: his lot be, cast lots, obtain
G2975.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; to lot, that is, determine (by implication receive) especially by lot: - his lot be, cast lots, obtain.

G2976.full: Probably of Hebrew origin [H499]; Lazarus (that is, Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary): - Lazarus.

G2977.full: Adverb from G2990; privately: - privily, secretly.

G2978.full: Of uncertain derivation; a whirlwind (squall): - storm, tempest.

G2979.full: From adverb ëá́î lax (heelwise); to recalcitrate: - kick.

G2980.firstSense: preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter
G2980.full: A prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, that is, utter words: - preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare G3004.

G2982.full: Of Hebrew origin ([H4100] with preposition prefixed); lama (that is, why): - lama.

G2983.firstSense: accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + fo…
G2983.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively [probably objective or active, to get hold of; whereas G1209 is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while G138 is more violent, to seize or remove]): - accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up).

G2984.full: Of Hebrew origin [H3929]; Lamech (that is, Lemek), a patriarch: - Lamech.

G2985.full: From G2989; a "lamp" or flambeau: - lamp, light, torch.

G2986.firstSense: bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white
G2986.full: From the same as G2985; radiant; by analogy limpid; figuratively magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance): - bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white.

G2988.full: Adverb from G2986; brilliantly, that is, (figuratively) luxuriously: - sumptuously.

G2989.full: A primary verb; to beam, that is, radiate brilliancy (literally or figuratively): - give light, shine.

G2990.firstSense: be hid, be ignorant of, unawares
G2990.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially unwittingly: - be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.

G2991.full: From a compound of ëá͂ò las (a stone) and the base of G3584 (in its original sense of scraping); rock quarried: - hewn in stone.

G2992.full: Apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from G1218, which denotes one's own populace): - people.

G2993.full: From a compound of G2992 and G1349; Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor: - Laodicea.

G2994.full: From G2993; a Laodicean, that is, inhabitant of Laodicia: - Laodicean.

G2995.full: Of uncertain derivative; the throat ("larynx"): - throat.

G2996.full: Of uncertain origin; Lasaea, a place in Crete: - Lasea.

G2997.full: A strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as an alternate in certain tenses; to crack open (from a fall): - burst asunder.

G2998.full: From the same as the first part of G2991 and the base of G5114; to quarry: - hew.

G2999.full: From G3000; ministration of God, that is, worship: - (divine) service.

G3000.full: From ëá́ôñéò latris (a hired menial); to minister (to God), that is, render religious homage: - serve, do the service, worship (-per).

G3001.full: From ëá÷áé́íù lachainō (to dig); a vegetable: - herb.

G3002.full: Of uncertain origin; Lebbaeus, a Christian: - Lebbus.

G3003.full: Of Latin origin; a "legion", that is, Roman regiment (figuratively): - legion.

G3004.firstSense: ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say (-ing, on), shew, speak…
G3004.full: A primary verb; properly to "lay" forth, that is, (figuratively) relate (in words [usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas G2036 and G5346 generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while G4483 is properly to break silence merely, and G2980 means an extended or random harangue]); by implication to mean: - ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say (-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter.

G3006.full: Apparently a primary word; smooth, that is, "level": - smooth.

G3007.full: A primary verb; to leave, that is, (intransitive or passive) to fail or be absent: - be destitute (wanting), lack.

G3008.full: From G3011; to be a public servant, that is, (by analogy) to perform religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve): - minister.

G3009.full: From G3008; public function (as priest ["liturgy"] or almsgiver): - ministration (-try), service.

G3010.full: From the same as G3008; functional publicly ("liturgic"), that is, beneficent: - ministering.

G3011.full: From a derivative of G2992 and G2041; a public servant, that is, a functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (generally) a worshipper (of God) or benefactor (of man): - minister (-ed).

G3012.full: Of Latin origin; a "linen" cloth, that is, apron: - towel.

G3013.full: From ëǻðù lepō (to peel); a flake: - scale.

G3014.full: From the same as G3013; scaliness, that is, "leprosy": - leprosy.

G3015.full: From the same as G3014; scaly, that is, leprous (a leper): - leper.

G3016.full: Neuter of a derivative of the same as G3013; something scaled (light), that is, a small coin: - mite.

G3017.full: Of Hebrew origin [H3878]; Levi, the name of three Israelites: - Levi. Compare G3018.

G3018.full: A form of G3017; Lewis (that is, Levi), a Christian: - Levi.

G3019.full: From G3017; a Levite, that is, descendant of Levi: - Levite.

G3020.full: From G3019; Levitic, that is, relating to the Levites: - Levitical.

G3021.full: From G3022; to whiten: - make white, whiten.

G3025.full: Apparently a primary word; a trough, that is, wine vat: - winepress.

G3026.full: Apparently a primary word; twaddle, that is, an incredible story: - idle tale.

G3027.full: From ëçé̈́́æïìáé lēizomai (to "plunder"); a brigand: - robber, thief.

G3029.full: Of uncertain affinity; much (adverb): - exceeding, great (-ly), sore, very (+ chiefest).

G3030.full: Of foreign origin [H3828]; the incense tree, that is, (by implication) incense itself: - frankincense.

G3031.full: From G3030; frankincense, that is, (by extension) a censer for burning it: - censer.

G3032.full: Of Latin origin; a Roman freedman: - Libertine.

G3033.full: Probably from G3047; Libye, a region of Africa: - Libya.

G3035.full: From G3037; stony, that is, made of stone: - of stone.

G3036.full: From a compound of G3037 and G906; to throw stones, that is, lapidate: - stone, cast stones.

G3037.full: Apparently a primary word; a stone (literally or figuratively): - (mill-, stumbling-) stone.

G3038.full: From G3037 and a derivative of G4766; stone strewed, that is, a tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed: - Pavement.

G3039.full: From ëéêìḯò likmos, the equivalent. of ëé́êíïí liknon (a winnowing fan or basket); to winnow, that is, (by analogy) to triturate: - grind to powder.

G3040.full: Apparently a primary word; a harbor: - haven. Compare G2568.

G3041.full: Probably from G3040 (through the idea of the nearness of shore); a pond (large or small): - lake.

G3042.full: Probably from G3007 (through the idea of destitution); a scarcity of food: - dearth, famine, hunger.

G3043.full: Probably a primary word; flax, that is, (by implication) "linen": - linen.

G3044.full: Perhaps from G3043; Linus, a Christian: - Linus.

G3045.full: From ëéðïò lipos (grease); fat, that is, (figuratively) sumptuous: - dainty.

G3046.full: Of Latin origin (libra); a pound in weight: - pound.

G3047.full: lips leeps Probably from ëåé́âù leibō (to pour a "libation"); the south (southwest) wind (as bringing rain), that is, (by extension) the south quarter: - southwest.

G3048.full: From G3056 (in the commercial sense); a contribution: - collection, gathering.

G3049.firstSense: conclude, (ac-) count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, sup…
G3049.full: Middle voice from G3056; to take an inventory, that is, estimate (literally or figuratively): - conclude, (ac-) count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on).

G3050.full: From G3056; rational ("logical"): - reasonable, of the word.

G3051.full: Neuter of G3052; an utterance (of God): - oracle.

G3052.full: From G3056; fluent, that is, an orator: - eloquent.

G3053.full: From G3049; computation, that is, (figuratively) reasoning (conscience, conceit): - imagination, thought.

G3054.full: From a compound of G3056 and G3164; to be disputatious (on trifles): - strive about words.

G3055.full: From the same as G3054; disputation about trifles ("logomachy"): - strife of words.

G3056.firstSense: account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matt…
G3056.full: From G3004; something said (including the thought); by implication a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension a computation; specifically (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (that is, Christ): - account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove, say (-ing), shew, X speaker, speech, talk, thing, + none of these things move me, tidings, treatise, utterance, word, work.

G3057.full: Perhaps a primary word; a "lance": - spear.

G3058.full: From G3060; to reproach, that is, vilify: - revile.

G3059.full: From G3060; slander or vituperation: - railing, reproach [-fully].

G3060.full: From ëïéäḯò loidos (mischief); abusive, that is, a black guard: - railer, reviler.

G3061.full: Of uncertain affinity; a plague (literally the disease, or figuratively a pest): - pestilence (-t).

G3062.firstSense: other, which remain, remnant, residue, rest
G3062.full: Masculine plural of a derivative of G3007; remaining ones: - other, which remain, remnant, residue, rest.

G3063.firstSense: besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then
G3063.full: Neuter singular of the same as G3062; something remaining (adverb): - besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then.

G3064.full: Genitive singular of the same as G3062; remaining time: - from henceforth.

G3065.full: Contracted from the Latin Lucanus; Lucas, a Christian: - Lucas, Luke.

G3066.full: Of Latin origin; illuminative; Lucius, a Christian: - Lucius.

G3067.full: From G3068; a bath, that is, (figuratively) baptism: - washing.

G3068.full: A primary verb; to bathe (the whole person; whereas G3538 means to wet a part only, and G4150 to wash, cleanse garments exclusively): - wash.

G3069.full: Of Hebrew origin [H3850]; Lydda (that is, Lod), a place in Palestine: - Lydda.

G3070.full: Properly feminine of Ëṍäéïò Ludios (of foreign origin; a Lydian, in Asia Minor); Lydia, a Christian woman: - Lydia.

G3071.full: Perhaps remotely from G3074; Lycaonia, a region of Asia Minor: - Lycaonia.

G3072.full: Adverb from a derivative of G3071; Lycaonistically, that is, in the language of the Lycaonians: - in the speech of Lycaonia.

G3073.full: Probably remotely from G3074; Lycia, a province of Asia Minor: - Lycia.

G3074.full: Perhaps akin to the base of G3022 (from the whitish hair); a wolf: - wolf.

G3075.full: Middle voice from a probable derivative of G3089 (meaning filth); properly to soil, that is, (figuratively) insult (maltreat): - make havock of.

G3076.firstSense: cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow (-ful), be (make) sorry
G3076.full: From G3077; to distress; reflexively or passively to be sad: - cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow (-ful), be (make) sorry.

G3077.full: Apparently a primary word; sadness: - grief, grievous, + grudgingly, heaviness, sorrow.

G3078.full: From G3080 and á̓íé́á ania (trouble); grief dispelling; Lysanias, a governor of Abilene: - Lysanias.

G3079.full: Of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman: - Lysias.

G3080.full: From G3089; a loosening, that is, (specifically) divorce: - to be loosed.

G3081.full: Third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a compound of G3080 and G5056; impersonally it answers the purpose, that is, is advantageous: - it is better.

G3082.full: Of uncertain origin; Lystra, a place in Asia Minor: - Lystra.

G3083.full: From G3089; something to loosen with, that is, a redemption price (figuratively atonement): - ransom.

G3084.full: From G3083; to ransom (literally or figuratively): - redeem.

G3085.full: From G3084; a ransoming (figuratively): - + redeemed, redemption.

G3087.full: From G3088; a lamp stand (literally or figuratively): - candlestick.

G3088.full: From the base of G3022; a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally or figuratively): - candle, light.

G3089.firstSense: break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-) loose, melt, put off
G3089.full: A primary verb; to "loosen" (literally or figuratively): - break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-) loose, melt, put off. Compare G4486.

G3090.full: Of uncertain origin; Lois, a Christian woman: - Lois.

G3091.full: Lōt lote Of Hebrew origin [H3876]; Lot, a patriarch: - Lot.

G3092.full: Probably of Hebrew origin; Maath, an Israelite: - Maath.

G3093.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H4026]); the tower; Magadala (that is, Migdala), a place in Palestine: - Magdala.

G3094.full: Feminine of a derivative of G3093; a female Magdalene, that is, inhabitant of Magdala: - Magdalene.

G3096.full: From G3097; to practice magic: - use sorcery.

G3097.full: Of foreign origin [H7248]; a Magian, that is, Oriental scientist; by implication a magician: - sorcerer, wise man.

G3098.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4031]; Magog, a foreign nation, that is, (figuratively) an Antichristian party: - Magog.

G3099.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4080]; Madian (that is, Midian), a region of Arabia: - Madian.

G3100.full: From G3101; intransitively to become a pupil; transitively to disciple, that is, enrol as scholar: - be disciple, instruct, teach.

G3101.full: From G3129; a learner, that is, pupil: - disciple.

G3102.full: Feminine from G3101; a female pupil: - disciple.

G3103.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4968]; Mathusala (that is, Methushelach), an antediluvian: - Mathusala.

G3104.full: Probably of Hebrew origin; Mainan, an Israelite: - Mainan.

G3105.full: Middle voice from a primary word ìá́ù maō (to long for; through the idea of insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac": - be beside self (mad).

G3106.full: From G3107; to beatify, that is, pronounce (or esteem) fortunate: - call blessed, count happy.

G3107.full: A prolonged form of the poetical ìá́êáñ makar (meaning the same); supremely blest; by extension fortunate, well off: - blessed, happy (X -ier).

G3108.full: From G3106; beatification, that is, attribution of good fortune: - blessedness.

G3109.full: From G3110; Macedonia, a region of Greece: - Macedonia.

G3110.full: Of uncertain derivation; a Macedon (Macedonian), that is, inhabitant of Macedonia: - of Macedonia, Macedonian.

G3111.full: Of Latin origin [macellum]; a butcher's stall, meat market or provision shop: - shambles.

G3112.full: Feminine accusative singular of G3117 (G3598 being implied); at a distance (literally or figuratively): - (a-) far (off), good (great) way off.

G3113.full: Adverb from G3117; from a distance or afar: - afar off, from far.

G3114.firstSense: bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure
G3114.full: From the same as G3116; to be long spirited, that is, (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient: - bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure.

G3115.full: From the same as G3116; longanimity, that is, (objectively) forbearance or (subjectively) fortitude: - longsuffering, patience.

G3116.full: Adverb of a compound of G3117 and G2372; with long (enduring) temper, that is, leniently: - patiently.

G3117.full: From G3372; long (in place [distant] or time [neuter plural]): - far, long.

G3118.full: From G3117 and G5550; long timed, that is, long lived: - live long.

G3119.full: From G3120; softness, that is, enervation (debility): - disease.

G3120.full: Of uncertain affinity; soft, that is, fine (clothing); figuratively a catamite: - effeminate, soft.

G3121.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4111]; Maleleel (that is, Mahalalel), an antediluvian: - Maleleel.

G3122.full: Neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb ìá́ëá mala (very); (adverb) most (in the greatest degree) or particularly: - chiefly, most of all, (e-) specially.

G3123.firstSense: + better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather
G3123.full: Neuter of the comparative of the same as G3122; (adverb) more (in a greater degree) or rather: - + better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather.

G3124.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4429]; Malchus, an Israelite: - Malchus.

G3125.full: Of natural origin ["mammy"]; a grandmother: - grandmother.

G3126.full: Of Chaldee origin (confidence, that is, figuratively wealth, personified); mammonas, that is, avarice (deified): - mammon.

G3127.full: Of uncertain origin; Manaen, a Christian: - Manaen.

G3128.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4519]; Manasses (that is, Menashsheh), an Israelite: - Manasses.

G3129.full: Prolonged from a primary verb, another form of which, ìáèǻù matheō, is used as an alternate in certain tenses; to learn (in any way): - learn, understand.

G3130.full: From G3105; craziness: - [+ make] X mad.

G3131.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4478]; manna (that is, man), an edible gum: - manna.

G3132.full: From a derivative of G3105 (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave through inspiration); to divine, that is, utter spells (under pretence of foretelling): - by soothsaying.

G3133.full: Of uncertain affinity; to extinguish (as fire), that is, (figuratively and passively) to pass away: - fade away.

G3134.full: Of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come); maranatha, that is, an exclamation of the approaching divine judgment: - Maran-atha.

G3135.full: From ìá́ñãáñïò margaros (a pearl oyster); a pearl: - pearl.

G3136.full: Probably of Chaldee origin (meaning mistress); Martha, a Christian woman: - Martha.

G3137.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4813]; Maria or Mariam (that is, Mirjam), the name of six Christian females: - Mary.

G3138.full: Of Latin origin; Marcus, a Christian: - Marcus, Mark.

G3139.full: From ìáñìáé́ñù marmairō (to glisten); marble (as sparkling white): - marble.

G3140.firstSense: charge, give [evidence], bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well r…
G3140.full: From G3144; to be a witness, that is, testify (literally or figuratively): - charge, give [evidence], bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have) testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness.

G3141.full: From G3144; evidence given (judicially or generally): - record, report, testimony, witness.

G3142.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G3144; something evidential, that is, (generally) evidence given or (specifically) the Decalogue (in the sacred Tabernacle): - to be testified, testimony, witness.

G3143.full: Middle voice from G3144; to be adduced as a witness, that is, (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation): - take to record, testify.

G3144.full: Of uncertain affinity; a witness (literally [judicially] or figuratively [generally]); by analogy a "martyr": - martyr, record, witness.

G3145.full: From a primary word ìá́óóù massō (to handle or squeeze); to chew: - gnaw.

G3146.full: From G3148; to flog (literally or figuratively): - scourge.

G3148.full: Probably from the base of G3145 (through the idea of contact); a whip (literally the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively a disease): - plague, scourging.

G3149.full: From the base of G3145; a (properly female) breast (as if kneaded up): - pap.

G3150.full: From G3151; random talk, that is, babble: - vain jangling.

G3151.full: From G3152 and G3004; an idle (that is, senseless or mischievous) talker, that is, a wrangler: - vain talker.

G3152.full: From the base of G3155; empty, that is, (literally) profitless, or (specifically) an idol: - vain, vanity.

G3153.full: From G3152; inutility; figuratively transientness; morally depravity: - vanity.

G3154.full: From G3152; to render (passively become) foolish, that is, (morally) wicked or (specifically) idolatrous: - become vain.

G3155.full: Accusative case of a derivative of the base of G3145 (through the idea of tentative manipulation, that is, unsuccessful search, or else of punishment); folly, that is, (adverbially) to no purpose: - in vain.

G3156.full: A shorter form of G3161; Matthaeus (that is, Matthitjah), an Israelite and Christian: - Matthew.

G3157.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4977]; Matthan (that is, Mattan), an Israelite: - Matthan.

G3158.full: Probably a shortened form of G3161; Matthat (that is, Mattithjah), the name of two Israelites: - Mathat.

G3159.full: Apparently a shortened form of G3161; Matthias (that is, Mattithjah), an Israelite: - Matthias.

G3160.full: Probably a shortened form of G3161 (compare [H4992]); Mattatha (that is, Mattithjah), an Israelite: - Mattatha.

G3161.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4993]; Mattathias (that is, Mattithjah), an Israelite and Christian: - Mattathias.

G3162.full: Probably feminine of a presumed derivative of G3163; a knife, that is, dirk; figuratively war, judicial punishment: - sword.

G3163.full: From G3164; a battle, that is, (figuratively) controversy: - fighting, strive, striving.

G3164.full: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to war, that is, (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute: - fight, strive.

G3165.full: me meh A shorter (and probably original) form of G1691; me: - I, me, my.

G3166.full: From a compound of G3173 and áõ̓÷ǻù aucheō (to boast; akin to G837 and G2744); to talk big, that is, be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic): - boast great things.

G3167.full: From G3173; magnificent, that is, (neuter plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection: - great things, wonderful works.

G3168.full: From G3167; superbness, that is, glory or splendor: - magnificence, majesty, mighty power.

G3169.full: From G3173 and G4241; befitting greatness or magnificence (majestic): - excellent.

G3170.full: From G3173; to make (or declare) great, that is, increase or (figuratively) extol: - enlarge, magnify, shew great.

G3172.full: From G3173; greatness, that is, (figuratively) divinity (often God himself): - majesty.

G3173.firstSense: (+ fear) exceedingly, great (-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), st…
G3173.full: Including the prolonged forms, femine ìåãá́ëç megalē, plural ìǻãá́ëïé megaloi, etc.; compare also G3176, G3187], big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application): - (+ fear) exceedingly, great (-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong, X to years.

G3175.full: Plural from G3176; grandees: - great men, lords.

G3176.full: Superlative of G3173; greatest or very great: - exceeding great.

G3177.full: From G3326 and G2059; to explain over, that is, translate: - (by) interpret (-ation).

G3178.full: Apparently a primary word; an intoxicant, that is, (by implication) intoxication: - drunkenness.

G3179.firstSense: put out, remove, translate, turn away
G3179.full: From G3326 and G2476; (second form used at 1Co_13:2) to transfer, that is, carry away, depose or (figuratively) exchange, seduce: - put out, remove, translate, turn away.

G3180.full: From a compound of G3326 and G3593 [compare "method"]; traveling over, that is, travesty, (trickery): - wile, lie in wait.

G3181.full: From G3326 and G3725; bounded alongside, that is, contiguous (neuter plural as noun, frontier): - border.

G3182.full: A prolonged (transitive) form of G3184; to intoxicate: - be drunk (-en).

G3183.full: From G3184; tipsy, that is, (as noun) a sot: - drunkard.

G3184.full: From another form of G3178; to drink to intoxication, that is, get drunk: - drink well, make (be) drunk (-en).

G3185.full: Neuter of G3187; (adverbially) in a greater degree: - the more.

G3186.full: Continued comparative of G3187; still larger (figuratively): - greater.

G3187.full: Irregular comparative of G3173; larger (literally or figuratively, specifically in age): - elder, greater (-est), more.

G3188.full: Neuter of G3189 as noun; ink: - ink.

G3189.full: Apparently a primary word; black: - black.

G3190.full: Of uncertain origin; Meleas, an Israelite: - Meleas.

G3191.full: From a presumed derivative of G3199; to take care of, that is, (by implication) revolve in the mind: - imagine, (pre-) meditate.

G3192.full: Apparently a primary word; honey: - honey.

G3193.full: From G3192; relating to honey, that is, bee (comb): - honeycomb.

G3194.full: Of uncertain origin; Melita, an island in the Mediterranean: - Melita.

G3195.firstSense: about, after that, be (almost), (that which is, things, + which was for) to come, inten…
G3195.full: A strengthened form of G3199 (through the idea of expectation); to intend, that is, be about to be, do, or suffer something (of persons or things, especially events; in the sense of purpose, duty, necessity, probability, possibility, or hesitation): - about, after that, be (almost), (that which is, things, + which was for) to come, intend, was to (be), mean, mind, be at the point, (be) ready, + return, shall (begin), (which, that) should (after, afterwards, hereafter) tarry, which was for, will, would, be yet.

G3196.full: Of uncertain affinity; a limb or part of the body: - member.

G3197.full: Of Hebrew origin ([H4428] with pronominal suffix, my king); Melchi (that is, Malki), the name of two Israelites: - Melchi.

G3198.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4442]; Melchisedek (that is, Malkitsedek), a patriarch: - Melchisedec.

G3199.full: A primary verb; to be of interest to, that is, to concern (only third person singular present indicative used impersonally it matters): - (take) care.

G3200.full: Of Latin origin ("membrane"); a (written) sheep skin: - parchment.

G3201.full: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to blame: - find fault.

G3202.full: From a presumed derivative of G3201 and ìïé͂ñá moira (fate; akin to the base of G3313); blaming fate, that is, querulous (discontented): - complainer.

G3303.firstSense: even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily
G3303.full: men men A primary particle; properly indicative of affirmation or concession (in fact); usually followed by a contrasted clause with G1161 (this one, the former, etc.: - even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily. Often compounded with other particles in an intensive or asseverative sense.

G3304.full: From G3303 and G3767 and G1065; so then at least: - nay but, yea doubtless (rather, verily).

G3305.full: From G3303 and G5104; indeed though, that is, however: - also, but, howbeit, nevertheless, yet.

G3306.firstSense: abide, continue, dwell, endure, be present, remain, stand, tarry (for), X thine own
G3306.full: A primary verb; to stay (in a given place, state, relation or expectancy): - abide, continue, dwell, endure, be present, remain, stand, tarry (for), X thine own.

G3307.firstSense: deal, be difference between, distribute, divide, give part
G3307.full: From G3313; to part, that is, (literally) to apportion, bestow, share, or (figuratively) to disunite, differ: - deal, be difference between, distribute, divide, give part.

G3308.full: From G3307 (through the idea of distraction); solicitude: - care.

G3309.full: From G3308; to be anxious about: - (be, have) care (-ful), take thought.

G3310.full: Feminine of G3313; a portion, that is, province, share or (abstractly) participation: - part (X -akers).

G3311.full: From G3307; a separation or distribution: - dividing asunder, gift.

G3313.firstSense: behalf, coast, course, craft, particular (+ -ly), part (+ -ly), piece, portion, respect…
G3313.full: From an obsolete but more primary form of ìåé́ñïìáé meiromai (to get as a section or allotment); a division or share (literally or figuratively, in a wide application): - behalf, coast, course, craft, particular (+ -ly), part (+ -ly), piece, portion, respect, side, some sort (-what).

G3314.full: From G3319 and G2250; midday; by implication the south: - noon, south.

G3315.full: From G3316; to interpose (as arbiter), that is, (by implication) to ratify (as surety): - confirm.

G3316.full: From G3319; a go between, that is, (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor): - mediator.

G3317.full: Neuter of a compound of G3319 and G3571; midnight (especially as a watch): - midnight.

G3318.full: From G3319 and G4215; Mesopotamia (as lying between the Euphrates and the Tigris; compare [H763]), a region of Asia: - Mesopotamia.

G3319.firstSense: among, X before them, between, + forth, mid [-day, -night], midst, way
G3319.full: From G3326; middle (as adjective or [neuter] noun): - among, X before them, between, + forth, mid [-day, -night], midst, way.

G3320.full: From G3319 and G5109; a partition (figuratively): - middle wall.

G3321.full: From a presumed compound of G3319 and G3772; mid-sky: - midst of heaven.

G3322.full: From G3319; to form the middle, that is, (in point of time), to be half way over: - be about the midst.

G3323.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4899]; the Messias (that is, Mashiach), or Christ: - Messias.

G3324.full: Of uncertain derivative; replete (literally or figuratively): - full.

G3325.full: From G3324; to replenish, that is, (by implication) to intoxicate: - fill.

G3326.firstSense: after (-ward),X that he again, against, among, X and, + follow, hence, hereafter, in, o…
G3326.full: A primary preposition (often used adverbially); properly denoting accompaniment; "amid" (local or causal); modified variously according to the case (genitive case association, or accusative case succession) with which it is joined; occupying an intermediate position between G575 or G1537 and G1519 or G4314; less intimate than G1722, and less close than G4862): - after (-ward),X that he again, against, among, X and, + follow, hence, hereafter, in, of, (up-) on, + our, X and setting, since, (un-) to, + together, when, with (+ -out). Often used in composition, in substantially the same relations of participation or proximity, and transfer or sequence.

G3327.full: From G3326 and the base of G939; to change place: - depart, go, pass, remove.

G3328.full: From G3326 and G906; to throw over, that is, (middle voice, figuratively) to turn about in opinion: - change mind.

G3329.full: From G3326 and G71; to lead over, that is, transfer (direct): - turn about.

G3330.full: From G3326 and G1325; to give over, that is, share: - give, impart.

G3331.full: From G3346; transposition, that is, transferral (to heaven), disestablishment (of a law): - change, removing, translation.

G3332.full: From G3326 and G142; to betake oneself, that is, remove (locally): - depart.

G3333.full: From G3326 and G2564; to call elsewhere, that is, summon: - call (for, hither).

G3334.full: From G3326 and G2795; to stir to a place elsewhere, that is, remove (figuratively): - move away.

G3335.firstSense: eat, have, be partaker, receive, take
G3335.full: From G3326 and G2983; to participate; generally to accept (and use): - eat, have, be partaker, receive, take.

G3337.full: From G3326 and G236; to exchange: - change.

G3338.full: From G3326 and the middle of G3199; to care afterwards, that is, regret: - repent (self).

G3339.full: From G3326 and G3445; to transform (literally or figuratively "metamorphose"): - change, transfigure, transform.

G3340.full: From G3326 and G3539; to think differently or afterwards, that is, reconsider (morally to feel compunction): - repent.

G3341.full: From G3340; (subjectively) compunction (for guilt, including reformation); by implication reversal (of [another's] decision): - repentance.

G3342.full: From G3326 and a form of G4862; betwixt (of place or person); (of time) as adjective intervening, or (by implication) adjoining: - between, mean while, next.

G3343.full: From G3326 and G3992; to send from elsewhere, that is, (middle voice) to summon or invite: - call (send) for.

G3344.full: From G3326 and G4762; to turn across, that is, transmute or (figuratively) corrupt: - pervert, turn.

G3345.full: From G3326 and a derivative of G4976; to transfigure or disguise; figuratively to apply (by accommodation): - transfer, transform (self).

G3346.firstSense: carry over, change, remove, translate, turn
G3346.full: From G3326 and G5087; to transfer, that is, (literally) transport, (by implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively) pervert: - carry over, change, remove, translate, turn.

G3347.full: From G3326 and G1899; thereafter: - afterward.

G3348.firstSense: be partaker, pertain, take part, use
G3348.full: From G3326 and G2192; to share or participate; by implication belong to, eat (or drink): - be partaker, pertain, take part, use.

G3349.full: From a compound of G3326 and a collateral form of G142 or perhaps rather of G109 (compare "meteor"); to raise in mid-air, that is, (figuratively) suspend (passively fluctuate or be anxious): - be of doubtful mind.

G3350.full: From a derivative of a compound of G3326 and G3624; a change of abode, that is, (specifically) expatriation: - X brought, carried (-ying) away (in-) to.

G3351.full: From the same as G3350; to transfer as a settler or captive, that is, colonize or exile: - carry away, remove into.

G3352.full: From G3348; participation, that is, intercourse: - fellowship.

G3353.full: From G3348; participant, that is, (as noun) a sharer; by implication an associate: - fellow, partaker, partner.

G3354.full: From G3358; to measure (that is, ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by implication to admeasure (that is, allot by rule); figuratively to estimate: - measure, mete.

G3355.full: From G3354; a measurer, that is, (specifically) a certain standard measure of capacity for liquids: - firkin.

G3356.full: From a compound of the base of G3357 and G3806; to be moderate in passion, that is, gentle (to treat indulgently): - have compassion.

G3357.full: Adverb from a derivative of G3358; moderately, that is, slightly: - a little.

G3358.full: An apparently primary word; a measure ("metre"), literally or figuratively; by implication a limited portion (degree): - measure.

G3359.full: From G3326 and ù̓́ø ōps (the face); the forehead (as opposite the countenance): - forehead.

G3360.full: From G3372; as far as, that is, up to a certain point (as preposition of extent [denoting the terminus, whereas G891 refers especially to the space of time or place intervening] or conjugation): - till, (un-) to, until.

G3361.firstSense: any, but, (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in)…
G3361.full: A primary particle of qualified negation (whereas G3756 expresses an absolute denial); (adverbially) not, (conjugationally) lest; also (as interrogitive implying a negative answer [whereas G3756 expects an affirmative one]); whether: - any, but, (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, [can-] not, nothing, that not, un [-taken], without. Often used in compounds in substantially the same relations. See also G3362, G3363, G3364, G3372, G3373, G3375, G3378.

G3362.firstSense: X before, but, except, if no, (if, + whosoever) not
G3362.full: That is, G1437 and G3361; if not, that is, unless: - X before, but, except, if no, (if, + whosoever) not.

G3363.full: That is, G2443 and G3361; in order (or so) that not: - albeit not, lest, that no (-t, [-thing]).

G3364.firstSense: any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), no…
G3364.full: ou mē oo may That is, G3756 and G3361; a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all: - any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise). Compare G3378.

G3365.full: Adverb from a compound of G3361 and á̓ìḯò amos (somebody); by no means: - not so.

G3366.firstSense: neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as)
G3366.full: From G3361 and G1161; but not, not even; in a continued negation, nor: - neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as).

G3367.firstSense: any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay
G3367.full: The masculine, feminine irregular (second form) and neuter (third form) from G3361 and G1520; not even one (man, woman, thing): - any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay.

G3368.full: From G3366 and G4218; not even ever: - never.

G3369.full: From G3366 and G4452; not even yet: - not yet.

G3370.full: Of foreign origin (compare [H4074]); a Median, or inhabitant of Media: - Mede.

G3371.firstSense: any longer, (not) henceforth, hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any…
G3371.full: From G3361 and G2089; no further: - any longer, (not) henceforth, hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any more.

G3372.full: Probably akin to G3173; length (literally or figuratively): - length.

G3373.full: From G3372; to lengthen, that is, (middle voice) to enlarge: - grow up.

G3374.full: From ìç͂ëïí mēlon (a sheep); a sheep skin: - sheepskin.

G3375.full: mēn mane A stronger form of G3303; a particle of affirmation (only with G2229); assuredly: - + surely.

G3376.full: mēn mane A primary word; a month: - month.

G3377.full: Probably from the same base as G3145 and G3415 (that is, ìá́ù maō [to strive]); to disclose (through the idea of mental effort and thus calling to mind), that is, report, declare, intimate: - shew, tell.

G3378.full: mē ouk may ook That is, G3361 and G3756; as interrogitive and negative is it not that? : - neither (followed by no), + never, not. Compare G3364.

G3379.firstSense: if peradventure, lest (at any time, haply), not at all, whether or not
G3379.full: From G3361 and G4218; not ever; also if (or lest) ever (or perhaps): - if peradventure, lest (at any time, haply), not at all, whether or not.

G3380.full: From G3361 and G4452; not yet: - not yet.

G3381.firstSense: lest (by any means, by some means, haply, perhaps)
G3381.full: From G3361 and G4458; lest somehow: - lest (by any means, by some means, haply, perhaps).

G3382.full: Perhaps a primary word; a thigh: - thigh.

G3383.full: From G3361 and G5037; not too, that is, (in continued negation) neither or nor; also, not even: - neither, (n-) or, so much as.

G3384.full: Apparently a primary word; a "mother" (literally or figuratively, immediate or remote): - mother.

G3385.firstSense: not [the particle usually not expressed, except by the form of the question]
G3385.full: From G3361 and the neuter of G5100; whether at all: - not [the particle usually not expressed, except by the form of the question].

G3386.full: From G3385 and G1065; not at all then, that is, not to say (the rather still): - how much more.

G3387.firstSense: any [sometimes unexpressed except by the simple interrogative form of the sentence]
G3387.full: From G3361 and G5100; whether any: - any [sometimes unexpressed except by the simple interrogative form of the sentence].

G3389.full: From G3384 and the base of G257; a mother thresher, that is, matricide: - murderer of mothers.

G3390.full: From G3384 and G4172; a mother city, that is, "metropolis": - chiefest city.

G3391.firstSense: a (certain), + agree, first, one, X other
G3391.full: Irregular feminine of G1520; one or first: - a (certain), + agree, first, one, X other.

G3392.full: Perhaps a primary verb; to sully or taint, that is, contaminate (ceremonially or morally): - defile.

G3393.full: From G3392 ("miasma"); (morally) foulness (properly the effect): - pollution.

G3394.full: From G3392; (morally) contamination (properly the act): - uncleanness.

G3396.full: A primary verb; to mix: - mingle.

G3397.full: Masculine or neuter singular of G3398 (as noun); a small space of time or degree: - a (little) (while).

G3398.full: Apparently a primary word, including the comparative (second form); small (in size, quantity, number or (figuratively) dignity): - least, less, little, small.

G3399.full: Of uncertain origin; Miletus, a city of Asia Minor: - Miletus.

G3400.full: Of Latin origin; a thousand paces, that is, a "mile": - mile.

G3401.full: Middle voice from ìé͂ìïò mimos (a "mimic"); to imitate: - follow.

G3403.full: A prolonged form of G3415 (from which some of the tenses are borrowed); to remind, that is, (middle voice) to recall to mind: - be mindful, remember.

G3404.full: From a primary word ìé͂óïò misos (hatred); to detest (especially to persecute); by extension to love less: - hate (-ful).

G3405.full: From G3406; requital (good or bad): - recompence of reward.

G3406.full: From G3409 and G591; a remunerator: - rewarder.

G3407.full: From G3408; a wage earner: - hired servant.

G3408.full: Apparently a primary word; pay for service (literally or figuratively), good or bad: - hire, reward, wages.

G3409.full: From G3408; to let out for wages, that is, (middle voice) to hire: - hire.

G3410.full: From G3409; a rented building: - hired house.

G3411.full: From G3409; a wage worker (good or bad): - hired servant, hireling.

G3412.full: For ìõôéëḉíç mutilēnē (abounding in shell fish); Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town in the island Lesbos: - Mitylene.

G3413.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4317]; Michael, an archangel: - Michael.

G3414.full: mna mnah Of Latin origin; a mna (that is, mina), a certain weight: - pound.

G3415.firstSense: be mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance
G3415.full: Middle voice of a derivative of G3306 or perhaps of the base of G3145 (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp); to bear in mind, that is, recollect; by implication to reward or punish: - be mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance. Compare G3403.

G3416.full: Of uncertain origin; Mnason, a Christian: - Mnason.

G3417.full: From G3415 or G3403; recollection; by implication recital: - mention, remembrance.

G3418.full: From G3415; a memorial, that is, sepulchral monument (burial place): - grave, sepulchre, tomb.

G3419.full: From G3420; a remembrance, that is, cenotaph (place of interment): - grave, sepulchre, tomb.

G3421.full: From a derivative of G3420; to exercise memory, that is, recollect; by implication to punish; also to rehearse: - make mention, be mindful, remember.

G3422.full: From G3421; a reminder (memorandum), that is, record: - memorial.

G3423.full: From a derivative of G3415; to give a souvenir (engagement present), that is, betroth: - espouse.

G3424.firstSense: having an impediment in his speech
G3424.full: From G3425 and G2980; hardly talking, that is, dumb (tongue tied): - having an impediment in his speech.

G3425.full: Adverb from a primary word ìḯãïò mogos (toil); with difficulty: - hardly.

G3426.full: Of Latin origin; a modius, that is, certain measure for things dry (the quantity or the utensil): - bushel.

G3427.full: moi moy The simpler form of G1698; to me: - I, me, mine, my.

G3428.full: A prolonged form of the feminine of G3432; an adulteress (literally or figuratively): - adulteress (-ous, -y).

G3429.full: From G3432; (middle voice) to commit adultery: - commit adultery.

G3431.full: From G3432; to commit adultery: - commit adultery.

G3432.full: Perhaps a primary word; a (male) paramour; figuratively apostate: - adulterer.

G3433.full: Probably by a variation for G3425; with difficulty: - hardly, scarce (-ly), + with much work.

G3434.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4432]; Moloch (that is, Molek), an idol: - Moloch.

G3435.full: Probably from G3189; to soil (figuratively): - defile.

G3436.full: From G3435; a stain, that is, (figuratively) immorality: - filthiness.

G3437.full: From G3201; blame, that is, (by implication) a fault: - quarrel.

G3438.full: From G3306; a staying, that is, residence (the act or the place): - abode, mansion.

G3439.full: monogenēs mon-og-en-ace From G3441 and G1096; only born, that is, sole: - only (begotten, child).

G3440.full: Neuter of G3441 as adverb; merely: - alone, but, only.

G3441.full: Probably from G3306; remaining, that is, sole or single; by implication mere: - alone, only, by themselves.

G3442.full: From G3441 and G3788; one eyed: - with one eye.

G3443.full: From G3441; to isolate, that is, bereave: - be desolate.

G3444.full: Perhaps from the base of G3313 (through the idea of adjustment of parts); shape; figuratively nature: - form.

G3445.full: From the same as G3444; to fashion (figuratively): - form.

G3446.full: From G3445; formation, that is, (by implication) appearance (semblance or [concretely] formula): - form.

G3447.full: From G3448 and G4160; to fabricate the image of a bullock: - make a calf.

G3448.full: Probably strengthened for ï̓́ó÷ïò oschos (a shoot); a young bullock: - calf.

G3449.full: From the base of G3425; toil, that is, (by implication) sadness: - painfulness, travail.

G3450.full: mou moo The simpler from of G1700; of me: - I, me, mine (own), my.

G3451.full: From ìïõóò Mousa (a Muse); "musical", that is, (as noun) a minstrel: - musician.

G3452.full: Perhaps a primary word; the marrow: - marrow.

G3453.full: From the base of G3466; to initiate, that is, (by implication) to teach: - instruct.

G3454.full: Perhaps from the same as G3453 (through the idea of tuition); a tale, that is, fiction ("myth"): - fable.

G3455.full: From a presumed derivative of ìṍæù muzō (to "moo"); to bellow (roar): - roar.

G3456.full: From a derivative of the base of G3455 (meaning snout, as that whence lowing proceeds from); to make mouths at, that is, ridicule: - mock.

G3457.full: From G3458; belonging to a mill: - mill [-stone].

G3458.full: Probably ultimately from the base of G3433 (through the idea of hardship); a "mill", that is, (by implication) a grinder (millstone): - millstone.

G3459.full: From G3458; a mill house: - mill.

G3460.full: Of uncertain derivation; Myra, a place in Asia Minor: - Myra.

G3461.full: From G3463; a ten thousand; by extension a "myriad" or indefinite number: - ten thousand.

G3462.full: From G3463; to apply (perfumed) unguent to: - anoint.

G3463.full: Plural of an apparently primary word (properly meaning very many); ten thousand; by extension innumerably many: - ten thousand.

G3464.full: Probably of foreign origin (compare [H4753] and G4666); "myrrh", that is, (by implication) perfumed oil: - ointment.

G3465.full: Of uncertain origin; Mysia, a region of Asia Minor: - Mysia.

G3466.full: From a derivative of ìṍù muō (to shut the mouth); a secret or "mystery" (through the idea of silence imposed by initiation into religious rites): - mystery.

G3467.full: From a compound of the base of G3466 and ùø ōps (the face: from G3700); to shut the eyes, that is, blink (see indistinctly): - cannot see afar off.

G3468.full: From ìù͂ëïò mōlos ("moil"; probably akin to the base of G3433) and probably ù̓́ø ōps (the face; from G3700); a mole ("black eye") or blow mark: - stripe.

G3469.full: From G3470; to carp at, that is, censure (discredit): - blame.

G3470.full: Perhaps from G3201; a flaw or blot, that is, (figuratively) disgraceful person: - blemish.

G3471.firstSense: become fool, make foolish, lose savour
G3471.full: From G3474; to become insipid; figuratively to make (passively act) as a simpleton: - become fool, make foolish, lose savour.

G3472.full: From G3474; silliness, that is, absurdity: - foolishness.

G3473.full: From a compound of G3474 and G3004; silly talk, that is, buffoonery: - foolish talking.

G3474.full: Probably form the base of G3466; dull or stupid (as if shut up), that is, heedless, (morally) blockhead, (apparently) absurd: - fool (-ish, X -ishness).

G3475.full: Of Hebrew origin [H4872]; Moseus, Moses or Mouses (that is, Mosheh), the Hebrew lawgiver: - Moses.

G3476.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5177]; Naasson (that is, Nachshon), an Israelite: - Naasson.

G3477.full: Probably of Hebrew origin (compare [H5052]); Nangae (that is, perhaps Nogach), an Israelite: - Nagge.

G3478.full: Of uncertain derivation; Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine: - Nazareth.

G3479.full: From G3478; a Nazarene, that is, inhabitant of Nazareth: - of Nazareth.

G3480.full: From G3478; a Nazoraean, that is, inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension a Christian: - Nazarene, of Nazareth.

G3481.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5416]; Nathan, an Israelite: - Nathan.

G3482.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5417]; Nathanael (that is, Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian: - Nathanael.

G3483.firstSense: even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes
G3483.full: nai nahee A primary particle of strong affirmation; yes: - even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes.

G3484.full: Probably of Hebrew origin (compare [H4999]); Nain, a place in Palestine: - Nain.

G3485.full: From a primary word íáé́ù naiō (to dwell); a fane, shrine, temple: - shrine, temple. Compare G2411.

G3486.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5151]; Naum (that is, Nachum), an Israelite: - Naum.

G3488.full: A flower of the same name, from íá́ñêç narkē (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); Narcissus, a Roman: - Narcissus.

G3489.full: From a compound of G3491 and G71; to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively: - make (suffer) shipwreck.

G3490.full: From G3491 and G2819 ("clerk"); a captain: - owner of a ship.

G3491.full: naus nowce From íá́ù naō̄ and íǻù neō (to float); a boat (of any size): - ship.

G3492.full: From G3491; a boatman, that is, seaman: - sailor, shipman.

G3493.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5152]; Nachor, the grandfather of Abraham: - Nachor.

G3494.full: From a derivative of G3501; a youth (up to about forty years): - young man.

G3495.full: From the same as G3494; a youth (under forty): - young man.

G3496.full: From G3501 and G4172; new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia: - Neapolis.

G3497.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5283]; Neeman (that is, Naaman), a Syrian: - Naaman.

G3498.full: From an apparently primary word íǻêõò nekus (a corpse); dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun): - dead.

G3499.full: From G3498; to deaden, that is, (figuratively) to subdue: - be dead, mortify.

G3500.full: From G3499; decease; figuratively impotency: - deadness, dying.

G3501.full: A primary word, including the comparative (second form); "new", that is, (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively regenerate: - new, young.

G3503.full: From G3501; newness, that is, youthfulness: - youth.

G3504.full: From G3501 and a derivative of G5453; newly planted, that is, (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte"): - novice.

G3505.full: Of Latin origin; Neron (that is, Nero), a Roman emperor: - Nero.

G3506.full: Apparently a primary verb; to "nod", that is, (by analogy) to signal: - beckon.

G3507.full: From G3509; properly cloudiness, that is, (concretely) a cloud: - cloud.

G3508.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5321]; Nephthaleim (that is, Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine: - Nephthalim.

G3509.full: Apparently a primary word; a cloud: - cloud.

G3510.full: Of uncertain affinity; a kidney (plural), that is, (figuratively) the inmost mind: - reins.

G3511.full: From a form of G3485 and êïñǻù koreō (to sweep); a temple servant, that is, (by implication) a votary: - worshipper.

G3512.full: From the compound of G3501; appertaining to younger persons, that is, juvenile: - youthful.

G3513.full: Probably an intensive form of G3483; a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as: - I protest by.

G3514.full: From íǻù neō of like meaning; to spin: - spin.

G3515.full: From G3516; to act as a babe, that is, (figuratively) innocently: - be a child.

G3516.full: From an obsolete particle íç ne; implying negation and G2031; not speaking, that is, an infant (minor); figuratively a simple minded person, an immature Christian: - babe, child (+ -ish).

G3517.full: Apparently from a derivative of the base of G3491 (meaning wet); Nereus, a Christian: - Nereus.

G3518.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5374]; Neri (that is, Nerijah), an Israelite: - Neri.

G3519.full: Diminutive of G3520; an islet: - island.

G3520.full: Probably from the base of G3491; an island: - island, isle.

G3521.full: From G3522; abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specifically the fast of the Day of Atonement: - fast (-ing.)

G3522.full: From G3523; to abstain from food (religiously): - fast.

G3523.full: From the negative particle íç nē and G2068; not eating, that is, abstinent from food (religiously): - fasting.

G3524.full: From G3525; sober, that is, (figuratively) circumspect: - sober, vigilant.

G3525.full: Of uncertain affinity; to abstain from wine (keep sober), that is, (figuratively) be discreet: - be sober, watch.

G3526.full: Of Latin origin; black; Niger, a Christian: - Niger.

G3527.full: Probably from G3528; victorious; Nicanor, a Christian: - Nicanor.

G3528.firstSense: conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory
G3528.full: From G3529; to subdue (literally or figuratively): - conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory.

G3529.full: Apparently a primary word; conquest (abstractly), that is, (figuratively) the means of success: - victory.

G3530.full: From G3534 and G1218; victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite: - Nicodemus.

G3531.full: From G3532; a Nicolaite, that is, adherent of Nicolaus: - Nicolaitane.

G3532.full: From G3534 and G2004; victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic: - Nicolaus.

G3533.full: From G3534 and G4172; victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia: - Nicopolis.

G3534.full: From G3529; a conquest (concretely), that is, (by implication) triumph: - victory.

G3535.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5210]; Ninevi (that is, Nineveh), the capital of Assyria: - Nineve.

G3536.full: From G3535; a Ninevite, that is, inhabitant of Nineveh: - of Nineve, Ninevite.

G3538.full: To cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face); ceremonially to perform ablution: - wash. Compare G3068.

G3539.full: From G3563; to exercise the mind (observe), that is, (figuratively) to comprehend, heed: - consider, perceive, think, understand.

G3540.full: From G3539; a perception, that is, purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself: - device, mind, thought.

G3541.full: Of uncertain affinity; a spurious or illegitimate son: - bastard.

G3542.full: Feminine from the same as G3551; pasture, that is, (the act) feeding (figuratively spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage: - X eat, pasture.

G3543.full: From G3551; properly to do by law (usage), that is, to accustom (passively be usual); by extension to deem or regard: - suppose, think, be wont.

G3544.full: From G3551; according (or pertaining) to law, that is, legal (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law: - about the law, lawyer.

G3545.full: Adverb from a derivative of G3551; legitimately (specifically agreeably to the rules of the lists): - lawfully.

G3546.full: From G3543; what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), that is, current coin: - money.

G3547.full: From G3551 and G1320; an expounder of the (Jewish) law, that is, a Rabbi: - doctor (teacher) of the law.

G3548.full: From G3550; legislation (specifically the institution of the Mosaic code): - giving of the law.

G3549.full: From G3550; to legislate, that is, (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them): - establish, receive the law.

G3550.full: From G3551 and a derivative of G5087; a legislator: - lawgiver.
