G3551.full: From a primary word íǻìù nemō (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals); law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), generally (regulation), specifically (of Moses [including the volume]; also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle): - law.

G3552.full: From G3554; to be sick, that is, (by implication of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively to harp upon): - dote.

G3554.full: Of uncertain affinity; a malady (rarely figurative of moral disability): - disease, infirmity, sickness.

G3555.full: From G3502; a brood (of chickens): - brood.

G3556.full: Diminutive of G3502; a birdling: - chicken.

G3557.full: Middle voice from íïóöé́ nosphi (apart or clandestinely); to sequestrate for oneself, that is, embezzle: - keep back, purloin.

G3558.full: Of uncertain affinity; the south (southwest) wind; by extension the southern quarter itself: - south (wind).

G3559.full: From G3563 and a derivative of G5087; calling attention to, that is, (by implication) mild rebuke or warning: - admonition.

G3560.full: From the same as G3559; to put in mind, that is, (by implication) to caution or reprove gently: - admonish, warn.

G3561.full: Feminine of a compound of G3501 and G3376 (as noun by implication of G2250); the festival of new moon: - new moon.

G3562.full: Adverb from a compound of the accusative of G3563 and G2192; in a mind having way, that is, prudently: - discreetly.

G3563.full: nous nooce Probably from the base of G1097; the intellect, that is, mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication meaning: - mind, understanding. Compare G5590.

G3564.full: Probably contracted for a compound of G3565 and G1435; nymph given (that is, born); Nymphas, a Christian: - Nymphas.

G3565.full: From a primary but obsolete verb íṍðôù nuptō (to veil as a bride; compare the Latin "nupto", to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife: - bride, daughter in law.

G3566.full: From G3565; a bride groom (literally or figuratively): - bridegroom.

G3567.full: From G3565; the bridal room: - bridechamber.

G3568.firstSense: henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time)
G3568.full: nun noon A primary particle of present time; "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate: - henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time). See also G3569, G3570.

G3569.full: From neuter plural of G3588 and G3568; the things now, that is, (adverb) at present: - (but) now.

G3570.full: A prolonged form of G3568 for emphasis; just now: - now.

G3571.full: nux noox A primary word; "night" (literally or figuratively): - (mid-) night.

G3572.full: Apparently a primary word; to prick ("nudge"): - pierce.

G3573.full: From a presumed derivative of G3506; to nod, that is, (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively to delay: - slumber.

G3574.full: From G3571 and G2250; a day and night, that is, full day of twenty four hours: - night and day.

G3575.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5146]; Noe, (that is, Noach), a patriarch: - Noe.

G3576.full: From a derivative of G3541; sluggish, that is, (literally) lazy, or (figuratively) stupid: - dull, slothful.

G3577.full: Of uncertain affinity; the back: - back.

G3578.full: From G3581; hospitality, that is, (by implication) a place of entertainment: - lodging.

G3579.full: From G3581; to be a host (passively a guest); by implication be (make, appear) strange: - entertain, lodge, (think it) strange.

G3580.full: From a compound of G3581 and G1209; to be hospitable: - lodge strangers.

G3581.full: Apparently a primary word; foreign (literally alien, or figuratively novel); by implication a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer: - host, strange (-r).

G3582.full: As if from îǻù xeō (which properly means to smooth; by implication [of friction] to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking), (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, that is, about a pint), that is, (specifically) a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy a pitcher): - pot.

G3583.firstSense: dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away)
G3583.full: From G3584; to desiccate; by implication to shrivel, to mature: - dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away).

G3584.full: From the base of G3582 (through the idea of scorching); arid; by implication shrunken, earth (as opposed to water): - dry, land, withered.

G3586.full: From another form of the base of G3582; timber (as fuel or material); by implication a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance: - staff, stocks, tree, wood.

G3587.full: From a derivative of the same as G3586 (meaning a razor); to shave or "shear" the hair: - shave.

G3588.firstSense: the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc
G3588.full: ho hē to ho, hay, to The masculine, feminine (second) and neuter (third) forms, in all their inflections; the definite article; the (sometimes to be supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom): - the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc.

G3589.full: From G3590; ten times eight: - fourscore.

G3591.full: Probably from the same as G43; a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), that is, burden (hindrance): - weight.

G3592.full: The masculine, feminine (second) and neuter (third) forms. From G3588 and G1161; the same, that is, this or that one (plural these or those); often used as personal pronoun: - he, she, such, these, thus.

G3594.full: From G3595; to show the way (literally or figuratively [teach]): - guide, lead.

G3595.full: From G3598 and G2233; a conductor (literally or figuratively [teacher]): - guide, leader.

G3596.full: From a compound of G3598 and G4198; to be a wayfarer, that is, travel: - go on a journey.

G3597.full: From the same as G3596; travel: - journey (-ing).

G3598.full: Apparently a primary word; a road; by implication a progress (the route, act or distance); figuratively a mode or means: - journey, (high-) way.

G3599.full: odous od-ooce Perhaps from the base of G2068; a "tooth": - tooth.

G3600.full: From G3601; to grieve: - sorrow, torment.

G3602.full: From a derivative of the base of G1416; moaning, that is, lamentation: - mourning.

G3603.firstSense: called, which is (make), that is (to say)
G3603.full: From the neuter of G3739 and the third person singular present indicative of G1510; which is: - called, which is (make), that is (to say).

G3604.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5818]; Ozias (that is, Uzzijah), an Israelite: - Ozias.

G3605.full: A primary verb (in a strengthened form); to scent (usually an ill "oder"): - stink.

G3606.full: From G3739 with the directive enclitic of source; from which place or source or cause (adverbially or conjugationally): - from thence, (from) whence, where (-by, -fore, -upon).

G3607.full: Of uncertain affinity; a linen cloth, that is, (especially) a sail: - sheet.

G3608.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G3607; a linen bandage: - linen clothes.

G3609.full: From G3624; domestic, that is, (as noun), a relative, adherent: - (those) of the (his own) house (-hold).

G3610.full: From G3611; a fellow resident, that is, menial domestic: - (household) servant.

G3611.full: From G3624; to occupy a house that is, reside (figuratively inhabit, remain, inhere); by implication to cohabit: - dwell. See also G3625.

G3612.full: From G3611; a tenement, that is, (specifically) a jail: - prison.

G3613.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G3611 (equivalent to G3612); a residence (literally or figuratively): - habitation, house.

G3614.full: From G3624; properly residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely) an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication a family (especially domestics): - home, house (-hold).

G3615.full: From G3614; familiar, that is, (as noun) relatives: - they (them) of (his own) household.

G3616.full: From G3617; to be the head of (that is, rule) a family: - guide the house.

G3617.firstSense: goodman (of the house), householder, master of the house
G3617.full: From G3624 and G1203; the head of a family: - goodman (of the house), householder, master of the house.

G3618.full: From the same as G3619; to be a house builder, that is, construct or (figuratively) confirm: - (be in) build (-er, -ing, up), edify, embolden.

G3619.full: Feminine (abstraction) of a compound of G3624 and the base of G1430; architecture, that is, (concretely) a structure; figuratively confirmation: - building, edify (-ication, -ing).

G3620.full: From the same as G3619; confirmation: - edifying.

G3621.full: From G3623; to manage (a house, that is, an estate): - be steward.

G3622.full: From G3623; administration (of a household or estate); specifically a (religious) "economy": - dispensation, stewardship.

G3623.full: From G3624 and the base of G3551; a house distributor (that is, manager), or overseer, that is, an employee in that capacity; by extension a fiscal agent (treasurer); figuratively a preacher (of the Gospel): - chamberlain, governor, steward.

G3624.full: Of uncertain affinity; a dwelling (more or less extensive, literally or figuratively); by implication a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively): - home, house (-hold), temple.

G3625.full: Feminine participle present passive of G3611 (as noun, by implication of G1093); land, that is, the (terrene part of the) globe; specifically the Roman empire: - earth, world.

G3626.full: From G3624 and ïõ̓͂ñïò ouros (a guard; be "ware"); a stayer at home, that is, domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper"): - keeper at home.

G3627.full: Also in certain tenses ïé̓êôåñǻù oiktereō oyk-ter-eh'-o; from ïé̓êôïò oiktos (pity); to exercise pity: - have compassion on.

G3629.full: From G3627; compassionate: - merciful, of tender mercy.

G3630.full: From G3631 and a derivative of the alternate of G4095; a tippler: - winebibber.

G3631.full: A primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin [H3196]); "wine" (literally or figuratively): - wine.

G3632.full: From G3631 and a form of the base of G5397; an overflow (or surplus) of wine, that is, vinolency (drunkenness): - excess of wine.

G3633.full: Middle voice apparently from G3634; to make like (oneself), that is, imagine (be of the opinion): - suppose, think.

G3634.firstSense: so (as), such as, what (manner of), which
G3634.full: Probably akin to G3588, G3739, and G3745; such or what sort of (as a correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverb) with the negative not so: - so (as), such as, what (manner of), which.

G3635.full: From ï̓́êíïò oknos (hesitation); to be slow (figuratively loath): - delay.

G3636.full: From G3635; tardy, that is, indolent; (figuratively) irksome: - grievous, slothful.

G3637.full: From G3638 and G2250; an eight day old person or act: - the eighth day.

G3639.full: From ï̓́ëëõìé ollumi a primary word (to destroy; a prolonged form); ruin, that is, death, punishment: - destruction.

G3640.full: From G3641 and G4102; incredulous, that is, lacking confidence (in Christ): - of little faith.

G3641.firstSense: + almost, brief [-ly], few, (a) little, + long, a season, short, small, a while
G3641.full: Of uncertain affinity; puny (in extent, degree, number, duration or value); especially neuter (adverbially) somewhat: - + almost, brief [-ly], few, (a) little, + long, a season, short, small, a while.

G3642.full: From G3641 and G5590; little spirited, that is, faint hearted: - feebleminded.

G3643.full: From a compound of G3641 and ù̓́ñá ōra ("care"); to have little regard for, that is, to disesteem: - despise.

G3644.full: From G3645; a ruiner, that is, (specifically) a venomous serpent: - destroyer.

G3645.full: From G3639; to spoil, that is, slay: - destroy.

G3646.full: From a derivative of a compound of G3650 and a derivative of G2545; a wholly consumed sacrifice ("holocaust"): - (whole) burnt offering.

G3647.full: From G3648; integrity, that is, physical wholeness: - perfect soundness.

G3648.full: From G3650 and G2819; complete in every part, that is, perfectly sound (in body): - entire, whole.

G3649.full: A reduplicated primary verb; to "howl" or "halloo", that is, shriek: - howl.

G3650.firstSense: all, altogether, every whit, + throughout, whole
G3650.full: A primary word; "whole" or "all", that is, complete (in extent, amount, time or degree), especially (neuter) as noun or adverb: - all, altogether, every whit, + throughout, whole.

G3651.full: From G3650 and G5056; complete to the end, that is, absolutely perfect: - wholly.

G3652.full: Probably a contraction from Ï̓ëõìðéḯäùñïò Ŏlumpiodōros (Olympian bestowed, that is, heaven descended); Olympas, a Christian: - Olympas.

G3653.full: Of uncertain derivative; an unripe (because out of season) fig: - untimely fig.

G3654.full: Adverb from G3650; completely, that is, altogether; (by analogy) everywhere; (negative) not by any means: - at all, commonly, utterly.

G3655.full: Of uncertain affinity; a thunder storm: - shower.

G3656.full: From G3658; to be in company with, that is, (by implication) to converse: - commune, talk.

G3657.full: From G3658; companionship ("homily"), that is, (by implication) intercourse: - communication.

G3658.full: From the base of G3674 and a derivative of the alternate of G138 (meaning a crowd); association together, that is, a multitude: - company.

G3659.full: From G3700; a sight, that is, (by implication) the eye: - eye.

G3660.full: A prolonged form of a primary but obsolete word, ï̓́ìù omō, for which another prolonged form (ï̓ìḯù omoō om-o'-o) is used in certain tenses. To swear, that is, take (or declare on) oath: - swear.

G3661.full: Adverb from a compound of the base of G3674 and G2372; unanimously: - with one accord (mind).

G3663.full: From G3664 and the alternate of G3958; similarly affected: - of (subject to) like passions.

G3664.full: From the base of G3674; similar (in appearance or character): - like, + manner.

G3665.full: From G3664; resemblance: - like as, similitude.

G3666.full: From G3664; to assimilate, that is, compare; passively to become similar: - be (make) like, (in the) liken (-ess), resemble.

G3667.firstSense: made like to, likeness, shape, similitude
G3667.full: From G3666; a form; abstractly resemblance: - made like to, likeness, shape, similitude.

G3668.full: Adverb from G3664; similarly: - likewise, so.

G3669.full: From G3666; assimilation, that is, resemblance: - similitude.

G3670.firstSense: con- (pro-) fess, confession is made, give thanks, promise
G3670.full: From a compound of the base of G3674 and G3056; to assent, that is, covenant, acknowledge: - con- (pro-) fess, confession is made, give thanks, promise.

G3671.full: From the same as G3670; acknowledgment: - con- (pro-) fession, professed.

G3672.full: Adverb of present passive participle of G3670; confessedly: - without controversy.

G3673.full: From the base of G3674 and G5078; a fellow artificer: - of the same craft.

G3674.full: Genitive case of ï̔ìḯò homos (the same; akin to G260) as adverb; at the same place or time: - together.

G3675.full: From the base of G3674 and G5424; like minded, that is, harmonious: - of one mind.

G3676.full: Adverb from the base of G3674; at the same time, that is, (conjugationally) notwithstanding, yet still: - and even, nevertheless, though but.

G3677.full: Of uncertain derivation; a dream: - dream.

G3678.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G3688; a little ass: - young ass.

G3679.firstSense: cast in teeth, (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid
G3679.full: From G3681; to defame, that is, rail at, chide, taunt: - cast in teeth, (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid.

G3681.full: Probably akin to the base of G3686; notoriety, that is, a taunt (disgrace): - reproach.

G3682.full: From G3685; profitable; Onesimus, a Christian: - Onesimus.

G3683.full: From a derivative of G3685 and G5411; profit bearer; Onesiphorus, a Christian: - Onesiphorus.

G3684.full: From G3688; belonging to an ass, that is, large (so as to be turned by an ass): - millstone.

G3685.full: A prolonged form of an apparent primary verb ï̓́íïìáé onomai; for which another prolonged form ï̓íá́ù onaō is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of G3686 through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, that is, (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from: - have joy.

G3686.full: From a presumed derivative of the base of G1097 (compare G3685); a "name" (literally or figuratively), (authority, character): - called, (+ sur-) name (-d).

G3687.full: From G3686; to name, that is, assign an appellation; by extension to utter, mention, profess: - call, name.

G3688.full: Apparently a primary word; a donkey: - ass.

G3689.firstSense: certainly, clean, indeed, of a truth, verily
G3689.full: Adverb of the oblique cases of G5607; really: - certainly, clean, indeed, of a truth, verily.

G3690.full: From G3691; vinegar, that is, sour wine: - vinegar.

G3691.full: Probably akin to the base of G188 ("acid"); keen; by analogy rapid: - sharp, swift.

G3692.full: Probably from G3700; a hole (as if for light), that is, cavern; by analogy a spring (of water): - cave, place.

G3693.full: From ï̓́ðéò opis (regard; from G3700) with enclitic of source; from the rear (as a secure aspect), that is, at the back (adverb and preposition of palce or time): - after, backside, behind.

G3694.full: From the same as G3693 with enclitic of direction; to the back, that is, aback (as adverb or preposition of time or place; or as noun): - after, back (-ward), (+ get) behind, + follow.

G3695.full: From G3696; to equip (with weapons [middle voice and figuratively]): - arm self.

G3696.full: Probably from the primary word å̔́ðù hepō(to be busy about); an implement or utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially offensive for war): - armour, instrument, weapon.

G3697.firstSense: what manner (sort) of, such as, whatsoever
G3697.full: From G3739 and G4169; of what kind that, that is, how (as) great (excellent) (specifically as indefinite correlation to antecedent definitely G5108 of quality): - what manner (sort) of, such as, whatsoever.

G3698.full: From G3739 and G4218; what (-ever) then, that is, (of time) as soon as: - when.

G3699.firstSense: in what place, where (-as, -soever), whither (+ soever)
G3699.full: From G3739 and G4225; what (-ever) where, that is, at whichever spot: - in what place, where (-as, -soever), whither (+ soever).

G3700.full: The first a (middle voice) prolonged form of the second (primary) which is used for it in certain tenses; and both as alternates of G3708; to gaze (that is, with wide open eyes, as at something remarkable; and thus differing from G991, which denotes simply voluntary observation; and from G1492, which expresses merely mechanical, passive or casual vision; while G2300, and still more emphatically its intensive G2334, signifies an earnest but more continued inspection; and G4648 a watching from a distance): - appear, look, see, shew self.

G3701.full: From a presumed derivative of G3700; visuality, that is, (concretely) an apparition: - vision.

G3702.full: From an obsolete verb akin to å̔́øù hepsō (to "steep"); cooked, that is, roasted: - broiled.

G3703.full: Apparently from the base of G3796 and G5610; properly even tide of the (summer) season (dog days), that is, (by implication) ripe fruit: - fruit.

G3704.full: From G3739 nad G4459; what (-ever) how, that is, in the manner that (as adverb or conjugation of coincidence, intentional or actual): - because, how, (so) that, to, when.

G3705.full: From G3708; something gazed at, that is, a spectacle (especially supernatural): - sight, vision.

G3706.full: From G3708; the act of gazing, that is, (external) an aspect or (internal) an inspired appearance: - sight, vision.

G3707.full: From G3708; gazed at, that is, (by implication) capable of being seen: - visible.

G3708.full: Properly to stare at (compare G3700), that is, (by implication) to discern clearly (physically or mentally); by extension to attend to; by Hebraism to experience; passively to appear: - behold, perceive, see, take heed.

G3709.full: From G3713; properly desire (as a reaching forth or excitement of the mind), that is, (by analogy) violent passion (ire, or [justifiable] abhorrence); by implication punishment: - anger, indignation, vengeance, wrath.

G3710.full: From G3709; to provoke or enrage, that is, (passively) become exasperated: - be angry (wroth).

G3712.full: From G3713; a stretch of the arms, that is, a fathom: - fathom.

G3713.full: Middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare G3735); to stretch oneself, that is, reach out after (long for): - covet after, desire.

G3714.full: From G3735; mountainous, that is, (feminine by implication of G5561) the Highlands (of Judaea): - hill country.

G3715.full: From G3713; excitement of the mind, that is, longing after: - lust.

G3716.full: From a compound of G3717 and G4228; to be straight footed, that is, (figuratively) to go directly forward: - walk uprightly.

G3717.full: Probably from the base of G3735; right (as rising), that is, (perpendicularly) erect (figuratively honest), or (horizontally) level or direct: - straight, upright.

G3718.full: From a compound of G3717 and the base of G5114; to make a straight cut, that is, (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message): - rightly divide.

G3719.full: From G3722; to use the dawn, that is, (by implication) to repair betimes: - come early in the morning.

G3720.full: From G3722; relating to the dawn, that is, matutinal (as an epithet of Venus, especially brilliant in the early day): - morning.

G3721.full: From G3722; in the dawn, that is, up at day break: - early.

G3722.full: From the same as G3735; dawn (as sun rise, rising of light); by extension morn: - early in the morning.

G3723.full: Adverb from G3717; in a straight manner, that is, (figuratively) correctly (also morally): - plain, right (-ly).

G3724.full: From G3725; to mark out or bound ("horizon"), that is, (figuratively) to appoint, decree, specify: - declare, determine, limit, ordain.

G3725.full: Neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary word ï̔́ñïò horos (a bound or limit); a boundary line, that is, (by implication) a frontier (region): - border, coast.

G3726.full: From G3727; to put on oath, that is, make swear; by analogy to solemnly enjoin: - adjure, charge.

G3727.full: From å̔́ñêïò herkos (a fence; perhaps akin to G3725); a limit, that is, (sacred) restraint (specifically oath): - oath.

G3728.full: From a compound of G3727 and a derivative of G3660; asseveration on oath: - oath.

G3729.full: From G3730; to start, spur or urge on, that is, (reflexively) to dash or plunge: - run (violently), rush.

G3730.full: Of uncertain affinity; a violent impulse, that is, onset: - assault.

G3731.full: From G3730; an attack, that is, (abstractly) precipitancy: - violence.

G3732.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G3733; a birdling: - bird, fowl.

G3733.full: Probably from a prolonged form of the base of G3735; a bird (as rising in the air), that is, (specifically) a hen (or female domestic fowl): - hen.

G3734.full: From a compound of the base of G3725 and a derivative of G5087; a limit placing, that is, (concretely) boundary line: - bound.

G3735.full: Probably a from an obsolete word ï̓́ñù orō (to rise or "rear"; perhaps akin to G142; compare G3733); a mountain (as lifting itself above the plain): - hill, mount (-ain).

G3736.full: Apparently a primary verb; to "burrow" in the ground, that is, dig: - dig.

G3737.full: Of uncertain affinity; bereaved ("orphan"), that is, parentless: - comfortless, fatherless.

G3738.full: Middle voice fromḯñ÷ïò orchos (a row or ring); to dance (from the ranklike or regular motion): - dance.

G3739.firstSense: one, (an-, the) other, some, that, what, which, who (-m, -se), etc
G3739.full: hos hē ho hos, hay, ho Probably a primary word (or perhaps a form of the article G3588); the relative (sometimes demonstrative) pronoun, who, which, what, that: - one, (an-, the) other, some, that, what, which, who (-m, -se), etc. See also G3757.

G3740.full: Multiple adverb from G3739; how (that is, with G302, so) many times as: - as oft (-en) as.

G3741.full: Of uncertain affinity; properly right (by intrinsic or divine character; thus distinguished from G1342, which refers rather to human statutes and relations; from G2413, which denotes formal consecration; and from G40, which relates to purity from defilement), that is, hallowed (pious, sacred, sure): - holy, mercy, shalt be.

G3744.full: From G3605; fragrance (literally or figuratively): - odour, savour.

G3745.firstSense: all (that), as (long, many, much) (as), how great (many, much), [in-] asmuch as, so man…
G3745.full: By reduplication from G3739; as (much, great, long, etc.) as: - all (that), as (long, many, much) (as), how great (many, much), [in-] asmuch as, so many as, that (ever), the more, those things, what (great, -soever), wheresoever, wherewithsoever, which, X while, who (-soever).

G3746.full: From G3739 and G4007; who especially: - whomsoever.

G3747.full: Of uncertain affinity; a bone: - bone.

G3748.firstSense: X and (they), (such) as, (they) that, in that they, what (-soever), whereas ye, (they)…
G3748.full: From G3739 and G5100; which some, that is, any that; also (definitely) which same: - X and (they), (such) as, (they) that, in that they, what (-soever), whereas ye, (they) which, who (-soever). Compare G3754.

G3749.full: From ï̓́óôñáêïí ostrakon ("oyster"), (a tile, that is, terra cotta); earthen ware, that is, clayey; by implication frail: - of earth, earthen.

G3750.full: From a derivative of G3605; smell (the sense): - smelling.

G3751.full: Of uncertain affinity; the loin (externally), that is, the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power: - loin.

G3752.firstSense: as long (soon) as, that, + till, when (-soever), while
G3752.full: From G3753 and G302; whenever (implying hypothesis or more or less uncertainty); also causative (conjugationally) inasmuch as: - as long (soon) as, that, + till, when (-soever), while.

G3753.firstSense: after (that), as soon as, that, when, while
G3753.full: From G3739 and G5037; at which (thing) too, that is, when: - after (that), as soon as, that, when, while. Second form also feminine, third form also neuter and fourth form simply the article G3588 followed by G5037; so written (in some editions) to distinguish them from G3752 and G5119.
G3753.xlit: hote ho te hē te tō te

G3754.firstSense: as concerning that, as though, because (that), for (that), how (that), (in) that, thoug…
G3754.full: Neuter of G3748 as conjugation; demonstrative that (sometimes redundant); causatively because: - as concerning that, as though, because (that), for (that), how (that), (in) that, though, why.

G3755.full: From the genitive case of G3748 (as adverb); during which same time, that is, whilst: - whiles.

G3756.firstSense: + long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, [can-] not, + nothing, + special, un ([-…
G3756.full: ou oo Also ïõ̓ê ouk ook used before a vowel and ïõ̓÷ ouch ookh before an aspirate. A primary word; the absolutely negative (compare G3361) adverb; no or not: - + long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, [can-] not, + nothing, + special, un ([-worthy]), when, + without, + yet but. See also G3364, G3372.

G3757.full: hou hoo Genitive case of G3739 as adverb; at which place, that is, where: - where (-in), whither ([-soever]).

G3758.full: A primary exclamation of surprise; "ah": - ah.

G3759.full: A primary excamation of grief; "woe": - alas, woe.

G3760.full: Adverb from (the feminine) of G3762; by no means: - not.

G3761.firstSense: neither (indeed), never, no (more, nor, not), nor (yet), (also, even, then) not (even,…
G3761.full: From G3756 and G1161; not however, that is, neither, nor, not even: - neither (indeed), never, no (more, nor, not), nor (yet), (also, even, then) not (even, so much as), + nothing, so much as.

G3762.firstSense: any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these thi…
G3762.full: Including the feminine ïõ̓äåìé́á oudemia oo-dem-ee'-ah and the neuter ïõ̓äǻí ouden oo-den' From G3761 and G1520; not even one (man, woman or thing), that is, none, nobody, nothing: - any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought.

G3763.firstSense: neither at any time, never, nothing at any time
G3763.full: From G3761 and G4218; not even at any time, that is, never at all: - neither at any time, never, nothing at any time.

G3764.firstSense: as yet not, never before (yet), (not) yet
G3764.full: From G3761 and G4452; not even yet: - as yet not, never before (yet), (not) yet.

G3765.firstSense: after that (not), (not) any more, henceforth (hereafter), not, no longer (more), not as…
G3765.full: Also (separately) ïõ̓ê å̓́ôé ouk eti ook et'-ee From G3756 and G2089; not yet, no longer: - after that (not), (not) any more, henceforth (hereafter), not, no longer (more), not as yet (now), now no more (not), yet (not).

G3766.full: From G3756 and G3767; is it not therefore that, that is, (affirmatively) hence or so: - then.

G3767.firstSense: and (so, truly), but, now (then), so (likewise then), then, therefore, verily, wherefore
G3767.full: oun oon Apparently a primary word; (adverbially) certainly, or (conjugationally) accordingly: - and (so, truly), but, now (then), so (likewise then), then, therefore, verily, wherefore.

G3768.full: From G3756 and G4452; not yet: - hitherto not, (no . . .) as yet, not yet.

G3769.full: Apparently a primary word; a tail: - tail.

G3770.full: From G3772; celestial, that is, belonging to or coming from the sky: - heavenly.

G3771.full: From G3772 and the enclitic of source; from the sky: - from heaven.

G3772.full: Perhaps from the same as G3735 (through the idea of elevation); the sky; by extension heaven (as the abode of God); by implication happiness, power, eternity; specifically the Gospel (Christianity): - air, heaven ([-ly]), sky.

G3773.full: Of Latin origin; Urbanus (of the city, "urbane"), a Christian: - Urbanus.

G3774.full: Of Hebrew origin [H223]; Urias (that is, Urijah), a Hittite: - Urias.

G3775.full: ous ooce Apparently a primary word; the ear (physically or mentally): - ear.

G3776.full: From the feminine of G5607; substance, that is, property (possessions): - goods, substance.

G3777.firstSense: neither, none, nor (yet), (no, yet) not, nothing
G3777.full: From G3756 and G5037; not too, that is, neither or nor; by analogy not even: - neither, none, nor (yet), (no, yet) not, nothing.

G3778.firstSense: he (it was that), hereof, it, she, such as, the same, these, they, this (man, same, wom…
G3778.full: Including the nominative masculine plural (second form), nominative feminine signular (third form), and the nominate feminine plural, (fourth form). From the article G3588 and G846; the he (she or it), that is, this or that (often with the article repeated): - he (it was that), hereof, it, she, such as, the same, these, they, this (man, same, woman), which, who.

G3779.firstSense: after that, after (in) this manner, as, even (so), for all that, like (-wise), no more,…
G3779.full: Or, before a vowel, ïõ̔́ôùò houtōs hoo'-toce. From G3778; in this way (referring to what precedes or follows): - after that, after (in) this manner, as, even (so), for all that, like (-wise), no more, on this fashion (-wise), so (in like manner), thus, what.

G3780.full: Intensive of G3756; not indeed: - nay, not.

G3781.full: From G3784; an ower, that is, a person indebted; figuratively a delinquent; morally a transgressor (against God): - debtor, which owed, sinner.

G3782.full: From G3784; indebtedness, that is, (concretely) a sum owed; figuratively obligation, that is, (conjugal) duty: - debt, due.

G3783.full: From (the alternate of) G3784; something owed, that is, (figuratively) a due.; morally a fault: - debt.

G3784.firstSense: behove, be bound, (be) debt (-or), (be) due (-ty), be guilty (indebted), (must) need (-…
G3784.full: Including its prolonged form (second form) used in certain tenses. Probably from the base of G3786 (through the idea of accruing); to owe (pecuniarily); figuratively to be under obligation (ought, must, should); morally to fail in duty: - behove, be bound, (be) debt (-or), (be) due (-ty), be guilty (indebted), (must) need (-s), ought, owe, should. See also G3785.

G3785.full: First person singular of a past tense of G3784; I ought (wish), that is, (interjectionally) oh that!: - would (to God).

G3786.full: From ï̓öǻëëù ophellō (to heap up, that is, accumulate or benefit); gain: - advantageth, profit.

G3787.full: From G3788 and G1397; sight labor, that is, that needs watching (remissness): - eye-service.

G3788.full: From G3700; the eye (literally or figuratively); by implication vision; figuratively envy (from the jealous side glance): - eye, sight.

G3789.full: Probably from G3700 (through the idea of sharpness of vision); a snake, figuratively (as a type of sly cunning) an artful malicious person, especially Satan: - serpent.

G3790.full: Perhaps from G3700 (through the idea of the shading or proximity to the organ of vision); the eye "brow" or forehead, that is, (figuratively) the brink of a precipice: - brow.

G3791.full: From G3793; to mob, that is, (by implication) to harass: - vex.

G3792.full: From G3793 and G4160; to make a crowd, that is, raise a public disturbance: - gather a company.

G3793.firstSense: company, multitude, number (of people), people, press
G3793.full: From a derivative of G2192 (meaning a vehicle); a throng (as borne along); by implication the rabble; by extension a class of people; figuratively a riot: - company, multitude, number (of people), people, press.

G3794.full: From a remote derivative of G2192 (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely); a castle (figuratively argument): - stronghold.

G3795.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G3702; a relish to other food (as if cooked sauce), that is, (specifically) fish (presumably salted and dried as a condiment): - fish.

G3796.full: From the same as G3694 (through the idea of backwardness); (adverbially) late in the day; by extension after the close of the day: - (at) even, in the end.

G3797.full: From G3796; later, that is, vernal (showering): - latter.

G3798.full: From G3796; late; feminine (as noun) afternoon (early eve) or nightfall (later eve): - even (-ing, [-tide]).

G3799.full: From G3700; properly sight (the act), that is, (by implication) the visage, an external show: - appearance, countenance, face.

G3800.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the same as G3795; rations for a soldier, that is, (by extension) his stipend or pay: - wages.

G3801.firstSense: which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be)
G3801.full: A phrase combining G3588 with the present participle and imperfect of G1510 and the present participle of G2064 by means of G2532; the one being and the one that was and the one coming, that is, the Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ. (Each "and" (G2532) was ommited from the phrase because of limited space.): - which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be).
G3801.xlit: ho ōn ho ēn ho erchomenos
G3801.pronunciation: ho own ho ane ho er-khom'-enos

G3803.full: From G4078; a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively a trick or stratagem (temptation): - snare

G3804.full: From a presumed derivative of G3806; something undergone, that is, hardship or pain; subjectively an emotion or influence: - affection, affliction, motion, suffering.

G3805.full: From the same as G3804; liable (that is, doomed) to experience pain: - suffer.

G3806.full: From the alternate of G3958; properly suffering ("pathos"), that is, (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence): - (inordinate) affection, lust.

G3807.full: From G3816 and a reduplication form of G71; a boy leader, that is, a servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication [figuratively] a tutor ["paedagogue"]): - instructor, schoolmaster.

G3808.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G3816; a little boy: - child, lad.

G3809.full: From G3811; tutorage, that is, education or training; by implication disciplinary correction: - chastening, chastisement, instruction, nurture.

G3810.full: From G3811; a trainer, that is, teacher or (by implication) discipliner: - which corrected, instructor.

G3811.full: From G3816; to train up a child, that is, educate, or (by implication) discipline (by punishment): - chasten (-ise), instruct, learn, teach.

G3812.full: Adverb (of source) from G3813; from infancy: - of a child.

G3813.full: Neuter diminutive of G3816; a childling (of either sex), that is, (properly) an infant, or (by extension) a half grown boy or girl; figuratively an immature Christian: - (little, young) child, damsel.

G3814.full: Feminine diminutive of G3816; a girl, that is, (specifically) a female slave or servant: - bondmaid (-woman), damsel, maid (-en).

G3815.full: From G3816; to sport (as a boy): - play.

G3816.firstSense: child, maid (-en), (man) servant, son, young man
G3816.full: pais paheece Perhaps from G3817; a boy (as often beaten with impunity), or (by analogy) a girl, and (generally) a child; specifically a slave or servant (especially a minister to a king; and by eminence to God): - child, maid (-en), (man) servant, son, young man.

G3817.full: A primary verb; to hit (as if by a single blow and less violently than G5180); specifically to sting (as a scorpion): - smite, strike.

G3818.full: Feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation; Pacatianian, a section of Phrygia: - Pacatiana.

G3819.firstSense: any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past
G3819.full: Probably another form for G3825 (through the idea of retrocession); (adverbially) formerly, or (relatively) sometime since; (elliptically as adjective) ancient: - any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past.

G3820.full: From G3819; antique, that is, not recent, worn out: - old.

G3822.full: From G3820; to make (passively become) worn out, or declare obsolete: - decay, make (wax) old.

G3823.full: From ðá́ëëù pallō (to vibrate; another form for G906); wrestling: - + wrestle.

G3824.full: From G3825 and G1078; (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), that is, (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specifically Messianic restoration: - regeneration.

G3825.full: Probably from the same as G3823 (through the idea of oscillatory repetition); (adverbially) anew, that is, (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjugationally) furthermore or on the other hand: - again.

G3826.full: Dative case (adverb) of a compound of G3956 and G4128; in full multitude, that is, concertedly or simultaneously: - all at once.

G3827.full: From G3956 and G4183; full many, that is, immense: - very great.

G3828.full: From a compound of G3956 and G5443; every tribal, that is, heterogeneous (G5561 being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor: - Pamphylia.

G3829.full: Neuter of a presumed compound of G3956 and a derivative of G1209; all receptive, that is, a public lodging place (caravanserai or khan): - inn.

G3830.full: From the same as G3829; an innkeeper (warden of a caravanserai): - host.

G3831.full: From G3956 and a derivative of G58; a mass meeting, that is, (figuratively) universal companionship: - general assembly.

G3832.full: Adverb from G3956 and G3624; with the whole family: - with all his house.

G3833.full: From a compound of G3956 and G3696; full armor ("panoply"): - all (whole) armour.

G3834.full: From G3835; adroitness, that is, (in a bad sense) trickery or sophistry: - (cunning) craftiness, subtilty.

G3835.full: From G3956 and G2041; all working, that is, adroit (shrewd): - crafty.

G3836.full: Adverb (of source) from G3837; from all directions: - from every quarter.

G3837.full: Genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of G3956; universally: - in all places, everywhere.

G3838.full: From G3956 and G5056; full ended, that is, entire (neuter as noun, completion): - + in [no] wise, uttermost.

G3839.full: Adverb (of manner) from G3956; wholly: - always.

G3840.full: Adverb (of source) from G3956; from (that is, on) all sides: - on every side, round about.

G3841.full: From G3956 and G2904; the all ruling, that is, God (as absolute and universal sovereign): - Almighty, Omnipotent.

G3842.full: From G3956 and G3753; every when, that is, at all times: - always (-s), ever (-more).

G3843.firstSense: by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in [no] wise, surely
G3843.full: From G3956; entirely; specifically at all events, (with negative following) in no event: - by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in [no] wise, surely.

G3844.firstSense: above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give [such things…
G3844.full: A primary preposition; properly near, that is, (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local [especially beyond or opposed to] or causal [on account of]). In compounds it retains the same variety of application: - above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give [such things as they], + that [she] had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side . . . by, in the sight of, than, [there-] fore, with. In compounds it retains the same variety of application.

G3845.full: From G3844 and the base of G939; to go contrary to, that is, violate a command: - (by) transgress (-ion).

G3846.full: From G3844 and G906; to throw alongside, that is, (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken: - arrive, compare.

G3848.full: From G3845; a violator: - breaker, transgress (-or).

G3849.full: From G3844 and the middle voice of G971; to force contrary to (nature), that is, compel (by entreaty): - constrain.

G3850.full: From G3846; a similitude ("parable"), that is, (symbolically) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apoth gm or adage: - comparison, figure, parable, proverb.

G3851.full: From G3844 and the middle of G1011; to misconsult, that is, disregard: - not (to) regard (-ing).

G3852.full: From G3853; a mandate: - charge, command.

G3853.full: From G3844 and the base of G32; to transmit a message, that is, (by implication) to enjoin: - (give in) charge, (give) command (-ment), declare.

G3854.full: From G3844 and G1096; to become near, that is, approach (have arrived); by implication to appear publicly: - come, go, be present.

G3855.full: From G3844 and G71; to lead near, that is, (reflexively or intransitively) to go along or away: - depart, pass (away, by, forth).

G3856.firstSense: make a public example, put to an open shame
G3856.full: From G3844 and G1165; to show alongside (the public), that is, expose to infamy: - make a public example, put to an open shame.

G3857.full: Of Oriental origin (compare [H6508]); a park, that is, (specifically) an Eden (place of future happiness, "paradise"): - paradise.

G3858.full: From G3844 and G1209; to accept near, that is, admit or (by implication) delight in: - receive.

G3859.full: From a compound of G3844 and G1304; misemployment, that is, meddlesomeness: - perverse disputing.

G3860.firstSense: betray, bring forth, cast, commit, deliver (up), give (over, up), hazard, put in prison…
G3860.full: From G3844 and G1325; to surrender, that is, yield up, intrust, transmit: - betray, bring forth, cast, commit, deliver (up), give (over, up), hazard, put in prison, recommend.

G3861.full: From G3844 and G1391 (in the sense of seeming); contrary to expectation, that is, extraordinary ("paradox"): - strange.

G3862.full: From G3860; transmission, that is, (concretely) a precept; specifically the Jewish traditionary law: - ordinance, tradition.

G3863.full: From G3844 and G2206; to stimulate alongside, that is, excite to rivalry: - provoke to emulation (jealousy).

G3864.full: From G3844 and G2281; along the sea, that is, maritime (lacustrine): - upon the sea coast.

G3865.full: From G3844 and G2334; to overlook or disregard: - neglect.

G3866.full: From G3908; a deposit, that is, (figuratively) trust: - committed unto.

G3867.full: From G3844 and G134; to mispraise, that is, recommend or advise (a different course): - admonish, exhort.

G3868.full: From G3844 and the middle of G154; to beg off, that is, deprecate, decline, shun: - avoid, (make) excuse, intreat, refuse, reject.

G3869.full: From G3844 and G2523; to sit down near: - sit.

G3870.firstSense: beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort (-ation), intreat, pray
G3870.full: From G3844 and G2564; to call near, that is, invite, invoke (by imploration, hortation or consolation): - beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort (-ation), intreat, pray.

G3871.full: From G3844 and G2572; to cover alongside, that is, veil (figuratively): - hide.

G3872.full: From a compound of G3844 and G2698; something put down alongside, that is, a deposit (sacred trust): - that (thing) which is committed (un-) to (trust).

G3873.full: From G3844 and G2749; to lie near, that is, be at hand (figuratively be prompt or easy): - be present.

G3874.full: From G3870; imploration, hortation, solace: - comfort, consolation, exhortation, intreaty.

G3876.full: From G3878; inattention, that is, (by implication) disobedience: - disobedience.

G3877.firstSense: attain, follow, fully know, have understanding
G3877.full: From G3844 and G190; to follow near, that is, (figuratively) attend (as a result), trace out, conform to: - attain, follow, fully know, have understanding.

G3878.full: From G3844 and G191; to mishear, that is, (by implication) to disobey: - neglect to hear.

G3879.full: From G3844 and G2955; to bend beside, that is, lean over (so as to peer within): - look (into), stoop down.

G3880.full: From G3844 and G2983; to receive near, that is, associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation); by analogy to assume an office; figuratively to learn: - receive, take (unto, with).

G3881.full: From G3844 and the middle of G3004 (in its original sense); (specifically) to lay one's course near, that is, sail past: - pass, sail by.

G3882.full: From G3844 and G251; beside the salt (sea), that is, maritime: - sea coast.

G3883.full: From a compound of G3844 and G236; transmutation (of phase or orbit), that is, (figuratively) fickleness: - variableness.

G3884.full: From G3844 and G3049; to misreckon, that is, delude: - beguile, deceive.

G3885.full: From a derivative of G3886; as if dissolved, that is, "paralytic": - that had (sick of) the palsy.

G3886.firstSense: feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy
G3886.full: From G3844 and G3089; to loosen beside, that is, relax (perfect passive participle paralyzed or enfeebled): - feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy.

G3887.full: From G3844 and G3306; to stay near, that is, remain (literally tarry; or figuratively be permanent, persevere): - abide, continue.

G3888.full: From G3844 and the middle of a derivative of G3454; to relate near, that is, (by implication) encourage, console: - comfort.

G3890.full: Neuter of G3889; consolation (properly concrete): - comfort.

G3891.full: From a compound of G3844 and G3551; to be opposed to law, that is, to transgress: - contrary to law.

G3892.full: From the same as G3891; transgression: - iniquity.

G3893.full: From G3844 and G4087; to embitter alongside, that is, (figuratively) to exasperate: - provoke.

G3895.full: From G3844 and G4098; to fall aside, that is, (figuratively) to apostatize: - fall away.

G3896.full: From G3844 and G4126; to sail near: - sail by.

G3897.full: Neuter of a compound of G3844 and the base of G4139 (as adverb); close by, that is, (figuratively) almost: - nigh unto.

G3898.full: Adverb from the same as G3897; in a manner near by, that is, (figuratively) similarly: - likewise.

G3899.full: From G3844 and G4198; to travel near: - go, pass (by).

G3900.full: From G3895; a side slip (lapse or deviation), that is, (unintentional) error or (wilful) transgression: - fall, fault, offence, sin, trespass.

G3901.full: From G3844 and the alternate of G4482; to flow by, that is, (figuratively) carelessly pass (miss): - let slip.

G3902.full: From G3844 and the base of G4591; side marked, that is, labelled (with a badge [figure head] of a ship): - sign.

G3903.full: From G3844 and a derivative of G4632; to furnish aside, that is, get ready: - prepare self, be (make) ready.

G3904.full: As if from G3903; readiness: - preparation.

G3905.full: From G3844 and ôåé́íù teinō (to stretch); to extend along, that is, prolong (in point of time): - continue.

G3906.full: From G3844 and G5083; to inspect alongside, that is, note insidiously or scrupulously: - observe, watch.

G3907.full: From G3906; inspection, that is, ocular evidence: - observation.

G3908.firstSense: allege, commend, commit (the keeping of), put forth, set before
G3908.full: From G3844 and G5087; to place alongside, that is, present (food, truth); by implication to deposit (as a trust or for protection): - allege, commend, commit (the keeping of), put forth, set before.

G3909.full: From G3844 and G5177; to chance near, that is, fall in with: - meet with.

G3910.full: From G3844 and a derivative of G846; at the very instant, that is, momentary: - but for a moment.

G3911.full: From G3844 and G5342 (including its alternate forms); to bear along or aside, that is, carry off (literally or figuratively); by implication to avert: - remove, take away.

G3912.full: From G3844 and G5426; to misthink, that is, be insane (silly): - as a fool.

G3913.full: From G3912; insanity, that is, foolhardiness: - madness.

G3914.full: From G3844 and G5492; to winter near, that is, stay with over the rainy season: - winter.

G3915.full: From G3914; a wintering over: - winter in.

G3916.full: From G3844 and G5536 (in its original sense); at the thing itself, that is, instantly: - forthwith, immediately, presently, straightway, soon.

G3917.full: Feminine of ðá́ñäïò pardos (a panther); a leopard: - leopard.

G3918.firstSense: come, X have, be here, + lack, (be here) present
G3918.full: From G3844 and G1510 (including its various forms); to be near, that is, at hand; neuter present participle (singular) time being, or (plural) property: - come, X have, be here, + lack, (be here) present.

G3919.full: From G3844 and G1521; to lead in aside, that is, introduce surreptitiously: - privily bring in.

G3920.full: From G3919; smuggled in: - unawares brought in.

G3921.full: From G3844 and a compound of G1519 and G1416; to settle in alongside, that is, lodge stealthily: - creep in unawares.

G3922.full: From G3844 and G1525; to come in along side, that is, supervene additionally or stealthily: - come in privily, enter.

G3923.full: From G3844 and G1533; to bear in alongside, that is, introduce simultaneously: - give.

G3924.full: From G3844 and G1622; near outside, that is, besides: - except, saving, without.

G3925.full: From a compound of G3844 and G1685; a throwing in beside (juxtaposition), that is, (specifically) battle array, encampment or barracks (tower Antonia): - army, camp, castle.

G3926.full: From G3844 and G1776; to harass further, that is, annoy: - trouble.

G3927.full: From G3844 and the base of G1927; an alien alongside, that is, a resident foreigner: - pilgrim, stranger.

G3928.firstSense: come (forth), go, pass (away, by, over), past, transgress
G3928.full: From G3844 and G2064; to come near or aside, that is, to approach (arrive), go by (or away), (figuratively) perish or neglect, (causatively) avert: - come (forth), go, pass (away, by, over), past, transgress.

G3929.full: From G2935; praetermission, that is, toleration: - remission.

G3930.firstSense: bring, do, give, keep, minister, offer, shew, + trouble
G3930.full: From G3844 and G2192; to hold near, that is, present, afford, exhibit, furnish occasion: - bring, do, give, keep, minister, offer, shew, + trouble.

G3931.full: From a compound of G3844 and a derivative of G58 (meaning to harangue an assembly); an address alongside, that is, (specifically) consolation: - comfort.

G3933.full: Of unknown origin; a maiden; by implication an unmarried daughter: - virgin.

G3934.full: Probably of foreign origin; a Parthian, that is, inhabitant of Parthia: - Parthian.

G3935.full: From G3844 and é́çìé hiēmi (to send); to let by, that is, relax: - hang down.

G3936.firstSense: assist, bring before, command, commend, give presently, present, prove, provide, shew,…
G3936.full: From G3844 and G2476; to stand beside, that is, (transitively) to exhibit, proffer, (specifically) recommend, (figuratively) substantiate; or (intransitively) to be at hand (or ready), aid: - assist, bring before, command, commend, give presently, present, prove, provide, shew, stand (before, by, here, up, with), yield.

G3937.full: Probaby by contraction for Ðáñìåíé́äçò Parmenidēs (a derivative of a compound of G3844 and G3306); constant; Parmenas, a Christian: - Parmenas.

G3938.full: From G3844 adn G3598; a by road, that is, (actively) a route: - way.

G3939.full: From G3844 and G3611; to dwell near, that is, reside as a foreigner: - sojourn in, be a stranger.

G3940.full: From G3941; foreign residence: - sojourning, X as strangers.

G3941.full: From G3844 and G3624; having a home near, that is, (as noun) a by-dweller (alien resident): - foreigner, sojourn, stranger.

G3942.full: From a compound of G3844 and perhaps a derivative of G3633; apparently a state alongside of supposition, that is, (concretely) an adage; specifically an enigmatical or fictitious illustration: - parable, proverb.

G3943.full: From G3844 and G3631; staying near wine, that is, tippling (a toper): - given to wine.

G3944.full: From G3844 and ïé́÷ïìáé oichomai (to depart); to escape along, that is, be gone: - past.

G3945.full: From G3946; to resemble: - be like unto.

G3946.full: From G3844 and G3664; alike nearly, that is, similar: - like.

G3947.full: From G3844 and a derivative of G3691; to sharpen alongside, that is, (figuratively) to exasperate: - easily provoke, stir.

G3948.full: From G3947 ("paroxysm"); incitement (to good), or dispute (in anger): - contention, provoke unto.

G3949.full: From G3844 and G3710; to anger alongside, that is, enrage: - anger, provoke to wrath.

G3951.full: From G3844 and ï̓ôñṍíù otrunō (to spur); to urge along, that is, stimulate (to hostility): - stir up.

G3952.full: From the present participle of G3918; a being near, that is, advent (often, return; specifically of Christ to punish Jerusalem, or finally the wicked); (by implication) physical aspect: - coming, presence.

G3953.full: From G3844 and the base of G3795; a side dish (the receptacle): - platter.

G3954.firstSense: bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly (-ness)
G3954.full: From G3956 and a derivative of G4483; all out spokenness, that is, frankness, bluntness, publicity; by implication assurance: - bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly (-ness).

G3955.full: Middle voice from G3954; to be frank in utterance, or confident in spirit and demeanor: - be (wax) bold, (preach, speak) boldly.

G3956.firstSense: all (manner of, means) alway (-s), any (one), X daily, + ever, every (one, way), as man…
G3956.full: pas pas Including all the forms of declension; apparently a primary word; all, any, every, the whole: - all (manner of, means) alway (-s), any (one), X daily, + ever, every (one, way), as many as, + no (-thing), X throughly, whatsoever, whole, whosoever.

G3957.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H6453]); the Passover (the meal, the day, the festival or the special sacrifices connected with it): - Easter, Passover.

G3958.full: Apparently a primary verb (the third form used only in certain tenses for it); to experience a sensation or impression (usually painful): - feel, passion, suffer, vex.

G3959.full: Probably of foreign origin; Patara, a place in Asia Minor: - Patara.

G3960.full: Probably a prolongation from G3817; to knock (gently or with a weapon or fatally): - smite, strike. Compare G5180.

G3961.full: From a derivative probably of G3817 (meaning a "path"); to trample (literally or figuratively): - tread (down, under foot).

G3962.full: Apparently a primary word; a "father" (literally or figuratively, near or more remote): - father, parent.

G3963.full: Of uncertain derivation; Patmus, an islet in the Mediterranean: - Patmos.

G3964.full: From G3962 and the same as the latter part of G3389; a parricide: - murderer of fathers.

G3965.full: As if feminine of a derivative of G3962; paternal descent, that is, (concretely) a group of families or a whole race (nation): - family, kindred, lineage.

G3966.full: From G3965 and G757; a progenitor ("patriarch"): - patriarch.

G3967.full: From G3962; paternal, that is, ancestral: - of fathers.

G3968.full: From G3962; a father land, that is, native town; (figuratively) heavenly home: - (own) country.

G3969.full: Perhaps a contraction for "patrobios" (a compound of G3962 and G979); father's life; Patrobas, a Christian: - Patrobas.

G3970.full: From G3962 and a derivative of G3860 (in the sense of handing over or down); traditionary: - received by tradition from fathers.

G3971.full: From G3962; paternal, that is, hereditary: - of fathers.

G3972.full: Of Latin origin; (little; but remotely from a derivative of G3973, meaning the same); Paulus, the name of a Roman and of an apostle: - Paul, Paulus.

G3973.full: A primn. verb ("pause"); to stop (transitive or intransitive), that is, restrain, quit, desist, come to an end: - cease, leave, refrain.

G3974.full: Of uncertain derivative; Paphus, a place in Cyprus: - Paphos.

G3975.full: From a derivative of G4078 (meaning thick); to thicken, that is, (by implication) to fatten (figuratively stupefy or render callous): - wax gross.

G3976.full: Ultimately from G4228; a shackle for the feet: - fetter.

G3977.full: From a derivative of G4228 (meaning the ground); level (as easy for the feet): - plain.

G3978.full: From the same as G3979; to foot a journey, that is, travel by land: - go afoot.

G3979.full: Dative feminine of a derivative of G4228 (as adverb); foot wise, that is, by walking: - a- (on) foot.

G3980.full: From a compound of G3982 and G757; to be persuaded by a ruler, that is, (generally) to submit to authority; by analogy to conform to advice: - hearken, obey (magistrates).

G3982.firstSense: agree, assure, believe, have confidence, be (wax) content, make friend, obey, persuade,…
G3982.full: A primary verb; to convince (by argument, true or false); by analogy to pacify or conciliate (by other fair means); reflexively or passively to assent (to evidence or authority), to rely (by inward certainty): - agree, assure, believe, have confidence, be (wax) content, make friend, obey, persuade, trust, yield.

G3983.full: From the same as G3993 (through the idea of pinching toil; "pine"); to famish (absolutely or comparatively); figuratively to crave: - be an hungered.

G3984.full: From the base of G4008 (through the idea of piercing); a test, that is, attempt, experience: - assaying, trial.

G3985.firstSense: assay, examine, go about, prove, tempt (-er), try
G3985.full: From G3984; to test (objectively), that is, endeavor, scrutinize, entice, discipline: - assay, examine, go about, prove, tempt (-er), try.

G3986.full: From G3985; a putting to proof (by experiment [of good], experience [of evil], solicitation, discipline or provocation); by implication adversity: - temptation, X try.

G3987.full: From G3984; to test (subjectively), that is, (reflexively) to attempt: - assay.

G3988.full: From a presumed derivative of G3982; persuadableness, that is, credulity: - persuasion.

G3989.full: Of uncertain affinity; deep or open sea, that is, the main: - depth, sea.

G3990.full: From a derivative of G4141 (meaning an axe); to chop off (the head), that is, truncate: - behead.

G3992.full: Apparently a primary verb; to dispatch (from the subjective view or point of departure, whereas é̔́çìé hiēmi [as a stronger form of åé̓͂ìé eimi] refers rather to the objective point or terminus ad quem, and G4724 denotes properly the orderly motion involved), especially on a temporary errand; also to transmit, bestow, or wield: - send, thrust in.

G3993.full: From a primary "peno" (to toil for daily subsistence); starving, that is, indigent: - poor. Compare G4434.

G3994.full: Feminine of G3995; a wife's mother: - mother in law, wife's mother.

G3995.full: Of uncertain affinity; a wife's father: - father in law.

G3996.full: From G3997; to grieve (the feeling or the act): - mourn, (be-) wail.

G3997.full: Strengthened from the alternate of G3958; grief: - mourning, sorrow.

G3998.full: Prolonged from the base of G3993; necessitous: - poor.

G3999.full: Multiplicative adverb from G4002; five times: - five times.

G4000.full: From G3999 and G5507; five times a thousand: - five thousand.

G4001.full: From G4002 and G1540; five hundred: - five hundred.

G4003.full: From G4002 and G2532 and G1182; five and tenth: - fifteenth.

G4005.full: Feminine of G4004; fiftieth (G2250 being implied) from Passover, that is, the festival of "pentecost": - Pentecost.

G4006.full: From the perfect of the alternate of G3958; reliance: - confidence, trust.

G4007.full: per per From the base of G4008; an enclitic particle significant of abundance (thoroughness), that is, emphasis; much, very or ever: - [whom-] soever.

G4008.full: Apparently the accusative case of an obsolete derivation of ðåé́ñù peirō (to "peirce"); through (as adverb or preposition), that is, across: - beyond, farther (other) side, over.

G4009.full: From the same as G4008; an extremity: - end, ut- (ter-) most part.

G4010.full: From G4444; fortified; Pergamus, a place in Asia Minor: - Pergamos.

G4011.full: Probably from the same as G4010; a tower; Perga, a place in Asia Minor: - Perga.

G4012.firstSense: (there-) about, above, against, at, on behalf of, X and his company, which concern, (as…
G4012.full: From the base of G4008; properly through (all over), that is, around; figuratively with respect to; used in various applications, of place, cause or time (with the genitive case denoting the subject or occasion or superlative point; with the accusative case the locality, circuit, matter, circumstance or general period): - (there-) about, above, against, at, on behalf of, X and his company, which concern, (as) concerning, for, X how it will go with, ([there-, where-]) of, on, over, pertaining (to), for sake, X (e-) state, (as) touching, [where-] by (in), with. In compounds it retains substantially the same meaning of circuit (around), excess (beyond), or completeness (through).

G4013.full: From G4012 and G71; to take around (as a companion); reflexively to walk around: - compass, go (round) about, lead about.

G4014.full: From G4012 and G138 (including its alternate); to remove all around, that is, unveil, cast off (anchor); figuratively to expiate: - take away (up).

G4015.full: From G4012 and G797; to flash all around, that is, envelop in light: - shine round (about).

G4016.firstSense: array, cast about, clothe (-d me), put on
G4016.full: From G4012 and G906; to throw all around, that is, invest (with a palisade or with clothing): - array, cast about, clothe (-d me), put on.

G4017.full: From G4012 and G991; to look all around: - look (round) about (on).

G4018.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4016; something thrown around one, that is, a mantle, veil: - covering, vesture.

G4019.full: From G4012 and G1210; to bind around one, that is, enwrap: - bind about.

G4020.full: From G4012 and G2038; to work all around, that is, bustle about (meddle): - be a busybody.

G4021.full: From G4012 and G2041; working all around, that is, officious (meddlesome, neuter plural magic): - busybody, curious arts.

G4022.firstSense: fetch a compass, vagabond, wandering about
G4022.full: From G4012 and G2064 (including its alternate); to come all around, that is, stroll, vacillate, veer: - fetch a compass, vagabond, wandering about.

G4023.full: From G4012 and G2192; to hold all around, that is, include, clasp (figuratively): - + astonished, contain, after [this manner].

G4024.full: From G4012 and G2224; to gird all around, that is, (middle or passive voice) to fasten on one's belt (literally or figuratively): - gird (about, self).

G4025.full: From G4060; a putting all around, that is, decorating oneself with: - wearing.

G4026.full: From G4012 and G2476; to stand all around, that is, (near) to be a bystander, or (aloof) to keep away from: - avoid, shun, stand by (round about).

G4027.full: From a compound of G4012 and G2508; something cleaned off all around, that is, refuse (figuratively): - filth.

G4028.full: From G4012 and G2572; to cover all around, that is, entirely (the face, a surface): - blindfold, cover, overlay.

G4029.full: From G4012 and G2749; to lie all around, that is, inclose, encircle, hamper (literally or figuratively): - be bound (compassed) with, hang about.

G4030.full: Feminine of a compound of G4012 and G2776; encirclement of the head, that is, a helmet: - helmet.

G4031.full: From G4012 and G2904; strong all around, that is, a master (manager): - + come by.

G4032.full: From G4012 and G2928; to conceal all around, that is, entirely: - hide.

G4033.full: From G4012 and G2944; to encircle all around, that is, blockade completely: - compass round.

G4034.full: From G4012 and G2989; to illuminate all around, that is, invest with a halo: - shine round about.

G4035.full: From G4012 and G3007; to leave all around, that is, (passively) survive: - remain.

G4036.full: From G4012 and G3077; grieved all around, that is, intensely sad: - exceeding (very) sorry (-owful).

G4037.full: From G4012 and G3306; to stay around, that is, await: - wait for.

G4038.full: Adverb from G4012; all around, that is, (as adjective) circumjacent: - round about.

G4039.full: From G4012 and G3611; to reside around, that is, be a neighbor: - dwell round about.

G4040.full: From G4012 and G3624; housed around, that is, neighboring (elliptically as noun): - neighbour.

G4041.full: From the present participle feminine of a compound of G4012 and G1510; being beyond usual, that is, special (one's own): - peculiar.

G4042.full: From G4023; a being held around, that is, (concretely) a passage (of Scripture, as circumscribed): - place.

G4043.full: From G4012 and G3961; to tread all around, that is, walk at large (especially as proof of ability); figuratively to live, deport oneself, follow (as a companion or votary): - go, be occupied with, walk (about).

G4044.full: From G4012 and the base of G4008; to penetrate entirely, that is, transfix (figuratively): - pierce through.

G4045.full: From G4012 and G4098; to fall into something that is all around, that is, light among or upon, be surrounded with: - fall among (into).

G4046.full: Middle voice from G4012 and G4160; to make around oneself, that is, acquire (buy): - purchase.

G4047.full: From G4046; acquisition (the act or the thing); by extension preservation: - obtain (-ing), peculiar, purchased, possession, saving.

G4048.full: From G4012 and G4486; to tear all around, that is, completely away: - rend off.

G4049.full: From G4012 and G4685; to drag all around, that is, (figuratively) to distract (with care): - cumber.

G4050.full: From G4052; surplusage, that is, superabundance: - abundance (-ant, [-ly]), superfluity.

G4051.firstSense: abundance, that was left, over and above
G4051.full: From G4052; a surplus, or superabundance: - abundance, that was left, over and above.

G4052.firstSense: (make, more) abound, (have, have more) abundance, (be more) abundant, be the better, en…
G4052.full: From G4053; to superabound (in quantity or quality), be in excess, be superfluous; also (transitively) to cause to superabound or excel: - (make, more) abound, (have, have more) abundance, (be more) abundant, be the better, enough and to spare, exceed, excel, increase, be left, redound, remain (over and above).

G4053.firstSense: exceeding abundantly above, more abundantly, advantage, exceedingly, very highly, beyon…
G4053.full: From G4012 (in the sense of beyond); superabundant (in quantity) or superior (in quality); by implication excessive; adverb (with G1537) violently; neuter (as noun) preeminence: - exceeding abundantly above, more abundantly, advantage, exceedingly, very highly, beyond measure, more, superfluous, vehement [-ly].

G4054.firstSense: more abundantly, a great deal, far more
G4054.full: Neuter of G4055 (as adverb); in a more superabundant way: - more abundantly, a great deal, far more.

G4055.full: Comparative of G4053; more superabundant (in number, degree or character): - more abundant, greater (much) more, overmuch.

G4056.firstSense: more abundant (-ly), X the more earnest, (more) exceedingly, more frequent, much more,…
G4056.full: Adverb from G4055; more superabundantly: - more abundant (-ly), X the more earnest, (more) exceedingly, more frequent, much more, the rather.

G4057.firstSense: exceedingly, out of measure, the more
G4057.full: Adverb from G4053; superabundantly: - exceedingly, out of measure, the more.

G4058.full: Of uncertain derivation; a pigeon: - dove, pigeon.

G4059.full: From G4012 and the base of G5114; to cut around, that is, (specifically) to circumcise: - circumcise.

G4060.firstSense: bestow upon, hedge round about, put about (on, upon), set about
G4060.full: From G4012 and G5087; to place around; by implication to present: - bestow upon, hedge round about, put about (on, upon), set about.

G4061.full: From G4059; circumcision (the rite, the condition or the people, literally or figuratively): - X circumcised, circumcision.

G4062.full: From G4012 and the base of G5157; to turn around, that is, (mentally) to craze: - + make mad.

G4063.full: From G4012 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run around, that is, traverse: - run through.

G4064.full: From G4012 and G5342; to convey around, that is, transport hither and thither: - bear (carry) about.

G4065.full: From G4012 and G5426; to think beyond, that is, depreciate (contemn): - despise.

G4066.firstSense: country (round) about, region (that lieth) round about
G4066.full: From G4012 and G5561; around the region, that is, circumjacent (as noun, with G1093 implied, vicinity): - country (round) about, region (that lieth) round about.

G4067.full: From a compound of G4012 and "psao" (to rub); something brushed all around, that is, off scrapings (figuratively scum): - offscouring.

G4068.full: Middle voice from ðǻñðåñïò perperos (braggart; perhaps by reduplication of the base of G4008); to boast: - vaunt itself.

G4069.full: A Persian woman; Persis, a Christian female: - Persis.

G4070.full: Adverb from G4009; the by gone, that is, (as noun) last year: - + a year ago.

G4071.full: Neuter of a derivative of G4072; a flying animal, that is, bird: - bird, fowl.

G4072.full: Including the prolonged form (second form) and contraction (third form) of the middle voice of a primary verb; to fly: - fly (-ing).

G4073.full: Feminine of the same as G4074; a (mass of) rock (literally or figuratively): - rock.

G4074.full: Apparently a primary word; a (piece of) rock (larger than G3037); as a name, Petrus, an apostle: - Peter, rock. Compare G2786.

G4075.full: From G4073 and G1491; rock like, that is, rocky: - stony.

G4076.full: From G4078; rue (from its thick or fleshy leaves): - rue.

G4077.full: Probably from G4078 (through the idea of gushing plumply); a fount (literally or figuratively), that is, source or supply (of water, blood, enjoyment), (not necessarily the original spring): - fountain, well.

G4078.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which in its simpler form occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to fix ("peg"), that is, (specifically) to set up (a tent): - pitch.

G4079.full: Neuter of a (presumed) derivative of ðçäḯí pēdon (the blade of an oar; from the same as G3976); a "pedal", that is, helm: - rudder.

G4080.full: A quantitative form (the feminine) of the base of G4225; how much (as indefinite), that is, in size or (figuratively) dignity: - how great (large).

G4081.full: Perhaps a primary word; clay: - clay.

G4082.full: Of uncertain affinity; a wallet or leather pouch for food: - scrip.

G4083.full: Of uncertain affinity; the fore arm, that is, (as a measure) a cubit: - cubit.

G4084.firstSense: apprehend, catch, lay hand on, take
G4084.full: Probably another form of G971; to squeeze, that is, seize (gently by the hand [press], or officially [arrest], or in hunting [capture]): - apprehend, catch, lay hand on, take. Compare G4085.

G4085.full: Another form for G4084; to pack: - press down.

G4086.full: From a compound of a derivative of G3982 and G3056; persuasive language: - enticing words.

G4087.full: From G4089; to embitter (literally or figuratively): - be (make) bitter.

G4088.full: From G4089; acridity (especially poison), literally or figuratively: - bitterness.

G4089.full: Perhaps from G4078 (through the idea of piercing); sharp (pungent), that is, acrid (literally or figuratively): - bitter.

G4090.full: Adverb from G4089; bitterly, that is, (figuratively) violently: - bitterly.

G4091.full: Of Latin origin; close pressed, that is, firm; Pilatus, a Roman: - Pilate.

G4092.full: A reduplicated and prolonged form of a primary word, ðñǻù preō, (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to fire, that is, burn (figuratively and passively become inflamed with fever): - be (X should have) swollen.

G4093.full: Diminutive of G4094; a tablet (for writing on): - writing table.

G4094.full: Apparently a form of G4109; a plate: - charger, platter.

G4095.full: The first is a prolonged form of the second, which (together with the third form) occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses; to imbibe (literally or figuratively): - drink.

G4096.full: From ðé́ùí piōn (fat; perhaps akin to the alternate of G4095 through the idea of repletion); plumpness, that is, (by implication) richness (oiliness): - fatness.

G4097.full: The first is a reduplicated and prolonged form of the second (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); contracted from ðåñá́ù peraō (to traverse; from the base of G4008); to traffic (by travelling), that is, dispose of as merchandise or into slavery (literally or figuratively): - sell.

G4098.full: The first is a reduplicated and contracted form of the second (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); probably akin to G4072 through the idea of alighting; to fall (literally of figuratively): - fail, fall (down), light on.

G4099.full: Probably of foreign origin; Pisidia, a region of Asia Minor: - Pisidia.

G4100.firstSense: believe (-r), commit (to trust), put in trust with
G4100.full: From G4102; to have faith (in, upon, or with respect to, a person or thing), that is, credit; by implication to entrust (especially one's spiritual well being to Christ): - believe (-r), commit (to trust), put in trust with.

G4101.full: From G4102; trustworthy, that is, genuine (unadulterated): - spike-[nard].

G4102.full: From G3982; persuasion, that is, credence; moral conviction (of religious truth, or the truthfulness of God or a religious teacher), especially reliance upon Christ for salvation; abstractly constancy in such profession; by extension the system of religious (Gospel) truth itself: - assurance, belief, believe, faith, fidelity.

G4103.full: From G3982; objectively trustworthy; subjectively trustful: - believe (-ing, -r), faithful (-ly), sure, true.

G4104.full: From G4103; to assure: - assure of.

G4105.firstSense: go astray, deceive, err, seduce, wander, be out of the way
G4105.full: From G4106; to (properly cause to) roam (from safety, truth, or virtue): - go astray, deceive, err, seduce, wander, be out of the way.

G4106.full: Feminine of G4108 (as abstraction); objectively fraudulence; subjectively a straying from orthodoxy or piety: - deceit, to deceive, delusion, error.

G4107.full: From G4108; a rover ("planet"), that is, (figuratively) an erratic teacher: - wandering.

G4108.full: Of uncertain affinity; roving (as a tramp), that is, (by implication) an impostor or misleader: - deceiver, seducing.

G4109.full: plax plax From G4111; a moulding board, that is, flat surface ("plate", or tablet, literally or figuratively): - table.

G4110.full: From G4111; something moulded: - thing formed.

G4111.full: A primary verb; to mould, that is, shape or fabricate: - form.

G4112.full: From G4111; moulded, that is, (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false): - feigned.

G4113.full: Feminine of G4116; a wide "plat" or "place", that is, open square: - street.

G4115.full: From G4116; to widen (literally or figuratively): - make broad, enlarge.

G4116.full: From G4111; spread out "flat" ("plot"), that is, broad: - wide.

G4117.full: From G4120; a plait (of hair): - broidered hair.

G4118.full: Irregular superlative of G4183; the largest number or very large: - very great, most.

G4119.firstSense: X above, + exceed, more excellent, further, (very) great (-er), long (-er), (very) many…
G4119.full: Comparative of G4183; more in quantity, number, or quality; also (in plural) the major portion: - X above, + exceed, more excellent, further, (very) great (-er), long (-er), (very) many, greater (more) part, + yet but.

G4120.full: A primary word; to twine or braid: - plait.

G4121.firstSense: abound, abundant, make to increase, have over
G4121.full: From G4119; to do, make or be more, that is, increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension to superabound: - abound, abundant, make to increase, have over.

G4122.firstSense: get an advantage, defraud, make a gain
G4122.full: From G4123; to be covetous, that is, (by implication) to over reach: - get an advantage, defraud, make a gain.

G4123.full: From G4119 and G2192; holding (desiring) more, that is, eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder): - covetous.

G4124.full: From G4123; avarice, that is, (by implication) fraudulency, extortion: - covetous (-ness) practices, greediness.

G4125.full: Of uncertain affinity; a rib, that is, (by extension) side: - side.

G4126.full: The first is another form for the second which is used as an alternate in certain tenses; probably a form of G4150 (through the idea of plunging through the water); to pass in a vessel: - sail. See also G4130.

G4127.full: From G4141; a stroke; by implication a wound; figuratively a calamity: - plague, stripe, wound (-ed).

G4128.full: From G4130; a fulness, that is, a large number, throng, populace: - bundle, company, multitude.

G4129.full: From another form of G4128; to increase (transitively or intransitively): - abound, multiply.

G4130.full: A prolonged form of a primary word ðëǻù pleō (which appears only as an alternate in certain tenses and in the reduplicated form of ðé́ìðëçìé pimplēmi to "fill" (literally or figuratively [imbue, influence, supply]); specifically to fulfil (time): - accomplish, full (. . . come), furnish.

G4131.full: From G4141; a smiter, that is, pugnacious (quarrelsome): - striker.

G4132.full: Prolongation from G4130; flood tide, that is, (by analogy) a freshet: - flood.

G4133.firstSense: but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than
G4133.full: plēn plane From G4119; moreover (besides), that is, albeit, save that, rather, yet: - but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than.
