G4134.full: From G4130; replete, or covered over; by analogy complete: - full.

G4135.firstSense: most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of
G4135.full: From G4134 and G5409; to carry out fully (in evidence), that is, completely assure (or convince), entirely accomplish: - most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of.

G4137.firstSense: accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, make) full (co…
G4137.full: From G4134; to make replete, that is, (literally) to cram (a net), level up (a hollow), or (figuratively) to furnish (or imbue, diffuse, influence), satisfy, execute (an office), finish (a period or task), verify (or coincide with a prediction), etc.: - accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, make) full (come), fully preach, perfect, supply.

G4138.firstSense: which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness
G4138.full: From G4137; repletion or completion, that is, (subjectively) what fills (as contents, supplement, copiousness, multitude), or (objectively) what is filled (as container, performance, period): - which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness.

G4139.full: Neuter of a derivative of ðǻëáò pelas (near); (adverb) close by; as noun, a neighbor, that is, fellow (as man, countryman, Christian or friend): - near, neighbour.

G4140.full: From a presumed derivative of G4130; a filling up, that is, (figuratively) gratification: - satisfying.

G4141.full: Apparently another form of G4111 (through the idea of flattening out); to pound, that is, (figuratively) to inflict with (calamity): - smite. Compare G5180.

G4142.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4143; a boat: - boat, little (small) ship.

G4143.full: From G4126; a sailer, that is, vessel: - ship (-ping).

G4144.full: From G4126; a sail, that is, navigation: - course, sailing, voyage.

G4145.full: From G4149; wealthy; figuratively abounding with: - rich.

G4147.firstSense: be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich
G4147.full: From G4148; to be (or become) wealthy (literally or figuratively): - be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich.

G4148.full: From G4149; to make wealthy (figuratively): - en- (make) rich.

G4149.full: From the base of G4130; wealth (as fulness), that is, (literally) money, possessions, or (figuratively) abundance, richness, (specifically) valuable bestowment: - riches.

G4150.full: A prolonged form of an obsolete ðëṍù pluō ploo'-o (to "flow"); to "plunge", that is, launder clothing: - wash. Compare G3068, G3538.

G4151.full: From G4154; a current of air, that is, breath (blast) or a breeze; by analogy or figuratively a spirit, that is, (human) the rational soul, (by implication) vital principle, mental disposition, etc., or (superhuman) an angel, daemon, or (divine) God, Christ's spirit, the Holy spirit: - ghost, life, spirit (-ual, -ually), mind. Compare G5590.

G4152.full: From G4151; non-carnal, that is, (humanly) ethereal (as opposed to gross), or (daemoniacally) a spirit (concretely), or (divinely) supernatural, regenerate, religious: - spiritual. Compare G5591.

G4153.full: Adverb from G4152; non-physically, that is, divinely, figuratively: - spiritually.

G4154.full: A primary word; to breathe hard, that is, breeze: - blow. Compare G5594.

G4155.full: Strengthened from G4154; to wheeze, that is, (causative by implication) to throttle or strangle (drown): - choke, take by the throat.

G4156.full: From G4155; throttled, that is, (neuter concretely) an animal choked to death (not bled): - strangled.

G4157.full: From G4154; respiration, a breeze: - breath, wind.

G4158.full: From G4228 and another element of uncertain affinity; a dress (G2066 implied) reaching the ankles: - garment down to the foot.

G4159.full: From the base of G4213 with enclitic adverb of origin; from which (as interrogitive) or what (as relative) place, state, source or cause: - whence.

G4160.firstSense: abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth),…
G4160.full: Apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary; to make or do (in a very wide application, more or less direct): - abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth), cast out, cause, commit, + content, continue, deal, + without any delay, (would) do (-ing), execute, exercise, fulfil, gain, give, have, hold, X journeying, keep, + lay wait, + lighten the ship, make, X mean, + none of these things move me, observe, ordain, perform, provide, + have purged, purpose, put, + raising up, X secure, shew, X shoot out, spend, take, tarry, + transgress the law, work, yield. Compare G4238.

G4161.full: From G4160; a product, that is, fabric (literally or figuratively): - thing that is made, workmanship.

G4162.full: From G4160; action, that is, performance (of the law): - deed.

G4163.full: From G4160; a performer; specifically a "poet": - doer, poet.

G4164.full: Of uncertain derivation; motley, that is, various in character: - divers, manifold.

G4165.full: From G4166; to tend as a shepherd (or figuratively superviser): - feed (cattle), rule.

G4166.full: Of uncertain affinity; a shepherd (literally or figuratively): - shepherd, pastor.

G4167.full: Contracted from G4165; a flock (literally or figuratively): - flock, fold.

G4168.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4167; a flock, that is, (figuratively) group (of believers): - flock.

G4169.full: From the base of G4226 and G3634; individualizing interrogitive (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one: - what (manner of), which.

G4170.full: From G4171; to be (engaged) in warfare, that is, to battle (literally or figuratively): - fight, (make) war.

G4171.full: From ðǻëïìáé pelomai (to bustle); warfare (literally or figuratively; a single encounter or a series): - battle, fight, war.

G4172.full: Probably from the same as G4171, or perhaps from G4183; a town (properly with walls, of greater or less size): - city.

G4173.full: From G4172 and G757; a town officer, that is, magistrate: - ruler of the city.

G4174.full: From G4177 ("polity"); citizenship; concretely a community: - commonwealth, freedom.

G4175.full: From G4176; a community, that is, (abstractly) citizenship (figuratively): - conversation.

G4176.full: Middle voice of a derivative of G4177; to behave as a citizen (figuratively): - let conversation be, live.

G4178.full: Multiplicative adverb from G4183; many times, that is, frequently: - oft (-en, -en-times, -times).

G4179.full: From G4183 and probably a derivative of G4120; manifold, that is, (neuter as noun) very much more: - manifold more.

G4180.full: From a compound of G4183 and G3056; loquacity, that is, prolixity: - much speaking.

G4181.full: Adverb from a compound of G4183 and G3313; in many portions, that is, variously as to time and agency (piecemeal): - at sundry times.

G4182.full: From G4183 and G4164; much variegated, that is, multifarious: - manifold.

G4183.firstSense: abundant, + altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age, deal, -l…
G4183.full: Including the forms from the alternate "pollos"; (singular) much (in any respect) or (plural) many; neuter (singular) as adverb largely; neuter (plural) as adverb or noun often, mostly, largely: - abundant, + altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age, deal, -ly, while), long, many, much, oft (-en [-times]), plenteous, sore, straitly. Compare G4118, G4119.

G4184.full: From G4183 and G4698 (figuratively), extremely compassionate: - very pitiful.

G4185.firstSense: costly, very precious, of great price
G4185.full: From G4183 and G5056; extremely expensive: - costly, very precious, of great price.

G4186.full: From G4183 and G5092; extremely valuable: - very costly, of great price.

G4187.full: Adverb from a compound of G4183 and G5158; in many ways, that is, variously as to method or form: - in divers manners.

G4188.full: From the alternate of G4095; a beverage: - drink.

G4189.full: From G4190; depravity, that is, (specifically) malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins: - iniquity, wickedness.

G4190.firstSense: bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked (-ness)
G4190.full: From a derivative of G4192; hurtful, that is, evil (properly in effect or influence, and thus differing from G2556, which refers rather to essential character, as well as from G4550, which indicates degeneracy from original virtue); figuratively calamitous; also (passively) ill, that is, diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, that is, derelict, vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural) guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners: - bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked (-ness). See also G4191.

G4191.full: Comparative of G4190; more evil: - more wicked.

G4192.full: From the base of G3993; toil, that is, (by implication) anguish: - pain.

G4193.full: From G4195; a Pontican, that is, native of Pontus: - born in Pontus.

G4194.full: Of Latin origin; apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman: - Pontius.

G4195.full: A sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor: - Pontus.

G4196.full: Of Latin origin; apparently "popular"; Poplius (that is, Publius), a Roman: - Publius.

G4197.full: From G4198; travel (by land); figuratively (plural) proceedings, that is, career: - journey [-ing], ways.

G4198.firstSense: depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a, take a) journey, walk
G4198.full: Middle voice from a derivative of the same as G3984; to traverse, that is, travel (literally or figuratively; especially to remove [figuratively die], live, etc.): - depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a, take a) journey, walk.

G4199.full: Prolonged version of ðǻñèù porthō (to sack); to ravage (figuratively): - destroy, waste.

G4200.full: From a derivative of ðḯñïò poros (a way, that is, means); furnishing (procuring), that is, (by implication) money getting (acquisition): - gain.

G4201.full: Of Latin origin; apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman: - Porcius.

G4202.full: From G4203; harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively idolatry: - fornication.

G4203.full: From G4204; to act the harlot, that is, (literally) indulge unlawful lust (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry: - commit (fornication).

G4204.full: Feminine of G4205; a strumpet; figuratively an idolater: - harlot, whore.

G4205.full: From ðǻñíçìé pernēmi (to sell; akin to the base of G4097); a (male) prostitute (as venal), that is, (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine): - fornicator, whoremonger.

G4206.full: Adverb from G4253; forwards, that is, at a distance: - far, a great way off. See also G4207.

G4207.full: From G4206 with adverbial enclitic of source; from far, or (by implication) at a distance, that is, distantly: - afar off.

G4208.full: Adverb comparative of G4206; farther, that is, a greater distance: - further.

G4209.full: Of Latin origin; the "purple" mussel, that is, (by implication) the red blue color itself, and finally, a garment dyed with it: - purple.

G4210.full: From G4209; purpureal, that is, bluish red: - purple.

G4211.full: Feminine of a compound of G4209 and G4453; a female trader in purple cloth: - seller of purple.

G4212.full: Multiplicative from G4214; how many times: - how oft (-en).

G4213.full: From the alternate of G4095; a drinking (the act), that is, (concretely) a draught: - drink.

G4214.full: From an obsolete "pos" (who, what) and G3739; interrogitive pronoun (of amount) how much (large, long or [plural] many): - how great (long, many), what.

G4215.full: Probably from a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (compare G4224); a current, brook or freshet (as drinkable), that is, running water: - flood, river, stream, water.

G4216.full: From G4215 and a derivative of G5409; river borne, that is, overwhelmed by a stream: - carried away of the flood.

G4217.full: Apparently from G4219 and the base of G4226; interrogitive whatever, that is, of what possible sort: - what (manner of).

G4218.firstSense: afore- (any, some-) time (-s), at length (the last), (+ n-) ever, in the old time, in t…
G4218.full: From the base of G4225 and G5037; indefinite adverb, at some time, ever: - afore- (any, some-) time (-s), at length (the last), (+ n-) ever, in the old time, in time past, once, when.

G4219.full: From the base of G4226 and G5037; interrogitive adverb, at what time: - + how long, when.

G4220.full: Neuter of a comparative of the base of G4226; interrogitive as adverb, which (of two), that is, is it this or that: - whether.

G4221.full: Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4095; a drinking vessel; by extension the contents thereof, that is, a cupful (draught); figuratively a lot or fate: - cup.

G4222.full: From a derivative of the alternate of G4095; to furnish drink, irrigate: - give (make) to drink, feed, water.

G4223.full: Of Latin origin; little wells, that is, mineral springs; Potioli (that is, Puteoli), a place in Italy: - Puteoli.

G4224.full: From the alternate of G4095; a drinking bout or carousal: - banqueting.

G4225.full: pou poo Genitive case of ðḯò pos, an indefinite pronoun (some) otherwise obsolete (compare G4214); as adverb of place, somewhere, that is, nearly: - about, a certain place.

G4226.full: pou poo Genitive case of ðḯò pos, an interrogitive pronoun, (what) otherwise obsolete (perhaps the same as G4225 used with the rising slide of inquiry); as adverb of place; at (by implication to) what locality: - where, whither.

G4227.full: Of Latin origin; modest; Pudes (that is, Pudens), a Christian: - Pudens.

G4228.full: pous pooce A primary word; a "foot" (figuratively or literally): - foot (-stool).

G4229.full: From G4238; a deed; by implication an affair; by extension an object (material): - business, matter, thing, work.

G4230.full: From G4231; a transaction, that is, negotiation: - affair.

G4231.full: From G4229; to busy oneself with, that is, to trade: - occupy.

G4232.full: Of Latin origin; the praetorium or governor's court room (sometimes including the whole edifice and camp): - (common, judgment) hall (of judgment), palace, praetorium.

G4233.full: From a derivative of G4238; a practiser, that is, (specifically) an official collector: - officer.

G4234.full: From G4238; practice, that is, (concretely) an act; by extension a function: - deed, office, work.

G4235.full: A form of G4239, used in certain parts; gentle, that is, humble: - meek.

G4236.full: From G4235; gentleness; by implication humility: - meekness.

G4237.full: Perhaps from ðñá́óïí prason (a leek, and so an onion patch); a garden plot, that is, (by implication of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism to indicate an arrangement): - in ranks.

G4238.firstSense: commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts
G4238.full: A primary verb; to "practise", that is, perform repeatedly or habitually (thus differing from G4160, which properly refers to a single act); by implication to execute, accomplish, etc.; specifically to collect (dues), fare (personally): - commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts.

G4239.full: Apparently a primary word; mild, that is, (by implication) humble: - meek. See also G4235.

G4240.full: From G4239; mildness, that is, (by implication) humility: - meekness.

G4241.full: Apparently a primary verb; to tower up (be conspicuous), that is, (by implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right): - become, comely.

G4242.full: From G4243; seniority (eldership), that is, (by implication) an embassy (concretely ambassadors): - ambassage, message.

G4243.full: From the base of G4245; to be a senior, that is, (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively preacher): - be an ambassador.

G4244.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4245; the order of elders, that is, (specifically) Israelite Sanhedrim or Christian "presbytery": - (estate of) elder (-s), presbytery.

G4245.full: Comparative of ðñǻóâõò presbus (elderly); older; as noun, a senior; specifically an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter": - elder (-est), old.

G4246.full: From the same as G4245; an old man: - aged (man), old man.

G4247.full: Feminine of G4246; an old woman: - aged woman.

G4248.full: From G4253; leaning (falling) forward ("prone"), that is, head foremost: - headlong.

G4249.full: A strengthened form of a primary word ðñé́ù priō, (to saw); to saw in two: - saw asunder.

G4250.full: prin prin Adverb from G4253; prior, sooner: - before (that), ere.

G4251.full: Of Latin origin; feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman: - Prisca. See also G4252.

G4252.full: Diminutive of G4251; Priscilla (that is, little Prisca), a Christian woman: - Priscilla.

G4253.full: pro pro A primary preposition; "fore", that is, in front of, prior (figuratively superior) to. In compounds it retains the same significations: - above, ago, before, or ever. In compounds it retains the same significations.

G4254.full: From G4253 and G71; to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively to precede (in place or time [participle previous]): - bring (forth, out), go before.

G4255.full: From G4253 and G138; to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), that is, (by implication) to propose (intend): - purpose.

G4256.full: From G4253 and a derivative of G156; to accuse already, that is, previously charge: - prove before.

G4257.full: From G4253 and G191; to hear already, that is, anticipate: - hear before.

G4258.full: From G4253 and G264; to sin previously (to conversion): - sin already, heretofore sin.

G4259.full: Neuter of a presumed compound of G4253 and G833; a fore-court, that is, vestibule (alley way): - porch.

G4260.firstSense: + be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken
G4260.full: From G4253 and the base of G939; to walk forward, that is, advance (literally or in years): - + be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken.

G4261.full: From G4253 and G906; to throw forward, that is, push to the front, germinate: - put forward, shoot forth.

G4262.full: From G4263; relating to sheep, that is, (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem: - sheep (market).

G4263.full: Properly the neuter of a presumed derivative of G4260; something that walks forward (a quadruped), that is, (specifically) a sheep (literally or figuratively): - sheep ([-fold]).

G4264.full: From G4253 and a reduplicated form of G971; to force forward, that is, bring to the front, instigate: - draw, before instruct.

G4265.full: From G4253 and G991; to look out beforehand, that is, furnish in advance: - provide.

G4266.full: From G4253 and G1096; to be already, that is, have previously transpired: - be past.

G4267.full: From G4253 and G1097; to know beforehand, that is, foresee: - foreknow (ordain), know (before).

G4269.full: From G4266; an ancestor, (grand-) parent: - forefather, parent.

G4270.firstSense: before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime)
G4270.full: From G4253 and G1125; to write previously; figuratively to announce, prescribe: - before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime).

G4271.full: From G4253 and G1212; plain before all men, that is, obvious: - evident, manifest (open) beforehand.

G4272.full: From G4253 and G1325; to give before the other party has given: - first give.

G4273.full: From G4272 (in the sense of giving forward into another's [the enemy's] hands); a surrender: - betrayer, traitor.

G4274.full: From the alternate of G4390; a runner ahead, that is, scout (figuratively precursor): - forerunner.

G4275.full: From G4253 and G1492; foresee: - foresee, saw before.

G4276.full: From G4253 and G1679; to hope in advance of other confirmation: - first trust.

G4277.full: From G4253 and G2036; to say already, to predict: - forewarn, say (speak, tell) before. Compare G4280.

G4278.full: From G4253 and G1728; to commence already: - begin (before).

G4279.full: Middle voice from G4253 and G1861; to promise of old: - promise before.

G4280.full: From G4253 and G2046; used as alternate of G4277; to say already, predict: - foretell, say (speak, tell) before.

G4281.firstSense: go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on
G4281.full: From G4253 and G2064 (including its alternate); to go onward, precede (in place or time): - go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on.

G4282.full: From G4253 and G2090; to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively): - ordain before, prepare afore.

G4283.full: Middle voice from G4253 and G2097; to announce glad news in advance: - preach before the gospel.

G4284.full: proechomai pro-ekh-om-ahee Middle voice from G4253 and G2192; to hold oneself before others, that is, (figuratively) to excel: - be better.

G4285.full: From G4253 and G2233; to lead the way for others, that is, show deference: - prefer.

G4286.full: From G4388; a setting forth, that is, (figuratively) proposal (intention); specifically the show bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God: - purpose, shew [-bread].

G4287.full: From G4253 and a derivative of G5087; fixed beforehand, that is, (feminine with G2250 implied) a designated day: - time appointed.

G4288.firstSense: forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind
G4288.full: From G4289; predisposition, that is, alacrity: - forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind.

G4289.full: From G4253 and G2372; forward in spirit, that is, predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity: - ready, willing.

G4290.full: Adverb from G4289; with alacrity: - willingly.

G4291.full: From G4253 and G2476; to stand before, that is, (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise: - maintain, be over, rule.

G4292.full: Middle voice from G4253 and G2564; to call forth to oneself (challenge), that is, (by implication) to irritate: - provoke.

G4293.full: From G4253 and G2605; to announce beforehand, that is, predict, promise: - foretell, have notice (shew) before.

G4294.full: From G4253 and G2675; to prepare in advance: - make up beforehand.

G4295.full: From G4253 and G2749; to lie before the view, that is, (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward): - be first, set before (forth).

G4296.full: From G4253 and G2784; to herald (that is, proclaim) in advance: - before (first) preach.

G4297.full: From G4298; progress, that is, advancement (subjectively or objectively): - furtherance, profit.

G4298.firstSense: increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax
G4298.full: From G4253 and G2875; to drive forward (as if by beating), that is, (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along): - increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax.

G4299.full: From a compound of G4253 and G2919; a prejudgment (prejudice), that is, prepossession: - prefer one before another.

G4300.full: From G4253 and G2964; to ratify previously: - confirm before.

G4301.full: From G4253 and G2983; to take in advance, that is, (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise: - come aforehand, overtake, take before.

G4302.full: From G4253 and G3004; to say beforehand, that is, predict, forewarn: - foretell, tell before.

G4303.full: From G4253 and G3143; to be a witness in advance, that is, predict: - testify beforehand.

G4304.full: From G4253 and G3191; to premeditate: - meditate before.

G4305.full: From G4253 and G3309; to care (anxiously) in advance: - take thought beforehand.

G4306.full: From G4253 and G3539; to consider in advance, that is, look out for beforehand (active voice by way of maintenance for others; middle voice by way of circumspection for oneself): - provide (for).

G4307.full: From G4306; forethought, that is, provident care or supply: - providence, provision.

G4308.full: From G4253 and G3708; to behold in advance, that is, (active voice) to notice (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own) view: - foresee, see before.

G4309.full: From G4253 and G3724; to limit in advance, that is, (figuratively) predetermine: - determine before, ordain, predestinate.

G4310.full: From G4253 and G3958; to undergo hardship previously: - suffer before.

G4311.firstSense: accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth
G4311.full: From G4253 and G3992; to send forward, that is, escort or aid in travel: - accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth.

G4312.full: From a compound of G4253 and G4098; falling forward, that is, headlong (figuratively precipitate): - heady, rash [-ly].

G4313.full: From G4253 and G4198; to precede (as guide or herald): - go before.

G4314.firstSense: about, according to, against, among, at, because of, before, between, ([where-]) by, fo…
G4314.full: pros pros A strengthened form of G4253; a preposition of direction; forward to, that is, toward (with the genitive case the side of, that is, pertaining to; with the dative case by the side of, that is, near to; usually with the accusative case the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the destination of the relation, that is, whither or for which it is predicated): - about, according to, against, among, at, because of, before, between, ([where-]) by, for, X at thy house, in, for intent, nigh unto, of, which pertain to, that, to (the end that), + together, to ([you]) -ward, unto, with (-in). In compounds it denotes essentially the same applications, namely, motion towards, accession to, or nearness at.

G4315.full: From G4253 and G4521; a fore sabbath, that is, the sabbath eve: - day before the sabbath. Compare G3904.

G4316.full: From G4314 and a derivative of G58 (meaning to harangue); to address, that is, salute by name: - call.

G4317.full: From G4314 and G71; to lead towards, that is, (transitively) to conduct near (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach: - bring, draw near,

G4319.full: From G4314 and G154; to ask repeatedly (importune), that is, solicit: - beg.

G4320.full: From G4314 and G305; to ascend farther, that is, be promoted (take an upper (more honorable) seat): - go up.

G4321.full: From G4314 and G355; to expend further: - spend.

G4322.full: From G4314 and G378; to fill up further, that is, furnish fully: - supply.

G4323.full: From G4314 and G394; to lay up in addition, that is, (middle voice and figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult: - in conference add, confer.

G4324.full: From G4314 and G546; to menace additionally: - threaten further.

G4325.full: From G4314 and G1159; to expend additionally: - spend more.

G4326.full: From G4314 and G1189; to require additionally, that is, want further: - need.

G4327.full: From G4314 and G1209; to admit (to intercourse, hospitality, credence or (figuratively) endurance); by implication to await (with confidence or patience): - accept, allow, look (wait) for, take.

G4328.firstSense: (be in) expect (-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for
G4328.full: From G4314 and äïêåṍù dokeuō (to watch); to anticipate (in thought, hope or fear); by implication to await: - (be in) expect (-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for.

G4329.full: From G4328; apprehension (of evil); by implication infliction anticipated: - expectation, looking after.

G4330.full: From G4314 and G1439; to permit further progress: - suffer.

G4331.full: From G4314 and G1448; to approach near: - come nigh.

G4332.full: From a compound of G4314 and the base of G1476; to sit near, that is, attend as a servant: - wait at.

G4333.full: From G4314 and G2038; to work additionally, that is, (by implication) acquire besides: - gain.

G4334.firstSense: (as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto)
G4334.full: From G4314 and G2064 (including its alternate); to approach, that is, (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent to: - (as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto).

G4335.full: From G4336; prayer (worship); by implication an oratory (chapel): - X pray earnestly, prayer.

G4336.full: From G4314 and G2172; to pray to God, that is, supplicate, worship: - pray (X earnestly, for), make prayer.

G4337.firstSense: (give) attend (-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed…
G4337.full: From G4314 and G2192; (figuratively) to hold the mind (G3563 implied) towards, that is, pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to: - (give) attend (-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed (to, unto) have regard.

G4338.full: From G4314 and a derivative of G2247; to peg to, that is, spike fast: - nail to.

G4339.full: From the alternate of G4334; an arriver from a foreign region, that is, (specifically) an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte"): - proselyte.

G4340.firstSense: dur- [eth] for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal
G4340.full: From G4314 and G2540; for the occasion only, that is, temporary: - dur- [eth] for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal.

G4341.full: Middle voice from G4314 and G2564; to call toward oneself, that is, summon, invite: - call (for, to, unto).

G4342.firstSense: attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (contin…
G4342.full: From G4314 and G2594; to be earnest towards, that is, (to a thing) to persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to (as a servitor): - attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (continually).

G4344.full: Neuter of a presumed compound of G4314 and G2776; something for the head, that is, a cushion: - pillow.

G4345.full: From G4314 and G2820; to give a common lot to, that is, (figuratively) to associate with: - consort with.

G4346.full: From a compound of G4314 and G2827; a leaning towards, that is, (figuratively) proclivity (favoritism): - partiality.

G4347.full: From G4314 and G2853; to glue to, that is, (figuratively) to adhere: - cleave, join (self).

G4348.full: From G4350; a stub, that is, (figuratively) occasion of apostasy: - offence, stumbling (-block,[-stone]).

G4349.full: From G4350; a stumbling, that is, (figuratively and concretely) occasion of sin: - offence.

G4350.full: From G4314 and G2875; to strike at, that is, surge against (as water); specifically to stub on, that is, trip up (literally or figuratively): - beat upon, dash, stumble (at).

G4351.full: From G4314 and G2947; to roll towards, that is, block against: - roll (to).

G4352.full: From G4314 and probably a derivative of G2965 (meaning to kiss, like a dog licking his master's hand); to fawn or crouch to, that is, (literally or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to, adore): - worship.

G4354.full: From G4314 and G2980; to talk to, that is, converse with: - speak to (with).

G4355.full: From G4314 and G2983; to take to oneself, that is, use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality): - receive, take (unto).

G4357.firstSense: abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with)
G4357.full: From G4314 and G3306; to stay further, that is, remain in a place, with a person; figuratively to adhere to, persevere in: - abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with).

G4358.full: From G4314 and a derivative of the same as G3730 (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); to moor to, that is, (by implication) land at: - draw to the shore.

G4359.full: From G4314 and G3784; to be indebted additionally: - over besides.

G4360.full: From G4314 and a form of ï̓÷èǻù ochtheō (to be vexed with something irksome); to feel indignant at: - be grieved with.

G4361.full: From G4314 and the same as G3983; hungering further, that is, intensely hungry: - very hungry.

G4362.full: From G4314 and G4078; to fasten to, that is, (specifically) to impale (on a cross): - crucify.

G4363.full: From G4314 and G4098; to fall towards, that is, (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm): - beat upon, fall (down) at (before).

G4364.full: Middle voice from G4314 and G4160; to do forward for oneself, that is, pretend (as if about to do a thing): - make as though.

G4365.full: From G4314 and G4198; to journey towards, that is, approach (not the same as G4313): - go before.

G4366.full: From G4314 and G4486; to tear towards, that is, burst upon (as a tempest or flood): - beat vehemently against (upon).

G4367.full: From G4314 and G5021; to arrange towards, that is, (figuratively) enjoin: - bid, command.

G4368.full: Feminine of a derivative of G4291; a patroness, that is, assistant: - succourer.

G4369.firstSense: add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more
G4369.full: From G4314 and G5087; to place additionally, that is, lay beside, annex, repeat: - add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more.

G4370.full: From G4314 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run towards, that is, hasten to meet or join: - run (thither to, to).

G4371.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4314 and G5315; something eaten in addition to bread, that is, a relish (specifically fish; compare G3795): - meat.

G4372.full: From G4253 and a derivative of G4969; previously (recently) slain (fresh), that is, (figuratively) lately made: - new.

G4374.firstSense: bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to
G4374.full: From G4314 and G5342 (including its alternate); to bear towards, that is, lead to, tender (especially to God), treat: - bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to.

G4375.full: From a presumed compound of G4314 and G5368; friendly towards, that is, acceptable: - lovely.

G4376.full: From G4374; presentation; concretely an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice: - offering (up).

G4377.full: From G4314 and G5455; to sound towards, that is, address, exclaim, summon: - call unto, speak (un-) to.

G4378.full: From a compound of G4314 and ÷ǻù cheō (to pour); a shedding forth, that is, affusion: - sprinkling.

G4379.full: From G4314 and øáṍù psauō (to touch); to impinge, that is, lay a finger on (in order to relieve): - touch.

G4380.full: From G4381; to favor an individual, that is, show partiality: - have respect to persons.

G4381.full: From G4383 and G2983; an accepter of a face (individual), that is, (specifically) one exhibiting partiality: - respecter of persons.

G4382.full: From G4381; partiality, that is, favoritism: - respect of persons.

G4383.firstSense: (outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence
G4383.full: From G4314 and ù̓́ø ōps (the visage; from G3700); the front (as being towards view), that is, the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication presence, person: - (outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence.

G4384.full: From G4253 and G5021; to pre-arrange, that is, prescribe: - before appoint.

G4385.full: From G4253 and ôåé́íù teinō (to stretch); to protend, that is, tie prostrate (for scourging): - bind.

G4386.full: Neuter of G4387 as adverb (with or without the article); previously: - before, (at the) first, former.

G4387.full: Comparative of G4253; prior or previous: - former.

G4388.full: Middle voice from G4253 and G5087; to place before, that is, (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine): - purpose, set forth.

G4389.full: Middle voice from G4253 and the base of G5157; to turn forward for oneself, that is, encourage: - exhort.

G4390.full: From G4253 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run forward, that is, outstrip, precede: - outrun, run before.

G4391.full: From G4253 and G5225; to exist before, that is, (adverbially) to be or do something previously: - + be before (-time).

G4392.full: From a compound of G4253 and G5316; an outward showing, that is, pretext: - cloke, colour, pretence, show.

G4393.full: From G4253 and G5342; to bear forward, that is, produce: - bring forth.

G4394.full: From G4396 ("prophecy"); prediction (scriptural or other): - prophecy, prophesying.

G4395.full: From G4396; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office: - prophesy.

G4396.full: From a compound of G4253 and G5346; a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy an inspired speaker; by extension a poet: - prophet.

G4397.full: From G4396; pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic"): - of prophecy, of the prophets.

G4398.full: Feminine of G4396; a female foreteller or an inspired woman: - prophetess.

G4399.full: From G4253 and G5348; to get an earlier start of, that is, anticipate: - prevent.

G4400.full: Middle voice from G4253 and a derivative of G5495; to handle for oneself in advance, that is, (figuratively) to purpose: - choose, make.

G4401.full: From G4253 and G5500; to elect in advance: - choose before.

G4402.full: From G4253 and G5525; before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian: - Prochorus.

G4403.full: Feminine of ðñõìíṍò prumnus (hindmost); the stern of a ship: - hinder part, stern.

G4404.full: Adverb from G4253; at dawn; by implication the day break watch: - early (in the morning), (in the) morning.

G4405.full: Feminine of a derivative of G4404 as noun; day dawn: - early, morning.

G4406.full: From G4404; dawning, that is, (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season): - early.

G4407.full: From G4404; pertaining to the dawn, that is, matutinal: - morning.

G4408.full: Feminine of a presumed derivation of G4253 as noun; the prow, that is, forward part of a vessel: - forepart (-ship).

G4409.full: From G4413; to be first (in rank or influence): - have the preeminence.

G4410.full: From G4413 and G2515; a sitting first (in the front row), that is, preeminence in council: - chief (highest, uppermost) seat.

G4411.full: From G4413 and G2828; a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner bed, that is, preeminence at meals: - chief (highest, uppermost) room.

G4412.firstSense: before, at the beginning, chiefly, (at, at the) first (of all)
G4412.full: Neuter of G4413 as an adverb (with or without G3588); firstly (in time, place, order, or importance): - before, at the beginning, chiefly, (at, at the) first (of all).

G4413.firstSense: before, beginning, best, chief (-est), first (of all), former
G4413.full: Contracted superlative of G4253; foremost (in time, place, order or importance): - before, beginning, best, chief (-est), first (of all), former.

G4414.full: From G4413 and G2476; one standing first in the ranks, that is, a captain (champion): - ringleader.

G4415.full: From G4416; primogeniture (as a privilege): - birthright.

G4416.full: From G4413 and the alternate of G5088; first born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively): - firstbegotten (-born).

G4417.full: A form of G4098; to trip, that is, (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation): - fall, offend, stumble.

G4418.full: Of uncertain derivation; the heel (figuratively): - heel.

G4419.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4420; a winglet, that is, (figuratively) extremity (top corner): - pinnacle.

G4420.full: From a derivative of G4072 (meaning a feather); a wing: - wing.

G4421.full: Contraction for G4071; a bird: - bird.

G4422.full: Probably akin to the alternate of G4098 (through the idea of causing to fall) or to G4072 (through that of causing to fly away); to scare: - frighten.

G4424.full: From "ptolemaios" (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); Ptolemais, a place in Palestine: - Ptolemais.

G4425.full: From G4429; a winnowing fork (as scattering like spittle): - fan.

G4426.full: From a presumed derivative of G4429 (and thus akin to G4422); to frighten: - terrify.

G4428.full: Probably akin to ðåôá́ííõìé petannumi (to spread; and thus apparently allied to G4072 through the idea of expansion, and to G4429 through that of flattening; compare G3961); to fold, that is, furl a scroll: - close.

G4429.full: A primary verb (compare G4428); to spit: - spit.

G4430.full: From the alternate of G4098; a ruin, that is, (specifically) lifeless body (corpse, carrion): - dead body, carcase, corpse.

G4431.full: From the alternate of G4098; a crash, that is, downfall (literally or figuratively): - fall.

G4432.full: From G4433; beggary, that is, indigence (literally or figuratively): - poverty.

G4433.full: From G4434; to be a beggar, that is, (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively): - become poor.

G4434.full: From ðôù́óóù ptōssō (to crouch; akin to G4422 and the alternate of G4098); a beggar (as cringing), that is, pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas G3993 properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed): - beggar (-ly), poor.

G4435.full: From a primary word, ðṍæ pux, (the fist as a weapon); the clenched hand, that is, (only in the dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing): - oft.

G4436.full: From Ðõèù́ Puthō (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located); a Python, that is, (by analogy with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying): - divination.

G4437.full: From the same as G4635; clasped (thick), that is, (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently: - often (-er).

G4438.full: From a derivative of the same as G4435; to box (with the fist), that is, contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively): - fight.

G4439.full: Apparently a primary word; a gate, that is, the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively): - gate.

G4440.full: From G4439; a gateway, door way or a building or city; by implication a portal or vestibule: - gate, porch.

G4441.full: Middle voice prolonged from ðṍèù puthō, a primary word, (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to question, that is, ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from G2065, which properly means a request as a favor; and from G154, which is strictly a demand of something due; as well as from G2212, which implies a search for something hidden; and from G1189, which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication to learn (by casual intelligence): - ask, demand, enquire, understand.

G4442.full: pur poor A primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specifically lightning): - fiery, fire.

G4444.full: Apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle: - tower.

G4445.full: From G4443; to be on fire, that is, (specifically) to have a fever: - be sick of a fever.

G4446.full: From G4445; inflamed, that is, (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever): - fever.

G4447.full: From G4443; fiery, that is, (by implication) flaming: - of fire.

G4448.firstSense: burn, fiery, be on fire, try
G4448.full: From G4442; to kindle, that is, (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust): - burn, fiery, be on fire, try.

G4449.full: From G4450; to redden (intransitively): - be red.

G4450.full: From G4442; fire like, that is, (specifically) flame colored: - red.

G4451.full: From G4448; ignition, that is, (specifically) smelting (figuratively conflagration, calamity as a test): - burning, trial.

G4452.firstSense: Another form of the base of G4458
G4452.full: Another form of the base of G4458; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in compounds.

G4453.full: Probably ultimately from ðǻëïìáé pelomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), that is, to sell: - sell, whatever is sold.

G4454.full: Apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", that is, (specifically) a young ass: - colt.

G4455.full: From G4452 and G4218; at any time, that is, (with negative particle) at no time: - at any time, + never (. . . to any man), + yet never man.

G4456.full: Apparently from ðù͂ñïò pōros (a kind of stone); to petrify, that is, (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous): - blind, harden.

G4457.full: From G4456; stupidity or callousness: - blindness, hardness.

G4458.full: pōs poce Adverb from the base of G4225; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in compounds: - haply, by any (some) means, perhaps. See G1513, G3381. Compare G4459.

G4459.full: pōs poce Adverb from the base of G4226; an interrogitive particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!: - how, after (by) what manner (means), that. [Occasionally unexpressed in English.]

G4460.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7343]; Raab (that is, Rachab), a Canaanitess: - Rahab. See also G4477.

G4461.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7227] with pronominal suffix; my master, that is, Rabbi, as an official title of honor: - Master, Rabbi.

G4462.full: Of Chaldee origin; corresponding to G4461: - Lord, Rabboni.

G4463.full: From G4464; to strike with a stick, that is, bastinado: - beat (with rods).

G4464.full: From the base of G4474; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty): - rod, sceptre, staff.

G4465.full: From G4464 and G2192; a rod (the Latin fasces) holder, that is, a Roman lictor (constable or executioner): - serjeant.

G4466.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7466]; Ragau (that is, Reu), a patriarch: - Ragau.

G4467.full: From a compound of ñ̔áͅäéïò rhadios (easy, that is, reckless) and G2041; easy going behavior, that is, (by extension) a crime: - lewdness.

G4468.full: From the same as G4467; recklessness, that is, (by extension) malignity: - mischief.

G4469.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H7386]); O empty one, that is, thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification): - Raca.

G4470.full: From G4486; a "rag", i. e. piece of cloth: - cloth.

G4471.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7414]; Rama (that is, Ramah), a place in Palestine: - Rama.

G4472.full: From a derivative of ñ̔áé́íù rhainō (to sprinkle); to render besprinkled, that is, asperse (ceremonially or figuratively): - sprinkle.

G4473.full: From G4472; aspersion (ceremonially or figuratively): - sprinkling.

G4474.firstSense: smite (with the palm of the hand)
G4474.full: From a derivative of ñ̔ǻðù rhepō, a primary word, (to let fall, "rap"); to slap (with the palm of the hand): - smite (with the palm of the hand). Compare G5180.

G4475.firstSense: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand
G4475.full: From G4474; a slap: - (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.

G4476.full: From ñ̔á́ðôù rhaptō, a primary word, (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474 through the idea of puncturing); a needle: - needle.

G4477.full: From the same as G4460; Rachab, a Canaanitess: - Rachab.

G4478.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7354]; Rachel, the wife of Jacob: - Rachel.

G4479.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7259]; Rebecca (that is, Ribkah), the wife of Isaac: - Rebecca.

G4480.full: Of Latin origin; a rheda, that is, four wheeled carriage (wagon for riding): - chariot.

G4481.full: By incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin [H3594]; Remphan (that is, Kijun), an Egyptian idol: - Remphan.

G4482.full: A primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form (ñ̔åṍù rheuō) is used; to flow ("run", as water): - flow.

G4483.full: For certain tenses of which a prolonged form (å̓ñǻù ereō) is used; and both as alternate for G2036; perhaps akin (or identical) with G4482 (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, that is, speak or say: - command, make, say, speak (of). Compare G3004.

G4484.full: Of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy: - Rhegium.

G4485.full: From G4486; something torn, that is, a fragment (by implication and abstraction, a fall): - ruin.

G4486.full: Both are prolonged forms of ñ̔ḉêù rhēko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of á̓́ãíõìé agnumi (see in G2608)); to "break", "wreck" or "crack", that is, (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; G2608 being its intensive (with the preposition in compounds), and G2352 a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like G3089) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication to convulse (with spasms); figuratively to give vent to joyful emotions: - break (forth), burst, rend, tear.

G4487.full: From G4483; an utterance (individually, collectively or specifically); by implication a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever: - + evil, + nothing, saying, word.

G4488.full: Probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for [H7509]); Resa (that is, Rephajah), an Israelite: - Rhesa.

G4489.full: From G4483; a speaker, that is, (by implication) a forensic advocate: - orator.

G4490.full: Adverb from a derivative of G4483; out spokenly, that is, distinctly: - expressly.

G4491.full: Apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively): - root.

G4492.full: From G4491; to root (figuratively become stable): - root.

G4493.full: From G4496; a jerk (of the eye, that is, (by analogy) an instant): - twinkling.

G4494.full: From a derivative of G4496 (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, that is, (by analogy) to agitate (into waves): - toss.

G4495.full: From a derivative of G4496; to toss up: - cast off.

G4496.full: A primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474, through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly with a quick toss, thus differing from G906, which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from ôåé́íù teinō (see in G1614), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension to disperse: - cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw.

G4497.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7346]; Roboam (that is, Rechabam), an Israelite: - Roboam.

G4498.full: Probably for ñ̔ḯäḉ rhodē (a rose); Rode, a servant girl: - Rhoda.

G4499.full: Probably from ñ̔ḯäïí rhodon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean: - Rhodes.

G4500.full: Adverb from a derivative of ñ̔ïé͂æïò rhoizos (a whir); whizzingly, that is, with a crash: - with a great noise.

G4501.full: Probably of foreign origin; a sabre, that is, a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively): - sword.

G4502.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7205]; Ruben (that is, Reuben), an Israelite: - Reuben.

G4503.full: Rhouth hrooth Of Hebrew origin [H7327]; Ruth, a Moabitess: - Ruth.

G4504.full: Of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian: - Rufus.

G4505.full: Prolonged from G4506 in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded): - lane, street.

G4506.full: Middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to G4482 (through the idea of a current; compare G4511); to rush or draw (for oneself), that is, rescue: - deliver (-er).

G4508.full: From G4509; dirty, that is, (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally wicked: - vile.

G4509.full: Of uncertain affinity; dirt, that is, (moral) depravity: - filth.

G4510.full: From G4509; to soil, that is, (intransitively) to become dirty (morally): - be filthy.

G4511.full: From G4506 in the sense of its congener G4482; a flux (of blood): - issue.

G4512.full: From G4506; a fold (as drawing together), that is, a wrinkle (especially on the face): - wrinkle.

G4513.full: From G4514; Romaic, that is, Latin: - Latin.

G4514.full: From G4516; Romaean, that is, Roman (as noun): - Roman, of Rome.

G4515.full: Adverb from a presumed derivative of G4516; Romaistically, that is, in the Latin language: - Latin.

G4516.full: From the base of G4517; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy: - Rome.

G4517.full: Prolonged from ñ̔ù́ïìáé rhōomai (to dart; probably akin to G4506); to strengthen, that is, (imperative passive) have health (as parting exclamation, good bye): - farewell.

G4518.full: Of Chaldee origin [H7662] with pronominal suffix; thou hast left me; sabachthani (that is, shebakthani), a cry of distress: - sabachthani.

G4519.full: Of Hebrew origin ([H6635] in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (that is, tsebaoth), a military epithet of God: - sabaoth.

G4520.full: From a derivative of G4521; a "sabbatism", that is, (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven): - rest.

G4521.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7676]; the Sabbath (that is, Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension a se'nnight, that is, the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications: - sabbath (day), week.

G4522.full: From a derivative of óá́ôôù sattō (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing: - net.

G4523.full: Probably from G4524; a Sadducaean (that is, Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite: - Sadducee.

G4524.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6659]; Sadoc (that is, Tsadok), an Israelite: - Sadoc.

G4525.full: Akin to G4579; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), that is, (generally) to shake (figuratively disturb): - move.

G4526.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8242]; "sack" cloth, that is, mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief): - sackcloth.

G4527.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7974]; Sala (that is, Shelach), a patriarch: - Sala.

G4528.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7597]; Salathiel (that is, Shealtiel), an Israelite: - Salathiel.

G4529.full: Probably from G4535 (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus: - Salamis.

G4530.full: Probably from the same as G4531; Salim, a place in Palestine: - Salim.

G4531.firstSense: move, shake (together), which can [-not] be shaken, stir up
G4531.full: From G4535; to waver, that is, agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively to disturb, incite: - move, shake (together), which can [-not] be shaken, stir up.

G4532.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8004]; Salem (that is, Shalem), a place in Palestine: - Salem.

G4533.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8012]; Salmon, an Israelite: - Salmon.

G4534.full: Perhaps of similar origin to G4529; Salmone, a place in Crete: - Salmone.

G4535.full: Probably from the base of G4525; a vibration, that is, (specifically) billow: - wave.

G4536.full: Perhaps from G4535 (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet: - trump (-et).

G4537.full: From G4536; to trumpet, that is, sound a blast (literally or figuratively): - (which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).

G4539.full: Probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from [H7965]); Salome (that is, Shelomah), an Israelitess: - Salome.

G4540.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8111]; Samaria (that is, Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine: - Samaria.

G4541.full: From G4540; a Samarite, that is, inhabitants of Samaria: - Samaritan.

G4542.full: Feminine of G4541; a Samaritess, that is, woman of Samaria: - of Samaria.

G4543.full: From G4544 and Èñá́ͅêç Thrakē (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean: - Samothrace.

G4544.full: Of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean: - Samos.

G4545.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8050]; Samuel (that is, Shemuel), an Israelite: - Samuel.

G4546.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8123]; Sampson (that is, Shimshon), an Israelite: - Samson.

G4547.full: Neuter of a derivative of óá́íäáëïí sandalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole pad: - sandal.

G4548.full: Of uncertain affinity; a plank: - board.

G4549.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7586]; Saul (that is, Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul: - Saul. Compare G4569.

G4550.full: From G4595; rotten, that is, worthless (literally or morally): - bad, corrupt. Compt. G4190.

G4551.full: Feminine of G4552; Sapphire, an Israelitess: - Sapphira.

G4552.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5601]; a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem: - sapphire.

G4553.full: Apparently of Hebrew origin [H8276]; a basket (as interwoven or wicker work): - basket.

G4554.full: Plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor: - Sardis.

G4555.full: From the same as G4556; sardine (G3037 being implied), that is, a gem, so called: - sardine.

G4556.full: Proper adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (G3037 being implied), that is, (as noun) the gem so called: - sardius.

G4557.full: From the base of G4556 and ï̓́íõî onux (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", that is, the gem so called: - sardonyx.

G4558.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6886]; Sarepta (that is, Tsarephath), a place in Palestine: - Sarepta.

G4559.full: From G4561; pertaining to flesh, that is, (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate: - carnal, fleshly.

G4560.full: From G4561; similar to flesh, that is, (by analogy) soft: - fleshly.

G4561.full: sarx sarx Probably from the base of G4563; flesh (as stripped of the skin), that is, (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred, or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specifically) a human being (as such): - carnal (-ly, + -ly minded), flesh ([-ly]).

G4562.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8286]; Saruch (that is, Serug), a patriarch: - Saruch.

G4563.full: From a derivative of óáéñù sairō (to brush off; akin to G4951) meaning a broom; to sweep: - sweep.

G4564.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8283]; Sarra (that is, Sarah), the wife of Abraham: - Sara, Sarah.

G4565.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8289]; Saron (that is, Sharon), a district of Palestine: - Saron.

G4566.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7854]; Satan, that is, the devil: - Satan. Compare G4567.

G4567.full: Of Chaldee origin corresponding to G4566 (with the definite article affixed); the accuser, that is, the devil: - Satan.

G4568.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5429]; a certain measure for things dry: - measure.

G4569.full: Of Hebrew origin, the same as G4549; Saulus (that is, Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul: - Saul.

G4570.full: A prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively): - go out, quench.

G4571.full: se seh Accusative singular of G4771; thee: - thee, thou, X thy house.

G4572.full: seautou seautō seauton sautou sautō sauton seh-ow-too', she-ow-to', she-ow-ton', sow-too', sow-to', sow-ton' The genitive case from G4571 and G846, with the dative and accusative of the same with contractions, respectively, of (with, to) thyself: - thee, thine own self, (thou) thy (-self).

G4573.full: Middle voice from a derivative of G4576; to venerate, that is, adore: - worship.

G4574.full: From G4573; something adored, that is, an object of worship (god, altar, etc.): - devotion, that is worshipped.

G4575.full: From G4573; venerable (august), that is, (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial: - Augustus (-').

G4576.full: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, that is, adore: - devout, religious, worship.

G4577.full: Probably from G4951 through its congener åé̓́ñù eirō (to fasten; akin to G138); a chain (as binding or drawing): - chain.

G4578.full: From G4579; a commotion, that is, (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake: - earthquake, tempest.

G4579.full: Apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly sideways or to and fro), that is, (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern): - move, quake, shake.

G4580.full: Of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian: - Secundus.

G4581.full: From Óǻëåõêïò Seleukos (Seleucus, a Syran king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria: - Seleucia.

G4582.full: From óǻëáò selas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of G138, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon: - moon.

G4583.full: Middle or passive voice from a presumed derivative of G4582; to be moon struck, that is, crazy: - be lunatic.

G4584.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8096]; Semei (that is, Shimi), an Israelite: - Semei.

G4585.full: Probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour: - fine flour.

G4586.full: From G4576; venerable, that is, honorable: - grave, honest.

G4587.full: From G4586; venerableness, that is, probity: - gravity, honesty.

G4588.full: Of Lat origin; Sergius, a Roman: - Sergius.

G4589.full: Sēth sayth Of Hebrew origin [H8352]; Seth (that is, Sheth), a patriarch: - Seth.

G4590.full: Sēm same Of Hebrew origin [H8035]; Sem (that is, Shem), a patriarch: - Sem.

G4591.full: From óç͂ìá sēma (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate: - signify.

G4592.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4591; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally: - miracle, sign, token, wonder.

G4593.full: From G4592; to distinguish, that is, mark (for avoidance): - note.

G4594.full: Neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article G3588 ("tau" changed to "sigma") and G2250; on the (that is, this) day (or night current or just passed); genitively now (that is, at present, hitherto): - this (to-) day.

G4595.full: Apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, that is, (figuratively) perish: - be corrupted.

G4596.full: From Óḉñ Sēr (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silkworm); Seric, that is, silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric): - silk.

G4597.full: sēs sace Apparently of Hebrew origin [H5580]; a moth: - moth.

G4598.full: From G4597 and a derivative of G977; moth eaten: - motheaten.

G4599.full: From óèǻíïò sthenos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of G2476); to strengthen, that is, (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power): - strengthen.

G4600.full: Of uncertain derivation; the jaw bone, that is, (by implication) the cheek or side of the face: - cheek.

G4601.full: From G4602; to keep silent (transitive or intransitive): - keep close (secret, silence), hold peace.

G4602.full: Apparently from óé́æù sizō (to hiss, that is, hist or hush); silence: - silence. Compare G4623.

G4603.full: From G4604; made of iron: - (of) iron.

G4605.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6721]; Sidon (that is, Tsidon), a place in Palestine: - Sidon.

G4606.full: From G4605; a Sidonian, that is, inhabitant of Sidon: - of Sidon.

G4607.full: Of Latin origin; a dagger man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans): - murderer. Compare G5406.

G4608.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7941]; an intoxicant, that is, intensely fermented liquor: - strong drink.

G4609.full: Contraction for G4610; Silas, a Christian: - Silas.

G4610.full: Of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian: - Silvanus. Compare G4609.

G4611.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7975]; Siloam (that is, Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem: - Siloam.

G4612.full: Of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half girding, that is, narrow covering (apron): - apron.

G4613.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8095]; Simon (that is, Shimon), the name of nine Israelites: - Simon. Compare G4826.

G4614.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5514]; Sina (that is, Sinai), a mountain in Arabia: - Sina.

G4615.full: Perhaps from óé́íïìáé sinomai (to hurt, that is, sting); mustard (the plant): - mustard.

G4616.full: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, that is, bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it): - (fine) linen (cloth).

G4617.full: From óéíéïí sinion (a sieve); to riddle (figuratively): - sift.

G4618.full: From a derivative of G4621; grain fed, that is, fattened: - fatted.

G4619.full: From a derivative of G4621; grained that is, fatted: - fatling.

G4620.full: From G4621 and G3358; a grain measure, that is, (by implication) ration (allowance of food): - portion of meat.

G4621.full: óé͂ôá sita see'-tah is the plural irregular neuter of the first form. Of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat: - corn, wheat.

G4622.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6726]; Sion (that is, Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively the Church (militant or triumphant): - Sion.

G4623.full: From óéùðç siōpē (silence, that is, a hush; properly muteness, that is, involuntary stillness, or inability ot speak; and thus differing from G4602, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like G2974 properly); figuratively to be calm (as quiet water): - dumb, (hold) peace.

G4624.full: To "scandalize"; from G4625; to entrap, that is, trip up (figuratively stumble [transitively] or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure): - (make to) offend.

G4625.firstSense: occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumbling-block
G4625.full: A "scandal"; probably from a derivative of G2578; a trap stick (bent sapling), that is, snare (figuratively cause of displeasure or sin): - occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumbling-block.

G4626.full: Apparently a primary verb; to dig: - dig.

G4627.full: A "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing): - boat.

G4628.full: Apparently from óêǻëëù skellō (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank): - leg.

G4629.full: From a derivative of "skepas" (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of G4649 through the idea of noticeableness); clothing: - raiment.

G4630.full: Apparently of Latin origin; left handed; Scevas (that is, Scaevus), an Israelite: - Sceva.

G4631.full: From G4632; furniture, that is, spare tackle: - tackling.

G4632.full: Of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specifically a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband]): - goods, sail, stuff, vessel.

G4633.full: Apparently akin to G4632 and G4639; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively): - habitation, tabernacle.

G4634.full: From G4636 and G4078; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes): - tabernacles.

G4635.full: From G4633 and G4160; a manufacturer of tents: - tentmaker.

G4636.full: From G4633; a hut or temporary residence, that is, (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit): - tabernacle.

G4637.full: From G4636; to tent or encamp, that is, (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specifically) to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol fo protection and communion): - dwell.

G4638.full: From G4637; an encampment, that is, (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul): - tabernacle.

G4639.full: Apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively [darkness of error or an adumbration]): - shadow.

G4640.full: Akin to óêáé́ñù skairō (to skip); to jump, that is, sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus): - leap (for joy).

G4641.full: Feminine of a compound of G4642 and G2588; hard heartedness, that is, (specifically) destitution of (spiritual) perception: - hardness of heart.

G4642.full: From the base of G4628; dry, that is, hard or tough (figuratively harsh, severe): - fierce, hard.

G4643.full: From G4642; callousness, that is, (figuratively) stubbornness: - hardness.

G4644.full: From G4642 and G5137; hard naped, that is, (figuratively) obstinate: - stiffnecked.

G4645.full: From G4642; to indurate, that is, (figuratively) render stubborn: - harden.

G4646.full: From the base of G4628; warped, that is, winding; figuratively perverse: - crooked, froward, untoward.

G4647.full: Perhaps form the base of G4628 and G3700; withered at the front, that is, a point or prickle (figuratively a bodily annoyance or disability): - thorn.

G4648.firstSense: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark
G4648.full: From G4649; to take aim at (spy), that is, (figuratively) regard: - consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare G3700.

G4649.full: ("scope"); From óêǻðôïìáé skeptomai (to peer about ["skeptic"]; perhaps akin to G4626 through the idea of concealment; compare G4629); a watch (sentry or scout), that is, (by implication) a goal: - mark.

G4650.full: Apparently from the same as G4651 (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, that is, (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal: - disperse abroad, scatter (abroad).

G4651.full: Probably from óêǻñðù skerpō, an obsolete word, (perhaps strengthened from the base of G4649 and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting): - scorpion.

G4652.full: From G4655; opaque, that is, (figuratively) benighted: - dark, full of darkness.

G4653.full: From G4655; dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively): - dark (-ness).

G4654.full: From G4655; to obscure (literally or figuratively): - darken.

G4655.full: From the base of G4639; shadiness, that is, obscurity (literally or figuratively): - darkness.

G4656.full: From G4655; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively): - be full of darkness.

G4657.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G1519 and G2965 and G906; what is thrown to the dogs, that is, refuse (ordure): - dung.

G4658.full: Probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, that is, (by implication) a savage: - Scythian.

G4659.full: From óêõèñḯò skuthros (sullen) and a derivative of G3700; angry visaged, that is, gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance: - of a sad countenance.

G4660.full: Apparently a primary verb; to flay, that is, (figuratively) to harass: - trouble (self).

G4661.full: Neuter from G4660; something stripped (as a hide), that is, booty: - spoil.

G4662.full: From G4663 and a derivative of G977; worm eaten, that is, diseased with maggots: - eaten of worms.

G4663.full: Of uncertain derivative; a grub, maggot or earth worm: - worm.

G4664.full: From G4665; consisting of emerald: - emerald.

G4665.full: Of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called: - emerald.

G4666.full: Apparently strengthened for G3464; myrrh: - myrrh.

G4667.full: The same as G4666; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor: - Smyrna.

G4668.full: From G4667; a Smyrnaean: - in Smyrna.

G4669.full: From G4667; to tincture with myrrh, that is, embitter (as a narcotic): - mingle with myrrh.

G4670.full: Plural, of Hebrew origin [H5467]; Sodoma (that is, Sedom), a place in Palestine: - Sodom.

G4671.full: soi soy Dative case of G4771; to thee: - thee, thine own, thou, thy.

G4672.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8010]; Solomon (that is, Shelomoh), the son of David: - Solomon.

G4673.full: Probably akin to the base of G4987; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), that is, (by analogy) a bier: - bier.

G4674.full: sos sos From G4771; thine: - thine (own), thy (friend).

G4675.firstSense: X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy
G4675.full: sou soo Genitive case of G4771; of thee, thy: - X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.

G4676.full: Of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat cloth), that is, towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse): - handerchief, napkin.

G4677.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7799] (feminine); lily; Susannah (that is, Shoshannah), an Israelitess: - Susanna.

G4678.full: From G4680; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual): - wisdom.

G4679.full: From G4680; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", that is, continue plausible error: - cunningly devised, make wise.

G4680.full: Akin to óáöḉò saphēs (clear); wise (in a most general application): - wise. Compare G5429.

G4681.full: Probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe: - Spain.

G4682.full: Prolongation from óðáé́ñù spairō̄ (to gasp; apparently strengthened from G4685 through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, that is, convulse with epilepsy: - rend, tear.

G4683.full: From óðá́ñãáíïí sparganon (a strip; from a derivative of the base of G4682 meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom): - wrap in swaddling clothes.

G4684.full: From óðáôá́ëç spatalē (luxury); to be voluptuous: - live in pleasure, be wanton.

G4685.full: A primary verb; to draw: - draw (out).

G4686.full: Of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of G138 in the sense of its cognate, G1507; a coil (spira, "spire"), that is, (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also [by analogy] a squad of Levitical janitors): - band.

G4687.full: Probably strengthened from G4685 (through the idea of extending); to scatter, that is, sow (literally or figuratively): - sow (-er), receive seed.

G4688.full: Of Latin origin; a speculator, that is, military scout (spy or [by extension] life guardsman): - executioner.

G4689.full: Apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, that is, (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend"): - (be ready to) be offered.

G4690.full: From G4687; somethng sown, that is, seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication offspring; specifically a remnant (figuratively as if kept over for planting): - issue, seed.

G4691.full: From G4690 and G3004; a seed picker (as the crow), that is, (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specifically a gossip or trifler in talk): - babbler.

G4692.full: Probably strengthened from G4228; to "speed" ("study"), that is, urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication to await eagerly: - (make, with) haste unto.

G4693.full: Neuter of a presumed derivation of óðǻïò speos (a grotto); a cavern; by implication a hiding place or resort: - cave, den.

G4694.full: Of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea: - spot [by confusion with G4696].

G4695.full: From G4696; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively): - defile, spot.

G4696.full: Of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, that is, (figuratively) defect, disgrace: - spot.

G4697.full: Middle voice from G4698; to have the bowels yearn, that is, (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity: - have (be moved with) compassion.

G4698.full: Probably strengthened from óðëḉí splēn (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively pity or sympathy: - bowels, inward affection, + tender mercy.

G4699.full: Perhaps of foreign origin; a "sponge": - spunge.

G4701.full: From G4687; a sowing, that is, (by implication) parentage: - seed.

G4702.full: From G4703; sown, that is, (neuter plural) a planted field: - corn (-field).

G4703.full: From G4687; a scattering (of seed), that is, (concretely) seed (as sown): - seed (X sown).

G4704.firstSense: do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study
G4704.full: From G4710; to use speed, that is, to make effort, be prompt or earnest: - do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.

G4705.full: From G4710; prompt, energetic, earnest: - diligent.

G4706.full: Neuter of G4707 as adverb; more earnestly than others), that is, very promptly: - very diligently.

G4707.full: Comparative of G4705; more prompt, more earnest: - more diligent (forward).

G4708.full: Adverb from G4707; more speedily, that is, sooner than otherwise: - more carefully.

G4709.full: Adverb from G4705; earnestly, promptly: - diligently, instantly.

G4710.full: From G4692; "speed", that is, (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness: - business, (earnest) care (-fulness), diligence forwardness, haste.

G4711.full: From G4687 (as woven); a hamper or lunch receptacle: - basket.

G4712.full: Or the masculine plural form, óôá́äéïò stadios stad'-ee-os. From the base of G2476 (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication a stadium or race course: - furlong, race.

G4713.full: From the base of G2476 (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank: - pot.

G4714.full: From the base of G2476; a standing (properly the act), that is, (by analogy) position (existence); by implication a popular uprising; figuratively controversy: - dissension, insurrection, X standing, uproar.

G4715.full: From the base of G2746; a stander (standard of value), that is, (specifically) a stater or certain coin: - piece of money.

G4716.full: From the base of G2476; a stake or post (as set upright), that is, (specifically) a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively exposure to death, that is, self denial; by implication the atonement of Christ: - cross.

G4717.full: From G4716; to impale on the cross; figuratively to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness: - crucify.

G4718.full: Probably from the base of G4735; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined): - grapes.

G4719.full: From the base of G2476; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk): - ear (of corn).

G4720.full: The same as G4719; Stachys, a Christian: - Stachys.

G4721.full: Strengthened from a primary word ôǻãïò tegos (a "thatch" or "deck" of building); a roof: - roof.

G4722.full: From G4721; to roof over, that is, (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently): - (for-) bear, suffer.

G4723.full: A contraction from G4731 (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile": - barren.

G4724.full: Probably strengthened from the base of G2476; properly to set fast ("stall"), that is, (figuratively) to repress (reflexively abstain from associating with): - avoid, withdraw self.

G4725.full: From the base of G4735; a wreath for show: - garland.

G4727.full: From G4728; to make (intransitively be) in straits, that is, (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly: - with grief, groan, grudge, sigh.

G4728.full: Probably from the base of G2476; narrow (from obstacles standing close about): - strait.

G4729.full: From the same as G4730; to hem in closely, that is, (figuratively) cramp: - distress, straiten.

G4730.full: From a compound of G4728 and G5561; narrowness of room, that is, (figuratively) calamity: - anguish, distress.

G4731.full: From G2476; stiff, that is, solid, stable (literally or figuratively): - stedfast, strong, sure.

G4732.full: From G4731; to solidify, that is, confirm (literally or figuratively): - establish, receive strength, make strong.

G4733.full: From G4732; something established, that is, (abstractly) confirmation (stability): - stedfastness.

G4734.full: Probably contraction for óôåöáíùôḯò stephanōtos (crowned; from G4737); Stephanas, a Christian: - Stephanas.

G4735.full: From an apparently primary "stepho" (to twine or wreathe); a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, G1238), literally or figuratively: - crown.

G4736.full: The same as G4735; Stephanus, a Christian: - Stephen.

G4737.full: From G4735; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively): - crown.

G4738.full: From G2476 (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, that is, chest: - breast.

G4739.full: From the perfect tense of G2476; to be stationary, that is, (figuratively) to persevere: - stand (fast).

G4741.full: From a presumed derivative of G2476 (like G4731); to set fast, that is, (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm: - fix, (e-) stablish, stedfastly set, strengthen.

G4742.full: From a primary word óôé́æù stizō (to "stick", that is, prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), that is, (figuratively) scar of service: - mark.

G4743.full: Feminine of G4742; a point of time, that is, an instant: - moment.

G4744.full: Apparently a primary verb; to gleam, that is, flash intensely: - shining.

G4745.full: Probably from G2476; a colonnade or interior piazza: - porch.

G4746.full: From a primary word óôåé́âù steibō (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, that is, (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed: - branch.

G4747.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4748; something orderly in arrangement, that is, (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively): - element, principle, rudiment.
