G4748.full: From a derivative of óôåé́÷ù steichō̄ (to range in regular line); to march in (military) rank (keep step), that is, (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety: - walk (orderly).

G4749.full: From G4724; equipment, that is, (specifically) a "stole" or long fitting gown (as a mark of dignity): - long clothing (garment), (long) robe.

G4750.full: Probably stregthened from a presumed derivative of the base of G5114; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication language (and its relations); figuratively an opening (in the earth); specifically the front or edge (of a weapon): - edge, face, mouth.

G4751.full: From G4750; an orifice (the gullet), that is, (specifically) the "stomach": - stomach.

G4752.full: From G4754; military service, that is, (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger): - warfare.

G4753.full: From G4754; an armament, that is, (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic): - army, soldier, man of war.

G4754.full: Middle voice from the base of G4756; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations: - soldier, (go to) war (-fare).

G4755.full: From the base of G4756 and G71 or G2233; a general, that is, (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (praetor), the chief (praefect) of the (Levitical) temple wardens: - captain, magistrate.

G4756.full: Feminine of a derivative of óôñáôḯò stratos (an army; from the base of G4766, as encamped); camp likeness, that is, an army, that is, (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries: - host.

G4757.full: From a presumed derivative of the same as G4756; a camperout, that is, a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively): - soldier.

G4758.full: From a compound of the base of G4756 and G3004 (in its original sense); to gather (or select) as a warrior, that is, enlist in the army: - choose to be a soldier.

G4759.full: From G4760 and G757; a ruler of an army, that is, (specifically) a Praetorian praefect: - captain of the guard.

G4760.full: From the base of G4756 and the same as G3977; a camping ground, that is, (by implication) a body of troops: - army.

G4761.full: From a derivative of G4762; to wrench, that is, (specifically) to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively to pervert: - wrest.

G4762.firstSense: convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about)
G4762.full: Strengthened from the base of G5157; to twist, that is, turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively): - convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).

G4763.full: From a presumed derivative of G4764; to be luxurious: - live deliciously.

G4764.full: Akin to G4731; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", that is, (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness): - delicacy.

G4765.full: Diminutive of óôñïõèḯò strouthos (a sparrow); a little sparrow: - sparrow.

G4766.full: Or a simpler form óôñùííṍù strōnnuō strone'-noo'-o, prolonged from a still simpler form óôñḯù stroō stro'-o (used only as an alternate in certain tenses; probably akin to G4731 through the idea of positing); to "strew", that is, spread (as a carpet or couch): - make bed, furnish, spread, strew.

G4767.full: From a derivative of an obsolete, apparently primary, word óôṍãù stugō (to hate); hated, that is, odious: - hateful.

G4768.full: From the same as G4767; to render gloomy, that is, (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech): - lower, be sad.

G4769.full: From óôṍù stuō (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of G2476); a post ("style"), that is, (figuratively) support: - pillar.

G4770.full: From G4745; a "stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), that is, adherent of a certain philosophy: - Stoick.

G4771.full: su soo The personal pronoun of the second person singular; thou: - thou. See also G4571, G4671, G4675; and for the plur. G5209, G5210, G5213, G5216.

G4772.full: From G4773; relationship, that is, (concretely) relatives: - kindred.

G4773.full: From G4862 and G1085; a relative (by blood); by extension a fellow countryman: - cousin, kin (-sfolk, -sman).

G4774.full: From a compound of G4862 and G1097; fellow knowledge, that is, concession: - permission.

G4775.full: From G4862 and G2521; to seat oneself in company with: - sit with.

G4776.full: From G4862 and G2523; to give (or take) a seat in company with: - (make) sit (down) together.

G4777.full: From G4862 and G2553; to suffer hardship in company with: - be partaker of afflictions.

G4778.full: From G4862 and G2558; to maltreat in company with, that is, (passively) endure persecution together: - suffer affliction with.

G4779.full: From G4862 and G2564; to convoke: - call together.

G4780.full: From G4862 and G2572; to conceal altogether: - cover.

G4781.full: From G4862 and G2578; to bend together, that is, (figuratively) to afflict: - bow down.

G4782.full: From G4862 and G2597; to descend in company with: - go down with.

G4783.full: From G4784; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, that is, (figuratively) accord with: - agreement.

G4784.full: Middle voice from G4862 and G2698; to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, that is, (figuratively) to accord with: - consent.

G4785.full: From G4862 and a compound of G2596 and G5585; to count down in company with, that is, enroll among: - number with.

G4786.full: From G4862 and G2767; to commingle, that is, (figuratively) to combine or assimilate: - mix with, temper together.

G4787.full: From G4682 and G2795; to move together, that is, (specifically) to excite as a mass (to sedition): - stir up.

G4788.full: From G4862 and G2808; to shut together, that is, include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to: - conclude, inclose, shut up.

G4789.full: From G4862 and G2818; a co-heir, that is, (by analogy) participant in common: - fellow (joint) -heir, heir together, heir with.

G4790.firstSense: communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of
G4790.full: From G4862 and G2841; to share in company with, that is, co-participate in: - communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of.

G4791.full: From G4862 and G2844; a co-participant: - companion, partake (-r, -r with).

G4792.full: From G4862 and G2865; to convey together, that is, collect or bear away in company with others: - carry.

G4793.full: From G4862 and G2919; to judge of one thing in connection with another, that is, combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance): - compare among (with).

G4794.full: From G4862 and G2955; to stoop altogether, that is, be completely overcome by: - bow together.

G4795.full: From a compound of G4862 and êõñǻù kureō (to light or happen; from the base of G2962); concurrence, that is, accident: - chance.

G4796.full: From G4862 and G5463; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate: - rejoice in (with).

G4797.firstSense: confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar
G4797.full: Or óõã÷ṍíù sugchunō soong-khoo'-no From G4862 and ÷ǻù "cheō" (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, that is, (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind): - confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.

G4798.full: From G4862 and G5530; to use jointly, that is, (by implication) to hold intercourse in common: - have dealings with.

G4799.full: From G4797; commixture, that is, (figuratively) riotous disturbance: - confusion.

G4800.full: From G4862 and G2198; to continue to live in common with, that is, co-survive (literally or figuratively): - live with.

G4801.full: From G4862 and the base of G2201; to yoke together, that is, (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage): - join together.

G4802.full: From G4862 and G2212; to investigate jointly, that is, discuss, controvert, cavil: - dispute (with), enquire, question (with), reason (together).

G4803.full: From G4802; mutual questioning, that is, discussion: - disputation (-ting), reasoning.

G4804.full: From G4802; a disputant, that is, sophist: - disputer.

G4805.full: From G4801; co-yoked, that is, (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as proper name; Syzygus, a Christian: - yokefellow.

G4806.full: From G4862 and G2227; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively): - quicken together with.

G4807.full: Of Hebrew origin [H8256] in imitation of G4809; a sycamore or fig tree: - sycamine tree.

G4808.full: From G4810; a fig tree: - fig tree.

G4809.full: From G4810 and ìḯñïí moron (the mulberry); the "sycamore" or fig tree: - sycamore tree. Compare G4807.

G4810.full: Apparently a primary word; a fig: - fig.

G4811.firstSense: accuse falsely, take by false accusation
G4811.full: From a compound of G4810 and a derivative of G5316; to be a fig informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycopant", that is, (generally and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort): - accuse falsely, take by false accusation.

G4812.full: From the base of G4813 and (the reduplicated form of) G71; to lead away as booty, that is, (figuratively) seduce: - spoil.

G4813.full: From a derivative of óṍëëù sullō̄ (to strip; probably akin to G138; compare G4661); to despoil: - rob.

G4814.full: From G4862 and G2980; to talk together, that is, converse: - commune (confer, talk) with, speak among.

G4815.full: From G4862 and G2983; to clasp, that is, seize (arrest, capture); specifically to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication to aid: - catch, conceive, help, take.

G4816.full: From G4862 and G3004 in its original sense; to collect: - gather (together, up).

G4817.full: From G4862 and G3049; to reckon together (with oneself), that is, deliberate: - reason with.

G4818.full: From G4862 and G3076; to afflict jointly, that is, (passively) sorrow at (on account of) some one: - be grieved.

G4819.full: From G4862 and the base of G939; to walk (figuratively transpire) together, that is, concur (take place): - be (-fall), happen (unto).

G4820.firstSense: confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder
G4820.full: From G4862 and G906; to combine, that is, (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack: - confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.

G4821.full: From G4862 and G936; to be co-regent (figuratively): - reign with.

G4822.firstSense: compact, assuredly, gather, instruct, knit together, prove
G4822.full: From G4862 and âéâá́æù bibazō (to force; causatively [by reduplication] of the base of G939); to drive together, that is, unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach: - compact, assuredly, gather, instruct, knit together, prove.

G4823.full: From G4862 and G1011; to give (or take) advice jointly, that is, recommend, deliberate or determine: - consult, (give, take) counsel (together).

G4824.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G4825; advisement; specifically a deliberative body, that is, the provincial assessors or lay court: - consultation, counsel, council.

G4825.full: From G4862 and G1012; a consultor, that is, adviser: - counsellor.

G4826.full: From the same as G4613; Symeon (that is, Shimon), the name of five Israelites: - Simeon, Simon.

G4827.full: From a compound of G4862 and G3129; a co-learner (of Christianity): - fellowdisciple.

G4828.full: From G4862 and G3140; to testify jointly, that is, corroborate by (concurrent) evidence: - testify unto, (also) bear witness (with).

G4829.full: Middle voice from G4862 and G3307; to share jointly, that is, participate in: - be partaker with.

G4830.full: From G4862 and G3353; a co-participant: - partaker.

G4831.full: From a presumed compound of G4862 and G3401; a co-imitator, that is, fellow votary: - follower together.

G4832.full: From G4862 and G3444; jointly formed, that is, (figuratively) similar: - conformed to, fashioned like unto.

G4833.full: From G4832; to render like, that is, (figuratively) to assimilate: - make conformable unto.

G4834.firstSense: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of
G4834.full: From G4835; to feel "sympathy" with, that is, (by implication) to commiserate: - have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.

G4835.full: From G4841; having a fellow feeling ("sympathetic"), that is, (by implication) mutually commiserative: - having compassion one of another.

G4836.full: From G4862 and G3854; to be present together, that is, to convene; by implication to appear in aid: - come together, stand with.

G4837.full: From G4862 and G3870; to console jointly: - comfort together.

G4838.full: From G4862 and G3880; to take along in company: - take with.

G4839.full: From G4862 and G3887; to remain in company, that is, still live: - continue with.

G4840.full: From G4862 and G3918; to be at hand together, that is, now present: - be here present with.

G4841.full: From G4862 and G3958 (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specifically persecution; to "sympathize"): - suffer with.

G4842.full: From G4862 and G3992; to despatch in company: - send with.

G4843.full: From G4862 and a compound of G4012 and G2983; to take by inclosing altogether, that is, earnestly throw the arms about one: - embrace.

G4844.full: From G4862 and G4095; to partake a beverage in company: - drink with.

G4845.full: From G4862 and G4137; to implenish completely, that is, (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passively be complete): - (fully) come, fill up.

G4846.full: From G4862 and G4155; to strangle completely, that is, (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd: - choke, throng.

G4847.full: From G4862 and G4177; a native of the same town, that is, (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow Christian): - fellow-citizen.

G4848.full: From G4862 and G4198; to journey together; by implication to assemble: - go with, resort.

G4849.full: Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4844; a drinking party ("symposium"), that is, (by extension) a room of guests: - company.

G4850.full: From G4862 and G4245; a co-presbyter: - presbyter, also an elder.

G4851.firstSense: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit (-able for)
G4851.full: From G4862 and G5342 (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), that is, (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as noun) advantage: - be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit (-able for).

G4852.full: From G4862 and G5346; to say jointly, that is, assent to: - consent unto.

G4853.full: From G4862 and a derivative of G5443; a co-tribesman, that is, native of the same country: - countryman.

G4854.full: From G4862 and a derivative of G5453; grown along with (connate), that is, (figuratively) closely united to: - planted together.

G4855.full: From G4862 and G5453; passively to grow jointly: - spring up with.

G4856.full: From G4859; to be harmonious, that is, (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact): - agree (together, with).

G4858.full: From G4859; unison of sound ("symphony"), that is, a concert of instruments (harmonious note): - music.

G4859.full: From G4862 and G5456; sounding together (alike), that is, (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement): - consent.

G4860.full: From G4862 and G5585; to compute jointly: - reckon.

G4861.full: From G4862 and G5590; co-spirited, that is, similar in sentiment: - like-minded.

G4862.full: sun soon A primary preposition denoting union; with or together (but much closer than G3326 or G3844), that is, by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc.: - beside, with. In compounds it has similar applications, including completeness.

G4863.firstSense: + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves togethe…
G4863.full: From G4862 and G71; to lead together, that is, collect or convene; specifically to entertain (hospitably): - + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.

G4864.full: From (the reduplicated form of) G4863; an assemblage of persons; specifically a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy a Christian church: - assembly, congregation, synagogue.

G4865.full: From G4862 and G75; to struggle in company with, that is, (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant): - strive together with.

G4866.full: From G4862 and G118; to wrestle in company with, that is, (figuratively) to seek jointly: - labour with, strive together for.

G4867.full: From G4862 and á̓èñïé́æù athroizō (to hoard); to convene: - call (gather) together.

G4868.full: From G4862 and G142; to make up together, that is, (figuratively) to compute (an account): - reckon, take.

G4869.full: From G4862 and G164; a co-captive: - fellowprisoner.

G4870.full: From G4862 and G190; to accompany: - follow.

G4871.full: From G4862 and á̔ëé́æù halizō (to throng); to accumulate, that is, convene: - assemble together.

G4872.full: From G4862 and G305; to ascend in company with: - come up with.

G4873.firstSense: sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat)
G4873.full: From G4862 and G345; to recline in company with (at a meal): - sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).

G4874.full: From G4862 and a compound of G303 and G3396; to mix up together, that is, (figuratively) associate with: - (have, keep) company (with).

G4875.full: Middle voice from G4862 and G373; to recruit oneself in company with: - refresh with.

G4876.full: From G4862 and a derivative of G473; to meet with; figuratively to occur: - befall, meet.

G4877.full: From G4876; a meeting with: - meet.

G4878.full: From G4862 and G482; to take hold of opposite together, that is, co-operate (assist): - help.

G4879.full: From G4862 and G520; to take off together, that is, transport with (seduce, passively yield): - carry (lead) away with, condescend.

G4880.full: From G4862 and G599; to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively) similarly to: - be dead (die) with.

G4881.full: From G4862 and G622; to destroy (middle voice or passive voice, be slain) in company with: - perish with.

G4882.full: From G4862 and G649; to despatch (on an errand) in company with: - send you.

G4883.full: From G4862 and a derivative of a compound of G719 and G3004 (in its original sense of laying); to render close jointed together, that is, organize compactly: - be fitly framed (joined) together.

G4884.full: From G4862 and G726; to snatch together, that is, seize: - catch.

G4885.full: From G4862 and G837; to increase (grow up) together: - grow together.

G4886.full: From G4862 and G1199; a joint tie, that is, ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control: - band, bond.

G4887.full: From G4862 and G1210; to bind with, that is, (passively) be a fellow prisoner (figuratively): - be bound with.

G4888.full: From G4862 and G1392; to exalt to dignity in company (that is, similarly) with: - glorify together.

G4889.full: From G4862 and G1401; a co-slave, that is, servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine): - fellowservant.

G4890.full: From (the alternate of) G4936; a running together, that is, (riotous) concourse: - run together.

G4891.full: From G4862 and G1453; to rouse (from death) in company with, that is, (figuratively) to revivify (spiritually) in resemblance to: - raise up together, rise with.

G4892.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4862 and the base of G1476; a joint session, that is, (specifically) the Jewish Sanhedrim; by analogy a subordinate tribunal: - council.

G4893.full: From a prolonged form of G4894; co-perception, that is, moral consciousness: - conscience.

G4894.firstSense: consider, know, be privy, be ware of
G4894.full: From G4862 and G1492; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of: - consider, know, be privy, be ware of.

G4895.full: From G4862 and G1510 (including its various inflections); to be in company with, that is, present at the time: - be with.

G4896.full: From G4862 and åé͂ìé eimi (to go); to assemble: - gather together.

G4897.firstSense: go in with, go with into
G4897.full: From G4862 and G1525; to enter in company with: - go in with, go with into.

G4898.full: From G4862 and the base of G1553; a co-absentee from home, that is, fellow traveller: - companion in travel, travel with.

G4899.full: From a compound of G4862 and G1586; chosen in company with, that is, co-elect (fellow Christian): - elected together with.

G4900.full: From G4862 and G1643; to drive together, that is, (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation): - + set at one again.

G4901.full: From G4862 and G1957; to testify further jointly, that is, unite in adding evidence: - also bear witness.

G4902.full: Middle voice from G4862 and a primary word å̔́ðù hepō (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with: - accompany.

G4903.full: From G4904; to be a fellow worker, that is, co-operate: - help (work) with, work (-er) together.

G4904.firstSense: companion in labour, (fellow-) helper (-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, wor…
G4904.full: From a presumed compound of G4862 and the base of G2041; a co-laborer, that is, coadjutor: - companion in labour, (fellow-) helper (-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.

G4905.firstSense: accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort
G4905.full: From G4862 and G2064; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specifically) cohabit (conjugally): - accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.

G4906.full: From G4862 and G2068 (including its alternate); to take food in company with: - eat with.

G4907.full: From G4920; a mental putting together, that is, intelligence or (concretely) the intellect: - knowledge, understanding.

G4908.full: From G4920; mentally put (or putting) together, that is, sagacious: - prudent. Compare G5429.

G4909.firstSense: allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure
G4909.full: From G4862 and G2106; to think well of in common, that is, assent to, feel gratified with: - allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure.

G4910.full: From G4862 and a derivative of a presumed compound of G2095 and a derivative of G2192 (meaning to be in good condition, that is, [by implication] to fare well, or feast); to entertain sumptuously in company with, that is, (middle or passive voice) to revel together: - feast with.

G4911.full: From G4862 and G2186; to stand up together, that is, to resist (or assault) jointly: - rise up together.

G4912.firstSense: constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken…
G4912.full: From G4862 and G2192; to hold together, that is, to compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy: - constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.

G4913.full: Middle voice from G4862 and the base of G2237; to rejoice in with oneself, that is, feel satisfaction concerning: - delight.

G4914.full: From a compound of G4862 and G2239; mutual habituation, that is, usage: - custom.

G4915.full: From G4862 and a derivative of G2244; a co-aged person, that is, alike in years: - equal.

G4916.full: From G4862 and G2290; to inter in company with, that is, (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin): - bury with.

G4917.full: From G4862 and èëá́ù thlaō (to crush); to dash together, that is, shatter: - break.

G4918.full: From G4862 and G2346; to compress, that is, crowd on all sides: - throng.

G4919.full: From G4862 and èñṍðôù thruptō (to crumble); to crush together, that is, (figuratively) to dispirit: - break.

G4920.full: From G4862 and é̔́çìé hiēmi (to send); to put together, that is, (mentally) to comprehend; by implication to act piously: - consider, understand, be wise.

G4921.full: soon-is-tah'-o, soon-is-tah'-an'-o, soon-is-tah'-ay-mee From G4862 and G2476 (including its collateral forms); to set together, that is, (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute: - approve, commend, consist, make, stand (with).

G4922.full: From G4862 and G3593; to travel in company with: - journey with.

G4923.full: From a compound of G4862 and G3598 ("synod"); companionship on a journey, that is, (by implication) a caravan: - company.

G4924.full: From G4862 and G3611; to reside together (as a family): - dwell together.

G4925.full: From G4862 and G3618; to construct, that is, (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively): - build together.

G4926.full: From G4862 and G3656; to converse mutually: - talk with.

G4927.full: From G4862 and a derivative of a compound of the base of G3674 and the base of G3725; to border together, that is, adjoin: - join hard.

G4928.full: From G4912; restraint, that is, (figuratively) anxiety: - anguish, distress.

G4929.full: From G4862 and G5021; to arrange jointly, that is, (figuratively) to direct: - appoint.

G4930.full: From G4931; entire completion, that is, consummation (of a dispensation): - end.

G4931.full: From G4862 and G5055; to complete entirely; generally to execute (literally or figuratively): - end, finish, fulfil, make.

G4932.full: From G4862 and the base of G5114; to contract by cutting, that is, (figuratively) do concisely (speedily): - (cut) short.

G4933.full: From G4862 and G5083; to keep closely together, that is, (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally to remember (and obey): - keep, observe, preserve.

G4934.full: Middle voice from G4862 and G5087; to place jointly, that is, (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur: - agree assent, covenant.

G4935.full: Adverb from a derivative of G4932; concisely (briefly): - a few words.

G4936.full: From G4862 and G5143 (including its alternate); to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively): - run (together, with).

G4937.firstSense: break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise
G4937.full: From G4862 and the base of G5147; to crush completely, that is, to shatter (literally or figuratively): - break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.

G4938.full: From G4937; concussion or utter fracture (properly concretely), that is, complete ruin: - destruction.

G4939.full: From G4862 and G5162 (in a passive sense); a fellow nursling, that is, comrade: - brought up with.

G4940.full: From G4862 and G5177; to chance together, that is, meet with (reach): - come at.

G4941.full: From G4940; an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female: - Syntyche.

G4942.full: From G4862 and G5271; to act hypocritically in concert with: - dissemble with.

G4943.full: From G4862 and a derivative of a compound of G5259 and the base of G2041; to be a co-auxiliary, that is, assist: - help together.

G4944.full: From G4862 and G5605; to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, that is, (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering): - travail in pain together.

G4945.full: From a compound of G4862 and G3660; a swearing together, that is, (by implication) a plot: - conspiracy.

G4946.full: Plural of uncertain derivation; Syracusae, the capital of Sicily: - Syracuse.

G4947.full: Probably of Hebrew origin [H6865]; Syria (that is, Tsyria or Tyre), a region of Asia: - Syria.

G4948.full: From the same as G4947; a Syran (that is, probably Tyrian), a native of Syria: - Syrian.

G4949.full: Feminine of a compound of G4948 and the same as G5403; a Syro-Phaenician woman, that is, a female native of Phaenicia in Syria: - Syrophenician.

G4950.full: From G4951; a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), that is, the Syrtis Major or great bay on the North coast of Africa: - quicksands.

G4951.full: Probably akin to G138; to trail: - drag, draw, hale.

G4952.full: From G4862 and G4682; to rend completely, that is, (by analogy) to convulse violently: - throw down.

G4953.full: Neuter of a compound of G4862 and the base of G4591; a sign in common, that is, preconcerted signal: - token.

G4954.full: From G4862 and G4983; of a joint body, that is, (figuratively) a fellow member of the Christian community: - of the same body.

G4955.full: From a compound of G4862 and a derivative of G4714; a fellow insurgent: - make insurrection with.

G4956.full: From a derivative of G4921; introductory, that is, recommendatory: - of commendation.

G4957.full: From G4862 and G4717; to impale in company with (literally or figuratively): - crucify with.

G4958.full: From G4862 and G4724; to send (draw) together, that is, enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval): - short, wind up.

G4959.full: From G4862 and G4727; to moan jointly, that is, (figuratively) experience a common calamity: - groan together.

G4960.full: From G4862 and G4748; to file together (as soldiers in ranks), that is, (figuratively) to correspond to: - answer to.

G4961.full: From G4862 and G4757; a co-campaigner, that is, (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil: - fellowsoldier.

G4962.full: From G4862 and G4762; to twist together, that is, collect (a bundle, a crowd): - gather.

G4963.full: From G4962; a twisting together, that is, (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd: - + band together, concourse.

G4964.firstSense: conform to, fashion self according to
G4964.full: From G4862 and a derivative of G4976; to fashion alike, that is, conform to the same pattern (figuratively): - conform to, fashion self according to.

G4965.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7941]; Sychar (that is, Shekar), a place in Palestine: - Sychar.

G4966.full: Of Hebrew origin [H7927]; Sychem (that is, Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine: - Sychem.

G4967.full: From G4969; butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or [figuratively] of men [destruction]): - slaughter.

G4968.full: Neuter of a derivative of G4967; a victim (in sacrifice): - slain beast.

G4969.full: A primary verb; to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specifically) to maim (violently): - kill, slay, wound.

G4970.full: Neuter plural of óöïäñḯò sphodros (violent; of uncertain derivation) as adverb; vehemently, that is, in a high degree, much: - exceeding (-ly), greatly, sore, very.

G4971.full: Adverbially from the same as G4970; very much: - exceedingly.

G4972.firstSense: (set a, set to) seal up, stop
G4972.full: From G4973; to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication to keep secret, to attest: - (set a, set to) seal up, stop.

G4973.full: Probably strengthened from G5420; a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively: - seal.

G4974.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as óöáé͂ñá sphaira (a ball, "sphere"; compare the feminine óöõ͂ñá sphura , a hammer); the ankle (as globular): - ancle bone.

G4975.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192 as an adverb; nigh, that is, nearly: - almost.

G4976.full: From the alternate of G2192; a figure (as a mode or circumstance), that is, (by implication) external condition: - fashion.

G4977.firstSense: break, divide, open, rend, make a rent
G4977.full: Apparently a primary verb; to split or sever (literally or figuratively): - break, divide, open, rend, make a rent.

G4978.full: From G4977; a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively: - division, rent, schism.

G4979.full: Diminutive of ó÷ïé͂íïò schoinos (a rush or flag plant; of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, that is, grass withe or tie (genitive case): - small cord, rope.

G4980.full: From G4981; to take a holiday, that is, be at leisure for (by implication devote oneself wholly to); figuratively to be vacant (of a house): - empty, give self.

G4981.full: Probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192; properly loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, that is, (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment): - school.

G4982.firstSense: heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole
G4982.full: From a primary word óù͂ò sōs̄ (contraction for the obsolete óá́ïò saos, "safe"); to save, that is, deliver or protect (literally or figuratively): - heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole.

G4983.full: From G4982; the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively: - bodily, body, slave.

G4984.full: From G4983; corporeal or physical: - bodily.

G4985.full: Adverb from G4984; corporeally or physically: - bodily.

G4986.full: From the base of G4982 and G3962; of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian: - Sopater. Compare G4989.

G4987.full: From another form of G4673; to pile up (literally or figuratively): - heap, load.

G4988.full: From the base of G4982 and that of G4599; of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian: - Sosthenes.

G4989.full: Prolongation for G4986; Sosipatrus, a Christian: - Sosipater.

G4990.full: From G4982; a deliverer, that is, God or Christ: - saviour.

G4991.full: Feminine of a derivative of G4990 as (properly abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally): - deliver, health, salvation, save, saving.

G4992.full: Neuter of the same as G4991 as (properly concrete) noun; defender or (by implication) defence: - salvation.

G4993.firstSense: be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly
G4993.full: From G4998; to be of sound mind, that is, sane, (figuratively) moderate: - be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly.

G4994.full: From G4998; to make of sound mind, that is, (figuratively) to discipline or correct: - teach to be sober.

G4995.full: From G4994; discipline, that is, self control: - sound mind.

G4996.full: Adverb from G4998; with sound mind, that is, moderately: - soberly.

G4997.full: From G4998; soundness of mind, that is, (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self control: - soberness, sobriety.

G4998.full: From the base of G4982 and that of G5424; safe (sound) in mind, that is, self controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion): - discreet, sober, temperate.

G4999.full: Plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden walled buildings; Tabernae: - taverns.

G5000.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H6646]); the gazelle; Tabitha (that is, Tabjetha), a Christian female: - Tabitha.

G5001.full: From G5021; something orderly in arrangement (a troop), that is, (figuratively) a series or succession: - order.

G5002.full: From G5021; arranged, that is, appointed or stated: - set.

G5003.full: From G5005; to be wretched, that is, realize one's own misery: - be afflicted.

G5004.full: From G5005; wretchedness, that is, calamity: - misery.

G5005.full: From the base of G5007 and a derivative of the base of G3984; enduring trial, that is, miserable: - wretched.

G5006.full: From G5007; talent like in weight: - weight of a talent.

G5007.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of ôëá́ù tlao4 (to bear; equivalent to G5342); a balance (as supporting weights), that is, (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent": - talent.

G5008.full: Of Chaldee origin (compare [H2924]); the fresh, that is, young girl; talitha (O maiden): - talitha.

G5009.full: Neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of ôáìé́áò tamias (a dispenser or distributor; akin to ôǻìíù temnō, to cut); a dispensary or magazine, that is, a chamber on the ground floor or interior of an Oriental house (generally used for storage or privacy, a spot for retirement): - secret chamber, closet, storehouse.

G5010.full: From G5021; regular arrangement, that is, (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity: - order.

G5011.firstSense: base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly
G5011.full: Of uncertain derivation; depressed, that is, (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition): - base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly.

G5012.firstSense: humbleness of mind, humility (of mind), lowliness (of mind)
G5012.full: From a compound of G5011 and the base of G5424; humiliation of mind, that is, modesty: - humbleness of mind, humility (of mind), lowliness (of mind).

G5013.full: From G5011; to depress; figuratively to humiliate (in condition or heart): - abase, bring low, humble (self).

G5014.firstSense: humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile
G5014.full: From G5013; depression (in rank or feeling): - humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile.

G5015.full: Of uncertain affinity; to stir or agitate (roil water): - trouble.

G5016.full: Feminine from G5015; disturbance, that is, (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition: - trouble (-ing).

G5017.full: Masculine From G5015; a disturbance, that is, (popular) tumult: - stir.

G5018.full: From G5019; a Tarsean, that is, native of Tarsus: - of Tarsus.

G5019.full: Perhaps the same as ôáñóḯò tarsos (a flat basket); Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor: - Tarsus.

G5020.full: From Ôá́ñôáñïò Tartaros̄ (the deepest abyss of Hades); to incarcerate in eternal torment: - cast down to hell.

G5021.full: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses); to arrange in an orderly manner, that is, assign or dispose (to a certain position or lot): - addict, appoint, determine, ordain, set.

G5022.full: Apparently a primary word (compare [H8450], "steer"); a bullock: - bull, ox.

G5023.firstSense: + afterward, follow, + hereafter, X him, the same, so, such, that, then, these, they, t…
G5023.full: Nomitive or accusative neuter plural of G3778; these things: - + afterward, follow, + hereafter, X him, the same, so, such, that, then, these, they, this, those, thus.

G5024.full: Neuter plural of G3588 and G846 as adverb; in the same way: - even thus, (manner) like, so.

G5025.full: Dative and accusative feminine plural respectively of G3778; (to or with or by, etc.) these: - hence, that, then, these, those.

G5026.firstSense: her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same)
G5026.full: Dative, accusative and genitive case respectively of the feminine singular of G3778; (towards or of) this: - her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same).

G5027.full: feminine from G2290; burial (the act): - X bury.

G5028.full: Masculine from G2290; a grave (the place of interment): - sepulchre, tomb.

G5029.full: As if neuter plural of G5036 (adverbially); shortly, that is, (figuratively) possibly: - peradventure (-haps).

G5030.full: Adverb from G5036; briefly, that is, (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly: - hastily, quickly, shortly, soon, suddenly.

G5031.full: From G5034; curt, that is, impending: - shortly, swift.

G5032.full: Neuter singular of the comparative of G5036 (as adverb); more swiftly, that is, (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily: - out [run], quickly, shortly, sooner.

G5033.full: Neuter plural of the superlative of G5036 (as adverb); most quickly, that is, (with G5613 prefixed) as soon as possible: - + with all speed.

G5034.full: From the same as G5036; a brief space (of time), that is, (with G1722 prefixed) in haste: - + quickly, + shortly, + speedily.

G5035.full: Neuter singular of G5036 (as adverb); shortly, that is, without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication of ease) readily: - lightly, quickly.

G5036.full: Of uncertain affinity; fleet, that is, (figuratively) prompt or ready: - swift.

G5037.firstSense: also, and, both, even, then whether
G5037.full: te teh A primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition; both or also (properly as a correlation of G2532): - also, and, both, even, then whether. Often used in compounds, usually as the latter part.

G5038.full: Akin to the base of G5088; a wall (as formative of a house): - wall.

G5039.full: tek-may'-ree-on; Neuter of a presumed derivative of ôåêìá́ñ tekmar (a goal or fixed limit); a token (as defining a fact), that is, criterion of certainty: - infallible proof.

G5040.full: Diminutive of G5043; an infant, that is, (plural figurative) darlings (Christian converts): - little children.

G5041.full: From a compound of G5043 and the base of G1096; to be a child bearer, that is, parent (mother): - bear children.

G5042.full: From the same as G5041; childbirth (parentage), that is, (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties): - childbearing.

G5043.full: From the base of G5098; a child (as produced): - child, daughter, son.

G5044.full: From a compound of G5043 and G5142; to be a child rearer, that is, fulfil the duties of a female parent: - bring up children.

G5045.full: From the base of G5098; an artificer (as producer of fabrics), that is, (specifically) a craftsman in wood: - carpenter.

G5046.full: From G5056; complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with G3588) completeness: - of full age, man, perfect.

G5047.full: From G5046; (the state) completeness (mentally or morally): - perfection (-ness).

G5048.full: From G5046; to complete, that is, (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character): - consecrate, finish, fulfil, (make) perfect.

G5049.full: Adverb from G5046; completely, that is, (of hope) without wavering: - to the end.

G5050.full: From G5448; (the act) completion, that is, (of prophecy) verification, or (of expiation) absolution: - perfection, performance.

G5051.full: From G5048; a completer, that is, consummater: - finisher.

G5052.full: From a compound of G5056 and G5342; to be a bearer to completion (maturity), that is, to ripen fruit (figuratively): - bring fruit to perfection.

G5053.full: From a presumed derivative of G5055; to finish life (by implication of G979), that is, expire (demise): - be dead, decease, die.

G5055.firstSense: accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform
G5055.full: From G5056; to end, that is, complete, execute, conclude, discharge (a debt): - accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform.

G5056.full: From a primary word ôǻëëù tellō (to set out for a definite point or goal); properly the point aimed at as a limit, that is, (by implication) the conclusion of an act or state (termination [literally, figuratively or indefinitely], result [immediate, ultimate or prophetic], purpose); specifically an impost or levy (as paid): - + continual, custom, end (-ing), finally, uttermost. Compare G5411.

G5057.full: From G5056 and G5608; a tax farmer, that is, collector of public revenue: - publican.

G5058.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of G5057; a tax gatherer's place of business: - receipt of custom.

G5059.full: Of uncertain affinity; a prodigy or omen: - wonder.

G5060.full: Of Latin origin; third; Tertius, a Christian: - Tertius.

G5061.full: Of uncertain derivation; Tertullus, a Roman: - Tertullus.

G5062.full: The decade of G5064; forty: - forty.

G5063.full: From G5062 and G2094; of forty years of age: - (+ full, of) forty years (old).

G5064.full: Neuter and a plural number; four: - four.

G5065.full: From G5064 and G2532 and G1182; fourteenth: - fourteenth.

G5066.full: From G5064; pertaining to the fourth day: - four days.

G5068.full: From G5064 and G1137; four cornered, that is, square: - foursquare.

G5069.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of ôǻôñáò tetras (a tetrad; from G5064); a quaternion or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers: - quaternion.

G5070.full: From the multiplicative adverb of G5064 and G5507; four times a thousand: - four thousand.

G5071.full: Neuter and plural from G5064 and G1540; four hundred: - four hundred.

G5072.full: Neuter of a compound of G5064 and G3376; a four months' space: - four months.

G5073.full: From G5064 and a derivative of the base of G4118; quadruple: - fourfold.

G5074.full: From G5064 and G4228; a quadruped: - fourfooted beast.

G5075.full: From G5076; to be a tetrarch: - (be) tetrarch.

G5076.full: From G5064 and G757; the ruler of a fourth part of a country ("tetrarch"): - tetrarch.

G5077.full: From ôǻöñá tephra (ashes); to incinerate, that is, consume: - turn to ashes.

G5078.full: From the base of G5088; art (as productive), that is, (specifically) a trade, or (generally) skill: - art, craft, occupation.

G5079.full: From G5078; an artisan; figuratively a founder (Creator): - builder, craftsman.

G5080.full: Apparently a primary verb; to liquefy: - melt.

G5081.full: tēlaugōs tay-low-goce Adverb from a compound of a derivative of G5056 and G827; in a far shining manner, that is, plainly: - clearly.

G5082.full: Masculine and feminine; from a compound of G3588 with G2245 and G3778; such as this, that is, (in [figuratively] magnitude) so vast: - so great, so mighty.

G5083.firstSense: hold fast, keep (-er), (ob-, pre-, re) serve, watch
G5083.full: From ôçñḯò teros (a watch; perhaps akin to G2334); to guard (from loss or injury, properly by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from G5442, which is properly to prevent escaping; and from G2892, which implies a fortress or full military lines of apparatus), that is, to note (a prophecy; figuratively to fulfil a command); by implication to detain (in custody; figuratively to maintain); by extension to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively to keep unmarried): - hold fast, keep (-er), (ob-, pre-, re) serve, watch.

G5084.full: From G5083; a watching, that is, (figuratively) observance, or (concretely) a prison: - hold.

G5085.full: From G5086; Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine: - Tiberias.

G5086.full: Of Latin origin; probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor: - Tiberius.

G5087.firstSense: + advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), ma…
G5087.full: A prolonged form of a primary word èǻù theō (which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses); to place (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from G2476, which properly denotes an upright and active position, while G2749 is properly reflexive and utterly prostrate): - + advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down.

G5088.firstSense: bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail
G5088.full: A strengthened from of a primary word ôǻêù tekō (which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses); to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literal or figurative: - bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.

G5089.full: Perhaps akin to the alternate of G138, and thus to G4951; to pull off: - pluck.

G5090.full: Probably of Chaldee origin (compare [H2931]); Timoeus (that is, Timay), an Israelite: - Timaeus.

G5091.full: From G5093; to prize, that is, fix a valuation upon; by implication to revere: - honour, value.

G5092.full: From G5099; a value, that is, money paid, or (concretely and collectively) valuables; by analogy esteem (especially of the highest degree), or the dignity itself: - honour, precious, price, some.

G5093.firstSense: dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation
G5093.full: Including the comparative ôé́ìéù́ôåñïò timiōteros and the superlative ôé́ìéù́ôáôïò timiōtatos; from G5092; valuable, that is, (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved: - dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation.

G5094.full: From G5093; expensiveness, that is, (by implication) magnificence: - costliness.

G5095.full: From G5092 and G2316; dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian: - Timotheus, Timothy.

G5096.full: From G5092; valuable; Timon, a Christian: - Timon.

G5097.full: From a compound of G5092 and ïõ̓͂ñïò ouros (a guard); properly to protect one's honor, that is, to avenge (inflict a penalty): - punish.

G5098.full: From G5097; vindication, that is, (by implication) a penalty: - punishment.

G5099.full: Strengthened for a primary word ôé́ù tiō (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses); to pay a price, that is, as a penalty: - be punished with.

G5100.firstSense: a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, o…
G5100.full: tis tis An enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object: - a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, -thing, -what), (+ that no-) thing, what (-soever), X wherewith, whom [-soever], whose ([-soever]).

G5101.firstSense: every man, how (much), + no (-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where ([-by, -fore, -of…
G5101.full: tis tis Probably emphatic of G5100; an interrogitive pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions): - every man, how (much), + no (-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where ([-by, -fore, -of, -unto, -with, -withal]), whether, which, who (-m, -se), why.

G5102.full: Of Latin origin; a titulus or "title" (placard): - title.

G5103.full: Of Latin origin but uncertain significance; Titus, a Christian: - Titus.

G5104.firstSense: [used only with other particles in compounds, as G2544, G3305, G5105, G5106, etc
G5104.full: toi toy Probably for the dative case of G3588; an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth: - [used only with other particles in compounds, as G2544, G3305, G5105, G5106, etc.]

G5105.full: From G5104 and G1063 and G3767; truly for then, that is, consequently: - there- (where-) fore.

G5106.full: From G5104 and G3568; truly now, that is, accordingly: - then, therefore.

G5107.full: (Including the other inflections); from a derivative of G5104 and G1161; such like then, that is, so great: - such.

G5108.full: (Including the other inflections); from G5104 and G3778; truly this, that is, of this sort (to denote character or individuality): - like, such (an one).

G5109.full: Another form of G5038; a wall: - wall.

G5110.full: From the base of G5088; interest on money loaned (as a produce): - usury.

G5111.full: From ôḯëìá tolma (boldness; probably itself from the base of G5056 through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while G2292 is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication to be courageous: - be bold, boldly, dare, durst.

G5112.full: Neuter of the compound of a derivative of the bse of G5111 (as adverb); more daringly, that is, with greater confidence than otherwise: - the more boldly.

G5113.full: From G5111; a daring (audacious) man: - presumptuous.

G5114.full: Compound of a derivative of the primary word ôǻìíù temnō (to cut; more comprehensive or decisive than G2875, as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen: - sharper.

G5115.full: From the base of G5088; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric): - bow.

G5116.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative (alternate) of ôḯðá́æïò topazos (a "topaz"; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite: - topaz.

G5117.firstSense: coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where
G5117.full: Apparently a primary word; a spot (generally in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas G5561 is a larger but particular locality), that is, location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively condition, opportunity; specifically a scabbard: - coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.

G5118.firstSense: as large, so great (long, many, much), these many
G5118.full: From ôḯóïò tosos (so much; apparently from G3588 and G3739) and G3778 (including its variations); so vast as this, that is, such (in quantity, amount, number or space): - as large, so great (long, many, much), these many.

G5119.full: From (the neuter of) G3588 and G3753; the when, that is, at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution): - that time, then.

G5120.full: tou too Properly the genitive case of G3588; sometimes used for G5127; of this person: - his.

G5121.full: Contraction for the neuter of G3588 and G1726; on the contrary: - contrariwise.

G5122.full: Contraction for the neuter of G3588 and G3686; the name (is): - named.

G5123.full: Contraction for G5124 and G2076; that is: - that is (to say).

G5124.firstSense: here [-unto], it, partly, self [-same], so, that (intent), the same, there [-fore, -unt…
G5124.full: Neuter, singular, nomitive or accusative of G3778; that thing: - here [-unto], it, partly, self [-same], so, that (intent), the same, there [-fore, -unto], this, thus, where [-fore].

G5125.firstSense: such, them, there [-in, -with], these, this, those
G5125.full: Dative, plural, masculine or neuter of G3778; to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things): - such, them, there [-in, -with], these, this, those.

G5126.full: Accusative, singular, masculine of G3778; this (person, as object of verb or preposition): - him, the same, that, this.

G5127.firstSense: here [-by], him, it, + such manner of, that, thence [-forth], thereabout, this, thus
G5127.full: Genitive singular masculine or neuter of G3778; of (from or concerning) this (person or thing): - here [-by], him, it, + such manner of, that, thence [-forth], thereabout, this, thus.

G5128.full: Accusative plural masculine of G3778; these (persons, as object of verb or preposition): - such, them, these, this.

G5129.firstSense: here [-by, -in], him, one, the same, there [-in], this
G5129.full: Dative singular masculine or neuter of G3778; to (in, with or by) this (person or thing): - here [-by, -in], him, one, the same, there [-in], this.

G5130.firstSense: such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those
G5130.full: Genitive plural masculine or neuter of G3778; of (from or concerning) these (persons or things): - such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those.

G5131.full: From the base of G5176; a he goat (as a gnawer): - goat.

G5132.full: Probably contracted from G5064 and G3979; a table or stool (as being four legged), usually for food (figuratively a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively a broker's office for loans at interest): - bank, meat, table.

G5133.full: From G5132; a money broker or banker: - exchanger.

G5134.full: From the base of ôéôñù́óêù titrōskō (to wound; akin to the base of G2352, G5147, G5149, etc.); a wound: - wound.

G5135.full: From G5134; to inflict a wound: - wound.

G5136.full: From G5137; to seize by the throat or neck, that is, to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally to lay bare): - opened.

G5137.full: Probably from G5143 (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), that is, (figuratively) life: - neck.

G5138.full: Perhaps strengthened from the base of G4486 (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy): - rock, rough.

G5139.full: From a derivative of G5138; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria: - Trachonitis.

G5141.full: Strengthened from a primary word ôñǻù treō (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear: - be afraid, trembling.

G5142.full: A primary verb (properly èñǻöù threphō; but perhaps strengthened from the base of G5157 through the idea of convolution); properly to stiffen, that is, fatten (by implication to cherish [with food, etc.], pamper, rear): - bring up, feed, nourish.

G5143.full: Apparently a primary verb (properly èñǻ÷ù threchō; compare G2359); which uses äñǻìù dremō, drem'-o (the base of G1408) as an alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively): - have course, run.

G5144.full: The decade of G5140; thirty: - thirty.

G5145.full: Plural from G5140 and G1540; three hundred: - three hundred.

G5146.full: From G5140 and G956; properly a crow foot (three pronged obstruction in war), that is, (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop): - brier, thistle.

G5147.full: From ôñé́âù tribō (to "rub"; akin to ôåé́ñù teirō, ôñṍù truō, and the base of G5131, G5134); a rut or worn track: - path.

G5148.full: From a compound of G5140 and G2094; a three years' period (triennium): - space of three years.

G5149.full: Apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), that is, (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy): - gnash.

G5150.full: Neuter of a compound of G5140 and G3376 as noun; a three months' space: - three months.

G5151.full: tris trece Adverb from G5140; three times: - three times, thrice.

G5152.full: Neuter of a compound of G5140 and G4721 as noun; a third roof (story): - third loft.

G5153.full: From G5151 and G5507; three times a thousand: - three thousand.

G5154.full: From G5140; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly: - third (-ly).

G5155.full: From G2359; hairy, that is, made of hair (mohair): - of hair.

G5156.full: From G5141; a "trembling", that is, quaking with fear: - + tremble (-ing).

G5157.full: From an apparently primary word ôñǻðù trepō (to turn); a turn ("trope"), that is, revolution (figuratively variation): - turning.

G5158.firstSense: (even) as, conversation, [+ like] manner (+ by any) means, way
G5158.full: From the same as G5157; a turn, that is, (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relatively prefixed as adverb like); figuratively deportment or character: - (even) as, conversation, [+ like] manner (+ by any) means, way.

G5159.full: From G5158 and G5409; to endure one's habits: - suffer the manners.

G5160.full: From G5142; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication rations (wages): - food, meat.

G5161.full: From G5160; nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian: - Trophimus.

G5162.full: From G5142; a nourisher, that is, nurse: - nurse.

G5163.full: From G5164; a track (as a wheel rut), that is, (figuratively) a course of conduct: - path.

G5164.full: From G5143; a wheel (as a runner), that is, (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects: - course.

G5165.full: Neuter of a presumed derivation of uncertain affinity; a bowl: - dish.

G5166.full: From a derivative of ôñṍãù trugō (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage: - gather.

G5167.full: From ôñṍæù truzō (to murmur; akin to G5149, but denoting a duller sound); a turtle dove (as cooing): - turtle-dove.

G5168.full: From a derivative of ôñṍù́ truō (to wear away; akin to the base of G5134, G5147 and G5176); an orifice, that is, a needle's eye: - eye. Compare G5169.

G5169.full: From a derivative of the base of G5168; an aperture, that is, a needle's eye: - eye.

G5170.full: From G5172; luxurious; Tryphaena, a Christian woman: - Tryphena.

G5171.full: From G5172; to indulge in luxury: - live in pleasure.

G5172.full: From èñṍðôù thruptō̄ (to break up or [figuratively] enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, that is, luxury or debauchery: - delicately, riot.

G5173.full: From G5172; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female: - Tryphosa.

G5174.full: From Ôñḯò Tros (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), that is, Troas, a place in Asia Minor: - Troas.

G5175.full: Of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor: - Trogyllium.

G5176.full: Probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of G5134 and G5147 through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of G5167 and G5149 through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, that is, (genitive case) to eat: - eat.

G5177.firstSense: be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh
G5177.full: Probably for an obsolete ôṍ÷ù tuchō (for which the middle voice of another alternate ôåṍ÷ù teuchō [to make ready or bring to pass] is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of G5088 through the idea of effecting; properly to affect; or (specifically) to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), that is, (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonally (with G1487), that is, perchance; or (present participle) as adjective usual (as if commonly met with, with G3756, extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb by accident (as it were): - be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh . . . self, + special. Compare G5180.

G5178.full: From a derivative of G5180 (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death: - torture.

G5179.firstSense: en- (ex-) ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print
G5179.full: From G5180; a die (as struck), that is, (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy a shape, that is, a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specifically a sampler ("type"), that is, a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning): - en- (ex-) ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.

G5180.full: A primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", that is, cudgel or pummel (properly with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from G3817 and G3960, which denote a [usually single] blow with the hand or any instrument, or G4141 with the fist [or a hammer], or G4474 with the palm; as well as from G5177, an accidental collision); by implication to punish; figuratively to offend (the conscience): - beat, smite, strike, wound.

G5181.full: A provincial form of the derivative of the base of G2962; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian: - Tyrannus.

G5182.full: From ôṍñâç turbē̄ (Latin turba, a crowd; akin to G2351); to make "turbid", that is, disturb: - trouble.

G5183.full: From G5184; a Tyrian, that is, inhabitant of Tyrus: - of Tyre.

G5184.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6865]; Tyrus (that is, Tsor), a place in Palestine: - Tyre.

G5185.full: From G5187; opaque (as if smoky), that is, (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally): - blind.

G5186.full: From G5185; to make blind, that is, (figuratively) to obscure: - blind.

G5187.firstSense: high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud
G5187.full: From a derivative of G5188; to envelop with smoke, that is, (figuratively) to inflate with self conceit: - high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.

G5188.full: Apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, that is, slowly consume without flame: - smoke.

G5189.full: From a derivative of G5188; stormy (as if smoky): - tempestuous.

G5190.full: From a derivative of G5177; fortuitous, that is, fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian: - Tychicus.

G5191.full: From G5192; "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", that is, deep blue: - jacinth.

G5192.full: Of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", that is, some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon: - jacinth.

G5193.full: From G5194; glassy, that is, transparent: - of glass.

G5194.full: Perhaps from the same as G5205 (as being transparent like rain); glass: - glass.

G5195.full: From G5196; to exercise violence, that is, abuse: - use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).

G5196.full: From G5228; insolence (as over bearing), that is, insult, injury: - harm, hurt, reproach.

G5197.full: From G5195; an insulter, that is, maltreater: - de-spiteful, injurious.

G5198.firstSense: be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole (-some)
G5198.full: From G5199; to have sound health, that is, be well (in body); figuratively to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine): - be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole (-some).

G5199.full: From the base of G837; healthy, that is, well (in body); figuratively true (in doctrine): - sound, whole.

G5200.full: From the base of G5205; wet (as if with rain), that is, (by implication) sappy (fresh): - green.

G5201.full: From G5204; a water jar, that is, receptacle for family supply: - waterpot.

G5202.full: From a compound of G5204 and a derivative of G4095; to be a water drinker, that is, to abstain from vinous beverages: - drink water.

G5203.full: From a compound of G5204 and a derivative of G3700 (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical": - have the dropsy.

G5204.full: From the base of G5205; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively: - water.

G5205.full: From a primary word õ̔́ù huō (to rain); rain, especially a shower: - rain.

G5206.full: From a presumed compound of G5207 and a derivative of G5087; the placing as a son, that is, adoption (figuratively Christian sonship in respect to God): - adoption (of children, of sons).

G5207.full: Apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figurative kinship: - child, foal, son.

G5208.full: Perhaps akin to G3586; a forest, that is, (by implication) fuel: - matter.

G5209.full: Accusative of G5210; you (as the object of a verb or preposition): - ye, you, (+ -ward), your (+ own).

G5210.full: Irregular plural of G4771; you (as subject of verb): - ye (yourselves), you.

G5211.full: From Õ̔ìḉí Humēn (the god of weddings); "hymenaeal"; Hymenaeus, an opponent of Christianity: - Hymenus.

G5212.full: From G5210; yours, that is, pertaining to you: - your (own).

G5213.full: Irregular dative case of G5210; to (with or by) you: - ye, you, your (-selves).

G5214.full: From G5215; to hymn, that is, sing a religious ode; by implication to celebrate (God) in song: - sing an hymn (praise unto).

G5215.full: Apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of õ̔́äǻù hudeō (to celebrate; probably akin to G103; compare G5567); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms): - hymn.

G5216.full: Genitive case of G5210; of (from or concerning) you: - ye, you, your (own, -selves).

G5217.full: From G5259 and G71; to lead (oneself) under, that is, withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively: - depart, get hence, go (a-) way.

G5218.full: From G5219; attentive hearkening, that is, (by implication) compliance or submission: - obedience, (make) obedient, obey (-ing).

G5219.full: From G5259 and G191; to hear under (as a subordinate), that is, to listen attentively; by implication to heed or conform to a command or authority: - hearken, be obedient to, obey.

G5220.full: From G5259 and G435; in subjection under a man, that is, a married woman: - which hath an husband.

G5221.full: From G5259 and a derivative of G473; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), that is, to encounter, fall in with: - (go to) meet.

G5222.full: From G5221; an encounter or concurrence (with G1519 for infinitive, in order to fall in with): - meeting.

G5223.full: From G5225; existency or proprietorship, that is, (concretely) property, wealth: - goods, substance.

G5224.firstSense: goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast
G5224.full: Neuter plural of present participle active of G5225 as noun; things extant or in hand, that is, property or possessions: - goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.

G5225.full: From G5259 and G756; to begin under (quietly), that is, come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as auxilliary to principal verb): - after behave, live.

G5226.full: From G5259 and åé̓́êù eikō (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender: - submit self.

G5227.full: From G5259 and G1727; under (covertly) contrary to, that is, opposed or (as noun) an opponent: - adversary, against.

G5228.firstSense: (+ exceeding abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concern…
G5228.full: A primary preposition; "over", that is, (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than. In compounds it retains many of the listed applications: - (+ exceeding abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to (-ward), very. In compounds it retains many of the above applications.

G5229.firstSense: exalt self, be exalted above measure
G5229.full: Middle voice from G5228 and G142; to raise oneself over, that is, (figuratively) to become haughty: - exalt self, be exalted above measure.

G5230.full: From G5228 and the base of G188; beyond the "acme", that is, figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth: - + pass the flower of (her) age.

G5231.full: From G5228 and G507; above upward, that is, greatly higher (in place or rank): - far above, over.

G5232.full: From G5228 and G837; to increase above ordinary degree: - grow exceedingly.

G5233.full: From G5228 and the base of G939; to transcend; that is, (figuratively) to overreach: - go beyond.

G5234.full: Adverb from present participle active of G5235; excessively: - beyond measure.

G5235.full: From G5228 and G906; to throw beyond the usual mark, that is, (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent): - exceeding, excel, pass.

G5236.firstSense: abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure
G5236.full: From G5235; a throwing beyond others, that is, (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with G1519 or G2596) pre-eminently: - abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.

G5237.full: From G5228 and G1492; to overlook, that is, not punish: - wink at.

G5238.full: From G5228 and the neuter plural of G1565; above those parts, that is, still farther: - beyond.

G5239.full: From G5228 and G1614; to extend inordinately: - stretch beyond.

G5240.full: From G5228 and the alternate form of G1632; to pour out over, that is, (passively) to overflow: - run over.

G5241.full: From G5228 and G1793; to intercede in behalf of: - make intercession for.

G5242.full: From G5228 and G2192; to hold oneself above, that is, (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority: - better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.

G5244.full: From G5228 and G5316; appearing above others (conspicuous), that is, (figuratively) haughty: - proud.

G5245.full: From G5228 and G3528; to vanquish beyond, that is, gain a decisive victory: - more than conquer.

G5246.full: From G5228 and G3591; bulging over, that is, (figuratively) insolent: - great swelling.

G5247.full: From G5242; prominence, that is, (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character): - authority, excellency.

G5248.full: From G5228 and G4052; to super abound: - abound much more, exceeding.

G5249.full: From G5228 and G4057; superabundantly, that is, exceedingly: - beyond measure.

G5250.full: From G5228 and G4121; to super abound: - be exceeding abundant.

G5251.full: From G5228 and G5312; to elevate above others, that is, raise to the highest position: - highly exalt.

G5252.full: From G5228 and G5426; to esteem oneself overmuch, that is, be vain or arrogant: - think more highly.

G5253.full: Neuter of a derivative of G5228; a higher part of the house, that is, apartment in the third story: - upper chamber (room).

G5254.full: From G5259 and G2192; to hold oneself under, that is, endure with patience: - suffer.

G5255.full: From G5219; attentively listening, that is, (by implication) submissive: - obedient.

G5256.full: From G5257; to be a subordinate, that is, (by implication) subserve: - minister (unto), serve.

G5257.full: From G5259 and a derivative of å̓ñǻóóù eressō (to row); an under oarsman, that is, (genitive case) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable): - minister, officer, servant.

G5258.full: From an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to G5259 through the idea of subsilience); sleep, that is, (figuratively) spiritual torpor: - sleep.

G5259.firstSense: among, by, from, in, of, under, with
G5259.full: A primary preposition; under, that is, (with the genitive) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative) of place (whither [underneath] or where [below]) or time (when [at]): - among, by, from, in, of, under, with. In compounds it retains the same genitive applications, especially of inferior position or condition, and specifically covertly or moderately.

G5260.full: From G5259 and G906; to throw in stealthily, that is, introduce by collusion: - suborn.

G5261.full: From a compound of G5259 and G1125; an underwriting, that is, copy for imitation (figuratively): - example.

G5262.full: From G5263; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively specimen, adumbration): - en- (ex-) ample, pattern.

G5263.full: From G5259 and G1166; to exhibit under the eyes, (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish): - show, (fore-) warn.

G5264.full: From G5259 and G1209; to admit under one's roof, that is, entertain hospitably: - receive.

G5265.full: From G5259 and G1210; to bind under one's feet, that is, put on shoes or sandals: - bind on, (be) shod.

G5266.full: From G5265; something bound under the feet, that is, a shoe or sandal: - shoe.

G5267.full: From G5259 and G1349; under sentence, that is, (by implication) condemned: - guilty.

G5268.full: Neuter of a compound of G5259 and G2218; an animal under the yoke (draught beast), that is, (specifically) a donkey: - ass.

G5269.full: From G5259 and G2224; to gird under, that is, frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck): - undergirt.

G5270.full: From G5259 and G2736; down under, that is, beneath: - under.

G5271.full: Middle voice from G5259 and G2919; to decide (speak or act) under a false part, that is, (figuratively) dissemble (pretend): - feign.

G5272.full: From G5271; acting under a feigned part; that is, (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy"): - condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy.

G5273.full: From G5271; an actor under an assumed character (stage player), that is, (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite"): - hypocrite.

G5274.full: From G5259 and G2983; to take from below, that is, carry upward; figuratively to take up, that is, continue a discourse or topic; mentally to assume (presume): - answer, receive, suppose.

G5275.full: From G5295 and G3007; to leave under (behind), that is, (passively) to remain (survive): - be left.

G5276.full: Neuter of a presumed compound of G5259 and G3025; vessel or receptacle under the press, that is, lower winevat: - winefat.

G5277.full: A prolonged form for G5275; to leave behind, that is, bequeath: - leave.

G5278.firstSense: abide, endure, (take) patient (-ly), suffer, tarry behind
G5278.full: From G5259 and G3306; to stay under (behind), that is, remain; figuratively to undergo, that is, bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere: - abide, endure, (take) patient (-ly), suffer, tarry behind.

G5279.firstSense: put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance
G5279.full: From G5259 and G3403; to remind quietly, that is, suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory: - put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.

G5280.full: From G5279; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection: - remembrance.

G5281.full: From G5278; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy: - enduring, patience, patient continuance (waiting).

G5282.full: From G5259 and G3539; to think under (privately), that is, to surmise or conjecture: - think, suppose, deem.

G5284.full: From G5259 and G4126; to sail under the lee of: - sail under.

G5285.full: From G5259 and G4154; to breathe gently, that is, breeze: - blow softly.

G5286.full: Neuter of a compound of G5259 and G4228; something under the feet, that is, a footrest (figuratively): - footstool.

G5287.full: From a compound of G5259 and G2476; a setting under (support), that is, (figuratively) concretely essence, or abstractly assurance (objectively or subjectively): - confidence, confident, person, substance.

G5288.full: From G5259 and G4724; to withhold under (out of sight), that is, (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve): - draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw.

G5289.full: From G5288; shrinkage (timidity), that is, (by implication) apostasy: - draw back.

G5290.firstSense: come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again)
G5290.full: From G5259 and G4762; to turn under (behind), that is, to return (literally or figuratively): - come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).

G5291.full: From G5259 and G4766; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet): - spread.

G5293.firstSense: be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), b…
G5293.full: From G5259 and G5021; to subordinate; reflexively to obey: - be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.

G5294.full: From G5259 and G5087; to place underneath, that is, (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest: - lay down, put in remembrance.

G5295.full: From G5259 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run under, that is, (specifically) to sail past: - run under.

G5296.full: From a compound of G5259 and a derivative of G5179; typification under (after), that is, (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation: - form, pattern.

G5297.full: From G5259 and G5342; to bear from underneath, that is, (figuratively) to undergo hardship: - bear, endure.

G5298.full: From G5259 and G5562; to vacate down, that is, retire quietly: - go aside, withdraw self.

G5299.full: From a compound of G5259 and a derivative of G3700; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), that is, (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions): - keep under, weary.

G5300.full: us hoos Apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine"): - sow.

G5302.firstSense: come behind (short), be destitute, fall, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse
G5302.full: From G5306; to be later, that is, (by implication) to be inferior; genitively to fall short (be deficient): - come behind (short), be destitute, fall, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.

G5303.firstSense: that which is behind, (that which was) lack (-ing), penury, want
G5303.full: From G5302; a deficit; specifically poverty: - that which is behind, (that which was) lack (-ing), penury, want.

G5304.full: From G5302; a falling short, that is, (specifically) penury: - want.

G5305.full: Neuter of G5306 as adverb; more lately, that is, eventually: - afterward, (at the) last (of all).

G5306.full: Comparatively from G5259 (in the sense of behind); later: - latter.

G5307.full: From õ̔öáé́íù huphainō (to weave); woven, that is, (perhaps) knitted: - woven.

G5308.full: From G5311; lofty (in place or character): - high (-er, -ly) (esteemed).

G5309.full: From a compound of G5308 and G5424; to be lofty in mind, that is, arrogant: - be highminded.

G5310.full: Superlative from the base of G5311; highest, that is, (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens: - most high, highest.

G5311.full: From a derivative of G5228; elevation, that is, (abstractly) altitude, (specifically) the sky, or (figuratively) dignity: - be exalted, height, (on) high.

G5312.full: From G5311; to elevate (literally or figuratively): - exalt, lift up.

G5313.full: From G5312; an elevated place or thing, that is, (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figurative): - height, high thing.

G5315.full: A primary verb (used as an alternate of G2068 in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively): - eat, meat.

G5316.firstSense: appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think
