G5316.full: Prolongation for the base of G5457; to lighten (shine), that is, show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative): - appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think.

G5317.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6389]; Phalek (that is, Peleg), a patriarch: - Phalec.

G5318.firstSense: abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open [+ -ly], outward ([+ -ly])
G5318.full: From G5316; shining, that is, apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally: - abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open [+ -ly], outward ([+ -ly]).

G5319.full: From G5318; to render apparent (literally or figuratively): - appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self).

G5320.full: Adverb from G5318; plainly, that is, clearly or publicly: - evidently, openly.

G5321.full: From G5319; exhibition, that is, (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment: - manifestation.

G5322.full: From G5316; a lightener, that is, light: - lantern.

G5323.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6439]; Phanuel (that is, Penuel), an Israelite: - Phanuel.

G5324.full: From a derivative of G5316; to make apparent, that is, (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle): - sight.

G5325.full: From a derivative of G5324; (properly abstractly) a (vain) show ("fantasy"): - pomp.

G5326.full: From G5324; (properly concretely) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), that is, spectre: - spirit.

G5327.full: Properly strengthened from the base of G4008 or rather of G4486; a gap or chasm, that is, ravine (winter torrent): - valley.

G5328.full: Of foreign origin [H6547]; Pharao (that is, Pharoh), an Egyptian king: - Pharaoh.

G5329.full: Of Hebrew origin [H6557]; Phares (that is, Perets), an Israelite: - Phares.

G5330.full: Of Hebrew origin (compare [H6567]); a separatist, that is, exclusively religious; a Pharisaean, that is, Jewish sectary: - Pharisee.

G5331.full: From G5332; medication ("pharmacy"), that is, (by extension) magic (literal or figurative): - sorcery, witchcraft.

G5332.full: From öá́ñìáêïí pharmakon (a drug, that is, spell giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, that is, (by extension) a magician: - sorcerer.

G5334.full: From G5346 (not the same as "phase", which is from G5316); a saying, that is, report: - tidings.

G5335.full: Prolongation from the same as G5346; to assert: - affirm, profess, say.

G5336.full: From ðáôǻïìáé pateomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder): - manger, stall.

G5337.full: Apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", that is, (figuratively) wicked: - evil.

G5338.full: Probably akin to the base of G5457 (compare G5350); brilliancy: - light.

G5339.full: Of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, that is, (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently: - forbear, spare.

G5340.full: Adverb from participle of G5339; abstemiously, that is, stingily: - sparingly.

G5341.full: By transposition for a derivation probably of G5316 (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout): - cloke.

G5342.firstSense: be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, l…
G5342.full: A primary verb (for which other and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely ïé̓́ù oiō̄̄ and å̓íǻãêù enegkō̄ to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively: - be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold.

G5343.full: Apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication to shun; by analogy to vanish: - escape, flee (away).

G5344.full: Of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (that is, Felix), a Roman: - Felix.

G5345.full: From G5346; a saying, that is, rumor ("fame"): - fame.

G5346.full: Properly the same as the base of G5457 and G5316; to show or make known one's thoughts, that is, speak or say: - affirm, say. Compare G3004.

G5347.full: Of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (that is, Festus), a Roman: - Festus.

G5348.full: Apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, that is, anticipate or precede; by extension to have arrived at: - (already) attain, come, prevent.

G5349.full: From G5351; decayed, that is, (by implication) perishable: - corruptible.

G5350.full: Probably akin to G5338 and thus to G5346; to utter a clear sound, that is, (genitive case) to proclaim: - speak.

G5351.full: Probably strengthened from öèé́ù phthiō (to pine or waste): properly to shrivel or wither, that is, to spoil (by any process) or (genitive) to ruin (especially figuratively by moral influences, to deprave): - corrupt (self), defile, destroy.

G5352.full: From a derivative of öèé́íù phthinō (to wane; akin to the base of G5351) and G3703 (meaning late autumn) autumnal (as stripped of leaves): - whose fruit withereth.

G5353.full: From G5350; utterance, that is, a musical note (vocal or instrumental): - sound.

G5354.full: From G5355; to be jealous of: - envy.

G5355.full: Probably akin to the base of G5351; ill will (as detraction), that is, jealousy (spite): - envy.

G5356.full: From G5351; decay, that is, ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively): - corruption, destroy, perish.

G5357.full: Of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"): - vial.

G5358.full: From G5384 and G18; fond of good, that is, a promoter of virtue: - love of good men.

G5359.full: From Öéëá́äǻëöïò Philadelphos (the same as G5361), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor: - Philadelphia.

G5360.firstSense: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren
G5360.full: From G5361; fraternal affection: - brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren.

G5361.full: From G5384 and G80; fond of brethren, that is, fraternal: - love as brethren.

G5362.full: From G5384 and G435; fond of man, that is, affectionate as a wife: - love their husbands.

G5363.full: From the same as G5364; fondness of mankind, that is, benevolence ("philanthropy"): - kindness, love towards man.

G5364.full: Adverb from a compound of G5384 and G444; fondly to man (philanthropically), that is, humanely: - courteously.

G5365.full: From G5366; avarice: - love of money.

G5366.full: From G5384 and G696; fond of silver (money), that is, avaricious: - covetous.

G5367.full: From G5384 and G846; fond of self, that is, selfish: - lover of own self.

G5368.full: From G5384; to be a friend to (fond of [an individual or an object]), that is, have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while G25 is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as G2309 and G1014, or as G2372 and G3563 respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specifically to kiss (as a mark of tenderness): - kiss, love.

G5369.full: From G5384 and G2237; fond of pleasure, that is, voluptuous: - lover of pleasure.

G5371.full: From G5368; friendly; Philemon, a Christian: - Philemon.

G5372.full: From G5368; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity: - Philetus.

G5374.full: From G5375; a Philippesian (Philippian), that is, native of Philippi: - Philippian.

G5375.full: Plural of G5376; Philippi, a place in Macedonia: - Philippi.

G5376.full: From G5384 and G2462; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites: - Philip.

G5377.full: From G5384 and G2316; fond of God, that is, pious: - lover of God.

G5378.full: From G5384 and G3056; fond of words, that is, talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian: - Philologus.

G5379.full: From G5380; quarrelsomeness, that is, a dispute: - strife.

G5380.full: From G5384 and íåé͂êïò neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to G3534); fond of strife, that is, disputatious: - contentious.

G5381.full: From G5382; hospitableness: - entertain strangers, hospitality.

G5382.full: From G5384 and G3581; fond of guests, that is, hospitable: - given to (lover of, use) hospitality.

G5383.full: From a compound of G5384 and G4413; to be fond of being first, that is, ambitious of distinction: - love to have the preeminence.

G5384.full: Properly dear, that is, a friend; actively fond, that is, friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.): - friend.

G5385.full: From G5386; "philosophy", that is, (specifically) Jewish sophistry: - philosophy.

G5386.full: From G5384 and G4680; fond of wise things, that is, a "philosopher": - philosopher.

G5387.full: From G5384 and óôïñãḉ storgē (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, that is, fraternal towards fellow Christians: - kindly affectioned.

G5388.full: From G5384 and G5043; fond of one's children, that is, maternal: - love their children.

G5389.full: Middle voice from a compound of G5384 and G5092; to be fond of honor, that is, emulous (eager or earnest to do somethng.): - labour, strive, study.

G5390.full: Adverb from G5391; with friendliness of mind, that is, kindly: - courteously.

G5391.full: From G5384 and G5424; friendly of mind, that is, kind: - courteous.

G5392.full: From öéìḯò phimos (a muzzle); to muzzle: - muzzle.

G5393.full: Active participle of the base of G5395; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian: - Phlegon.

G5394.full: From G5395; to cause a blaze, that is, ignite (figuratively to inflame with passion): - set on fire.

G5395.full: phlox flox From a primary öëǻãù phlegō (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze: - flame (-ing).

G5396.full: From G5397; to be a babbler or trifler, that is, (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously: - prate against.

G5397.full: From öëṍù phluō (to bubble); a garrulous person, that is, prater: - tattler.

G5398.full: From G5401; frightful, that is, (objectively) formidable: - fearful, terrible.

G5399.full: From G5401; to frighten, that is, (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy to be in awe of, that is, revere: - be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence.

G5400.full: Neuter of a derivative of G5399; a frightening thing, that is, terrific portent: - fearful sight.

G5401.full: From a primary öǻâïìáé phebomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright: - be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.

G5402.full: Feminine of Öïé͂âïò Phoibos (bright; probably akin to the base of G5457); Phaebe, a Christian woman: - Phebe.

G5403.full: From G5404; palm country; Phaenice (or Phaenicia), a region of Palestine: - Phenice, Phenicia.

G5404.full: Of uncertain derivation; a palm tree: - palm (tree).

G5405.full: Probably the same as G5404; Phaenix, a place in Crete: - Phenice.

G5406.full: From G5408; a murderer (always of criminal [or at least intentional] homicide; which G443 does not necessarily imply; while G4607 is a special term for a public bandit): - murderer.

G5407.full: From G5406; to be a murderer (of): - kill, do murder, slay.

G5408.full: From an obsolete primary öǻíù phenō (to slay); murder: - murder, + be slain with, slaughter.

G5409.full: From G5411; to have a burden, that is, (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment: - bear, wear.

G5410.full: Of Latin origin; a forum or market place; only in compounds with G675; a station on the Appian road: - forum.

G5411.full: From G5342; a load (as borne), that is, (figuratively) a tax (properly an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas G5056 is usually a general toll on goods or travel): - tribute.

G5412.full: From G5414; to load up (properly as a vessel or animal), that is, (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety): - lade, be heavy laden.

G5413.full: Diminutive of G5414; an invoice (as part of freight), that is, (figuratively) a task or service: - burden.

G5414.full: From G5342; something carried, that is, the cargo of a ship: - lading.

G5415.full: Of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian: - Fortunatus.

G5416.full: Neuter of a derivative from the base of G5417; a whip, that is, Roman lash as a public punishment: - scourge.

G5417.full: From a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, that is, lash as a public punishment: - scourge.

G5418.full: From G5420; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively): - hedge (+ round about), partition.

G5419.full: Probably akin to G5420 through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), that is, (specifically) to expound: - declare.

G5420.full: Apparently a strengthened form of the base of G5424; to fence or inclose, that is, (specifically) to block up (figuratively to silence): - stop.

G5421.full: Of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), that is, a cistern or well; figuratively an abyss (as a prison): - well, pit.

G5422.full: From G5423; to be a mind misleader, that is, delude: - deceive.

G5423.full: From G5424 and G539; a mind misleader, that is, seducer: - deceiver.

G5424.full: phrēn frane Probably from an obsolete öñá́ù phraō (to rein in or curb; compare G5420); the midrif (as a partition of the body), that is, (figuratively and by implication of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension [also in the plural] the mind or cognitive faculties): - understanding.

G5425.full: Apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, that is, shudder (fear): - tremble.

G5426.firstSense: set the affection on, (be) care (-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let…
G5426.full: From G5424; to exercise the mind, that is, entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience): - set the affection on, (be) care (-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind (-ed, regard, savour, think.

G5427.full: From G5426; (mental) inclination or purpose: - (be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind (-ed).

G5428.full: From G5426; mental action or activity, that is, intellectual or moral insight: - prudence, wisdom.

G5429.full: From G5424; thoughtful, that is, sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while G4680 denotes practical skill or acumen; and G4908 indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative): - wise (-r).

G5431.full: From a derivative of G5424; to exercise thought, that is, be anxious: - be careful.

G5432.full: From a compound of G4253 and G3708; to be a watcher in advance, that is, to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively to hem in, protect: - keep (with a garrison). Compare G5083.

G5433.full: Akin to G1032, G1031; to snort (as a spirited horse), that is, (figuratively) to make a tumult: - rage.

G5434.full: Neuter of a presumed derivative of öñṍãù phrugō (to roast or parch; akin to the base of G5395); something desiccated, that is, a dry twig: - stick.

G5435.full: Probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor: - Phrygia.

G5436.full: Probably from G5343; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian: - Phygellus.

G5437.full: From G5343; a fleeing, that is, escape: - flight.

G5438.full: From G5442; a guarding or (concretely guard), the act, the parson; figuratively the place, the condition, or (specifically) the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively: - cage, hold, (im-) prison (-ment), ward, watch.

G5440.full: Neuter of a derivative of G5442; a guard case, that is, "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts: - phylactery.

G5441.full: From G5442; a watcher or sentry: - keeper.

G5442.full: Probably from G5443 through the idea of isolation; to watch, that is, be on guard (literally or figuratively); by implication to preserve. obey, avoid: - beware, keep (self), observe, save. Compare G5083.

G5443.full: From G5453 (compare G5444); an offshoot, that is, race or clan: - kindred, tribe.

G5444.full: From the same as G5443; a sprout, that is, leaf: - leaf.

G5445.full: From a prolonged form of öṍñù phurō (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to G5453 through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough: - lump.

G5446.full: From G5449; "physical", that is, (by implication) instinctive: - natural. Compare G5591.

G5447.full: Adverb frm G5446; "physically", that is, (by implication) instinctively: - naturally.

G5448.full: From G5449 in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, that is, (figuratively) make proud (haughty): - puff up.

G5449.full: From G5453; growth (by germination or expansion), that is, (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension a genus or sort; figuratively native disposition, constitution or usage: - ([man-]) kind, nature ([-al]).

G5450.full: From G5448; inflation, that is, (figuratively) haughtiness: - swelling.

G5451.full: From G5452; trans planting, that is, (concretely) a shrub or vegetable: - plant.

G5452.full: From a derivative of G5453; to set out in the earth, that is, implant. Figuratively to instil doctrine: - plant.

G5453.full: A primary verb; probably originally to "puff" or blow, that is, to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively: - spring (up).

G5454.full: Of uncertain derivation; a burrow or lurking place: - hole.

G5455.full: From G5456; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication to address in words or by name, also in imitation: - call (for), crow, cry.

G5456.full: Probably akin to G5316 through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication an address (for any purpose), saying or language: - noise, sound, voice.

G5457.full: phōs foce From an obsoleteöá́ù phaō (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare G5316 and G5346); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative): - fire, light.

G5458.full: From G5457; an illuminator, that is, (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy: - light.

G5459.full: From G5457 and G5342; light bearing ("phosphorus"), that is, (specifically) the morning star (figuratively): - day star.

G5460.full: From G5457; lustrous, that is, transparent or well illuminated (figurative): - bright, full of light.

G5461.firstSense: enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see
G5461.full: From G5457; to shed rays, that is, to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively): - enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.

G5463.firstSense: farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hail, joy (-fully), rejoice
G5463.full: A primary verb; to be full of "cheer", that is, calmly happy or well off; impersonal especially as a salutation (on meeting or parting), be well: - farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hail, joy (-fully), rejoice.

G5465.full: From the base of G5490; to lower (as into a void): - let down, strike.

G5466.full: Probably of Hebrew origin [H3778]; a Chaldaean (that is, Kasdi), or native of the region of the lower Euphrates: - Chaldan.

G5467.full: Perhaps from G5465 through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, that is, dangerous, or (by implication) furious: - fierce, perilous.

G5468.full: From a compound of G5469 and the reduplicated form of G71; to be a bit leader, that is, to curb (figuratively): - bridle.

G5469.full: From G5465 a curb or head stall (as curbing the spirit): - bit, bridle.

G5471.full: From G5475; a copper worker or brazier: - coppersmith.

G5472.full: From G5475 and perhaps G1491; copper like, that is, "chalcedony": - chalcedony.

G5473.full: Diminutive from G5475; a copper dish: - brazen vessel.

G5474.full: Neuter of a compound of G5475 and G3030 (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre: - fine brass.

G5475.full: Perhaps from G5465 through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it): - brass, money.

G5476.full: Adverb perhaps from the base of G5490 through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, that is, prostrate: - on (to) the ground.

G5477.full: Of Hebrew origin [H3667]; Chanaan (that is, Kenaan), the early name of Palestine: - Chanaan.

G5478.full: From G5477; a Chanaanaean (that is, Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine: - of Canaan.

G5479.firstSense: gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy (-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous)
G5479.full: From G5463; cheerfulness, that is, calm delight: - gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy (-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).

G5480.full: From the same as G5482; a scratch or etching, that is, stamp (as a badge of servitude), or sculptured figure (statue): - graven, mark.

G5481.full: From the same as G5482; a graver (the tool or the person), that is, (by implication) engraving (["character"], the figure stamped, that is, an exact copy or [figuratively] representation): - express image.

G5482.full: From "charasso" (to sharpen to a point; akin to G1125 through the idea of scratching); a stake, that is, (by implication) a palisade or rampart (millitary mound for circumvallation in a siege): - trench.

G5483.full: Middle voice from G5485; to grant as a favor, that is, gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue: - deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely) give, grant.

G5484.firstSense: be- (for) cause of, for sake of, +
G5484.full: Accusative case of G5485 as preposition; through favor of, that is, on account of: - be- (for) cause of, for sake of, + . . . fore, X reproachfully.

G5485.firstSense: acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace (-ious), joy liberality, pleasure, thank (-s,…
G5485.full: From G5463; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude): - acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace (-ious), joy liberality, pleasure, thank (-s, -worthy).

G5486.full: From G5483; a (divine) gratuity, that is, deliverance (from danger or passion); (specifically) a (spiritual) endowment, that is, (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty: - (free) gift.

G5487.full: From G5485; to grace, that is, indue with special honor: - make accepted, be highly favoured.

G5488.full: Of Hebrew origin [H2771]; Charrhan (that is, Charan), a place in Mesopotamia: - Charran.

G5489.full: From the same as G5482; a sheet ("chart") of writing material (as to be scribbled over): - paper.

G5490.full: From a form of an obsolete primary "chao" (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval): - gulf.

G5491.full: From a form of the same as G5490; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively a margin (of water): - lip, shore.

G5492.full: From the same as G5494; to storm, that is, (passively) to labor under a gale: - to tossed with tempest.

G5493.full: From the base of G5494 and G4482; a storm runlet, that is, winter torrent: - brook.

G5494.full: From a derivation of ÷ǻù cheō (to pour; akin to the base of G5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication the rainy season, that is, winter: - tempest, foul weather, winter.

G5495.full: cheir khire Perhaps from the base of G5494 in the sense of its congener the base of G5490 (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively [power]; especially [by Hebraism] a means or instrument): - hand.

G5496.full: From G5497; to be a hand leader, that is, to guide (a blind person): - lead by the hand.

G5497.firstSense: some to lead by the hand
G5497.full: From G5495 and a reduplicated form of G71; a hand leader, that is, personal conductor (of a blind person): - some to lead by the hand.

G5498.full: Neuter of a compound of G5495 and G1125; something hand written ("chirograph"), that is, a manuscript (specifically a legal document or bond (figuratively)): - handwriting.

G5499.full: From G5495 and a derivative of G4160; manufactured, that is, of human construction: - made by (make with) - hands.

G5500.full: From a compound of G5495 and ôåé́íù teinō (to stretch); to be a hand reacher or voter (by raising the hand), that is, (genitive) to select or appoint: - choose, ordain.

G5501.full: Irregular compound of G2556; from an obsolete equivalent ÷ǻñçò cherēs (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally): - sorer, worse.

G5502.full: Plural of Hebrew origin [H3742]; "cherubim" (that is, cherubs or kerubim): - cherubims.

G5503.full: Feminine of a presumed derivation apparently from the base of G5490 through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively: - widow.

G5504.full: chthes khthes Of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension in time past or hitherto: - yesterday.

G5506.full: From G5507 and G757; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"), that is, colonel: - (chief, high) captain.

G5507.full: Plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand: - thousand.

G5508.full: Of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean: - Chios.

G5509.full: Of foreign origin [H3801]; a tunic or shirt: - clothes, coat, garment.

G5510.full: Perhaps akin to the base of G5490 (G5465) or G5494 (as descending or empty); snow: - snow.

G5511.full: Of uncertain derivation; a military cloak: - robe.

G5512.full: From a derivative probably of G5491; to throw out the lip, that is, jeer at: - mock.

G5514.full: Feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloe, a Christian female: - Chloe.

G5515.full: From the same as G5514; greenish, that is, verdant, dun-colored: - green, pale.

G5516.full: The 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (G4742 as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; 666 as a numeral: - six hundred threescore and six.

G5517.full: From G5522; dusty or dirty (soil like), that is, (by implication) terrene: - earthy.

G5518.full: Of uncertain derivation; a chaenix or certain dry measure: - measure.

G5519.full: Of uncertain derivation; a hog: - swine.

G5520.full: From G5521; to be bilious, that is, (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric"): - be angry.

G5521.full: Feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as G5514 (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, that is, (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.): - gall.

G5522.full: From the base of G5494; a heap (as poured out), that is, rubbish; lose dirt: - dust.

G5523.full: Of uncertain derivation, Chorazin, a place in Palestine: - Chorazin.

G5524.full: From a compound of G5525 and G71; to be a dance leader, that is, (genitive case) to furnish: - give, minister.

G5525.full: Of uncertain derivation; a ring, that is, round dance ("choir"): - dancing.

G5526.full: From G5528; to fodder, that is, (genitive case) to gorge (supply food in abundance): - feed, fill, satisfy.

G5527.full: From G5526; forage, that is, food: - sustenance.

G5528.full: Apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", that is, (by implication of pasture) herbage or vegetation: - blade, grass, hay.

G5529.full: Of uncertain origin, Chuzas, an officer of Herod: - Chuza.

G5530.full: Middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from G5495, to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" [touch slightly], light upon, etc.), that is, (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner: - entreat, use. Compare G5531, G5534.

G5531.full: Probably the same as the base of G5530; to loan: - lend.

G5532.firstSense: business, lack, necessary (-ity), need (-ful), use, want
G5532.full: From the base of G5530 or G5534; employment, that is, an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution: - business, lack, necessary (-ity), need (-ful), use, want.

G5533.full: From a derivative of G5531 and G3781; a loan ower, that is, indebted person: - debtor.

G5534.full: chrē khray Third person singular of the same as G5530 or G5531 used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be: - ought.

G5535.full: From G5532; to make (that is, have) necessity, that is, be in want of: - (have) need.

G5536.full: Something useful or needed, that is, wealth, price: - money, riches.

G5537.firstSense: be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak
G5537.full: From G5536; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of G5530), that is, divinely intimate; by implication (compare the secular sense of G5532) to constitute a firm for business, that is, (genitive) bear as a title: - be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak.

G5538.full: From G5537; a divine response or revelation: - answer of God.

G5540.full: From G5530; employment, that is, (specifically) sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body): - use.

G5541.full: Middle voice from G5543; to show oneself useful, that is, act benevolently: - be kind.

G5542.full: From a compound of G5543 and G3004; fair speech, that is, plausibility: - good words.

G5543.full: From G5530; employed, that is, (by implication) useful (in manner or morals): - better, easy, good (-ness), gracious, kind.

G5544.full: From G5543; usefulness, that is, moral excellence (in character or demeanor): - gentleness, good (-ness), kindness.

G5545.full: From G5548; an unguent or smearing, that is, (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit: - anointing, unction.

G5546.full: From G5547; a Christian, that is, follower of Christ: - Christian.

G5547.full: From G5548; anointed, that is, the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus: - Christ.

G5548.full: Probably akin to G5530 through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, that is, (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service: - anoint.

G5549.full: From G5550; to take time, that is, linger: - delay, tarry.

G5550.firstSense: + years old, season, space, (X often-) time (-s), (a) while
G5550.full: Of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in genitive case, and thus properly distinguished from G2540, which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from G165, which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension an individual opportunity; by implication delay: - + years old, season, space, (X often-) time (-s), (a) while.

G5551.full: From a presumed compound of G5550 and the base of G5147; to be a time wearer, that is, to procrastinate (linger): - spend time.

G5552.full: From G5557; made of gold: - of gold, golden.

G5553.full: Diminutive of G5557; a golden article, that is, gold plating, ornament, or coin: - gold.

G5554.full: From G5557 and G1146; gold ringed, that is, wearing a golden finger ring or similar jewelry: - with a gold ring.

G5555.full: From G5557 and G3037; gold stone, that is, a yellow gem ("chrysolite"): - chrysolite.

G5556.full: From G5557 and ðñá́óïí prason (a leek); a greenish yellow gem ("chrysoprase"): - chrysoprase.

G5557.full: Perhaps from the base of G5530 (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension a golden article, as an ornament or coin: - gold.

G5558.full: From G5557; to gild, that is, bespangle with golden ornaments: - deck.

G5559.full: chrōs khroce Probably akin to the base of G5530 through the idea of handling; the body (properly its surface or skin): - body.

G5560.full: Apparently a primary word; "halt", that is, limping: - cripple, halt, lame.

G5561.firstSense: coast, county, fields, grounds, land, region
G5561.full: Feminine of a derivative of the base of G5490 through the idea of empty expanse; room, that is, a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants): - coast, county, fields, grounds, land, region. Compare G5117.

G5562.firstSense: come, contain, go, have, place, (can, be room to) receive
G5562.full: From G5561; to be in (give) space, that is, (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively): - come, contain, go, have, place, (can, be room to) receive.

G5563.full: From G5561; to place room between, that is, part; reflexively to go away: - depart, put asunder, separate.

G5564.firstSense: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession
G5564.full: Diminutive of G5561; a spot or plot of ground: - field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession.

G5565.full: Adverb from G5561; at a space, that is, separately or apart from (often as preposition): - beside, by itself, without.

G5566.full: Of Latin origin; the north west wind: - north west.

G5567.full: Probably strengthened from øá́ù psaō (to rub or touch the surface; compare G5597); to twitch or twang, that is, to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes): - make melody, sing (psalms).

G5568.full: From G5567; a set piece of music, that is, a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively the book of the Psalms: - psalm. Compare G5603.

G5569.full: From G5571 and G80; a spurious brother, that is, pretended associate: - false brethren.

G5570.full: From G5571 and G652; a spurious apostle, that is, pretended preacher: - false teacher.

G5571.full: From G5574; untrue, that is, erroneous, deceitful, wicked: - false, liar.

G5572.full: From G5571 and G1320; a spurious teacher, that is, propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine: - false teacher.

G5573.full: From G5571 and G3004; mendacious, that is, promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine: - speaking lies.

G5574.full: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood: - falsely, lie.

G5575.full: From G5571 and a kindred form of G3144; a spurious witness, that is, bearer of untrue testimony: - false witness.

G5576.full: From G5575; to be an untrue testifier, that is, offer falsehood in evidence: - be a false witness.

G5577.full: From G5575; untrue testimony: - false witness.

G5578.full: From G5571 and G4396; a spurious prophet, that is, pretended foreteller or religious impostor: - false prophet.

G5579.full: From G5574; a falsehood: - lie, lying.

G5580.full: From G5571 and G5547; a spurious Messiah: - false Christ.

G5581.full: From G5571 and G3686; untruly named: - falsely so called.

G5582.full: From G5574; a fabrication, that is, falsehood: - lie.

G5584.full: From the base of G5567 (compare G5586); to manipulate, that is, verify by contact; figuratively to search for: - feel after, handle, touch.

G5585.full: From G5586; to use pebbles in enumeration, that is, (genitive case) to compute: - count.

G5586.full: From the same as G5584; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), that is, (by implication of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote: - stone, voice.

G5587.full: From a derivative of øé́èïò psithos (a whisper; by implication a slander; probably akin to G5574); whispering, that is, secret detraction: - whispering.

G5588.full: From the same as G5587; a secret calumniator: - whisperer.

G5589.full: Diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5567 (meaning a crumb); a little bit or morsel: - crumb.

G5590.firstSense: heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you
G5590.full: From G5594; breath, that is, (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from G4151, which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from G2222, which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew [H5315], [H7307] and [H2416]: - heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you.

G5591.full: From G5590; sensitive that is, animate (in distinction on the one hand from G4152, which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from G5446, which is the lower or bestial nature): - natural, sensual.

G5593.full: From G5592; chilly (literally or figuratively): - cold.

G5594.full: A primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently; thus differing on the one hand from G4154, which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of G109, which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), that is, (by implication of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively): - wax cold.

G5595.full: From the base of G5596; to supply with bits, that is, (genitive case) to nourish: - (bestow to) feed.

G5596.full: Diminutive from a derivation of the base of G5597; a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), that is, a mouthful: - sop.

G5597.full: Prolongation from the same base as G5567; to triturate, that is, (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand): - rub.

G5598.full: The last letter of the Greek alphabet, that is, (figuratively) the finality: - Omega.

G5599.full: As a sign of the vocative O; as a note of exclamation. oh: - O.

G5600.firstSense: + appear, are, (may, might, should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, shoul…
G5600.full: Including the oblique forms, as well as ç̓͂ò ēs ace; ç̓͂ ē ay, etc.; the subjunctive of G1510; (may, might, can, could, would, must, etc.; also with G1487 and its compounds, as well as with other particles) be: - + appear, are, (may, might, should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were.

G5601.full: Of Hebrew origin [H5744]; Obed, an Israelite: - Obed.

G5602.full: From an adverb form of G3592; in this same spot, that is, here or hither: - here, hither, (in) this place, there.

G5603.full: From G103; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while G5215 denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and G5568 still more specifically a Hebrew cantillation: - song.

G5604.full: Akin to G3601; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth: - pain, sorrow, travail.

G5605.full: From G5604; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively): - travail in (birth).

G5606.full: Perhaps from the alternate of G5342; the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne): - shoulder.

G5607.full: The feminine, the neuter and the present participle of G1510; being: - be, come, have.

G5608.full: Middle voice from an apparently primary word ù̓͂íïò ōnos (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier G4092): - buy.

G5609.full: Apparently a primary word; an egg: - egg.

G5610.firstSense: day, hour, instant, season, X short, [even-] tide, (high) time
G5610.full: Apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or figuratively): - day, hour, instant, season, X short, [even-] tide, (high) time.

G5611.full: From G5610; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), that is, (by implication) flourishing (beauteous [figuratively]): - beautiful.

G5612.full: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar": - roar.

G5613.firstSense: about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like…
G5613.full: hōs hoce Probably adverb of compound from G3739; which how, that is, in that manner (very variously used as shown): - about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when ([-soever]), while, X with all speed.

G5614.full: Of Hebrew origin [H3467] and [H4994]; oh save!; hosanna (that is, hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration: - hosanna.

G5615.firstSense: even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner
G5615.full: From G5613 and an adverb from G846; as thus, that is, in the same way: - even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner.

G5616.firstSense: about, as (it had been, it were), like (as)
G5616.full: From G5613 and G1487; as if: - about, as (it had been, it were), like (as).

G5617.full: Of Hebrew origin [H1954]; Hosee (that is, Hoshea), an Israelite: - Osee.

G5618.full: From G5613 and G4007; just as, that is, exactly like: - (even, like) as.

G5619.full: From G5618 and G1487; just as if, that is, as it were: - as.

G5620.firstSense: (insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore
G5620.full: From G5613 and G5037; so too, that is, thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as shown): - (insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore.

G5621.full: Diminutive of G3775; an earlet, that is, one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear: - ear.

G5622.full: From a derivative of the base of G5624; usefulness, that is, benefit: - advantage, profit.

G5623.full: From the same as G5622; to be useful, that is, to benefit: - advantage, better, prevail, profit.

G5624.full: From a form of G3786; helpful or serviceable, that is, advantageous: - profit (-able).

H1.full: A primitive word; father in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application: - chief, (fore-) father ([-less]), X patrimony, principal. Compare names in "Abi-"

H3.full: From the same as H24; a green plant: - greenness, fruit.

H5.full: ab-ag-thaw' Of foreign origin; Abagtha, a eunuch of Xerxes: - Abagtha.

H6.firstSense: break, destroy (-uction), + not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, X a…
H6.full: aw-bad' A primitive root; properly to wander away, that is lose oneself; by implication to perish (causatively, destroy): - break, destroy (-uction), + not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, X and surely, take, be undone, X utterly, be void of, have no way to flee.

H7.full: ab-ad' (Chaldee); corresponding to H6: - destroy, perish.

H8.full: Active participle of H6; (concretely) wretched or (abstractly) destruction: - perish.

H9.full: From H6; concretely something lost; abstractly destruction, that is Hades: - lost. Compare H10.

H10.full: ab-ad-do' The same as H9, miswritten for H11; a perishing: - destruction.

H11.full: ab-ad-done' Intensively from H6; abstractly a perishing; concretely Hades: - destruction.

H12.full: ab-dawn' From H6; a perishing: - destruction.

H13.full: ob-dawn' From H6; a perishing: - destruction.

H14.firstSense: consent, rest content, will, be willing
H14.full: A primitive root; to breathe after, that is (figuratively) to be acquiescent: - consent, rest content, will, be willing.

H16.full: ay-beh' From H14 (in the sense of bending towards); the papyrus: - swift.

H17.full: From H14 (in the sense of desiring); want: - sorrow.

H18.full: From H75; a manger or stall: - crib.

H19.full: ib-khaw' From an unused root (apparently meaning to turn); brandishing of a sword: - point.

H20.full: Of uncertain derivation; a melon (only plural): - melon.

H21.full: From H1; fatherly; Abi, Hezekiah's mother: - Abi.

H22.full: From H1 and H410; father (that is possessor) of God; Abiel, the name of two Israelites: - Abiel.

H23.full: From H1 and H622; father of gathering (that is gatherer); Abiasaph, an Israelite: - Abiasaph.

H24.firstSense: Abib, ear, green ears of corn
H24.full: From an unused root (meaning to be tender); green, that is a young ear of grain; hence the name of the month Abib or Nisan: - Abib, ear, green ears of corn.

H25.full: From H1 and H1391; father (that is founder) of Gibon; Abi-Gibon, perhaps an Israelite: - father of Gibeon.

H26.full: ab-ee-gah'yil, ab-ee-gal' From H1 and H1524; father (that is source) of joy; Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses: - Abigal.

H27.full: From H1 and H1777; father of judgment (that is judge); Abidan, an Israelite: - Abidan.

H28.full: From H1 and H3045; father of knowledge (that is knowing); Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah: - Abida, Abidah.

H29.full: From H1 and H3050; father (that is worshipper) of Jah; Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses: - Abiah, Abijah.

H30.full: From H1 and H1931; father (that is worshipper) of Him (that is God); Abihu, a son of Aaron: - Abihu.

H31.full: From H1 and H1935; father (that is, possessor) of renown; Abihud, the name of two Israelites: - Abihud.

H32.full: ab-ee-hah'-yil, ab-ee-khah'-yil (More correct in its second form); from H1 and H2428; father (that is, possessor) of might; Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses: - Abihail.

H33.full: From H44 with the article inserted; father of the Ezrite; and Abiezrite or descendant of Abiezer: - Abiezrite.

H34.full: eb-yone' From H14, in the sense of want (especially in feeling); destitute: - beggar, needy, poor (man).

H35.full: From H14; provocative of desire; the caper berry (from its stimulative taste): - desire.

H36.full: From H1 and H2898; father of goodness (that is, good); Abitub, an Israelite: - Abitub.

H37.full: From H1 and H2919; father of dew (that is, fresh); Abital, a wife of King David: - Abital.

H38.full: From H1 and H3220; father of (the) sea (that is, seaman); Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah: - Abijam.

H39.full: From H1 and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe); Abimael, a son of Joktan: - Abimael.

H40.full: ab-ee-mel'-ek From H1 and H4428; father of (the) king; Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites: - Abimelech.

H41.full: From H1 and H5068; father of generosity (that is, liberal); Abinadab, the name of four Israelites: - Abinadab.

H42.full: From H1 and H5278; father of pleasantness (that is, gracious); Abinoam, an Israelite: - Abinoam.

H43.full: eb-yaw-sawf' Construction from H23; Ebjasaph, an Israelite: - Ebiasaph.

H44.full: From H1 and H5829; father of help (that is, helpful); Abiezer, the name of two Israelites: - Abiezer.

H45.full: From H1 and an unused root of uncertain derivation; probably father of strength (that is, valiant); Abialbon, an Israelite: - Abialbon.

H46.full: From H82; mighty (spoken of God): - mighty (one).

H47.firstSense: angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout [-hearted], strong (one), valiant
H47.full: ab-beer' For H46: - angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout [-hearted], strong (one), valiant.

H48.full: From H1 and H7311; father of height (that is, lofty); Abiram, the name of two Israelites: - Abiram.

H49.full: ab-ee-shag' From H1 and H7686; father of error (that is, blundering); Abishag, a concubine of David: - Abishag.

H50.full: From H1 and H7171; father of plenty (that is, prosperous); Abishua, the name of two Israelites: - Abishua.

H51.full: From H1 and H7791; father of (the) wall (that is, perhaps mason), Abishur, an Israelites: - Abishur.

H52.full: ab-ee-shah'ee, ab-shah'ee From H1 and H7862; father of a gift (that is, probably generous); Abishai, an Israelite: - Abishai.

H53.full: ab-ee-shaw-lome', ab-shaw-lome' From H1 and H7965; father of peace (that is, friendly); Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite: - Abishalom, Absalom.

H54.full: eb-yaw-thawr' Contracted from H1 and H3498; father of abundance (that is, liberal); Ebjathar, an Israelite: - Abiathar.

H55.full: aw-bak' A primitive root; probably to coil upward: - mount up.

H56.full: aw-bal' A primitive root; to bewail: - lament, mourn.

H58.full: From an unused root (meaning to be grassy); a meadow: - plain. Compare also the proper names beginning with Abel-.

H59.full: From H58; a meadow; Abel, the name of two places in Palestine: - Abel.

H61.full: Apparently from H56 through the idea of negation; nay, that is, truly or yet: - but, indeed, nevertheless, verily.

H62.full: From H58 and H1004 and H4601; meadow of Beth-Maakah; Abel of Beth-Maakah, a place in Palestine: - Abel-beth-maachah, Abel of Beth-maachah.

H63.full: aw-bale' hash-shit-teem' From H58 and the plural of H7848, with the article inserted; meadow of the acacias; Abel hash-Shittim, a place in Palestine: - Abel-shittim.

H64.full: aw-bale' ker-aw-meem' From H58 and the plural of H3754; meadow of vineyards; Abel-Keramim, a place in Palestine: - plain of the vineyards.

H65.full: aw-bale' mekh-o-law' From H58 and H4246; meadow of dancing; Abel-Mecholah, a place in Palestine: - Abel-meholah.

H66.full: aw-bale' mah'-yim From H58 and H4325; meadow of water; Abel-Majim, a place in Palestine: - Abel-maim.

H67.full: aw-bale' mits-rah'-yim From H58 and H4714; meadow of Egypt; Abel-Mitsrajim, a place in Palestine: - Abel-mizraim.

H68.firstSense: + carbuncle, + mason, + plummet, [chalk-, hail-, bead-, sling-] stone (-ny), (divers) w…
H68.full: eh'-ben From the root of H1129 through the meaning, to build; a stone: - + carbuncle, + mason, + plummet, [chalk-, hail-, bead-, sling-] stone (-ny), (divers) weight (-s).

H70.full: o'-ben From the same as H68; a pair of stones (only dual); a potter's wheel or a midwife's stool (consisting alike of two horizontal disks with a support between): - wheel, stool.

H71.full: Perhaps feminine of H68; stony; Abanah, a river near Damascus: - Abana. Compare H549.

H72.full: eh'-ben haw-e'-zer From H68 and H5828 with the article inserted; stone of the help; Eben ha-Ezer, a place in Palestine: - Ebenezer.

H73.full: Of uncertain derivation; a belt: - girdle.

H74.full: ab-nare', ab-ee-nare' From H1 and H5216; father of light (that is, enlightening); Abner, an Israelite: - Abner.

H75.full: aw-bas' A primitive root; to fodder: - fatted, stalled.

H76.full: (By reduplication) from an unused root (meaning to belch forth); an inflammatory pustule (as eruption): - blains.

H77.full: eh'-bets From an unused root, probably means to gleam; conspicuous; Ebets, a place in Palestine: - Abez.

H78.full: ib-tsawn' From the same as H76; splendid; Ibtsan, an Israelite: - Ibzan.

H79.full: aw-bak' A primitive root; probably to float away (as vapor), but used only as denominative from H80; to bedust, that is, grapple: - wrestle.

H80.full: From root of H79; light particles (as volatile): - (small) dust, powder.

H82.full: aw-bar' A primitive root; to soar: - fly.

H83.full: ay-ber' From H82; a pinion: - [long-] wing (-ed).

H84.full: eb-raw' Feminine of H83: - feather, wing.

H85.full: ab-raw-hawm' Contracted from H1 and an unused root (probably meaning to be populous); father of a multitude; Abraham, the later name of Abram: - Abraham.

H86.full: ab-rake' Probably an Egyptian word meaning kneel: - bow the knee.

H87.full: ab-rawm' Contracted from H48; high father; Abram, the original name of Abraham: - Abram.

H88.full: Plural of H178; water skins; oboth, a place in the Desert: - Oboth.

H89.full: Of uncertain derivation (compare H90); Age, an Israelite: - Agee.

H90.full: ag-ag' Of uncertain derivation (compare H89); flame; Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings: - Agag.

H91.full: Patrial or patronymic from H90; an Agagite or descendant (subject) of Agag: - Agagite.

H92.full: Feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to bind); a band, bundle, knot, or arch: - bunch, burden, troop.

H93.full: Probably of Persian origin; a nut: - nut.

H94.full: Passive participle of H103; gathered (that is, received among the sages); Agur, a fanciful name of Solomon: - Agur.

H95.full: From the same as H94; properly something gathered, that is, perhaps a grain or berry; used only of a small (silver) coin: - piece [of] silver.

H96.full: eh'-ghel From an unused root (meaning to flow down or together as drops); a reservoir: - drop.

H97.full: eg-lah'-yim Dual of H96; a double pond; Eglajim, a place in Moab: - Eglaim.

H98.full: ag-am' From an unused root (meaning to collect as water); a marsh; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds: - pond, pool, standing [water].

H99.full: Probably from the same as H98 (in the sense of stagnant water); figuratively sad: - pond.

H100.full: ag-mone' From the same as H98; a marshy pool (others from a different root, a kettle); by implication a rush (as growing there); collectively a rope of rushes: - bulrush, caldron, hook, rush.

H101.full: ag-gawn' Probably from H5059; a bowl (as pounded out hollow): - basin, cup, goblet.

H102.full: ag-gawf' Probably from H5062 (through the idea of impending); a cover or heap; that is, (only plural) wings of an army, or crowds of troops: - bands.

H103.full: aw-gar' A primitive root; to harvest: - gather.

H104.full: ig-er-aw' (Chaldee); of Persian origin; an epistle (as carried by a state courier or postman): - letter.

H105.full: Of uncertain derivation; a basin: - charger.

H106.full: eg-rofe' From H1640 (in the sense of grasping); the clenched hand: - fist.

H107.full: ig-eh'-reth Feminine of H104; an epistle: - letter.

H108.full: From the same as H181 (in the sense of enveloping); a fog: - mist, vapor.

H109.full: aw-dab' A primitive root; to languish: - grieve.

H110.full: ad-beh-ale' Probably from H109 (in the sense of chastisement) and H410; disciplined of God; Adbeel, a son of Ishmael: - Adbeel.

H111.full: ad-ad' Probably an orthographical variation for H2301; Adad (or Hadad), an Edomite: - Hadad.

H112.full: id-do Of uncertain derivation; Iddo, an Israelite: - Iddo.

H113.full: From an unused root (meaning to rule); sovereign, that is, controller (human or divine): - lord, master, owner. Compare also names beginning with "Adoni-".

H114.full: ad-done' Probably intensive for H113; powerful; Addon, apparently an Israelite: - Addon.

H115.full: ad-o-rah'-yim Dual from H142 (in the sense of eminence); double mound; Adorajim, a place in Palestine: - Adoraim.

H116.full: ed-ah'-yin (Chaldee); of uncertain derivation; then (of time): - now, that time, then.

H117.firstSense: excellent, famous, gallant, glorious, goodly, lordly, mighty (-ier, one), noble, princi…
H117.full: ad-deer' From H142; wide or (generally) large; figuratively powerful: - excellent, famous, gallant, glorious, goodly, lordly, mighty (-ier, one), noble, principal, worthy.

H118.full: ad-al-yaw' Of Persian derivation; Adalja, a son of Haman: - Adalia.

H119.full: aw-dam' To show blood (in the face), that is, flush or turn rosy: - be (dyed, made) red (ruddy).

H120.firstSense: X another, + hypocrite, + common sort, X low, man (mean, of low degree), person
H120.full: From H119; ruddy, that is, a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.): - X another, + hypocrite, + common sort, X low, man (mean, of low degree), person.

H121.full: The same as H120; Adam, the name of the first man, also of a place in Palestine: - Adam.

H123.full: From H122; red (see Gen_25:25); Edom, the elder twin-brother of Jacob; hence the region (Idumaea) occuped by him: - Edom, Edomites, Idumea.

H124.full: o'-dem From H119; redness, that is, the ruby, garnet, or some other red gem: - sardius.

H125.full: ad-am-dawm' Reduplicated from H119; reddish: - (somewhat) reddish.

H126.full: ad-maw' Contracted for H127; earthy; Admah, a place near the Dead Sea: - Admah.

H127.full: From H119; soil (from its general redness): - country, earth, ground, husband [-man] (-ry), land.

H128.full: The same as H127; Adamah, a place in Palestine: - Adamah.

H129.full: From H127; earthy; Adami, a place in Palestine: - Adami.

H130.full: Patronymic from H123; an Edomite, or descendant from (or inhabitant of) Edom: - Edomite. See H726.

H131.full: Plural of H121; red spots; Adummim, a pass in Palestine: - Adummim.

H132.full: ad-mo-nee', ad-mo-nee' From H119; reddish (of the hair or the complexion): - red, ruddy.

H133.full: ad-maw-thaw' Probably of Persian derivation; Admatha, a Persian nobleman: - Admatha.

H134.full: eh'-den From the same as H113 (in the sense of strength); a basis (of a building, a column, etc.): - foundation, socket.

H135.full: ad-dawn' Intensive from the same as H134; firm; Addan, an Israelite: - Addan.

H136.full: An emphatic form of H113; the Lord (used as a proper name of God only): - (my) Lord.

H137.full: ad-o''-nee-beh'-zek From H113 and H966; lord of Bezek; Adoni-Bezek, a Canaanitish king: - Adoni-bezek.

H138.full: From H113 and H3050; lord (that is, worshipper) of Jah; Adonijah, the name of three Israelites: - Adonijah.

H139.full: ad-o''-nee-tseh'-dek From H113 and H6664; lord of justice; Adoni-Tsedek, a Canaanitish king: - Adonizedec.

H140.full: From H113 and H6965; lord of rising (that is, high); Adonikam, the name of one or two Israelites: - Adonikam

H141.full: From H113 and H7311; lord of height; Adoniram, an Israelite: - Adoniram.

H142.full: aw-dar A primitive root; to expand, that is, be great or (figuratively) magnificent: - (become) glorious, honourable.

H143.full: Probably of foreign derivation; perhaps meaning fire; Adar, the H12 th Hebrew month: - Adar.

H145.full: eh'-der From H142; amplitude, that is, (concretely) a mantle; also (figuratively) splendor: - goodly, robe.

H146.full: ad-dawr' Intensive from H142; ample; Addar, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite: - Addar.

H147.full: id-dar' (Chaldee); intensive from a root corresponding to H142; ample, that is, a threshing-floor: - threshingfloor.

H148.full: ad-ar''-gaw-zare' (Chaldee); from the same as H147, and H1505; a chief diviner, or astrologer: - judge.

H149.full: ad-raz-daw' (Chaldee); probably of Persian origin; quickly or carefully: - dilligently.

H150.full: ad-ar-kone' Of Persian origin; a daric or Persian coin: - dram.

H151.full: Contracted for H141; Adoram (or Adoniram), an Israelite: - Adoram.

H152.full: ad-ram-meh'-lek From H142 and H4428; splendor of (the) king; Adrammelek, the name of an Assyrian idol, also of a son of Sennacherib: - Adrammelech.

H153.full: (Chaldee); an orthographical variation for H1872; an arm, that is, (figuratively) power: - force.

H154.full: ed-reh'-ee From the equivalent of H153; mighty; Edrei, the name of two places in Palestine: - Edrei.

H155.full: ad-deh'-reth Feminine of H117; something ample (as a large vine, a wide dress); also the same as H145: - garment, glory, goodly, mantle, robe.

H156.full: aw-dash' A primitive root; to tread out (grain): - thresh.

H157.full: A primitive root; to have affection for (sexually or otherwise): - (be-) love (-d, -ly, -r), like, friend.

H158.full: ah'-hab From H157; affection (in a good or a bad sense): - love (-r).

H159.full: o'-hab From H156; meaning the same as H158: - love.

H160.full: a-hab-aw' Feminine of H158 and meaning the same: - love.

H161.full: o'-had From an unused root meaning to be united; unity; Ohad, an Israelite: - Ohad.

H162.full: Apparently a primitive word expressing pain exclamatorily; Oh!: - ah, alas.

H163.full: Probably of foreign origin; Ahava, a river of Babylonia: - Ahava.

H164.full: From the same as H161; united; Ehud, the name of two or three Israelite: - Ehud.

H165.firstSense: I will be (Hos_13:10, Hos_13:14) [which is often the rendering of the same Hebrew form…
H165.full: Apparently an orthographical variation for H346; where. (Used in Hos_13:10, Hos_13:14). "I will be" is often the rendering of the same Hebrew form from H1961: - I will be (Hos_13:10, Hos_13:14) [which is often the rendering of the same Hebrew form from H1961].

H166.full: aw-hal' A primitive root; to be clear: - shine.

H167.full: aw-hal' A denominative from H168; to tent: - pitch (remove) a tent.

H168.full: o'-hel From H166; a tent (as clearly conspicuous from a distance): - covering, (dwelling) (place), home, tabernacle, tent.

H169.full: o'-hel The same as H168; Ohel, an Israelite: - Ohel.

H170.full: o-hol-aw', o-hol-aw' The first form is in form a feminine of H168, but is in fact for the second form; from H168; her tent (that is, idolatrous sanctuary); Oholah, a symbolic name for Samaria: - Aholah.

H171.full: From H168 and H1; tent of (his) father; Oholiab, an Israelite: - Aholiab.

H172.full: o''-hol-ee-baw', o''-hol-e-baw' (As with H170 the first form is in form a feminine of H168, but is in fact for the second form); from H168; my tent (is) in her; Oholibah, a symbolic name for Judah: - Aholibah.

H173.full: From H168 and H1116; tent of (the) height; Oholibamah, a wife of Esau: - Aholibamah.

H174.full: (The second form, which is feminine, is used only in the plural); of foreign origin; aloe wood (that is, sticks): - (tree of lign-) aloes.

H175.full: a-har-one' Of uncertain derivation; Aharon, the brother of Moses: - Aaron.

H176.firstSense: also, and, either, if, at the least, X nor, or, otherwise, then, whether
H176.full: o, av The first form is presumed to be the "constructive" or genitival form of the second form which is short for H185; desire (and so probably in Pro_31:4); hence (by way of alternative) or, also if: - also, and, either, if, at the least, X nor, or, otherwise, then, whether.

H177.full: From H176 and H410; wish of God; Uel, an Israelite: - Uel.

H178.full: From the same as H1 (apparently through the idea of prattling a father's name); properly a mumble, that is, a water skin (from its hollow sound); hence a necromancer (ventriloquist, as from a jar): - bottle, familiar spirit.

H179.full: Probably from H56; mournful; Obil, an Ishmaelite: - Obil.

H180.full: From H2986 (in the sense of H2988); a stream: - river.

H181.full: From an unused root meaning to rake together; a poker (for turning or gathering embers): - (fire-) brand.

H182.full: From the same as H181; turnings (that is, occasions); (adverbially) on account of: - (be-) cause, concerning, sake.

H183.firstSense: covet, (greatly) desire, be desirous, long, lust (after)
H183.full: A primitive root; to wish for: - covet, (greatly) desire, be desirous, long, lust (after).

H184.full: A primitive root; to extend or mark out: - point out.

H185.full: av-vaw' From H183; longing: - desire, lust after, pleasure.

H186.full: oo-zah'ee Perhaps by permutation for H5813, strong; Uzai, an Israelite: - Uzai.

H187.full: Of uncertain derivation; Uzal, a son of Joktan: - Uzal.

H188.full: Probably from H183 (in the sense of crying out after); lamentation; also interjectionally, Oh!: - alas, woe.

H189.full: Probably from H183; desirous; Evi, a Midianitish chief: - Evi.

H191.full: From an unused root (meaning to be perverse); (figuratively) silly: - fool (-ish) (man).

H192.full: ev-eel' mer-o-dak' Of Chaldee derivation and probably meaning soldier of Merodak; Evil-Merodak, a Babylonian king: - Evil-merodach.

H193.full: From an unused root meaning to twist, that is, (by implication) be strong; the body (as being rolled together) also powerful: - mighty, strength.

H194.firstSense: if so be, may be, peradventure, unless
H194.full: oo-lah'ee, oo-lah'ee From H176; if not; hence perhaps: - if so be, may be, peradventure, unless.

H195.full: oo-lah'ee Of Persian derivation; the Ulai (or Eulaeus), a river of Persia: - Ulai.

H196.full: ev-ee-lee' From H191; silly, foolish; hence (morally) impious: - foolish.

H197.full: From H481 (in the sense of tying); a vestibule (as bound to the building): - porch.

H198.full: Apparently from H481 (in the sense of dumbness); solitary; Ulam, the name of two Israelites: - Ulam.

H199.firstSense: as for, but, howbeit, in very deed, surely, truly, wherefore
H199.full: Apparently a variation of H194; however or on the contrary: - as for, but, howbeit, in very deed, surely, truly, wherefore.

H200.full: iv-veh'-leth From the same as H191; silliness: - folly, foolishly (-ness).

H201.full: From H559; talkative; Omar, a grandson of Esau: - Omar.

H202.full: Probably from the same as H205 (in the sense of effort, but successful); ability, power, (figuratively) wealth: - force, goods, might, strength, substance.

H203.full: The same as H202; On, an Israelite: - On.

H204.full: Of Egyptian derivation; On, a city of Egypt: - On.

H205.firstSense: affliction, evil, false, idol, iniquity, mischief, mourners (-ing), naught, sorrow, unj…
H205.full: aw'-ven From an unused root perhaps meaning properly to pant (hence to exert oneself, usually in vain; to come to naught); strictly nothingness; also trouble, vanity, wickedness; specifically an idol: - affliction, evil, false, idol, iniquity, mischief, mourners (-ing), naught, sorrow, unjust, unrighteous, vain, vanity, wicked (-ness.) Compare H369.

H206.full: aw'-ven The same as H205; idolatry; Aven, the contemptuous synonym of three places, one in Coele Syria, one in Egypt (On), and one in Palestine (Bethel): - Aven. See also H204, H1007.

H207.full: From H202; strong; Ono, a place in Palestine: - Ono.

H208.full: A variation of H209; strong; Onam, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite: - Onam.

H209.full: A variation of H207; strong; Onan, a son of Judah: - Onan.

H210.full: Perhaps a corruption of H211; Uphaz, a famous gold region: - Uphaz.

H211.full: o-feer', o-feer', o-feer' Of uncertain derivation; Ophir, the name of a son of Joktan, and of a gold region in the East: - Ophir.

H212.full: From an unused root meaning to revolve; a wheel: - wheel.

H213.full: oots A primitive root; to press; (by implication) to be close, hurry, withdraw: - (make) haste (-n, -y), labor, be narrow.

H214.full: From H686; a depository: - armory, cellar, garner, store(-house), treasure (-house) (-y).

H215.firstSense: X break of day, glorious, kindle, (be, en-, give, show) light (-en, -ened), set on fire…
H215.full: A primitive root; to be (causatively make) luminous (literally and metaphorically): - X break of day, glorious, kindle, (be, en-, give, show) light (-en, -ened), set on fire, shine.

H216.firstSense: bright, clear, + day, light (-ning), morning, sun
H216.full: From H215; illumination or (concretely) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.): - bright, clear, + day, light (-ning), morning, sun.

H217.full: From H215; flame, hence (in the plural) the East (as being the region of light): - fire, light. See also H224.

H218.full: The same as H217; Ur, a place in Chaldaea; also an Israelite: - Ur.

H219.full: Feminine of H216; luminousness, that is, (figuratively) prosperity; also a plant (as being bright): - herb light.

H220.full: By transposition for H723; a stall: - cote.

H221.full: From H217; fiery; Uri, the name of three Israelites: - Uri.

H222.full: From H217 and H410; flame of God; Uriel, the name of two Israelites: - Uriel.

H223.full: From H217 and H3050; flame of Jah; Urijah, the name of one Hittite and five Israelites: - Uriah, Urijah.

H224.full: Plural of H217; lights; Urim, the oracular brilliancy of the figures in the high priest's breastplate: - Urim.

H225.full: ooth A primitive root; properly to come, that is, (impliedly) to assent: - consent.

H226.full: oth Probably from H225 (in the sense of appearing); a signal (literally or figuratively), as a flag, beacon, monument, omen, prodigy, evidence, etc.: - mark, miracle, (en-) sign, token.

H227.firstSense: beginning, for, from, hitherto, now, of old, once, since, then, at which time, yet
H227.full: A demonstrative adverb; at that time or place; also as a conjugation, therefore: - beginning, for, from, hitherto, now, of old, once, since, then, at which time, yet.

H228.full: (Chaldee); to kindle; (by implication) to heat: - heat, hot.

H229.full: ez-bah'ee Probably from H231; hyssop like; Ezbai, an Israelite: - Ezbai.

H230.full: (Chaldee); of uncertain derivation; firm: - be gone.

H231.full: Probably of foreign derivation; hyssop: - hyssop.

H232.full: From H246; something girt; a belt, also a band: - girdle.

H233.full: az-ah'ee Probably from H227; at that time: - then.

H234.full: az-kaw-raw' From H2142; a reminder; specifically remembrance offering: - memorial.

H235.firstSense: fail, gad about, go to and fro [but in Eze_27:19 the word is rendered by many "from Uza…
H235.full: aw-zal' A primitive root; to go away, hence to disappear: - fail, gad about, go to and fro [but in Eze_27:19 the word is rendered by many "from Uzal," by others "yarn"], be gone (spent).

H236.full: az-al' (Chaldee); the same as H235; to depart: - go (up).

H237.full: eh'-zel From H235; departure; ezel, a memorial stone in Palestine: - Ezel.

H238.full: aw-zan' A primitive root; probably to expand; but used only as a denominative from H241; to broaden out the ear (with the hand), that is, (by implication) to listen: - give (perceive by the) ear, hear (-ken). See H239.

H239.full: aw-zan' A primitive root (rather identical with H238 through the idea of scales as if two ears); to weigh, that is, (figuratively) ponder: - give good heed.

H240.full: From H238; a spade or paddle (as having a broad end): - weapon.

H241.firstSense: + advertise, audience, + displease, ear, hearing, + show
H241.full: o'-zen From H238; broadness, that is, (concretely) the ear (from its form in man): - + advertise, audience, + displease, ear, hearing, + show.

H242.full: ooz-zane' sheh-er-aw' From H238 and H7609; plat of Sheerah (that is, settled by him); Uzzen Sheerah, a place in Palestine: - Uzzen-sherah.

H243.full: az-noth' taw-bore' From H238 and H8396; flats (that is, tops) of Tabor (that is, situated on it); aznoth Tabor, a place in Palestine: - Aznoth-tabor.

H244.full: oz-nee' From H241; having (quick) ears; Ozni, an Israelite; also an Oznite (collectively), his descendants: - Ozni, Oznites.

H245.full: az-an-yaw' From H238 and H3050; heard by Jah; Azanjah, an Israelite: - Azaniah.

H246.full: az-ik-keem' A variation for H2131; manacles: - chains.

H247.full: aw-zar' A primitive root; to belt: - bind (compass) about, gird (up, with).

H248.full: A variation for H2220; the arm: - arm.

H249.firstSense: bay tree, (home-) born (in the land), of the (one's own) country (nation)
H249.full: ez-rawkh' From H2224 (in the sense of springing up); a spontaneous growth, that is, native (tree or persons): - bay tree, (home-) born (in the land), of the (one's own) country (nation).

H250.full: ez-raw-khee' Patronymic from H2246; an Ezrachite or descendants of Zerach: - Ezrahite.

H251.full: awkh A primitive word; a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance (like H1)): - another, brother (-ly), kindred, like, other. Compare also the proper names beginning with "Ah-" or "Ahi-".

H253.full: awkh A variation for H162; Oh! (expressive of grief or surprise): - ah, alas.

H254.full: awkh Of uncertain derivation; a fire pot or chafing dish: - hearth.

H255.full: o'-akh Probably from H253; a howler or lonesome wild animal: - doleful creature.

H256.full: akh-awb', ekh-awb' The second form used once (by contraction) in Jer_29:22; from H251 and H1; brother (that is, friend) of (his) father; Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon: - Ahab.

H257.full: akh-bawn' From H251 and H995; brother (that is, possessor) of understanding; Achban, an Israelite: - Ahban.

H258.full: aw-khad' Perhaps a primitive root; to unify, that is, (figuratively) collect (one's thoughts): - go one way or other.

H259.firstSense: a, alike, alone, altogether, and, any (-thing), apiece, a certain [dai-] ly, each (one)…
H259.full: ekh-awd' A numeral from H258; properly united, that is, one; or (as an ordinal) first: - a, alike, alone, altogether, and, any (-thing), apiece, a certain [dai-] ly, each (one), + eleven, every, few, first, + highway, a man, once, one, only, other, some, together.

H260.full: Of uncertain (perhaps Egyptian) derivation; a bulrush or any marshy grass (particularly that along the Nile): - flag, meadow.

H261.full: From H258; united; Echud, the name of three Israelites: - Ehud.

H262.full: akh-vaw' From H2331 (in the sense of H2324); an utterance: - declaration.

H263.full: akh-av-aw' (Chaldee); corresponding to H262; solution (of riddles): - showing.

H265.full: akh-o'-akh By reduplication from H251; brotherly; Achoach, an Israelite: - Ahoah.

H266.full: Patronymic from H264; an Achochite or descendants of Achoach: - Ahohite.

H267.full: akh-oo-mah'ee Perhaps from H251 and H4325; brother (that is, neighbour) of water; Achumai, an Israelite: - Ahumai.

H268.firstSense: after (-ward), back (part, -side, -ward), hereafter, (be-) hind (-er part), time to com…
H268.full: From H299; the hinder part; hence (adverbially) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West: - after (-ward), back (part, -side, -ward), hereafter, (be-) hind (-er part), time to come, without.

H269.full: aw-khoth' Irregular feminine of H251; a sister (used very widely (like H250), literally and figuratively): - (an-) other, sister, together.

H270.firstSense: + be affrighted, bar, (catch, lay, take) hold (back), come upon, fasten, handle, portio…
H270.full: aw-khaz' A primitive root; to seize (often with the accessory idea of holding in possession): - + be affrighted, bar, (catch, lay, take) hold (back), come upon, fasten, handle, portion, (get, have or take) possess (-ion).

H271.full: From H270; possessor; Achaz, the name of a Jewish king and of an Israelite: - Ahaz.

H272.full: Feminine passive participle of H270; something seized, that is, a possession (especially of land): - possession.

H273.full: akh-zah'ee From H270; seizer; Achzai, an Israelite: - Ahasai.

H274.full: akh-az-yaw', akh-az-yaw'-hoo From H270 and H3050; Jah has seized; Achazjah, the name of a Jewish and an Israelitish king: - Ahaziah.

H275.full: From H270; seizure; Achuzzam, an Israelite: - Ahuzam.

H276.full: akh-ooz-zath' A variation of H272; possession; Achuzzath, a Philistine: - Ahuzzath.

H277.full: From H251; brotherly; Achi, the name of two Israelites: - Ahi.

H278.full: Probably the same as H277; Echi, an Israelite: - Ehi.

H279.full: From H251 and H517; brother of the mother (that is, uncle); Achiam, an Israelite: - Ahiam.

H280.full: (Chaldee); corresponding to H2420, an enigma: - hard sentence.

H281.full: From H251 and H3050; brother (that is, worshipper) of Jah; Achijah, the name of nine Israelites: - Ahiah, Ahijah.

H282.full: From H251 and H1935; brother (that is, possessor) of renown; Achihud, an Israelite: - Ahihud.

H283.full: akh-yo' Prolonged from H251; brotherly; Achio, the name of three Israelites: - Ahio.

H284.full: akh-ee-khood' From H251 and H2330; brother of a riddle (that is, mysterious); Achichud, an Israelite: - Ahihud.

H285.full: From H251 and H2898; brother of goodness; Achitub, the name of several priests: - Ahitub.

H286.full: From H251 and H3205; brother of one born; Achilud, an Israelite: - Ahilud.

H287.full: akh-ee-moth' From H251 and H4191; brother of death; Achimoth, an Israelite: - Ahimoth.

H288.full: akh-ee-meh'-lek From H251 and H4428; brother of (the) king; Achimelek, the name of an Israelite and of a Hittite: - Ahimelech.

H289.full: akh-ee-man', akh-ee-mawn' From H251 and H4480; brother of a portion (that is, gift); Achiman, the name of an Anakite and of an Israelite: - Ahiman.

H290.full: akh-ee-mah'-ats From H251 and the equivalent of H4619; brother of anger; Achimaats, the name of three Israelites: - Ahimaaz.

H291.full: akh-yawn' From H251; brotherly; Achjan, an Israelite: - Ahian.

H292.full: From H251 and H5068; brother of liberality; Achinadab, an Israelite: - Ahinadab.

H293.full: From H251 and H5278; brother of pleasantness; Achinoam, the name of two Israelitesses: - Ahinoam.

H294.full: From H251 and H5564; brother of support; Achisamak, an Israelite: - Ahisamach.

H295.full: akh-ee-eh'-zer From H251 and H5828; brother of help; Achiezer, the name of two Israelites: - Ahiezer.

H296.full: From H251 and H6965; brother of rising (that is, high); Achikam, an Israelite: - Ahikam.

H297.full: From H251 and H7311; brother of height (that is, high); Achiram, an Israelite: - Ahiram.

H298.full: Patronymic from H297; an Achiramite or descendants (collectively) of Achiram: - Ahiramites.

H299.full: From H251 and H7451; brother of wrong; Achira, an Israelite: - Ahira.

H300.full: akh-ee-shakh'-ar From H251 and H7837; brother of (the) dawn; Achishachar, an Israelite: - Ahishar.

H301.full: akh-ee-shawr' From H251 and H7891; brother of (the) singer; Achishar, an Israelite: - Ahishar.

H302.full: akh-ee-tho'-fel From H251 and H8602; brother of folly; Achithophel, an Israelite: - Ahithophel.

H303.full: akh-lawb' From the same root as H2459; fatness (that is, fertile); Achlab, a place in Palestine: - Ahlab.

H304.full: akh-lah'ee The same as H305; wishful; Achlai, the name of an Israelitess and of an Israelite: - Ahlai.

H305.full: ak-al-ah'ee, akh-al-ay' Probably from H253 and a variation of H3863; would that!: - O that, would God.

H306.full: akh-law'-maw Perhaps from H2492 (and thus dream stone); a gem, probably the amethyst: - amethyst.

H307.full: akh-me-thaw' Of Persian derivation; Achmetha (that is, Ecbatana), the summer capital of Persia: - Achmetha.

H308.full: akh-as-bah'ee Of uncertain derivation; Achasbai, an Israelite: - Ahasbai.

H309.firstSense: continue, defer, delay, hinder, be late (slack), stay (there), tarry (longer)
H309.full: aw-khar' A primitive root; to loiter (that is, be behind); by implication to procrastinate: - continue, defer, delay, hinder, be late (slack), stay (there), tarry (longer).

H310.firstSense: after (that, -ward), again, at, away from, back (from, -side), behind, beside, by, foll…
H310.full: akh-ar' From H309; properly the hind part; generally used as an adverb or conjugation, after (in various senses): - after (that, -ward), again, at, away from, back (from, -side), behind, beside, by, follow (after, -ing), forasmuch, from, hereafter, hinder end, + out (over) live, + persecute, posterity, pursuing, remnant, seeing, since, thence [-forth], when, with.

H311.full: akh-ar' (Chaldee); corresponding to H310; after: - [here-] after.

H312.full: akh-air' From H309; properly hinder; generally next, other, etc.: - (an-) other (man), following, next, strange.

H313.full: akh-air' The same as H312; Acher, an Israelite: - Aher.

H314.firstSense: after (-ward), to come, following, hind (-er, -ermost, -most), last, latter, rereward,…
H314.full: akh-ar-one', akh-ar-one' From H309; hinder; generally late or last; specifically (as facing the east) western: - after (-ward), to come, following, hind (-er, -ermost, -most), last, latter, rereward, ut(ter)most.

H315.full: akh-rakh From H310 and H251; after (his) brother; Achrach, an Israelite: - Aharah.

H316.full: akh-ar-kale' From H310 and H2426; behind (the) intrenchment (that is, safe); Acharchel, an Israelite: - Aharhel.

H318.full: okh-or-ane', okh-or-ane' (Chaldee); from H317; last: - at last.

H319.firstSense: (last, latter) end (time), hinder (utter) -most, length, posterity, remnant, residue, r…
H319.full: akh-ar-eeth' From H310; the last or end, hence the future; also posterity: - (last, latter) end (time), hinder (utter) -most, length, posterity, remnant, residue, reward.

H320.full: akh-ar-eeth' (Chaldee); from H311; the same as H319; later: - latter.

H321.full: okh-or-awn' (Chaldee); from H311; the same as H317; other: - (an-) other.

H322.full: akh-o-ran-neeth' Prolonged from H268; backwards: - back(-ward, again).

H323.full: akh-ash-dar-pan' Of Persian derivation; a satrap or governor of a main province (of Persia): - lieutenant.

H325.full: akh-ash-vay-rosh', akh-ash-rosh' Of Persian origin; Achashverosh (that is, Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, but in this case Xerxes), the title (rather than name) of a Persian king: - Ahasuerus.

H326.full: akh-ash-taw-ree' Probably of Persian derivation; an achastarite (that is, courier); the designation (rather than name) of an Israelite: - Haakashtari [includ. the article.]

H327.full: akh-ash-taw-rawn' Of Persian origin; a mule: - camel.

H328.full: From an unused root perhaps meaning to move softly; (as a noun) a necromancer (from their soft incantations), (as an adverb) gently: - charmer, gently, secret, softly.

H329.full: From an unused root probably meaning to pierce or make fast; a thorn tree (especially the buckthorn): - Atad, bramble, thorn.

H330.full: From an unused root (probably meaning to bind); properly twisted (yarn), that is, tapestry: - fine linen.

H331.full: A primitive root; to close (the lips or ears); by analogy to contract (a window by bevelled jambs): - narrow, shut, stop.

H332.full: A primitive root; to close up: - shut.

H333.full: From H332; maimed; Ater, the name of three Israelites: - Ater.

H334.full: From H332; shut up, the is, impeded (as to the use of the right hand): - + left-handed.

H335.firstSense: how, what, whence, where, whether, which (way)
